\section[\texttt{a2ac} -- AFM to AFM plus Composites]{\texttt{a2ac} -- AFM to AFM plus Composites}\label{pkg:a2ac}
\index{Package!a2ac}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/a2ac}
\item[name] \texttt{a2ac}
\item[caption] AFM to AFM plus Composites
\item[author] Olšák, Petr
\index{Author!Olšák, Petr}
\item[license] other-nonfree = License that prevents distribution (not free)
\index{License!other-nonfree}
\index{License!License that prevents distribution}
\item[version] 2
\item[description] (no language specified) Enables the use of PostScript fonts while typesetting texts in languages where inflected letters are 
          used. The font will typically not contain the complete alphabet of a given language; the program will 
          derive composite glyph structures using accent glyphs, and output their details in the derived AFM file.

          The configuration files of the program are independent of the PostScript font encoding and of the typesetting 
          system encoding. The program may be used to prepare a font for any typesetting system, especially TeX.
\item[documentation] \textit{Package documentation (English)}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/a2ac/a2ac-eng.txt}

\index{Topic!font-proc}

\section[\texttt{a2ping} -- Advanced PS, PDF, EPS converter]{\texttt{a2ping} -- Advanced PS, PDF, EPS converter}\label{pkg:a2ping}
\index{Package!a2ping}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/a2ping}
\item[name] \texttt{a2ping}
\item[caption] Advanced PS, PDF, EPS converter
\item[author] Szabó, Péter
\index{Author!Szabó, Péter}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 2.84p (2019-11-17)
\item[last changes] 2019-11-17
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) a2ping is a Perl script command line utility written for Unix that converts many raster image and vector 
          graphics formats to EPS or PDF and other page description formats. Accepted input file formats are: PS 
          (PostScript), EPS, PDF, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, PNM, BMP, GIF, LBM, XPM, PCX, TGA. Accepted output formats are: 
          EPS, PCL5, PDF, PDF1, PBM, PGM, PPM, PS, markedEPS, markedPS, PNG, XWD, BMP, TIFF, JPEG, GIF, XPM. a2ping 
          delegates the low-level work to Ghostscript (GS), pdftops and  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/sam2p}{sam2p} . 
          a2ping fixes many glitches during the EPS to EPS conversion, so its output is often more compatible and 
          better embeddable than its input.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/a2ping/README.txt}
\item[contact] \textit{repository}: \url{https://github.com/pts/a2ping}
\index{Contact!repository}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/a2ping}
\item[on Mik\TeX] \texttt{a2ping}
\item[on \TeX Live] \texttt{a2ping}
\item[keyword] \texttt{graphics-prep} (prepare graphics for use with *TeX)
\index{Topic!graphics-prep}
\item[language(s)] no language specified
\index{Language in description/documentation!no language specified}

\end{labeling}

\item[version] 1.2g
\item[description] (no language specified) Provides support for A4 paper sizes, superseding a LaTeX 2.09 package of the same name (the package was 
          developed from a now-extinct package called a4dutch).

          The package is mostly superseded by the  \texttt{a4paper} option of LaTeX itself and by the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry}{geometry} package. 
          Its margins are slightly narrower than those of the \texttt{a4paper} option (there are those 
          that claim this is a typographically poor choice), but it also has a \texttt{widemargins} option.

          The package is now distributed as part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ntgclass}{ntgclass} bundle.

\section[\texttt{abbrevs} -- Text abbreviations in LaTeX]{\texttt{abbrevs} -- Text abbreviations in LaTeX}\label{pkg:abbrevs}
\index{Package!abbrevs}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/abbrevs}
\item[name] \texttt{abbrevs}
\item[caption] Text abbreviations in LaTeX
\item[author] Swift, Matt
\index{Author!Swift, Matt}
\item[copyright] Matt Swift (1995-2001)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.4
\item[description] (no language specified) A LaTeX package defining abbreviation macros, which expand to defined text and insert following space 
          intelligently, based on context. They can also expand to one thing the first time they are used and another 
          thing on subsequent invocations. Thus they can be abbreviations in two senses, in the source and in the 
          document. Also includes a facility for suffixes like 1900{\textbackslash}BC and 6:00{\textbackslash}PM 
          which correctly handles following periods.

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/frankenstein}{frankenstein} bundle.

\index{Package!aboensis}

\item[name] \texttt{Aboensis}
\item[caption] A late medieval OpenType cursive font
\item[author] Syrjänen, Tommi
\index{Author!Syrjänen, Tommi}
\item[copyright] Tommi Syrjänen (2021)
\item[license] cc-by-4 = CC BY 4.0 (free)
\index{License!cc-by-4}
\index{License!CC BY 4.0}
\item[license] ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
\index{License!ofl}
\index{License!The SIL Open Font License}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version]  (2021-07-24)
\item[last changes] 2021-07-24
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package contains the free OpenType medieval cursive font Aboensis and a style file to use it in XeLaTeX 
          documents.

          The font is based on Codex Aboensis, that is a law book written in Sweden in the 1430s. Since medieval 
          cursive is very difficult to read for modern people, the font is not suitable for use as an ordinary 
          book font, but is intended for emulating late medieval manuscripts.

          The font contains two sets of initials: Lombardic and cursive to go with the basic alphabet, and there 
          is support for writing two-colored initials and capitals. There are also a large number of abbreviation 
          sigla that can be accessed as ligature substitutions.

          The style file contains macros that help to use the extended features of the font such as initials and 
          two-colored capitals. There are also macros to help achieve even pages with consistent line spacing.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/aboensis/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/aboensis/aboensis.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5487295112-aboensis.pdf|

\section[\texttt{abspos} -- Absolute placement with coffins]{\texttt{abspos} -- Absolute placement with coffins}\label{pkg:abspos}
\index{Package!abspos}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/abspos}
\item[name] \texttt{abspos}
\item[caption] Absolute placement with coffins
\item[author] Hetland, Magnus Lie
\index{Author!Hetland, Magnus Lie}
\item[copyright] Magnus Lie Hetland (2021-2022)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version] 0.1 (2022-09-22)
\item[last changes] 2022-09-22
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package lets you place contents at an absolute position, anchored at some specified part of the 
          contents, similar to how  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} nodes work, though without 
          using the two-pass strategy of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} . It also avoids 
          messing with the order of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}{beamer} overlays, which 
          is what happens when one uses the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/textpos}{textpos} package 
          with the \texttt{overlay} option.

          The solution used is quite straightforward, combining  \emph{coffins} (using \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel}{l3coffins} ) 
          with the placement mechanisms of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/atbegshi}{atbegshi} .

\section[\texttt{academicons} -- Font containing high quality icons of online academic profil\ldots]{\texttt{academicons} -- Font containing high quality icons of online academic profiles}\label{pkg:academicons}
\index{Package!academicons}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/academicons}
\item[name] \texttt{academicons}
\item[caption] Font containing high quality icons of online academic profiles
\item[author] Fernandes, Diogo A. B.
\index{Author!Fernandes, Diogo A. B.}
\item[copyright] Diogo A. B. Fernandes (2015-2021)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[license] ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
\index{License!ofl}
\index{License!The SIL Open Font License}
\item[version] 1.9.6-2 (2025-09-20)
\item[last changes] 2025-09-20
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \texttt{academicons} package provides access in (La)TeX to 146 high quality icons of 
          online academic profiles included in the free ''Academicons'' font. This package works with both Xe(La)TeX 
          or Lua(La)TeX by using \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec}{fontspec} to load the included 
          font, as well as with pdf(La)TeX by loading a Type 1 converted format of the original font.

          The ''Academicons'' font was designed by James Walsh and released (see  \href{http://jpswalsh.github.io/academicons/}{http://jpswalsh.github.io/academicons/} ) 
          under the open SIL Open Font License. This package is a redistribution of the free ''Academicons'' font 
          with specific bindings for (La)TeX. It is inspired and based on the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontawesome}{fontawesome} package.

          The generic  \texttt{{\textbackslash}aiicon} macro takes as mandatory argument the \texttt{⟨name⟩} of 
          the desired icon. Icons can also be accessed directly by their respective macro. For example, \texttt{{\textbackslash}aiicon{\textbraceleft}googlescholar{\textbraceright}} yields 
          the same result as \texttt{{\textbackslash}aiGoogleScholar} . The full list of icons 
          with their respective names and direct commands can be found in the manual.

\item[version] 2.0.3 (2019-11-02)
\item[last changes] 2019-11-02
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \texttt{accessibility} package is intended to create tagged, structured PDF documents 
          from LaTeX source code. It allows to produce tagged PDF output following Adobe’s PDF-1.5 and 1.6 specifications.

          This package is predominantly targeted at documents produced using the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script}{KOMA-Script} document 
          classes.

          However, the author told us towards the end of June 2020: ''Based on feedback to the ‘accessibility’ 
          package and discussions with a few folks, I’d like to discourage people from using the package any more. 
          It’s evident that it’s not going to work in it’s current form, and I don’t have the skills or time to 
          update it. \\I know the general concept is very important, and so I’m looking at getting support 
          from various funding agencies to employ someone to completely refactor the code in a more future-proof 
          fashion. I’ll coordinate this with the core LaTeX Team once I have more solid ideas.''

\item[description] (no language specified) The accfonts package contains three utilities to permit easy manipulation of fonts, in particular the 
          creation of unusual accented characters. Mkt1font works on Adobe Type 1 fonts, vpl2vpl works on TeX virtual 
          fonts and vpl2ovp transforms a TeX font to an Omega one. All three programs read in a font (either the 
          font itself or a property list), together with a simple definition file containing lines such as ‘ \texttt{128 
          z acute} ’; they then write out a new version of the font with the requested new characters in the 
          numerical slots specified. Great care is taken over the positioning of accents, and over the provision 
          of kerning information for new characters; mkt1font also generates suitable ''hints'' to enhance quality 
          at small sizes or poor resolutions. The programs are written in Perl.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme and documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/accfonts/README}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/accfonts}
\item[on Mik\TeX] \texttt{accfonts}
\item[on \TeX Live] \texttt{accfonts}

\section[\texttt{acroflex} -- Create a graphing widget in a PDF file]{\texttt{acroflex} -- Create a graphing widget in a PDF file}\label{pkg:acroflex}
\index{Package!acroflex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/acroflex}
\item[name] \texttt{acroflex}
\item[caption] Create a graphing widget in a PDF file
\item[author] Story, Donald P.
\index{Author!Story, Donald P.}
\item[copyright] D. P. Story (2008-2016)
\item[license] lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
\index{License!lppl1}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1}
\item[version] 1.7 (2020-08-07)
\item[last changes] 2020-08-07
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) The acroflex package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/aeb-pro}{AeB Pro} family 
          of packages. It is a package that creates a graphing screen using the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/rmannot}{rmannot} package. 
          The user can type in functions and graph them. A graphing screen can be populated with pre-packaged functions 
          for the user to scrutinize and interact with. The package can graph functions of a single variable \emph{x} , 
          a pair of parametric equations that are functions of \emph{t} , and a polar function of \emph{t} .

          The graphing screen is a rich media annotation what uses a specially developed SWF file, called the AcroFLeX 
          Graphing widget. This package takes advantage of rich media annotations, which is a version 9 feature 
          of Acrobat. This package requires Acrobat Pro and Distiller version 9. The user needs to use Adobe Reader 
          9.0 in order to obtain the graphing functionality.

          This package has become obsolete as of December 2020. Since December 2020, Adobe no longer supports Flash 
          player (SWF, FLV). This package uses a custom SWF file ( \texttt{acroflex.swf} ); as a result 
          this package will no longer function in Adobe Acrobat Reader DC. The package will continue to produce 
          PDFs as designed, but only if built using Acrobat XI (or a version Acrobat prior to December 2020) and 
          viewed in Adobe Acrobat Reader XI (or a version of Reader prior to December 2020).

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[name] \texttt{AcroMemory}

\item[author] Story, Donald P.
\index{Author!Story, Donald P.}
\item[copyright] D. P. Story (2006,2020)
\item[license] lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)

\item[version]  (2020-06-23)
\item[last changes] 2020-06-23
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package implements two variations of a memory game:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item a single game board consisting of a number of tiles, each tile has a matching twin, the object is to find all the matching twins; and
          \item two game boards, both identical except one has been randomly rearranged, the object is the find the matching pieces in each of the two game boards.
          \end{itemize}
All LaTeX workflows are now supported: pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and dvips → distiller.

\item[author] Goulet, Vincent

\item[author] Beauchemin, David
\index{Author!Beauchemin, David}

\item[last changes] 2019-06-13
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides commands to compose actuarial symbols of life contingencies and financial mathematics 
          characterized by subscripts and superscripts on both sides of a principal symbol. The package also features 
          commands to easily and consistently position precedence numbers above or below statuses in symbols for 
          multiple lives contracts.

          Since the actuarial notation can get quite involved, the package defines a number of shortcut macros 
          to ease entry of the most common elements.

          Appendix A of the package documentation lists the commands to typeset a large selection of symbols of 
          life contingencies.

          This package requires  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/actuarialangle}{actuarialangle} .

\section[\texttt{adjustbox} -- Graphics package-alike macros for “general” boxes]{\texttt{adjustbox} -- Graphics package-alike macros for “general” boxes}\label{pkg:adjustbox}
\index{Package!adjustbox}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/adjustbox}
\item[name] \texttt{adjustbox}
\item[caption] Graphics package-alike macros for “general” boxes
\item[author] Scharrer, Martin
\index{Author!Scharrer, Martin}
\item[copyright] Martin Scharrer (2011-2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.3c (2025-02-26)
\item[last changes] 2025-02-26
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides several macros to adjust boxed content. One purpose is to supplement the standard 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics}{graphics} package, which defines the macros \texttt{{\textbackslash}resizebox} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}scalebox} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}rotatebox} , 
          with the macros \texttt{{\textbackslash}trimbox} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}clipbox} . 
          The main feature is the general \texttt{{\textbackslash}adjustbox} macro which extends 
          the '' \texttt{key=value} '' interface of \texttt{{\textbackslash}includegraphics} from 
          the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics}{graphics} package and applies it to general 
          text content. Additional provided box macros are \texttt{{\textbackslash}lapbox} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}marginbox} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}minsizebox} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}maxsizebox} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}phantombox} .

          All macros use the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/collectbox}{collectbox} package to read 
          the content as a box and not as a macro argument. This allows for all forms of content including special 
          material like verbatim content. A special feature of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/collectbox}{collectbox} is 
          used to provide matching environments with the identical names as the macros.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/adjustbox/adjustbox.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./1706718596-adjustbox.pdf|

          fonts, supposedly stands for ''Almost European''. The main use of the package was to produce PDF files 
          using Adobe Type 1 versions of the CM fonts instead of bitmapped EC fonts.

\item[name] \texttt{AeB Pro}
\item[caption] Items from the AeB Pro Family of Software
\item[author] Story, Donald P.
\index{Author!Story, Donald P.}

\item[license] lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.2}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2}
\item[version]  (2021-06-20)
\item[last changes] 2021-06-20
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) The AeB Pro bundle provides further functionality for the user of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/acrotex}{AcroTeX 
          eDucation Bundle} . Except as noted in the documentation, the bundle is aimed at users of Acrobat 
          Pro 7.0 or later and deals with using distiller to create PDF.

          AeB Pro itself implements a number of features:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item AeB Central (this can be used by non-distiller users);
          \item Complete support for set up the initial view of the document;
          \item Extensive support for document actions: document level JS, set document actions (willSave, didSave, etc.) and open document actions;
          \item Complete support for page actions;
          \item Complete support for full screen mode, and all the
          \item current transition effects through version 8;
          \item Methods to easily attach documents;
          \item document assembly methods, methods used immediately following distillation;
          \item Methods for linking to attachments and launching attachments;
          \item Support for creating PDF Packages;
          \item Initializing fields using unicode; and
          \item Basic support for layers, rollovers and animations.
          \end{itemize}
The bundle also contains '' \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/robot-man}{Robot Man} '', a less 
          than totally serious demo application.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{AeB Pro README}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/aeb_pro/aeb_pro/README.md}

\section[\texttt{aecc} -- Almost European Concrete Roman virtual fonts]{\texttt{aecc} -- Almost European Concrete Roman virtual fonts}\label{pkg:aecc}
\index{Package!aecc}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/aecc}
\item[name] \texttt{aecc}
\item[caption] Almost European Concrete Roman virtual fonts
\item[author] Rivera, Luis
\index{Author!Rivera, Luis}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides a set of virtual fonts (built from the standard Concrete fonts) providing a set 
          of fonts that almost cover the T1 encoding.

          The main characters missing, of those specified in the T1 specification are eth, thorn, and the Sami 
          letter eng. Sometimes the £ (pound sterling) character is also missing. For the typewriter fonts, the 
          situation is  \emph{worse} .

          According to the author, the purpose of this package is nowadays better served by a combination of the 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mltex}{MLTeX} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ccfonts}{ccfonts} packages.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/fonts/aecc/README}

\section[\texttt{afterpage} -- Execute command after the next page break]{\texttt{afterpage} -- Execute command after the next page break}\label{pkg:afterpage}
\index{Package!afterpage}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/afterpage}
\item[name] \texttt{afterpage}
\item[caption] Execute command after the next page break
\item[author] Carlisle, David
\index{Author!Carlisle, David}
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[copyright] The LaTeX3 Project et al. (1993-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.08 (2023-07-04)
\item[last changes] 2023-07-04
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) Implements a command that causes the commands specified in its argument to be expanded after the current 
          page is output. For example, LaTeX's float positioning mechanism sometimes gets overloaded and all floating 
          figures and table drift to the end of the document. One may flush out all the unprocessed floats by issuing 
          a  \texttt{{\textbackslash}clearpage} command, but this has the effect of making the 
          current page end prematurely. Now you can issue \texttt{{\textbackslash}afterpage{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}clearpage{\textbraceright}} and 
          the current page will be filled up with text as usual, but then the \texttt{{\textbackslash}clearpage} command 
          will flush out all the floats before the next text page begins.

          This package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools}{latex-tools} bundle 
          in the LaTeX \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/required}{required} distribution.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/afterpage.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./2716337552-afterpage.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools}
\item[installation]\url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/macros/latex/required/latex-tools.tds.zip}

\item[name] \texttt{aifont}
\item[caption] Remap Computer Modern fonts
\item[author] Collins, Skip
\index{Author!Collins, Skip}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) Virtual fonts and other related files for remapping the BSR/Y\&Y/AMS Type 1 Computer Modern fonts; 
          the remapping creates fonts which have no characters in the numeric range 0–31 (mod 128), and the virtual 
          fonts map Knuth’s original encodings to the remapped fonts.

          These mechanisms aid the production of robust PDF output from TeX-related systems, when they use CM fonts.

          The original impetus for developing this bundle came from problems with Adobe Illustrator (hence the 
          first two letters of the bundle name). Current versions of Adobe Illustrator can apparently use the CM 
          fonts without remapping, so the bundle is not needed for such use.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/fonts/cm/ai/README.aifont}

          and HDDL used in hierarchical planning. The package is useful for researchers and students to create

          using an input syntax very similar to the actual Algobox program text.

          It gives better results than Algobox’s own LaTeX export which does not look like the editor rendition, 
          produces standalone documents cumbersome to customize, and has arbitrary and inconsistent differences 
          between the input syntax and the program text.

          This package depends upon the following other LaTeX packages:  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/environ}{environ} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse}{xparse} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor}{xcolor} .

\section[\texttt{almfixed} -- Arabic-Latin Modern Fixed extends TeX-Gyre Latin Modern Mono\ldots]{\texttt{almfixed} -- Arabic-Latin Modern Fixed extends TeX-Gyre Latin Modern Mono 10 Regular to full Arabic Unicode support}\label{pkg:almfixed}
\index{Package!almfixed}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/almfixed}
\item[name] \texttt{almfixed}
\item[caption] Arabic-Latin Modern Fixed extends TeX-Gyre Latin Modern Mono 10 Regular to full Arabic Unicode support
\item[author] Hamid, Idris Samawi
\index{Author!Hamid, Idris Samawi}
\item[license] gfl = The GUST Font License (GFL) (free)
\index{License!gfl}
\index{License!The GUST Font License (GFL)}
\item[version] 0.92
\item[description] (no language specified) Arabic-Latin Modern Fixed is an extension of TeX-Gyre Latin Modern Mono 10 Regular. Every glyph and OpenType 
          feature of the Latin Modern Mono has been retained, with minor improvements. On the other hand, we have 
          changed the vertical metrics of the font. Although the Arabic script is designed to use the same x-size 
          as Latin Modern Mono, the former script needs greater ascender and descender space.

          Every Arabic glyph in each Unicode-code block is supported (up to Unicode 7.0): Arabic, Arabic Supplement, 
          Arabic Extended, Arabic Presentation-Forms A, and Arabic Presentation-Forms B.

          There are two versions of the font: otf and ttf. The ?penType version is for print applications (and 
          usually the default for TeX). The TrueType version is for on-screen applications such as text editors. 
          Hinting in the ttf version is much better for on-screen, at least on Microsoft Windows.

          The unique feature of Arabic-Latin Modern is its treatment of vowels and diacritics. Each vowel and diacritic 
          (ALM Fixed contains a total of 68 such glyphs) may now be edited horizontally within any text editor 
          or processor. The author believes this is the very first OpenType Arabic font ever to have this capability. 
          Editing complex Arabic texts will now be much easier to input and to proofread.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/almfixed/doc/almfixed-dtk.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./8394692933-almfixed-dtk.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/almfixed/README}

\section[\texttt{amscdx} -- Enhanced commutative diagrams]{\texttt{amscdx} -- Enhanced commutative diagrams}\label{pkg:amscdx}
\index{Package!amscdx}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/amscdx}
\item[name] \texttt{amscdx}
\item[caption] Enhanced commutative diagrams
\item[author] Vermeer, Martin
\index{Author!Vermeer, Martin}
\item[copyright] Martin Vermeer (2019)
\item[copyright] American Mathematical Society (1995, 1999)
\item[copyright] LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society (2016-2017)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 2.2x (2019-07-02)
\item[last changes] 2019-07-02
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) The original  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amscd}{amscd} package provides a CD environment 
          that emulates the commutative diagram capabilities of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amstex}{AMS-TeX} version 
          2.x. This means that only simple rectangular diagrams are supported, with no diagonal arrows or more 
          exotic features.

          This enhancement package implements double (''fat''), dashed, and bidirectional arrows (left-right and 
          up-down), and color attributes for arrows and their annotations. The restriction to rectangular geometry 
          remains. This nevertheless allows the drawing of a much broader class of ''commutative-diagram-like'' 
          diagrams.

          This update, 2.2x of 2019-07-02, fixes the dashed-arrows parts placement bug, and adds the package option 
          'lyx', for use with lyx to prevent conflict with the already loaded amscd. The packages xcolor and graphicx 
          are made required.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/amscdx/amscdx.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./9229182283-amscdx.pdf|

          of publications based on one of the AMS document classes  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsart}{amsart} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsbook}{amsbook} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsproc}{amsproc} and

          source files. The Handbooks comprise the user documentation for the pertinent document classes.

          between the various components.

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts}
\item[name] \texttt{amsfonts}
\item[caption] TeX fonts from the American Mathematical Society
\item[author] The American Mathematical Society
\index{Author!The American Mathematical Society}
\item[license] ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
\index{License!ofl}
\index{License!The SIL Open Font License}
\item[version] 3.04
\item[description] (no language specified) An extended set of fonts for use in mathematics, including: extra mathematical symbols; blackboard bold 
          letters (uppercase only); fraktur letters; subscript sizes of bold math italic and bold Greek letters; 
          subscript sizes of large symbols such as sum and product; added sizes of the Computer Modern small caps 
          font; cyrillic fonts (from the University of Washington); Euler mathematical fonts. All fonts are provided 
          as Adobe Type 1 files, and all except the Euler fonts are provided as Metafont source.

          The distribution also includes the canonical Type 1 versions of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cm}{Computer 
          Modern family of fonts} .

          Basic LaTeX support for the symbol fonts is provided by  \texttt{amsfonts.sty} , with names 
          of individual symbols defined in \texttt{amssymb.sty} . The Euler fonts are supported by 
          separate packages; details can be found in the documentation.

\section[\texttt{amsmath} -- AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX]{\texttt{amsmath} -- AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX}\label{pkg:amsmath}
\index{Package!amsmath}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}
\item[name] \texttt{amsmath}
\item[caption] AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[copyright] LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society (2016-2023)
\item[copyright] American Mathematical Society (1995, 2000, 2013)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}

\item[version] 2.17t (2024-11-05)
\item[last changes] 2024-11-05
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The principal package in the AMS-LaTeX distribution. It adapts for use in LaTeX most of the mathematical 
          features found in AMS-TeX; it is highly recommended as an adjunct to serious mathematical typesetting 
          in LaTeX.

          When amsmath is loaded, AMS-LaTeX packages  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsbsy}{amsbsy} (for 
          bold symbols), \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsopn}{amsopn} (for operator names) and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amstext}{amstext} (for 
          text embedded in mathematics) are also loaded.

          amsmath is part of the LaTeX required distribution; however, several contributed packages add still further 
          to its appeal; examples are  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/empheq}{empheq} , which provides 
          functions for decorating and highlighting mathematics, and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ntheorem}{ntheorem} , 
          for specifying theorem (and similar) definitions.

\item[version] 2.01 (2021-08-26)
\item[last changes] 2021-08-26
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) AMS-TeX is a TeX macro package, originally written by Michael Spivak for the American Mathematical Society 
          (AMS) during 1983–1985 and is described in the book  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/joy-of-tex}{‘The 
          Joy of TeX’} . It is based on Plain TeX, and provides many features for producing more professional-looking 
          maths formulas with less burden on authors.

          This is the final archival distribution of AMS-TeX. AMS-TeX is no longer supported by the AMS, nor is 
          it used by the AMS publishing program. The AMS does not recommend creating any new documents using AMS-TeX; 
          this distribution will be left on CTAN to facilitate processing of legacy documents and as a historical 
          record of a pioneering TeX macro collection that played a key role in popularizing TeX and revolutionizing 
          mathematics publishing.

          In addition to the  \href{http://mirrors.ctan.org/macros/amstex/doc/amsguide.pdf}{''User’s 
          Guide to AMS-TeX''} , the AMS has also made the full text of the most recent reprint of the second 
          edition of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/joy-of-tex}{''The Joy of TeX''} by Michael Spivak 
          available as a pdf file.

          AMS-TeX is the historical basis of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amslatex}{amslatex} , 
          which should now be used to prepare submissions for the AMS.

\section[\texttt{anima} -- Create slideshows with simple animations]{\texttt{anima} -- Create slideshows with simple animations}\label{pkg:anima}
\index{Package!anima}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/anima}
\item[name] \texttt{anima}
\item[caption] Create slideshows with simple animations
\item[author] Gomes de Santana, Adriano
\index{Author!Gomes de Santana, Adriano}
\item[copyright] Adriano Gomes de Santana (2009-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.1 (2024-12-14)
\item[last changes] 2024-12-14
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The idea for this package arose from noticing that including the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}pause} command 
          from the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}{beamer} class within the \texttt{{\textbackslash}foreach} loop 
          command from the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} package creates a sequence of 
          frames, where each slide presents a step in the construction of the image. The purpose of the \texttt{anima} class 
          is to provide macros that simplify the use of this effect for creating animated slide presentations.

          Although the functionality of this class can be compared to the transition effects of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}{beamer} class, 
          it is not a dependency of the \texttt{anima} class. However, the class makes extensive use 
          of the image creation language provided by the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} package.

          Lastly, it is worth noting a comparison between this class and the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/animate}{animate} package. 
          The \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/animate}{animate} package can create embedded animations 
          within the document, while the \texttt{anima} class produces an animation where each frame 
          corresponds to a page of the document. This distinction highlights the different design goals of the \texttt{anima} class.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/anima/README.txt}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/anima/anima-doc.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./8786389361-anima-doc.pdf|

\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/anonymous-acm}
\item[name] \texttt{anonymous-acm}
\item[caption] Typeset anonymous versions for ACM articles
\item[author] Becker, Brett A.
\index{Author!Becker, Brett A.}
\item[copyright] Brett A. Becker (2020)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.0 (2020-05-09)
\item[last changes] 2020-05-09
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) Academics often need to submit anonymous versions of their papers for peer-review. This often requires 
          anonymization which at some future date needs to be reversed. However de-anonymizing an anonymized paper 
          can be laborious and error-prone.

          This LaTeX package allows anonymization options to be specified at the time of writing for authors using 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/acmart}{acmart.cls} , the official Association of Computing 
          Machinery (ACM) master article template. Anonymization or deanonymization is carried out by simply changing 
          one option and recompiling.

\item[author] Nowacki, Janusz Marian
\index{Author!Nowacki, Janusz Marian}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}

\item[description] (no language specified) \emph{This package is obsolete, its replacement is the new}  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/poltawski}{poltawski}  \emph{package} .

          A replica of Antykwa Półtawskiego font in PostScript Type 1 format — preliminary version. This font was 
          designed in the 'twenties and the 'thirties of XX century by a Polish graphic artist and a typographer 
          Adam Półtawski. It was widely used by Polish printing houses as long as metal types were in use (until 
          ca. the 'sixties). Antykwa Półtawskiego was perhaps the first complete font family programmed and parametrized 
          in MetaPost.

\section[\texttt{anyfontsize} -- Select any font size in LaTeX]{\texttt{anyfontsize} -- Select any font size in LaTeX}\label{pkg:anyfontsize}
\index{Package!anyfontsize}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/anyfontsize}
\item[name] \texttt{anyfontsize}
\item[caption] Select any font size in LaTeX
\item[author] Szabó, Péter
\index{Author!Szabó, Péter}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version]  (2007-11-22)
\item[last changes] 2007-11-22
\item[year] 2007
\index{Year!2007}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package allows the to user select any font size (via e.g.  \texttt{{\textbackslash}fontsize{\textbraceleft}...{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}...{\textbraceright}{\textbackslash}selectfont} ), 
          even those sizes that are not listed in the .fd file. If such a size is requested, LaTeX will search 
          for and select the nearest listed size; anyfontsize will then scale the font to the size actually requested.

          Similar functionality is available for the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/type1cm}{CM family} , 
          for the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/type1ec}{EC family} , or for \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fix-cm}{either 
          computer modern encoding} ; the present package generalises the facility.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/anyfontsize/anyfontsize.pdf}

\item[caption] Arbitrary precision numbers implemented by TeX macros
\item[author] Olšák, Petr
\index{Author!Olšák, Petr}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[version] 1.7
\item[description] (no language specified) The basic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, power to an integer) are implemented 
          by TeX macros in this package. Operands may be numbers with arbitrary numbers of digits; scientific notation 
          is allowed.

          The expression scanner is also provided.

          As of version 1.4 (December 2015) the calculation of common functions (sqrt, exp, ln, sin, cos, tan, 
          asin, acos, atan, pi) with arbitrary precision in the result has been added.

          Exhaustive documentation (including detailed TeXnical documentation) is included. The macro includes 
          many optimizations and uses only TeX primitives (from classic TeX) and  \texttt{{\textbackslash}newcount} macro.

\item[version] 1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) This package fixes the frame numbering in  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}{beamer} when 
          using an appendix such that the slides from the appendix are not counted in the total frame number of 
          the main part of the document. The total frame number counter is reset to 0 when entering the appendix.

          The standard usage is to include  \texttt{{\textbackslash}usepackage{\textbraceleft}appendixnumberbeamer{\textbraceright}} in 
          the preamble and then declare the beginning of the appendix as usual using the \texttt{{\textbackslash}appendix} command.

\section[\texttt{apxproof} -- Proofs in appendix]{\texttt{apxproof} -- Proofs in appendix}\label{pkg:apxproof}
\index{Package!apxproof}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/apxproof}
\item[name] \texttt{apxproof}
\item[caption] Proofs in appendix
\item[author] Senellart, Pierre
\index{Author!Senellart, Pierre}
\item[copyright] Pierre Senellart (2016-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.3.0 (2026-04-14)
\item[last changes] 2026-04-14
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package makes it easier to write articles where proofs and other material are deferred to the appendix.

          The appendix material is written in the LaTeX code along with the main text which it naturally complements, 
          and it is automatically deferred.

          The package can automatically send proofs to the appendix, can repeat in the appendix the theorem environments 
          stated in the main text, can section the appendix automatically based on the sectioning of the main text, 
          and supports a separate bibliography for the appendix material.

          It depends on the following other packages:  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsthm}{amsthm} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibunits}{bibunits} (if 
          the bibliography option is set to \texttt{separate} ), \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/environ}{environ} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox}{etoolbox} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyvrb}{fancyvrb} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ifthen}{ifthen} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/kvoptions}{kvoptions} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/apxproof/README.md}

\section[\texttt{arabi} -- (La)TeX support for Arabic and Farsi, compliant with Babel]{\texttt{arabi} -- (La)TeX support for Arabic and Farsi, compliant with Babel}\label{pkg:arabi}
\index{Package!arabi}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/arabi}
\item[name] \texttt{arabi}
\item[caption] (La)TeX support for Arabic and Farsi, compliant with Babel
\item[author] Jabri, Youssef
\index{Author!Jabri, Youssef}
\item[copyright] Youssef Jabri (2006)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides an Arabic and Farsi script support for TeX without the need of any external pre-processor, 
          and in a way that is compatible with  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} . The 
          bi-directional capability supposes that the user has a TeX engine that knows the four primitives \texttt{{\textbackslash}beginR} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}endR} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}beginL} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}endL} . 
          That is the case in both the TeX--XeT and e-TeX engines. Arabi will accept input in several 8-bit encodings, 
          including UTF-8.

          Arabi can make use of a wide variety of Arabic and Farsi fonts, and provides one of its own. PDF files 
          generated using Arabi may be searched, and text may be copied from them and pasted elsewhere.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/arabic/arabi/README}

\index{Package!arabluatex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/arabluatex}
\item[name] \texttt{arabluatex}
\item[caption] ArabTeX for LuaLaTeX
\item[author] Alessi, Robert
\index{Author!Alessi, Robert}
\item[copyright] Robert Alessi (2016-2020)
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[license] cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
\index{License!cc-by-sa-4}
\index{License!CC BY-SA 4.0}
\item[version] 1.20 (2020-03-23)
\item[last changes] 2020-03-23
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides for LuaLaTeX an  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/arabtex}{ArabTeX} -like 
          interface to generate Arabic writing from an ascii transliteration. It is particularly well-suited for 
          complex documents such as technical documents or critical editions where a lot of left-to-right commands 
          intertwine with Arabic writing. \texttt{arabluatex} is able to process any ArabTeX input 
          notation. Its output can be set in the same modes of vocalization as ArabTeX, or in different roman transliterations. 
          It further allows many typographical refinements. It will eventually interact with some other packages 
          yet to come to produce from \texttt{.tex} source files, in addition to printed books, TEI 
          xml compliant critical editions and/or lexicons that can be searched, analyzed and correlated in various 
          ways.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Example of use}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/arabluatex/samples/al-Jahiz.pdf}

          may be in ASCII transliteration or other encodings (including UTF-8); output may be Arabic, Hebrew, or 
          any of several languages that use the Arabic script.

\item[name] \texttt{arabxetex}
\item[caption] An ArabTeX-like interface for XeLaTeX
\item[author] bidi-tex GitHub Organisation
\index{Author!bidi-tex GitHub Organisation}
\item[author] Charette, François
\index{Author!Charette, François}
\item[author] Khalighi, Vafa
\index{Author!Khalighi, Vafa}

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}

\item[version] 1.2.1
\item[description] (no language specified) ArabXeTeX provides a convenient  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/arabtex}{ArabTeX} -like user-interface 
          for typesetting languages using the Arabic script in XeLaTeX, with flexible access to font features. 
          Input in ArabTeX notation can be set in three different vocalization modes or in roman transliteration. 
          Direct UTF-8 input is also supported. The parsing and converting of ArabTeX input to Unicode is done 
          by means of TECkit mappings. Version 1.0 provides support for Arabic, Maghribi Arabic, Farsi (Persian), 
          Urdu, Sindhi, Kashmiri, Ottoman Turkish, Kurdish, Jawi (Malay) and Uighur. The documentation covers topics 
          such as typesetting the Holy Quran and typesetting bidirectional critical editions with the package ednotes.

\section[\texttt{arev} -- Fonts and LaTeX support files for Arev Sans]{\texttt{arev} -- Fonts and LaTeX support files for Arev Sans}\label{pkg:arev}
\index{Package!arev}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[name] \texttt{arev}
\item[caption] Fonts and LaTeX support files for Arev Sans
\item[author] Hartke, Stephen
\index{Author!Hartke, Stephen}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package arev provides type 1 and virtual fonts, together with LaTeX packages for using  \href{http://tavmjong.free.fr/FONTS/}{Arev 
          Sans} in both text and mathematics. Arev Sans is a derivative of Bitstream Vera Sans created by 
          Tavmjong Bah, adding support for Greek and Cyrillic characters. Bah also added a few variant letters 
          that are more appropriate for mathematics. The primary purpose for using Arev Sans in LaTeX is presentations, 
          particularly when using a computer projector. In such a context, Arev Sans is quite readable, with large 
          x-height, "open letters", wide spacing, and thick stems. The style is very similar to the SliTeX font 
          lcmss, but heavier.

          Arev is one of a very small number of sans-font mathematics support packages. Others are  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cmbright}{cmbright} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hvmath}{hvmath} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/kerkis}{kerkis} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/arev/arevdoc.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) ArmTeX is a system for typesetting Armenian text with Plain TeX or LaTeX(2e). It may be used with input:

          
          \begin{itemize}
          \item from a standard Latin keyboard without any special encoding and/or support for Armenian letters,
          \item from any keyboard which uses an encoding that has Armenian letters in the second half (characters 128-255) of the extended ASCII table (for example ArmSCII8 Armenian standard),
          \item from an Armenian keyboard using UTF-8 encoding.
          \end{itemize}
Users should note that the manuals still mostly describe the previous version of the package (ArmTeX 
          2.0). However, a description of the new features of ArmTeX 3.0 is provided at the end of the README file.

\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides array data structures in (La)TeX, in the meaning of the classical procedural programming 
          languages like Fortran, Ada or C, and macros to manipulate them. Arrays can be mono or bi-dimensional. 
          This is useful for applications which require high level programming techniques, like algorithmic graphics 
          programmed in the TeX language.

          The package is now superseded by the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/arrayjobx}{arrayjobx} package, 
          which has the same specification but is less error-prone.

\section[\texttt{arsenal} -- Open Type font by Andrij Shevchenko]{\texttt{arsenal} -- Open Type font by Andrij Shevchenko}\label{pkg:arsenal}
\index{Package!arsenal}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/arsenal}

\item[author] Veytsman, Boris
\index{Author!Veytsman, Boris}
\item[license] ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
\index{License!ofl}

\item[version] 1.1 (2025-12-13)
\item[last changes] 2025-12-13
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) In 2011 Andrij’s typeface became a winner of the Ukrainian Type Design Competition ''Mystetsky Arsenal'' 
          in which three main criteria were sought for: being zeitgeist, practical, and Ukrainian. Andrij’s winning 
          entry was crowned Arsenal and made publicly available.

          Arsenal is a semi-grotesque with traditional forms. It is primarily designed for body text and intended 
          for various professional communication. Its special qualities of letter shapes and subtle contrast modulation 
          articulate grace and expressivity. Arsenal’s somewhat lyrical sentiment abides to the Ukrainian nature 
          of the font.

          This package provides the fonts and LaTeX support for them with matching math. It needs LuaLaTeX or XeLaTeX.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/arsenal/README}

\item[license] noinfo = noinfo 
\index{License!noinfo}
\index{License!noinfo}
\item[version] 1.00b
\item[description] (no language specified) ArTeX is a Perl script which simplifies the exchange of LaTeX documents between collaborating authors 
          or between author and publisher.

          ArTeX analyzes a LaTeX 2e document to determine whether it loads any non-standard files. If non-standard 
          files are identified, ArTeX creates filecontents or filecontents* environments for them and adds these 
          environments to the input document. The new document can be processed successfully on any system with 
          a standard installation of LaTeX 2e.

\item[description] (no language specified) This package facilitates the creation of PDF article threads, a concept/feature of Adobe Reader/Acrobat 
          that has been around since the product’s beginning. The use of article threads typically only makes sense 
          in a document in which the text is in a multi-column format.

          Set the article threads after the composition of the document is completed. The method of setting the 
          threads is very visual, not automatic as in the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/threadcol}{threadcol} package 
          of Scott Pakin (available for \texttt{pdftex} only).

          This package supports all drivers:  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvips}{dvips} , \texttt{pdflatex} , \texttt{lualatex} , \texttt{xelatex} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipdfm}{dvipdfm} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipdfmx}{dvipdfmx} .

\section[\texttt{asmeconf} -- A LaTeX template for ASME conference papers]{\texttt{asmeconf} -- A LaTeX template for ASME conference papers}\label{pkg:asmeconf}
\index{Package!asmeconf}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/asmeconf}
\item[name] \texttt{asmeconf}
\item[caption] A LaTeX template for ASME conference papers
\item[author] Lienhard, John H.
\index{Author!Lienhard, John H.}
\item[copyright] John Lienhard (2021-2026)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version] 1.46 (2026-01-10)
\item[last changes] 2026-01-10
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) The asmeconf class provides a LaTeX template for ASME conference papers, following ASME’s guidelines 
          for margins, fonts, headings, captions, and reference formats as of 2025.

          This LaTeX template is intended to be used with the asmeconf.bst BibTeX style, for reference formatting, 
          which is part of this distribution. Unlike older ASME conference LaTeX templates, asmeconf pdfs will 
          contain hyperlinks, bookmarks, and metadata; and the references can include the DOI and URL fields. This 
          LaTeX template enables inline author names, following ASME’s current style, but it can also produce the 
          traditional grid style. Options include line numbering, final column balancing, various math options, 
          government copyright, archivability and accessibility (PDF/A), and multilingual support. The code is 
          compatible with pdfLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

          This LaTeX template is not a publication of ASME, but it does conform to ASME’s currently published guidelines 
          for conference papers.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/asmeconf/README.md}

\item[description] (no language specified) GNU Aspell is a Free and Open Source spell checker designed to replace  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ispell}{Ispell} . 
          It can either be used as a library or as an independent spell checker. Its main feature is that it does 
          a superior job of suggesting possible replacements for a misspelled word than just about any other spell 
          checker out there for the English language. Aspell can check documents in UTF-8 without having to use 
          a special dictionary; and will do its best to respect the current locale setting.

          A wide range of language-specific dictionaries is available.

\item[description] (no language specified) The Aspen package implements LaTeX commands closely related to what is often called  \emph{security 
          protocol notation} , \emph{standard protocol engineering notation} , \emph{standard 
          protocol notation} , or \emph{protocol narrations} .

          Optionally, the Aspen package also implements LaTeX commands for Burrows–Abadi–Needham logic (BAN logic).

          The name Aspen can be an abbreviation for  \emph{A Security Protocol Engineering Notation} , 
          but another possible abbreviation is \emph{Anderson-inspired Standard Protocol Engineering Notation} , 
          in memory of the late Professor Ross J. Anderson who has meant so much for the fields of computer security, 
          distributed systems, and, in particular, security engineering.

\item[caption] LaTeX support for creating association matrices
\item[author] Whisperity
\index{Author!Whisperity}

\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}

\item[last changes] 2022-10-29
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package allows the creation of association matrices in an clear and concise fashion, without having 
          to deal with manually generating and modifying the tables while working. All you have to do is define 
          the rows and the columns by their unique identifier, and then specify which cells should be marked as 
          associated. Then, the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}amxgenerate} command generates a table 
          that shows in the cells with a blip (•) where the association was added.

          The package depends on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox}{etoolbox} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/forloop}{forloop} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ifthen}{ifthen} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/textcomp}{textcomp} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse}{xparse} .

          from separate files, rather than within the document, as is standard in the \texttt{asymptote} package, 
          which is provided as part of the Asymptote bundle. The \texttt{asymptote} way can prove cumbersome

\index{Package!atenddvi}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/atenddvi}
\item[name] \texttt{atenddvi}
\item[caption] Provides the {\textbackslash}AtEndDvi command
\item[author] Oberdiek, Heiko
\index{Author!Oberdiek, Heiko}
\item[copyright] Oberdiek Package Support Group (2016-2020)
\item[copyright] Heiko Oberdiek (2007)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.5 (2020-11-11)
\item[last changes] 2020-11-11
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package is unneeded and does nothing when used with a LaTeX format 2020-10-01 or newer as in this 
          case the  \emph{format} provides the \texttt{{\textbackslash}AtEndDvi} command.

          For older formats it implements  \texttt{{\textbackslash}AtEndDvi} , a counterpart 
          to \texttt{{\textbackslash}AtBeginDvi} . The execution of its argument is delayed to 
          the end of the document at the end of the last page. Thus \texttt{{\textbackslash}special} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}write} remain 
          effective, because they are put into the last page. This is the main difference to \texttt{{\textbackslash}AtEndDocument} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/atenddvi/README.md}

\item[author] Pakin, Scott
\index{Author!Pakin, Scott}
\item[copyright] Scott Pakin (2010, 2015-2016)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.9
\item[description] (no language specified) Starting with PDF 1.3 (Adobe Acrobat 4.0), PDF files can contain file attachments — arbitrary files that 
          a reader can extract, just like attachments to an e-mail message. The attachfile package brings this 
          functionality to pdfLaTeX and provides some additional features not available in Acrobat, such as the 
          ability to use arbitrary LaTeX code for the file icon — including things like {\textbackslash}includegraphics, 
          tabular, and mathematics. Settings can be made either globally or on a per-attachment basis. Attachfile 
          makes it easy to attach files and customize their appearance in the enclosing document.

          The package supports the Created, Modified, and Size keys in the EmbeddedFile’s Params dictionary.

\item[description] (no language specified) A LaTeX package that defines the command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}attrib} , used to 
          provide attribution for block elements of a text. The argument of \texttt{{\textbackslash}attrib} may 
          be pretty much anything; the command will print the attribution at the right margin of the block. If 
          the block is prose, \texttt{{\textbackslash}attrib} will attempt to fit the attribution 
          at the end of the last line.

\item[description] (no language specified) The auncial and allauncl packages provide Metafont fonts based on the Artificial Uncial manuscript book-hand 
          used between the 6th and 10th century AD. The font consists of minuscules and digits, with some appropriate 
          period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided. Note that the font is available 
          separately in Adobe Type 1 format, as the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/auncial-new}{artificial 
          uncial ‘new’} package.

          This is one of a  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bookhands}{set of manuscript fonts} . Access 
          to the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/docmfp}{docmfp} package is desirable but not essential.

          with some appropriate period punctuation marks. Both normal and bold versions are provided, and the font 
          is distributed in Adobe Type 1 format. This is an experimental new version of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/auncial}{auncial} bundle, 
          which is one of a series of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bookhands}{bookhand fonts} .

          The font follows the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/b1encoding}{B1 encoding} developed for 
          bookhands. Access to the encoding is essential. The encoding mainly follows the standard T1 encoding.

\section[\texttt{autolatex} -- Automate compilation of large scale LaTeX projects]{\texttt{autolatex} -- Automate compilation of large scale LaTeX projects}\label{pkg:autolatex}
\index{Package!autolatex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/autolatex}
\item[name] \texttt{AutoLaTeX}
\item[caption] Automate compilation of large scale LaTeX projects
\item[author] Galland, Stéphane
\index{Author!Galland, Stéphane}
\item[copyright] Stéphane Galland (1998-2022)
\item[license] gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
\index{License!gpl2}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 2}
\item[version] 41.1
\item[description] (no language specified) AutoLaTeX is a set of GNU Make and Perl scripts that may be used to compile LaTeX projects. AutoLaTeX 
          automates the compilation process by calling (pdf)LaTeX and BibTeX as they are required. It supports 
          pdfLaTeX, LaTeX, dvips, epstopdf and BibTeX. AutoLaTeX also provides a powerfull feature for automatic 
          generation of the figures that are included in the LaTeX project: for several figure sources (xfig, dia, 
          umbrello, png, svg, xmi...) AutoLaTeX is able to generate the appropriate PDF picture. AutoLaTeX also 
          supports pstex format (from xfig and gnuplot for example) and dot format (from the Graphviz package).

          The use of AutoLaTeX on the command line is similar to GNU Make. AutoLaTeX should be called with several 
          targets to run.

\section[\texttt{autosp} -- A Preprocessor that generates note-spacing commands for Musi\ldots]{\texttt{autosp} -- A Preprocessor that generates note-spacing commands for MusiXTeX scores}\label{pkg:autosp}
\index{Package!autosp}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/autosp}
\item[name] \texttt{autosp}
\item[caption] A Preprocessor that generates note-spacing commands for MusiXTeX scores
\item[author] Tennent, Bob
\index{Author!Tennent, Bob}
\item[license] gpl2+ = GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl2+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer}
\item[version]  (2023-10-07)
\item[last changes] 2023-10-07
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) This program simplifies the creation of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/musixtex}{MusiXTeX} scores 
          by converting (non-standard) commands of the form \texttt{{\textbackslash}anotes … {\textbackslash}en} into 
          one or more conventional note-spacing commands, as determined by the note values themselves, with \texttt{{\textbackslash}sk} spacing 
          commands inserted as necessary. The coding for an entire measure can be entered one part at a time, without 
          concern for note-spacing changes within the part or spacing requirements of other parts.

          For example,  \texttt{{\textbackslash}anotes{\textbackslash}qa J{\textbackslash}qa 
          K\&{\textbackslash}ca l{\textbackslash}qa m{\textbackslash}ca n{\textbackslash}en} generates \texttt{{\textbackslash}Notes{\textbackslash}qa 
          J{\textbackslash}sk{\textbackslash}qa K{\textbackslash}sk\&{\textbackslash}ca 
          l{\textbackslash}qa m{\textbackslash}sk{\textbackslash}ca n{\textbackslash}en} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/autosp/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/autosp/doc/autosp.pdf}

\item[author] Murru, Nadir

\item[author] Coriasco, Sandro
\index{Author!Coriasco, Sandro}
\item[copyright] Anna Capietto, Sandro Coriasco, Tiziana Armano, Boris Doubrov, Alexander Kozlovskiy, Nadir Murru, Dragan Ahmetovic, Cristian Bernareggi (2018-2020)

\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 3.0
\item[description] (no language specified) PDF documents containing formulas generated by LaTeX are usually not accessible by assistive technologies 
          for visually impaired people and people with special educational needs (i.e., by screen readers and braille 
          displays). The axessibility package manages this issue, allowing to create a PDF document where the formulas 
          are read by these assistive technologies, since it automatically generates hidden comments in the PDF 
          document (by means of the /ActualText attribute and/or suitable tags) in correspondence to each formula.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/axessibility/README}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/axodraw2}
\item[name] \texttt{axodraw2}
\item[caption] Feynman diagrams in a LaTeX document
\item[author] Vermaseren, Jos
\index{Author!Vermaseren, Jos}
\item[author] Collins, John
\index{Author!Collins, John}
\item[copyright] John Collins and Jos Vermaseren (1994-2021)
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[version] 2.1.1c (2021-03-05)
\item[last changes] 2021-03-05
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package defines macros for drawing Feynman graphs in LaTeX documents.

          It is an important update of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/axodraw}{axodraw} package, 
          but since it is not completely backwards compatible, we have given the style file a changed name.

          Many new features have been added, with new types of line, and much more flexibility in their properties.

          In addition, it is now possible to use  \texttt{axodraw2} with pdfLaTeX, as well as with 
          the LaTeX-dvips method. However with pdfLaTeX (and also LuaLaTeX and XeLaTeX), an external program, \texttt{axohelp} , 
          is used to perform the geometrical calculations needed for the pdf code inserted in the output file. 
          The processing involves a run of pdfLaTeX, a run of \texttt{axohelp} , and then another run 
          of pdfLaTeX.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/axodraw2/README}

\section[\texttt{babel} -- Multilingual support for LaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and Plain\ldots]{\texttt{babel} -- Multilingual support for LaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and Plain TeX}\label{pkg:babel}
\index{Package!babel}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}
\item[name] \texttt{babel}
\item[caption] Multilingual support for LaTeX, LuaLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and Plain TeX
\item[author] Bezos López, Javier
\index{Author!Bezos López, Javier}
\item[author] Braams, Johannes L.
\index{Author!Braams, Johannes L.}
\item[copyright] Johannes Braams et al. (1989-2012)
\item[copyright] Javier Bezos and Johannes L. Braams (2012-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 26.6 (2026-04-15)
\item[last changes] 2026-04-15
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) Babel is the multilingual environment for LaTeX (tailored for LuaTeX, pdfTeX and XeTeX), and sometimes 
          Plain. Its aim is to provide a comprehensive localization framework for different languages, scripts 
          and cultures based on the latest advances on international standards (Unicode, W3C, OpenType). It supports 
          about 300 languages (with various levels of coverage) across about 45 scripts, including complex (like 
          CJK, Indic) and RTL ones.

          Besides the traditional  \texttt{.ldf} files, there are many locales built on a modern core 
          that utilizes descriptive \texttt{.ini} files, with tools providing precise control over 
          hyphenation and line breaking, captions, date formats (across various calendars), spacing, transliteration, 
          numbering and other locale-specific typographical rules.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/babel/base/README.md}

\item[name] \texttt{babel-azerbaijani}
\item[caption] Support for Azerbaijani within babel
\item[author] Bezos López, Javier
\index{Author!Bezos López, Javier}
\item[copyright] Namig J. Guliyev et al. (2014-2017)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}

\item[version] 1.0a (2017-05-03)
\item[last changes] 2017-05-03
\item[year] 2017
\index{Year!2017}
\item[description] (no language specified) This is the babel style for Azerbaijani.

          This language poses special challenges because no ''traditional'' font encoding contains the full character 
          set, and therefore a mixture must be used (e.g., T2A and T1).

          This package is compatible with Unicode engines (LuaTeX, XeTeX), which are very likely the most convenient

\index{Package!babel-hebrew}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel-hebrew}
\item[name] \texttt{babel-hebrew}
\item[caption] Babel support for Hebrew
\item[author] Bezos López, Javier
\index{Author!Bezos López, Javier}
\item[author] Braams, Johannes L.
\index{Author!Braams, Johannes L.}
\item[author] Lavva, Boris
\index{Author!Lavva, Boris}
\item[author] Rosendahl, Arthur
\index{Author!Rosendahl, Arthur}
\item[author] Fogiel, Udi
\index{Author!Fogiel, Udi}
\item[copyright] Boris Lavva and Johannes Braams (1997-2005)
\item[copyright] Udi Fogiel (2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 2.5 (2026-02-16)
\item[last changes] 2026-02-16
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the language definition file for support of Hebrew in  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} . 
          Macros to control the use of text direction control of TeX--XeT and e-TeX are provided (and may be used 
          elsewhere).

          Some shortcuts are defined, as well as translations to Hebrew of standard ''LaTeX names''. For questions, 
          bug reports, or support, please open an issue in the repository.

          Note: the package is in maintenance mode. Bugs will be fixed, but no new features will be added.

          The  \texttt{.ldf} file is only compatible with pdfLaTeX or LaTeX. Even then, for documents 
          containing more than a short text in Hebrew, it is strongly recommended to use LuaTeX (with babel's \texttt{.ini} file 
          or polyglossia). For short texts with pdfTeX, use the \texttt{.ini} file. Consult the documentation 
          of babel for better settings for Hebrew.

\section[\texttt{babel-spanglish} -- Simplified Spanish support for Babel]{\texttt{babel-spanglish} -- Simplified Spanish support for Babel}\label{pkg:babel-spanglish}
\index{Package!babel-spanglish}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel-spanglish}
\item[name] \texttt{babel-spanglish}
\item[caption] Simplified Spanish support for Babel
\item[author] Rivera, Luis
\index{Author!Rivera, Luis}
\item[copyright] J. Luis Rivera N. (2008-2015)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.3 (2015-05-20)
\item[last changes] 2015-05-20
\item[year] 2015
\index{Year!2015}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides very simplified (or ultra sloppy) support for Spanish in  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{Babel} , 
          mostly as a fallback in case \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel-spanish}{spanish.ldf} fails 
          for some reason. The package provides basic support for Spanish hyphenation, captions, date, frenchspacing, 
          indentfirst, symbolic footnotes, enumerations, small caps roman numerals, and a handful of shorthands 
          and Spanish mathematical operators. No options or attributes for customization are provided.

          According to the author, the purpose of this package is nowadays better served by the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} package 
          with option \texttt{spanish.mexico} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/macros/latex/contrib/babel-contrib/spanglish/README}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/macros/latex/contrib/babel-contrib/spanglish}
\item[on Mik\TeX] \texttt{spanglish}
