\item[description] (no language specified) The backrefx package is now obsolete after the release of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/backref}{backref} v1.23, 
          because all the functionality of backrefx is now provided by backref. This release of backrefx is only 
          provided for backward compatibility of existing documents.

          The backrefx package enhanced the backref package of David Carlisle and Sebastian Rahtz. It enables backref 
          to print the bibliographic back references in a more typographically sound manner (similar to the back 
          references in TeX Unbound of Hoenig), for example: (Cited on page 10.) (Cited on pages 10 and 12.) (Cited 
          on pages 10, 12 and 15.)

          Editor; (2) Text Editor + DVI Viewer - Clasical IDE. The system supports the use of scalable fonts (OpenType, 
          TrueType, PostScript Type 1 and Type 3). It supports import of EPS, PDF, FIG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, TIFF, HPGL, 
          DXY, PCX, MSP, BMP, and WMF graphical formats. In advance, PostScript enabled graphics engine handles 
          such packages as PSTricks, PSfrag, PowerDot, Prosper, Beamer, etc. The system supports generation of 
          PDF, SVG, PNG, HTML, PS, and printing on any printer supported by a driver under MS-Windows.

\section[\texttt{bakoma-games} -- BaKoMa modules for music and games]{\texttt{bakoma-games} -- BaKoMa modules for music and games}\label{pkg:bakoma-games}
\index{Package!bakoma-games}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bakoma-games}
\item[name] \texttt{bakoma-games}
\item[caption] BaKoMa modules for music and games
\item[author] Malyshev, Basil
\index{Author!Malyshev, Basil}
\item[license] shareware = Shareware: A fee is required (not free)
\index{License!shareware}
\index{License!Shareware: A fee is required}
\item[description] (no language specified) This module includes popular macro packages described in chapters 7 (Preparing music scores: MusiXTeX) 
          and 8 (Playing games: Chess, Xiangqi — Chinese Chess, Go, Backgammon, Bridge, Crosswords) of the ‘LaTeX 
          graphics Companion’. They are precompiled for use, together with fonts and documentation, directly in 
          BaKoMa TeX. Fonts used by some packages are converted into formats suitable both for printing and for 
          PDF generation. For example, for Chess the diagram fonts are converted into vector Type 3 font format. 
          Board black squares are coded as a gray color instead of dashing. This approach gives the best results 
          on printers and displays. Fonts for in-line notation are in Type 1 font format. For Go the special fonts 
          are too hard to convert automatically and have been efficiently coded in Type 3 font format. For Backgammon 
          the fonts were originally dithered as halftone, making them unsuitable for PDF. The halftone was emulated 
          by using a grey colour in Type 3 fonts.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Summary of the bundle}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/systems/win32/bakoma/macros/games.html}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/systems/win32/bakoma/macros/games.bkz}

\section[\texttt{bankstatement} -- A LaTeX class for bank statements based on csv data]{\texttt{bankstatement} -- A LaTeX class for bank statements based on csv data}\label{pkg:bankstatement}
\index{Package!bankstatement}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bankstatement}
\item[name] \texttt{bankstatement}
\item[caption] A LaTeX class for bank statements based on csv data
\item[author] Kleber, Josef
\index{Author!Kleber, Josef}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.9.2 (2015-11-14)
\item[last changes] 2015-11-14
\item[year] 2015
\index{Year!2015}
\item[description] (no language specified) More and more banks allow their customers to download posting records in various formats. By using the 
          \texttt{bankstatement} class, you can create bank statements, as long as a csv format is 
          available. At the moment, the csv-mt940 and csv-camt formats — used by many german Sparkassen — are supported. 
          You can quite easily add support for other csv formats. Simply define the order of the keys in the csv 
          data file and how to use them.

          The terminology in this class — such as BIC (Business Identifier Code) or IBAN (International Bank Account 
          Number) — is based on usage in the SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area).

          The user may adjust the terminology to suit local needs.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package example}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/bankstatement/bankstatement-example.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package uses Acrobat forms and Acrobat JavaScript API to create and manipulate interactive bar graphs. 
          This means the user can enter data in a couple of formats, to populate the bar graphs. The package can 
          also be used to create and display discrete probability distributions, for both the probability mass 
          function (pmf) and the cumulative distribution function (cdf) of a distribution.

          Any bar graph created by this package requires Adobe Reader DC (or Acrobat) for full functionality.

          PDF Creators: Any of the usual PDF creators can be used; however, to repeat, an Adobe PDF reader is required 
          for full functionality.

\item[version] 0.93
\item[description] (no language specified) The package makes it possible to execute Unix bash shell scripts from within LaTeX. The main application 
          is in writing computer-science texts, in which you want to make sure the programs listed in the document 
          are executed directly from the input. The package may use other Unix shells than bash, but does not work 
          without modification in a Windows environment.

          The package requires the  \texttt{-shell-escape} flag when LaTeX is processing your document.

\section[\texttt{beamer} -- A LaTeX class for producing presentations and slides]{\texttt{beamer} -- A LaTeX class for producing presentations and slides}\label{pkg:beamer}
\index{Package!beamer}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}
\item[name] \texttt{beamer}
\item[caption] A LaTeX class for producing presentations and slides
\item[author] Miletić, Vedran
\index{Author!Miletić, Vedran}
\item[author] Tantau, Till
\index{Author!Tantau, Till}
\item[author] Wright, Joseph

\item[copyright] Till Tantau (2003-2007)
\item[copyright] Joseph Wright, samcarter (2019-2026)
\item[copyright] Vedran Miletić, Joseph Wright (2011-2015)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[license] gpl2+ = GNU General Public License, version 2 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl2+}

\item[version] 3.77 (2026-01-22)
\item[last changes] 2026-01-22
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) The beamer LaTeX class can be used for producing slides. The class works in both PostScript and direct 
          PDF output modes, using the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{pgf} graphics system for 
          visual effects.

          Content is created in the frame environment, and each frame can be made up of a number of slides using 
          a simple notation for specifying material to appear on each slide within a frame. Short versions of title, 
          authors, institute can also be specified as optional parameters. Whole frame graphics are supported by 
          plain frames. The class supports figure and table environments, transparency effects, varying slide transitions 
          and animations. Beamer also provides compatibility with other packages like  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/prosper}{prosper} .

          The package now incorporates the functionality of the former  \texttt{translator} package, 
          which is used for customising the package for use in other language environments.

          Beamer depends on the following other packages:  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/atbegshi}{atbegshi} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox}{etoolbox} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ifpdf}{ifpdf} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{pgf} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/translator}{translator} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/beamer/doc/beameruserguide.pdf}

\item[name] \texttt{beamer-reveal}
\item[caption] Convert beamer slides to reveal.js HTML presentations
\item[author] Daems, Walter
\index{Author!Daems, Walter}
\item[copyright] Walter Daems (2025-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}

\item[version] 1.10 (2026-04-08)
\item[last changes] 2026-04-08
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}{Beamer} is a very powerful and convenient document 
          class to create presentations and slides. However, integrating multimedia in it, is still a bit of a 
          faff. The (limited) functionality heavily relies on the availability of acroread. This package allows 
          you to convert your beamer presentation to the reveal.js framework, rendering your presentation as an 
          HTML website in your browser. This allows for easy incorporation of videos, audio fragments, iframe chunks, 
          images and LaTeX animations.

\item[last changes] 2016-03-15
\item[year] 2016
\index{Year!2016}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a flexible dark or light colour theme designed for maximum readability in environments 
          where most themes fall flat.

          Main features:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Dark color theme for presenting in low-light conditions.
          \item Optional light color theme for presenting in bright ambient light.
          \item Redefines color names ''red'', ''green'', ''blue'', ''yellow'' to values that are visible when displayed by certain projectors, particularly those with a very bright green channel and dim red and blue channels. This behaviour can be optionally disabled, with the provided colours also available as ''OwlRed'', ''OwlGreen'', etc.
          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{beamerposter} -- Extend beamer and a0poster for custom sized posters]{\texttt{beamerposter} -- Extend beamer and a0poster for custom sized posters}\label{pkg:beamerposter}
\index{Package!beamerposter}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamerposter}
\item[name] \texttt{beamerposter}
\item[caption] Extend beamer and a0poster for custom sized posters
\item[author] Deselaers, Thomas
\index{Author!Deselaers, Thomas}
\item[author] Dreuw, Philippe
\index{Author!Dreuw, Philippe}
\item[copyright] Philippe Dreuw and Thomas Deselaers (2015,2018)
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.13
\item[description] (no language specified) The package enables the user to use  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}{beamer} style 
          operations on a canvas of the sizes provided by \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/a0poster}{a0poster} ; 
          font scaling is available (using packages such as \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/type1cm}{type1cm} if 
          necessary).

          In addition, the package allows the user to benefit from the nice colour box handling and alignment provided 
          by the beamer class (for example, with rounded corners and shadows). Good looking posters may be created 
          very rapidly.

          Features include:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item scalable fonts using the fp and type1cm packages;
          \item posters in A-series sizes, and custom sizes like double A0 are possible;
          \item still applicable to custom beamer slides, e.g. 16:9 slides for a wide-screen (i.e. 1.78 aspect ratio);
          \item orientation may be portrait or landscape; a ‘debug mode’ is provided.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/beamerposter/README}

\section[\texttt{beamertheme-durham} -- A content-first Beamer theme for teaching, research, and lon\ldots]{\texttt{beamertheme-durham} -- A content-first Beamer theme for teaching, research, and long-form academic presentations}\label{pkg:beamertheme-durham}
\index{Package!beamertheme-durham}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamertheme-durham}
\item[name] \texttt{beamertheme-durham}
\item[caption] A content-first Beamer theme for teaching, research, and long-form academic presentations
\item[author] Rizwan, Suhail
\index{Author!Rizwan, Suhail}
\item[copyright] Suhail Rizwan (2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.1.0 (2026-02-23)
\item[last changes] 2026-02-23
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides the Durham Beamer Theme, a content-first presentation theme for LaTeX  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}{Beamer} designed 
          for teaching, research, and long-form academic presentations.

          The theme emphasizes structural clarity, pacing awareness, and layout stability under dense textual and 
          mathematical content. It is implemented entirely from first principles and not derived from any existing 
          Beamer theme.

          Conceptual inspiration from established themes such as  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamertheme-metropolis}{Metropolis} is 
          acknowledged; no external code is reused. The color palette is inspired by the visual identity of Durham 
          University. This package is an independent academic contribution and not an official or endorsed Durham 
          University template.

          The package includes a modular theme implementation, a demo document with compiled PDF, and a user manual.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/beamer-contrib/themes/beamertheme-durham/durham-manual.pdf}

\section[\texttt{beamertheme-trigon} -- A modern, elegant, and versatile theme for Beamer]{\texttt{beamertheme-trigon} -- A modern, elegant, and versatile theme for Beamer}\label{pkg:beamertheme-trigon}
\index{Package!beamertheme-trigon}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamertheme-trigon}
\item[name] \texttt{beamertheme-trigon}
\item[caption] A modern, elegant, and versatile theme for Beamer
\item[author] Lambert, Thomas
\index{Author!Lambert, Thomas}
\item[copyright] Thomas Lambert (2021-2023)
\item[license] cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
\index{License!cc-by-sa-4}
\index{License!CC BY-SA 4.0}
\item[version] 0.7.0 (2023-02-20)
\item[last changes] 2023-02-20
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a modern, elegant and versatile theme for  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}{Beamer} , 
          with a high degree of customization.

          Trigon found its origin and inspiration in the graphical guidelines resulting from the visual identity 
          overhaul of the University of Liège. Although directly inspired from these guidelines, the theme was 
          stripped out of any mention or specificities related to the University and its faculties. This makes 
          the Trigon theme perfectly suitable for many different contexts.

          The final product provides a modern, elegant and versatile theme with a high degree of customization. 
          The main design focuses on triangular shapes for major layout elements and noise minimization for the 
          main body of the work.

          The theme’s implementation is heavily inspired from the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamertheme-metropolis}{Metropolis 
          theme} . Most options from \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamertheme-metropolis}{Metropolis} have 
          been ported to Trigon in order to improve customization and ease-of-use. Trigon also includes different 
          styles and layouts for the main title page, the section page and the default slide background.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/beamer-contrib/themes/beamertheme-trigon/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Example of use}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/beamer-contrib/themes/beamertheme-trigon/demo/trigon_demo.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) A modern and elegant Beamer theme designed for academic and professional presentations. It offers customizable 
          footer styles (quarter-circle, full bar, classic), decorative elements that can be enabled/disabled, 
          and enhanced typography options for headers. The theme includes special layouts for code listings, section 
          pages, and standout frames. Color scheme can be customized through theme options, with support for both 
          main and accent colors. The typography system supports both serif and sans-serif variants, and provides 
          flexible font styling across different elements. Focused on readability and visual appeal, Celestia offers 
          a clean and professional look for presentations.

          Currently, it has native support for Chinese (both simplified and traditional), English, French, German, 
          Italian, Japanese, Portuguese (European and Brazilian), Russian and Spanish typesetting. It compiles 
          with either XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

          depends on \texttt{colorist.sty} from the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/colorist}{colorist} package.

          The package name ''beaulivre'' is taken from the French words ''beau'' (= ''beautiful'') and ''livre'' 
          (= ''book'').

\section[\texttt{bestpapers} -- A BibTeX package to produce lists of authors’ best papers]{\texttt{bestpapers} -- A BibTeX package to produce lists of authors’ best papers}\label{pkg:bestpapers}
\index{Package!bestpapers}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bestpapers}
\item[name] \texttt{bestpapers}
\item[caption] A BibTeX package to produce lists of authors’ best papers
\item[author] Veytsman, Boris
\index{Author!Veytsman, Boris}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) Many people preparing their résumés find the requirement ''please list five (or six, or ten) papers authored 
          by you''. The same requirement is often stated for reports prepared by professional teams. The creation 
          of such lists may be a cumbersome task. Even more difficult is it to support such lists over the time, 
          when new papers are added.

          The BibTeX style  \texttt{bestpapers.bst} is intended to facilitate this task. It is based 
          on the idea that it is easier to score than to sort: We can assign a score to a paper and then let the 
          computer select the papers with highest scores.

          This work was commissioned by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, United States Treasury.

          This package is in the public domain.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/contrib/bestpapers/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/contrib/bestpapers/bestpapers-guide.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./6846205077-bestpapers-guide.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/contrib/bestpapers}

\section[\texttt{bezierplot} -- Approximate smooth function graphs with cubic bezier splines\ldots]{\texttt{bezierplot} -- Approximate smooth function graphs with cubic bezier splines for use with TikZ or MetaPost}\label{pkg:bezierplot}
\index{Package!bezierplot}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bezierplot}
\item[name] \texttt{bezierplot}
\item[caption] Approximate smooth function graphs with cubic bezier splines for use with TikZ or MetaPost
\item[author] Romer, Linus
\index{Author!Romer, Linus}
\item[copyright] Linus Romer (2018-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.6 (2024-11-02)
\item[last changes] 2024-11-02
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package consists of a Lua program as well as a (Lua)LaTeX  \texttt{.sty} file.

          Given a smooth function,  \texttt{bezierplot} returns a smooth bezier path written in TikZ 
          notation (which also matches MetaPost) that approximates the graph of the function. For polynomial functions 
          of degree $<=$ 3 and their inverses the approximation is exact (up to numeric precision).

          \texttt{bezierplot} also finds special points such as extreme points and inflection points 
          and reduces the number of used points.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/bezierplot/README}

\item[version] 2.11
\item[description] (no language specified) The bgteubner document class has been programmed by order of the Teubner Verlag, Wiesbaden, Germany, 
          to ensure that books of this publisher have a unique layout. Unfortunately, most of the documentation 
          is only available in German.

          Since the document class is intended to generate a unique layout, many things (layout etc.) are fixed 
          and cannot be altered by the user. If you want to use the document class for another purpose than publishing 
          with the Teubner Verlag, this may arouse unwanted restrictions (for instance, the document class provides 
          only two paper sizes: DIN A5 and 17cm x 24cm; only two font families are supported: Times and European 
          Computer Modern).

\item[description] (no language specified) \texttt{BHCexam.cls} is a LaTeX document class designed for typesetting exams. It is currently 
          used by the \href{https://database.mathcrowd.cn/}{Mathcrowd Problem Database} to generate 
          exam PDF files. The class supports the following features:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Support for configuring whether to display answers.
          \item Ability to set whether the document is formatted in multiple columns.
          \item Alignment customization options.
          \item Automatic alignment of option lengths to a grid.
          \item Ability to adjust the width of blank lines based on the length of fill-in-the-blank answers.
          \item Option to display or hide scores for question groups.
          \item Customizable answer space for each question.
          \item Ability to restart numbering in question groups.
          \item Support for sub-questions and nested sub-questions in short-answer questions.
          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{bib2gls} -- Command line application to convert .bib files to glossaries\ldots]{\texttt{bib2gls} -- Command line application to convert .bib files to glossaries-extra.sty resource files}\label{pkg:bib2gls}
\index{Package!bib2gls}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bib2gls}
\item[name] \texttt{bib2gls}
\item[caption] Command line application to convert .bib files to glossaries-extra.sty resource files
\item[author] Talbot, Nicola
\index{Author!Talbot, Nicola}
\item[copyright] Nicola L. C. Talbot (2017-2025)
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[version] 4.7 (2025-11-13)
\item[last changes] 2025-11-13
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This Java command line application may be used to extract glossary information stored in a  \texttt{.bib} file 
          and convert it into glossary entry definition commands.

          This application should be used with  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries-extra}{glossaries-extra.sty} ’s 
          ‘record’ package option. It performs two functions in one:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item selects entries according to records found in the  \texttt{.aux} file (similar to \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{bibtex} ),
          \item hierarchically sorts entries and collates location lists (similar to  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex}{makeindex} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xindy}{xindy} ).
          \end{itemize}
The glossary entries can then be managed in a system such as  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/jabref}{JabRef} , 
          and only the entries that are actually required will be defined, reducing the resources required by TeX.

          The supplementary application  \texttt{convertgls2bib} can be used to convert existing \texttt{.tex} files 
          containing definitions ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}newglossaryentry} etc.) to the \texttt{.bib} format 
          required by \texttt{bib2gls} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/bib2gls/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Introductory Guide}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/bib2gls/bib2gls-begin.pdf}

\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 2.35
\item[description] (no language specified) bib2xhtml is a program that converts BibTeX files into HTML (specifically XHTML 1.0). The conversion 
          is mostly done by specialized BibTeX style files, derived from a converted bibliography style template. 
          This ensures that the original BibTeX styles are faithfully reproduced. Some postprocessing is performed 
          by Perl code.

          This is an update of the bib2html program written by David Hull in 1996 and maintained by him until 1998. 
          I have been a happy user of the program since 1995, using the program to keep my publication list up 
          to date, and, lately, to generate the on-line bibliography list for my book Code Reading: The Open Source 
          Perspective (Addison-Wesley 2003). After 1998 no other changes were made to the program, and I failed 
          to locate an active program home page. Since there were a number of changes I needed to bring the program 
          up to date with evolving web standards, I decided to adopt bib2html for maintenance, evolution, and further 
          distribution. The first new public release made in 2004, features support for XHTML 1.0.

\section[\texttt{bibarts} -- “Arts”-style bibliographical information]{\texttt{bibarts} -- “Arts”-style bibliographical information}\label{pkg:bibarts}
\index{Package!bibarts}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibarts}
\item[name] \texttt{BibArts}
\item[caption] “Arts”-style bibliographical information
\item[author] Baumann, Timo
\index{Author!Baumann, Timo}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 2.6
\item[description] (no language specified) BibArts is a LaTeX package to assist in making bibliographical features common in the arts and the humanities 
          (history, political science, philosophy, etc.).

          \texttt{bibarts.sty} provides commands for quotations, abbreviations, and especially for 
          a formatted citation of literature, journals (periodicals), edited sources, and archive sources. In difference 
          to earlier versions, BibArts 2.x helps to use slanted fonts (italics) and is able to set ibidem automatically 
          in footnotes. It will also copy all citation information, abbreviations, and register key words into 
          lists for an automatically generated appendix. These lists may refer to page and footnote numbers. BibArts 
          has nothing to do with \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} . The lists are created 
          by \texttt{bibsort} (see below).

          BibArts requires the program  \texttt{bibsort} , for which the sources and a Windows executable 
          are provided. This program creates the bibliography without using \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex}{MakeIndex} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} . 
          Its source is not written with any specific operating system in mind. A summary of contents is in English; 
          the full documentation is in German.
\item[documentation]  (German) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/bibarts/bibarts.pdf}

\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) Biber is a  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} replacement for users of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} .

          Biber supports full UTF-8, can (re)-encode input and output, supports highly configurable sorting, dynamic 
          bibliography sets and many other features.

          The CTAN distribution offers a compressed tar archive of the sources, etc., together with ''binary'' 
          distributions for a variety of platforms.

          Note: on SourceForge biber is formally named ''biblatex-biber'', to distinguish it from an earlier (now 
          apparently moribund) project called ''biber''.

\section[\texttt{bibextract} -- Utilities to extract BibTeX data]{\texttt{bibextract} -- Utilities to extract BibTeX data}\label{pkg:bibextract}
\index{Package!bibextract}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibextract}
\item[name] \texttt{bibextract}
\item[caption] Utilities to extract BibTeX data
\item[author] Beebe, Nelson H. F.
\index{Author!Beebe, Nelson H. F.}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 1.09
\item[description] (no language specified) A set of scripts for extracting entries from .bib file, in particular those cited in a particular document.

          Bibextract itself extracts from a list of BibTeX .bib files those bibliography entries that match a pair 
          of specified regular expressions, sending them to stdout, together with all BibTeX  \texttt{@Preamble{\textbraceleft}...{\textbraceright}} and \texttt{@String{\textbraceleft}...{\textbraceright}} commands.

          Citefind from a list of BibTeX .bib files those bibliography entries that match a specified list of citation 
          tags, possibly produced by citetags.

          Citetags extracts BibTeX citation tags from a LaTeX source file or .aux file and sends them to stdout, 
          possibly for later input to citefind.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Bibextract man page (text)}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/utils/bibextract/bibextract.txt}

\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}

\item[description] (no language specified) This is a small gawk script to put all the  \texttt{pages=} page ranges in a \texttt{.bib} file 
          into a uniform format, either 1234-1256 or upon request 1234-56; null ranges such as 1234-1234 are always 
          scrunched to just 1234. The script squeezes out spaces around the separator; can make all separators 
          one- or two-hyphens upon request. The script is very conservative: it is probably impossible for it actually 
          to mess up a file.

\item[author] Nardello, Massimo
\index{Author!Nardello, Massimo}
\item[license] gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
\index{License!gpl3}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3}
\item[version] 1.2.8
\item[description] (no language specified) Bibfilex is a free bibliographic manager for GNU/Linux, Windows and OS X. It is useful for creating and 
          managing archives of bibliographical items with possible attachments of any kind according to BibLaTeX 
          structure and rules, but it may also be used with a wordprocessor like Writer or Word.

          Bibfilex is less advanced than other bibliographic managers like  \href{http://jabref.sourceforge.net/}{JabRef} or 
          KBibTeX and allows only few customizations. Its strength is simplicity and speed, since it's a compiled 
          software and uses a fast database, Sqlite, for storing data.

          Bibfilex is written in Free Pascal with Lazarus.

          made that major breakthrough, etc. You can use Perl regexes in your search string and hence wield the 
          awesome power of Perl’s pattern matching.

          files, which together allow you to output a bibliography as a collection of HTML files. The references 
          in the text are linked directly to the corresponding bibliography entry, and if a URL is defined in the 
          entry within the BibTeX database file, then the generated bibliography entry is linked to this. The package

\section[\texttt{biblatex} -- Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX]{\texttt{biblatex} -- Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX}\label{pkg:biblatex}
\index{Package!biblatex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}
\item[name] \texttt{BibLaTeX}
\item[caption] Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX
\item[author] Kime, Philip
\index{Author!Kime, Philip}
\item[author] Lehman, Philipp
\index{Author!Lehman, Philipp}
\item[copyright] Philip Kime, Audrey Boruvka, Joseph Wright (2012-2025)
\item[copyright] Philip Kime, Moritz Wemheuer (2018-2025)
\item[copyright] Philipp Lehman (2006-2012)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 3.21 (2025-07-10)
\item[last changes] 2025-07-10
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) BibLaTeX is a complete reimplementation of the bibliographic facilities provided by LaTeX. Formatting 
          of the bibliography is entirely controlled by LaTeX macros, and a working knowledge of LaTeX should be 
          sufficient to design new bibliography and citation styles. BibLaTeX uses its own data backend program 
          called  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biber}{''biber''} to read and process the bibliographic 
          data. With \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biber}{biber} , BibLaTeX has many features rivalling 
          or surpassing other bibliography systems. To mention a few:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Full Unicode support
          \item Highly customisable sorting using the Unicode Collation Algorithm + CLDR tailoring
          \item Highly customisable bibliography labels
          \item Complex macro-based on-the-fly data modification without changing your data sources
          \item A tool mode for transforming bibliographic data sources
          \item Multiple bibliographies and lists of bibliographic information in the same document with different sorting
          \item Highly customisable data source inheritance rules
          \item Polyglossia and babel support for automatic language switching for bibliographic entries and citations
          \item Automatic bibliography data recoding (UTF-8 -\&gt; latin1, LaTeX macros -\&gt; UTF-8 etc)
          \item Remote data sources
          \item Highly sophisticated automatic name and name list disambiguation system
          \item Highly customisable data model so users can define their own bibliographic data types
          \item Validation of bibliographic data against a data model
          \item Subdivided and/or filtered bibliographies, bibliographies per chapter, section etc.
          \end{itemize}
Apart from the features unique to BibLaTeX, the package also incorporates core features of the following 
          packages:  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babelbib}{babelbib} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtopic}{bibtopic} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibunits}{bibunits} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/chapterbib}{chapterbib} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cite}{cite} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/inlinebib}{inlinebib} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mcite}{mcite} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mciteplus}{mciteplus} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mlbib}{mlbib} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/multibib}{multibib} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/splitbib}{splitbib} .

          The package strictly requires

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etex}{e-TeX} 
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} , \texttt{bibtex8} , or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biber}{Biber} 
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox}{etoolbox}            .1 or later
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/logreq}{logreq} 1.0 or later
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/keyval}{keyval} 
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ifthen}{ifthen} 
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/url}{url} 
          \end{itemize}
 \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biber}{Biber} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} / \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia}{polyglossia} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/csquotes}{csquotes} 4.4 or later are strongly recommended.

\section[\texttt{biblatex-abs-annote} -- Annotated bibliographies with abstracts and annotations for \ldots]{\texttt{biblatex-abs-annote} -- Annotated bibliographies with abstracts and annotations for BibLaTeX}\label{pkg:biblatex-abs-annote}
\index{Package!biblatex-abs-annote}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-abs-annote}
\item[name] \texttt{biblatex-abs-annote}
\item[caption] Annotated bibliographies with abstracts and annotations for BibLaTeX
\item[author] Wimpy, Cameron
\index{Author!Wimpy, Cameron}
\item[copyright] Cameron Wimpy (2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.1.1 (2026-04-19)
\item[last changes] 2026-04-19
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package extends any BibLaTeX style with an annotated-bibliography presentation: below each reference 
          it renders the entry's abstract and the user's annotation, both drawn from standard BibLaTeX fields (abstract, 
          and annotation or annote). Either field may be omitted on a per-entry basis, so the same bibliography 
          can mix plain and annotated citations freely. The package patches the sixteen standard BibLaTeX drivers 
          via xpatch, so it composes with any bibliography style that uses the standard driver names (authoryear, 
          apa, numeric, chicago-authordate, etc.). All visual aspects (e.g., labels, fonts, indentation, and spacing) 
          are controlled by redefinable commands and lengths. The package is the LaTeX component of the cross-format 
          ab-annotate toolchain, which shares the same .bib conventions with companion packages for Typst and Quarto.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-abs-annote/biblatex-abs-annote.pdf}

\section[\texttt{biblatex-accursius} -- Citing features for Italian jurists]{\texttt{biblatex-accursius} -- Citing features for Italian jurists}\label{pkg:biblatex-accursius}
\index{Package!biblatex-accursius}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-accursius}
\item[name] \texttt{biblatex-accursius}
\item[caption] Citing features for Italian jurists
\item[author] Contini, Francesco
\index{Author!Contini, Francesco}
\item[copyright] Francesco Contini (2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) This style is primarily aimed at Italian legal jurists and provides them with the ability to cite legal 
          materials, such as legislative acts, regulations, soft law, treaties and case law. Additionally, the 
          style codifies the most prevalent citation practices amongst Italian legal scholars.

          Specifically, with regard to the citation of legal materials, this style, instead of developing the entry 
          types  \texttt{@jurisdiction} , \texttt{@legal} , and \texttt{@legislation} , 
          creates a new one: \texttt{@itprov} , which can describe a wide range of legal sources. Furthermore, 
          it creates a second new entry type: \texttt{@notetoprov} , which is used specifically to 
          cite so-called ''note a sentenza'' (notes to judgement), which closely mirrors \texttt{@itprov} , 
          but is literature and, therefore, is intended to have the same treatment as standard entry types.

          The citation commands are the standard ones.

          The  \texttt{@itprov} entry type comprises the list \texttt{institution} to indicate 
          which authority adopted the cited act; the \texttt{kindprov} , \texttt{nprov} , \texttt{provtitle} (or \texttt{titleparties} ) 
          fields to indicate the minimal ‘ID’ of the act and many others. Finally, the entry type allows to specify 
          where the cited act was consulted, whether from an official bulletin (the \texttt{ofbull} field), 
          an official portal or a private database (the \texttt{ofportal} field), or a journal or collection.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-accursius/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-accursius/biblatex-accursius.pdf}

\item[last changes] 2019-12-30

\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides additional  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} styles 
          for German humanities. Its core purpose is to enable the referencing rules of the Romano-Germanic Commission 
          ( \emph{\&gt;Römisch-Germanische Kommission} ), the department of prehistory of the German 
          Archaeological Institute ( \emph{Deutsches Archäologisches Institut} ), since these are referenced 
          by most guidelines in German prehistory and medieval archaeology and serve as a kind of template. \texttt{biblatex-archaeology} provides 
          verbose, numeric and author date styles as well and adaptions to specific document types like exhibition 
          and auction catalogues.

\item[description] (no language specified) This is a  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} style that combines the features 
          of the styles authoryear-comp (omission of recurring author/year in multiple-reference-citations) and 
          authoryear-ibid (replacement of repeated citations by the abbreviation ibidem). The implementation relies 
          heavily on unmodified BibLaTeX macros, and no attempt has been made to add further features not present 
          in core BibLaTeX.

\section[\texttt{biblatex-claves} -- A tool to manage claves of old literature with BibLaTeX]{\texttt{biblatex-claves} -- A tool to manage claves of old literature with BibLaTeX}\label{pkg:biblatex-claves}
\index{Package!biblatex-claves}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-claves}
\item[name] \texttt{biblatex-claves}
\item[caption] A tool to manage claves of old literature with BibLaTeX
\item[author] Rouquette, Maïeul
\index{Author!Rouquette, Maïeul}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.2.1 (2017-11-19)
\item[last changes] 2017-11-19
\item[year] 2017
\index{Year!2017}
\item[description] (no language specified) When studying antique and medieval literature, we may find many different texts published with the same 
          title, or, in contrary, the same text published with different titles.

          To avoid confusion, scholars have published claves, which are books listing ancient texts, identifying 
          them by an identifier — a number or a string of text. For example, for early Christianity, we have the 
          Bibliotheca Hagiographica Graeca, the Clavis Apocryphorum Novi Testamenti and other claves.

          It could be useful to print the identifier of a texts in one specific clavis, or in many claves. The 
          package allows us to create new field for different claves, and to present all these fields in a consistent 
          way.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-claves/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-claves/documentation/biblatex-claves.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./7595149914-biblatex-claves.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-claves}

          used simply by loading BibLaTeX with the appropriate option:

          or later, and works with both \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biber}{Biber} as

\section[\texttt{biblatex-ms} -- Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX (multiscript version)]{\texttt{biblatex-ms} -- Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX (multiscript version)}\label{pkg:biblatex-ms}
\index{Package!biblatex-ms}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-ms}
\item[name] \texttt{biblatex-ms}
\item[caption] Sophisticated Bibliographies in LaTeX (multiscript version)
\item[author] Kime, Philip
\index{Author!Kime, Philip}
\item[copyright] Philipp Lehman (2006-2012)
\item[copyright] Philipp Lehman, Joseph Wright, Audrey Boruvka, Philip Kime (2012-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 4.0-1
\item[description] (no language specified) This package is the ''multiscript'' version of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} package 
          intended to solve the issues faced by those wishing to create multilingual bibliographies. It is intended 
          to be backwards-compatible with the standard \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} package 
          and includes significantly enhanced optional functionality:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Fields in data files can have different form/language alternates in the same entry
          \item Options to select/print a specific alternate are generally available
          \item babel/polyglossia language switching is done automatically based on the language associated with a field
          \end{itemize}
The intention is that this version will eventually replace standard BibLaTeX and is being released as 
          an independent package to allow for wider testing and feedback. It can be installed in parallel with 
          standard BibLaTeX and the package name is  \texttt{biblatex-ms} . It requires the use of 
          the multiscript version of biber (biber-ms).

\section[\texttt{biblatex-opcit-booktitle} -- Use op. cit. for the booktitle of a subentry]{\texttt{biblatex-opcit-booktitle} -- Use op. cit. for the booktitle of a subentry}\label{pkg:biblatex-opcit-booktitle}
\index{Package!biblatex-opcit-booktitle}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-opcit-booktitle}
\item[name] \texttt{biblatex-opcit-booktitle}
\item[caption] Use op. cit. for the booktitle of a subentry
\item[author] Rouquette, Maïeul
\index{Author!Rouquette, Maïeul}
\item[copyright] Maïeul Rouquette (2015-2018)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.9.0 (2018-10-24)
\item[last changes] 2018-10-24
\item[year] 2018
\index{Year!2018}
\item[description] (no language specified) The default citation styles verbose-trad1+; verbose-trad2 ; verbose-trad3 use the op. cit. form in order 
          to have a shorter reference when a title has already been cited. However, when you cite two entries which 
          share the same booktitle but not the same  \texttt{title} , the op. cit. mechanism does not 
          work.

          This package enables to obtain references like this:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Author1, Title, in Booktitle, Location, Publisher, Year, pages
          \item xxx
          \item Author2, Title2, in Booktitle, op. cit, pages.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-opcit-booktitle/README}

\section[\texttt{biblatex-oxref} -- BibLaTeX styles inspired by the Oxford Guide to Style]{\texttt{biblatex-oxref} -- BibLaTeX styles inspired by the Oxford Guide to Style}\label{pkg:biblatex-oxref}
\index{Package!biblatex-oxref}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-oxref}
\item[name] \texttt{biblatex-oxref}
\item[caption] BibLaTeX styles inspired by the Oxford Guide to Style
\item[author] Ball, Alex
\index{Author!Ball, Alex}
\item[copyright] Alex Ball (2016-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 3.4 (2026-04-14)
\item[last changes] 2026-04-14
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This bundle provides four BibLaTeX styles that implement (many of) the stipulations and examples provided 
          by the 2014  \emph{New Hart’s Rules} and the 2002 \emph{Oxford Guide to Style} :

          
          \begin{itemize}
          \item ‘oxnotes’ is a style similar to the standard ‘verbose’, intended for use with footnotes;
          \item ‘oxnum’ is a style similar to the standard ‘numeric’, intended for use with numeric in-text citations;
          \item ‘oxalph’ is a style similar to the standard ‘alphabetic’, intended for use with alphabetic in-text citations;
          \item ‘oxyear’ is a style similar to the standard ‘author-year’, intended for use with parenthetical in-text citations.
          \end{itemize}
The bundle provides support for a wide variety of content types, including manuscripts, audiovisual resources, 
          social media and legal references.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-oxref/README.md}

          which reads a \texttt{.bbl} file created by \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biber}{Biber} .

\section[\texttt{biblatex-shortfields} -- Use short forms of fields with BibLaTeX]{\texttt{biblatex-shortfields} -- Use short forms of fields with BibLaTeX}\label{pkg:biblatex-shortfields}
\index{Package!biblatex-shortfields}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-shortfields}
\item[name] \texttt{biblatex-shortfields}
\item[caption] Use short forms of fields with BibLaTeX
\item[author] Rouquette, Maïeul
\index{Author!Rouquette, Maïeul}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.0.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The BibLaTeX package provides  \texttt{shortseries} and \texttt{shortjournal} field, 
          but the default styles don't use them.

          It also provides a mechanism to print the equivalence between short forms of fields and long fields ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}printbiblist} ), 
          but this mechanism does not allow to mix between different type of short fields, for example, between 
          short forms of journal title and short forms of series titles.

          This package provides a solution to these two problems: 
          \begin{itemize}
          \item If a  \texttt{shortjournal} field is defined, it prints it instead of the \texttt{{\textbackslash}journal} field.
          \item If a  \texttt{shortseries} field is defined, it prints it instead of the \texttt{{\textbackslash}series} field.
          \item It provides a  \texttt{{\textbackslash}printbibshortfields} command to print a list of the sort forms of the fields.
          \item This list also includes the claves defined with the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex-claves}{biblatex-claves} package version 1.2 or later.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-shortfields/documentation/biblatex-shortfields.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5533266253-biblatex-shortfields.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-shortfields/README}

\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 2.0.0
\item[description] (no language specified) This package deals with a limitation of the  \texttt{citepages=omit} option of the verbose 
          family of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} citestyles.

          The option works when you  \texttt{{\textbackslash}cite[xx]{\textbraceleft}key{\textbraceright}} , 
          but not when you \texttt{{\textbackslash}cite[{\textbackslash}pno{\textasciitilde}xx, 
          some text]{\textbraceleft}key{\textbraceright}} .

          The package corrects this problem.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex-contrib/biblatex-true-citepages-omit/biblatex-true-citepages-omit.pdf}

\section[\texttt{biblatex2bibitem} -- Convert BibLaTeX-generated bibliography to bibitems]{\texttt{biblatex2bibitem} -- Convert BibLaTeX-generated bibliography to bibitems}\label{pkg:biblatex2bibitem}
\index{Package!biblatex2bibitem}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex2bibitem}
\item[name] \texttt{biblatex2bibitem}
\item[caption] Convert BibLaTeX-generated bibliography to bibitems
\item[author] Avdeev, Nikolai
\index{Author!Avdeev, Nikolai}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.2.2 (2022-01-17)
\item[last changes] 2022-01-17
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) Some journals accept the reference list only as  \texttt{{\textbackslash}bibitem} s. 
          If you use \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} , there is no problem: just paste 
          the content of the \texttt{.bbl} file into your document. However, there was no out-of-the-box 
          way to do the same for \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{biblatex} , and you had to 
          struggle with searching appropriate \texttt{.bst} files, or formatting your reference list 
          by hand, or something like that.

          Using the workaround provided by this package solves the problem.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex2bibitem/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Minimal working example}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex2bibitem/biblatex2bibitem-mwe.pdf}

\section[\texttt{bibtex} -- Process bibliographies (bib files) for LaTeX or other format\ldots]{\texttt{bibtex} -- Process bibliographies (bib files) for LaTeX or other formats}\label{pkg:bibtex}
\index{Package!bibtex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}
\item[name] \texttt{bibtex}
\item[caption] Process bibliographies (bib files) for LaTeX or other formats
\item[author] Patashnik, Oren
\index{Author!Patashnik, Oren}
\item[license] knuth = Knuth License (free)
\index{License!knuth}
\index{License!Knuth License}
\item[version] 0.99e
\item[description] (no language specified) BibTeX allows the user to store his citation data in generic form, while printing citations in a document 
          in the form specified by a BibTeX style, to be specified in the document itself (one often needs a LaTeX 
          citation-style package, such as  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/natbib}{natbib} , as well).

          BibTeX knows nothing about Unicode sorting algorithms or scripts, although it will pass on whatever bytes 
          it reads. Its descendant  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtexu}{bibtexu} does support Unicode, 
          via the ICU library. The older alternative \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex8}{bibtex8} supports 
          8-bit character sets.

          Another Unicode-aware alternative is the (independently developed)  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biber}{biber} program, 
          used with the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} package to typeset its output.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Using BibTeX}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/base/btxdoc.pdf}

\index{Package!bibtools}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtools}
\item[name] \texttt{bibtools}
\item[caption] Bib management tools
\item[author] Kotz, David
\index{Author!Kotz, David}
\item[author] Gildea, Daniel
\index{Author!Gildea, Daniel}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) A set of bibliography tools. Includes:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{aux2bib} , a perl script which will take an \texttt{.aux} file and make a portable \texttt{.bib} file to go with it;
          \item  \texttt{bibify} , a shell script that will optimise away one pass of the LaTeX/BibTeX cycle, in some cases;
          \item  \texttt{bibkey} , a shell script that finds entries whose '' \texttt{keyword} '' field matches the given keys (uses sed and awk);
          \item  \texttt{cleantex} , a shell script to tidy up after a LaTeX run;
          \item  \texttt{looktex} , a shell script to list entries that match a given regexp;
          \item  \texttt{makebib} , a shell script to make an exportable \texttt{.bib} file from an existing (set of) \texttt{.bib} file(s) and an optional set of citations (uses sed)
          \item  \texttt{printbib} , a shell script to make a \texttt{dvi} file from a \texttt{.bib} file, sorted by cite key, and including fields like '' \texttt{keyword} '', '' \texttt{abstract} '', and '' \texttt{comment} ''.
          \item  \texttt{bib2html} , a perl script that makes a browsable HTML version of a bibliography (several \texttt{.bst} files are supplied); and
          \item  \texttt{citekeys} , a shell script that lists the citation keys of a \texttt{.bib} file.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/utils/bibtools/README}

\item[version] 1.1a
\item[description] (no language specified) The package allows the user to include several bibliographies covering different ‘topics’ or bibliographic 
          material into a document (e.g., one bibliography for primary literature and one for secondary literature). 
          The package provides commands to include either all references from a  \texttt{.bib} file, 
          only the references actually cited or those not cited in your document. The user has to construct a separate \texttt{.bib} file 
          for each bibliographic ‘topic’, each of which will be processed separately by BibTeX.

          If you want to have bibliographies specific to one part of a document, see the packages  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibunits}{bibunits} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/chapterbib}{chapterbib} .

          or bibunit-environments) of a text. The package separates the citations of each unit of text into a separate

          the document and citations can be placed in both the local unit and the global bibliographies at the 
          same time.

          with the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} French option frenchb.

\section[\texttt{bibutils} -- A collection of bibliography format convertors]{\texttt{bibutils} -- A collection of bibliography format convertors}\label{pkg:bibutils}
\index{Package!bibutils}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibutils}
\item[name] \texttt{bibutils}
\item[caption] A collection of bibliography format convertors
\item[author] Putnam, Chris
\index{Author!Putnam, Chris}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 6.6
\item[description] (no language specified) The bibutils program set interconverts between various bibliography formats using a common MODS-format 
          XML intermediate. For example, one can convert RIS-format files to BibTeX by doing two transformations: 
          RIS->MODS->BibTeX. By using a common intermediate for N formats, only 2N programs are required and not 
          N{\textasciicircum}2-N. These programs operate on the command line and are styled after standard 
          UNIX-like filters.

          The author reckons to use the tools at the command line, but they are suitable for scripting and have 
          been incorporated into a number of different bibliographic projects.
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/utils/bibutils}

\item[author] Palmieri, John H.
\index{Author!Palmieri, John H.}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) A utility to automatically retrieve mathematical bibliographical information, in BibTeX format, from 
          the American Mathematical Society‘s MathSciNet database. More precisely, it acts as a front-end to BibTeX; 
          it converts any citations that BibTeX can‘t find into queries to the MathSciNet database, it carries 
          out those queries, and returns the answers in BibTeX format. Included in the package are: the perl script 
          bibweb, documentation (in various formats), and a test file.

\section[\texttt{bigfoot} -- Footnotes for critical editions]{\texttt{bigfoot} -- Footnotes for critical editions}\label{pkg:bigfoot}
\index{Package!bigfoot}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bigfoot}
\item[name] \texttt{bigfoot}
\item[caption] Footnotes for critical editions
\item[author] Kastrup, David
\index{Author!Kastrup, David}
\item[license] gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
\index{License!gpl2}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 2}
\item[version] 2.1 (2015-08-30)
\item[last changes] 2015-08-30
\item[year] 2015
\index{Year!2015}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package aims to provide a ‘one-stop’ solution to requirements for footnotes. It offers:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Multiple footnote apparatus superior to that of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/manyfoot}{manyfoot} 
          \item Footnotes can be formatted in separate paragraphs, or be run into a single paragraph (this choice may be selected per footnote series);
          \item Things you might have expected (such as  \texttt{{\textbackslash}verb} -like material in footnotes, and colour selections over page breaks) now work.
          \end{itemize}
Note that the majority of the bigfoot package's interface is identical to that of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/manyfoot}{manyfoot} ; 
          users should seek information from that package's documentation.

          The bigfoot bundle also provides the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/perpage}{perpage} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/suffix}{suffix} packages.

\index{License!noinfo}
\index{License!noinfo}
\item[version]  (1993-04-02)
\item[last changes] 1993-04-02
\item[year] 1993
\index{Year!1993}
\item[description] (no language specified) Defines a  \texttt{Tabular} environment, which is (in effect) a \texttt{tabular*} environment 
          that can split across pages. The major distinction is that \texttt{{\textbackslash}Tabular} doesn't 
          take an optional argument. It behaves much like \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}tabular*{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}linewidth{\textbraceright}} with \texttt{{\textbackslash}Tabularleftskip} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}Tabularrightskip} used 
          as the stretchable glue on either side.

          The package feels as if it were a predecessor of the current LaTeX  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable}{longtable} package.

\section[\texttt{bitelist} -- Split list, in TeX’s mouth]{\texttt{bitelist} -- Split list, in TeX’s mouth}\label{pkg:bitelist}
\index{Package!bitelist}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bitelist}
\item[name] \texttt{bitelist}
\item[caption] Split list, in TeX’s mouth
\item[author] Lück, Uwe
\index{Author!Lück, Uwe}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides commands for ''splitting'' a token list at the first occurrence of another (specified) 
          token list. I.e., for given token lists  \emph{s} , \emph{t} return \emph{b} and 
          the shortest \emph{a} , such that \emph{t = a s b} .

          The package’s mechanism differs from those of packages providing similar features, in the following ways:

          
          \begin{itemize}
          \item the method uses TeX’s mechanism of reading delimited macro parameters;
          \item splitting macros work by pure expansion, without assignments;
          \item the operation is carried out in a single macro call.
          \end{itemize}
A variant of the operation is provided, that retains outer braces.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/bitelist/bitelist.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./7051268628-bitelist.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/bitelist/README}
\item[contact] \textit{support}: \url{http://www.webdesign-bu.de/uwe_lueck/contact.html}
\index{Contact!support}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/bitelist}
\item[installation]\url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/install/macros/generic/bitelist.tds.zip}
\item[on Mik\TeX] \texttt{bitelist}
\item[on \TeX Live] \texttt{bitelist}

\index{Topic!macro-supp}
\item[keyword] \texttt{text-manip} (manipulate strings (typically in token lists))

\item[license] noinfo = noinfo 
\index{License!noinfo}
\index{License!noinfo}
\item[description] (no language specified) Font metrics, dvips maps, and macro support in LaTeX2e, for Bitstream fonts that were (allegedly) freely 
          available at some time. All the fonts are listed for purchase on font distribution sites.

          Font families supported are:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Bitstream Charter;
          \item Caslon 540 and Caslon Openface;
          \item Courier 10 Pitch;
          \item De Vinne Text;
          \item Elegant Garamond, otherwise known as Granjon;
          \item Humanist 521, otherwise known as Gill Sans;
          \item ‘Melior’, otherwise known as Zapf Elliptical 711;
          \item Optima, otherwise known as Zapf Humanist 601;
          \item Modern 735, based on Bodoni Campanile;
          \item Modern No.20;
          \item Palatino, otherwise known as Zapf Calligraphic 801;
          \item Peignot, otherwise known as Exotic 350 Bold;
          \item Plantin, otherwise known as Aldine 721;
          \item Stempel Garamond, otherwise known as Original Garamond;
          \item Schneidler;
          \item Univers, otherwise known as Zurich.
          \end{itemize}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/psfonts/bitstrea}

\section[\texttt{blkarray} -- Extended array and tabular]{\texttt{blkarray} -- Extended array and tabular}\label{pkg:blkarray}
\index{Package!blkarray}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/blkarray}
\item[name] \texttt{blkarray}
\item[caption] Extended array and tabular
\item[author] Carlisle, David
\index{Author!Carlisle, David}
\item[copyright] David Carlisle (1992, 1999, 2015)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.07
\item[description] (no language specified) An experimental package which implements an environment, blockarray, that may be used in the same way 
          as the array or tabular environments of standard LaTeX, or their extended versions defined in  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/array}{array} . 
          If used in math-mode, blockarray acts like array, otherwise it acts like tabular.

          The package implements a new method of defining column types, and also  \texttt{block} and \texttt{block*} environments, 
          for specifying sub-arrays of the main array. What’s more, the \texttt{{\textbackslash}footnote} command 
          works inside a blockarray.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/blkarray/blkarray.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./6611848855-blkarray.pdf|

\item[description] (no language specified) The bm package defines a command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}bm} which makes its argument 
          bold. The argument may be any maths object from a single symbol to an expression. This is closely related 
          to the specification of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsbsy}{ \texttt{{\textbackslash}boldsymbol} } command 
          in AMS-LaTeX, but \texttt{{\textbackslash}bm} is rather more careful in the way it 
          does things.

          in the LaTeX \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/required}{required} distribution.

\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}bnumeval} , which extends 
          LaTeX's \texttt{{\textbackslash}inteval} with support for arbitrarily big integers, \texttt{//} for 
          floored division, \texttt{/:} for the associated remainder, \texttt{{\textasciicircum}} and \texttt{**} for 
          powers, \texttt{!} for factorials, \texttt{0b} , \texttt{0o} and \texttt{'} , \texttt{0x} and \texttt{"} , 
          as prefixes for binary, octal, or hexadecimal inputs. With the optional argument \texttt{[h]} (or \texttt{[o]} or \texttt{[b]} ) 
          the output is converted to hexadecimal (or octal, or binary).

\section[\texttt{bodeplot} -- Draw Bode, Nyquist and Nichols plots with gnuplot or pgfplot\ldots]{\texttt{bodeplot} -- Draw Bode, Nyquist and Nichols plots with gnuplot or pgfplots}\label{pkg:bodeplot}
\index{Package!bodeplot}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bodeplot}
\item[name] \texttt{bodeplot}
\item[caption] Draw Bode, Nyquist and Nichols plots with gnuplot or pgfplots
\item[author] Kamalapurkar, Rushikesh
\index{Author!Kamalapurkar, Rushikesh}
\item[copyright] Rushikesh Kamalapurkar (2021-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 3.0.3 (2026-01-15)
\item[last changes] 2026-01-15
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This is a LaTeX package to plot Bode, Nichols, and Nyquist diagrams. It provides added functionality 
          over the similar  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bodegraph}{bodegraph} package:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item New  \texttt{{\textbackslash}BodeZPK} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}BodeTF} commands to generate Bode plots of any transfer function given either poles, zeros, gain, and delay, or numerator and denominator coefficients and delay
          \item Support for unstable poles and zeros.
          \item Support for complex poles and zeros.
          \item Support for general stable and unstable second order transfer functions.
          \item Support for both  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gnuplot}{Gnuplot} (default) and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgfplots}{pgfplots} (package option \texttt{pgf} ).
          \item Support for linear and asymptotic approximation of magnitude and phase plots of any transfer function given poles, zeros, and gain.
          \end{itemize}

\item[author] Folkertsma, Geert

\index{License!lppl1.3}

\item[version] 1.0.1 (2015-03-23)
\item[last changes] 2015-03-23
\item[year] 2015
\index{Year!2015}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package is used to draw bond graphs in LaTeX. It uses a recent version (3.0+) of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{PGF 
          and TikZ} for the drawing, hence, it is mainly a set of TikZ styles that makes the drawing of bond 
          graphs easier.

          Compared to the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bondgraph}{bondgraph} package this package 
          relies more on TikZ styles and less on macros, to generate the drawings. As such it can be more flexible 
          than his, but requires more TikZ knowledge of the user.

\section[\texttt{bookhands} -- A collection of book-hand fonts]{\texttt{bookhands} -- A collection of book-hand fonts}\label{pkg:bookhands}
\index{Package!bookhands}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/bookhands}
\item[name] \texttt{bookhands}
\item[caption] A collection of book-hand fonts
\item[author] Wilson, Peter R.
\index{Author!Wilson, Peter R.}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) This is a set of book-hand (Metafont) fonts and packages covering manuscript scripts from the 1st century 
          until Gutenberg and Caxton. The included hands are:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/sqrcaps}{Square Capitals (1st century onwards)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/rustic}{Roman Rustic (1st–6th centuries)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/inslrmin}{Insular Minuscule (6th cenury onwards)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/carolmin}{Carolingian Minuscule (8th–12th centuries)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/egothic}{Early Gothic (11th–12th centuries)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tgothic}{Gothic Textura Quadrata (13th–15th centuries)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgothic}{Gothic Textura Prescisus vel sine pedibus (13th century onwards)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/rotunda}{Rotunda (13–15th centuries)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/humanist}{Humanist Minuscule (14th century onwards)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/uncial}{Uncial (3rd–6th centuries)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/huncial}{Half Uncial (3rd–9th centuries)} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/auncial}{Artificial Uncial (6th–10th centuries)} ; and
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/inslrmaj}{Insular Majuscule (6th–9th centuries)} .
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/bookhands/README.PRW}

\section[\texttt{booktabstabular} -- Automatic application of the booktabs style]{\texttt{booktabstabular} -- Automatic application of the booktabs style}\label{pkg:booktabstabular}
\index{Package!booktabstabular}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/booktabstabular}
\item[name] \texttt{booktabstabular}
\item[caption] Automatic application of the booktabs style
\item[author] Schäfer, Moritz R.
\index{Author!Schäfer, Moritz R.}
\item[copyright] Moritz R. Schäfer (2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The booktabstabular package provides wrapper environments around  \texttt{tabular} and \texttt{tabular*} that 
          insert \texttt{{\textbackslash}toprule} at the beginning, \texttt{{\textbackslash}bottomrule} at 
          the end, and locally remap the legacy \texttt{{\textbackslash}hline} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}cline} commands 
          to their booktabs equivalents \texttt{{\textbackslash}midrule} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}cmidrule} . 
          It also provides commands to temporarily override the standard tabular and tabular* environments so that 
          existing documents can opt into this behaviour without rewriting each table.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/booktabstabular/README}
