\item[caption] Convert graphs generated by Graphviz to LaTeX friendly formats
\item[author] Fauske, Kjell Magne
\index{Author!Fauske, Kjell Magne}
\item[copyright] Kjell Magne Fauske (2006-2007)
\item[license] other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
\index{License!other-free}
\index{License!Free license not otherwise listed}
\item[version] 2.7.0
\item[description] (no language specified) Dot2tex is a tool for converting graphs rendered by Graphviz to formats that can be used with LaTeX.

          The purpose of dot2tex is to give graphs generated by Graphviz a more LaTeX friendly look and feel. This 
          is accomplished by converting xdot output from Graphviz to a series of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ 
          and PGF} , or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base}{PSTricks} commands. This 
          approach allows:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Typesetting labels with LaTeX, allowing mathematical notation;
          \item Using native PSTricks and PGF/TikZ commands for drawing arrows; and
          \item Using backend specific styles to customize the output.
          \end{itemize}
Dot2tex requires a Python interpreter v2.4 or better.

\section[\texttt{dozenal} -- Typeset documents using base twelve numbering (also called “\ldots]{\texttt{dozenal} -- Typeset documents using base twelve numbering (also called “dozenal”)}\label{pkg:dozenal}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/dozenal}
\item[name] \texttt{dozenal}
\item[caption] Typeset documents using base twelve numbering (also called “dozenal”)
\item[author] Goodman, Donald P.
\index{Author!Goodman, Donald P.}
\item[copyright] Donald P. Goodman (2008-2018)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 7.2 (2018-05-11)
\item[last changes] 2018-05-11
\item[year] 2018
\index{Year!2018}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package supports typesetting documents whose counters are represented in base twelve, also called 
          ''dozenal''. It includes a macro by David Kastrup for converting positive whole numbers to dozenal from 
          decimal (base ten) representation. The package also includes a few other macros and redefines all the 
          standard counters to produce dozenal output.

          Fonts, in Roman, italic, slanted, and boldface versions, provide ten and eleven (the Pitman characters 
          preferred by the Dozenal Society of Great Britain). The fonts were designed to blend well with the Computer 
          Modern fonts, and are available both as Metafont source and in Adobe Type 1 format.

\item[description] (no language specified) Das Puzzle Spiel is a LaTeX package (dps) for creating a puzzle, a message actually, and a series of 
          questions and answers. The document consumer matches the questions with the answers. With each match, 
          another letter appears in the puzzle. Upon completion of all questions, the message hidden in the puzzle 
          is revealed. The puzzle is primarily designed for the screen, but you can optionally create the game 
          for paper.

          The package itself is distributed as a zip file embedded in the package documentation.

          the macro \texttt{{\textbackslash}protect} s the active character when it appears in 
          a moving argument.

          defined with \texttt{{\textbackslash}DeclareRobustActChar} , in the same way that \texttt{{\textbackslash}renewcommand} works 
          for ordinary commands.

          or on the first page of a document. Typical usage may consist in writing words such as DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL 
          across document pages.

          The package performs a similar function to that of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/draftcopy}{draftcopy} , 
          but its implementation is output device independent.

          As of December 2020, the package relies on the new shipout hooks directly provided by LaTeX. For users 
          of older versions of LaTeX, the package also provides a legacy version of itself (that is automatically 
          loaded, currently being at release 2.3) which relies on the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/everypage}{everypage} package. 
          Note that this legacy version will progressively lag behind in terms of features.

\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides access to the DRM (Don's Revised Modern) family of fonts, which includes a variety 
          of optical sizes in Roman (in four weights), italic, and small caps, among other shapes, along with a 
          set of symbols and ornaments. It is intended to be a full-body text font, but its larger sizes can also 
          be used for simple display purposes, and its significant body of symbols can stand on its own. It comes 
          complete with textual (''old-style'') and lining figures, and even has small-caps figures. It also comes 
          with extensible decorative rules to be used with ornaments from itself or other fonts, along with an 
          extremely flexible ellipsis package.

\section[\texttt{droid} -- LaTeX support for the Droid font families]{\texttt{droid} -- LaTeX support for the Droid font families}\label{pkg:droid}
\index{Package!droid}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/droid}
\item[name] \texttt{droid}
\item[caption] LaTeX support for the Droid font families
\item[author] El Morabity, Mohamed
\index{Author!El Morabity, Mohamed}
\item[author] Matteson, Steve
\index{Author!Matteson, Steve}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[license] apache2 = Apache License, version 2.0 (free)
\index{License!apache2}
\index{License!Apache License, version 2.0}
\item[version] 3.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The Droid typeface family was designed in the fall of 2006 by Steve Matteson, as a commission from Google 
          to create a set of system fonts for its Android platform. The goal was to provide optimal quality and 
          comfort on a mobile handset when rendered in application menus, web browsers and for other screen text. 
          The Droid family consists of Droid Serif, Droid Sans and Droid Sans Mono fonts, licensed under the Apache 
          License Version 2.0.

          The bundle includes the fonts in both TrueType and Adobe Type 1 formats.

          that are usually employed in digital signal processing publications.

          DSPTricks provides facilities for standard discrete-time ''lollipop'' plots, continuous-time and frequency 
          plots, and pole-zero plots. \\The companion package DSPFunctions ( \texttt{dspfunctions.sty} )

          supports DSP block diagrams.

\section[\texttt{dtxdescribe} -- Describe additional object types in dtx source files]{\texttt{dtxdescribe} -- Describe additional object types in dtx source files}\label{pkg:dtxdescribe}
\index{Package!dtxdescribe}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/dtxdescribe}
\item[name] \texttt{dtxdescribe}
\item[caption] Describe additional object types in dtx source files
\item[author] Dunn, Brian
\index{Author!Dunn, Brian}
\item[copyright] Brian Dunn (2016-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.09 (2024-01-20)
\item[last changes] 2024-01-20
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/doc}{doc} package includes tools for describing macros 
          and environments in LaTeX source .dtx format. The dtxdescribe package adds additional tools for describing 
          booleans, lengths, counters, hooks, sockets, plug, keys, packages, classes, options, files, commands, 
          arguments, and other objects, and also works with the standard document classes as well, for those who 
          do not wish to use the .dtx format.

          Each item is given a margin tag similar to  \texttt{{\textbackslash}DescribeEnv} , 
          and is listed in the index by itself and also by category. Each item may be sorted further by an optional 
          class. All index entries except code lines are hyperlinked.

          The dtxexample environment is provided for typesetting example code and its results. Contents are displayed 
          verbatim along with a caption and cross-referencing. They are then input and executed, and the result 
          is shown.

          Environments are also provided for displaying verbatim or formatted source code, user-interface displays, 
          and sidebars with titles.

          Macros are provided for formatting the names of inline LaTeX objects such as packages and booleans, as 
          well as program and file names, file types, internet objects, the names of certain programs, a number 
          of logos, and inline dashes and slashes.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/dtxdescribe/README.txt}

\index{Package!duckuments}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/duckuments}
\item[name] \texttt{duckuments}
\item[caption] Create duckified dummy content
\item[author] Spratte, Jonathan P.
\index{Author!Spratte, Jonathan P.}
\item[copyright] Jonathan P. Spratte (2018-2019)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.5 (2019-10-03)
\item[last changes] 2019-10-03
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides facilities to create duckified dummy contents. It was inspired by the question '' \href{https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/419751/}{Getting 
          ducks in example images} '' on TeX-LaTeX Stack Exchange.

          The following macros are available:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}duckument[key=val]} - print a short duckument
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}blindduck[key=val]} - print a paragraph
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ducklist(*){\textbraceleft}environment{\textbraceright}} - create a list of type \texttt{environment} 
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ducklistlist(*){\textbraceleft}environment{\textbraceright}} - create nested lists
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}duckitemize} - \texttt{ducklist{\textbraceleft}itemize{\textbraceright}} 
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}duckenumerate} - \texttt{ducklist{\textbraceleft}enumerate{\textbraceright}} 
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}duckdescription} - \texttt{ducklist{\textbraceleft}description{\textbraceright}} 
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}duckumentsCreateExampleFile} 
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}duckumentsDrawRandomDucks} 
          \end{itemize}
The package works with pdfTeX, LuaTeX, and XeTeX.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/duckuments/README.md}

\section[\texttt{dvdcoll} -- A class for typesetting DVD archives]{\texttt{dvdcoll} -- A class for typesetting DVD archives}\label{pkg:dvdcoll}
\index{Package!dvdcoll}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvdcoll}
\item[name] \texttt{dvdcoll}
\item[caption] A class for typesetting DVD archives
\item[author] Kleber, Josef
\index{Author!Kleber, Josef}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.1a
\item[description] (no language specified) Having lost the overview of my DVD archives, I simply could not remember if I already recorded the documentary 
          running on TV that day. I chose to recreate the index using LaTeX: the design aim was a hyperlinked and 
          fully searchable PDF-document, listing my DVDs with all titles, lengths and so on. Further requirements 
          were support for seasons of tv series and a list with all faulty or missing programs for rerecording. 
          The dvdcoll class supports all these requirements.

          dvdcoll.cls follows the structure <number><title><length>. As a result, the class is not limited to DVDs—you 
          can of course typeset archives of CD-ROMs, Audio-CDs and so on.

          Supported languages at the moment: English, French, German, Italian, Polish, Portuguese, Spanish. Some 
          help is needed for other languages!
\item[documentation]  (English) \textit{Class documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/dvdcoll/doc/dvdcoll.pdf}

\item[author] Tobin, Geoffrey
\index{Author!Tobin, Geoffrey}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[version] 3.51
\item[description] (no language specified) Dvgt is a development of DVItoVDU, a very early previewer.

          Dvgt has Terse, Box and Full preview modes. Terse mode uses the text mode of the VDU, and is insensitive 
          to zoom. Box mode shows the bounding boxes of characters. Full mode gives a graphically rendered preview. 
          On non-graphic terminals at low screen magnifications, Terse mode is the most useful, but as one zooms 
          in, Box and Full modes become more and more accurate.

\section[\texttt{dvi2bitmap} -- Utility to convert TeX DVI files directly to bitmaps]{\texttt{dvi2bitmap} -- Utility to convert TeX DVI files directly to bitmaps}\label{pkg:dvi2bitmap}
\index{Package!dvi2bitmap}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvi2bitmap}
\item[name] \texttt{dvi2bitmap}
\item[caption] Utility to convert TeX DVI files directly to bitmaps
\item[author] Gray, Norman
\index{Author!Gray, Norman}
\item[license] gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
\index{License!gpl2}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 2}
\item[version] 1.0 (2015-01-12)
\item[last changes] 2015-01-12
\item[year] 2015
\index{Year!2015}
\item[description] (no language specified) A utility to convert TeX DVI files directly to bitmaps, without going through the complicated (and slow!) 
          route of conversion via PostScript and PNM. The prime motivation for this is to prepare mathematical 
          equations for inclusion in HTML files but there are many other uses beyond that. It can generate XBM 
          and GIF bitmaps, plus PNG, if you have the libpng library installed. It uses the same kpathsea font-searching 
          library as other TeX programs, again as long as you have the appropriate library installed. The program 
          is written in C++, and incidentally provides a good object interface for DVI and PK files.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/dviware/dvi2bitmap/README}

          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dviconcat}{dviconcat} , for concatenating pages of DVI file(s);

\section[\texttt{dvii} -- Extract information from a DVI file]{\texttt{dvii} -- Extract information from a DVI file}\label{pkg:dvii}
\index{Package!dvii}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvii}
\item[name] \texttt{dvii}
\item[caption] Extract information from a DVI file
\item[author] Lewenberg, Adam
\index{Author!Lewenberg, Adam}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.44
\item[description] (no language specified) A utility written in C that extracts information from a DVI file. Information displayed can include a 
          summary of the file comment (usually the date the file was compiled), file size, the number of (physical) 
          pages, and the number of fonts. More detailed information may also include font names for all fonts used, 
          lists of the fonts which appear on each page, a list of physical page number/TeX page number pairs, and 
          a list of all  \texttt{{\textbackslash}special} s and the pages on which they appear.

          To compile, you need a C compiler along with the standard C libraries but precompiled executables are 
          available for DOS, Win 9X/NT, Solaris, OSF/1, and Linux.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/dviware/dvii/README}

          to support multi-byte character encodings and large character sets for East Asian languages. Dvipdfmx, 
          if ''called'' with the name dvipdfm, operates in a ''dvipdfm compatibility'' mode, so that users of the 
          both packages need only keep one executable.

          A secondary design goal is to support as many ''PDF'' features as does  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex}{pdfTeX} .

          The current version of the package is no longer maintained on CTAN as a separate entity; development 
          now takes place within the TeX Live framework, and it is no longer available as a separate package. For 
          download, support, and other information, please see  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/texlive}{TeX 
          Live} . However, the information on this page is maintained and should be current.

\section[\texttt{dvipng} -- A fast DVI to PNG/GIF converter]{\texttt{dvipng} -- A fast DVI to PNG/GIF converter}\label{pkg:dvipng}
\index{Package!dvipng}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipng}
\item[name] \texttt{dvipng}
\item[caption] A fast DVI to PNG/GIF converter
\item[author] Larsson, Jan-Åke
\index{Author!Larsson, Jan-Åke}
\item[copyright] Jan-Åke Larsson (2002-2020)
\item[license] lgpl3 = GNU Lesser General Public License 3 (free)
\index{License!lgpl3}
\index{License!GNU Lesser General Public License 3}
\item[version] 1.18 (2025-02-02)
\item[last changes] 2025-02-02
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This program makes PNG and/or GIF graphics from DVI files as obtained from TeX and its relatives. Its 
          benefits include:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Speed. It offers very fast rendering of DVI as bitmap files, which makes it suitable for generating large amounts of images on-the-fly, as needed in  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/preview-latex}{preview-latex} , WeBWorK and others;
          \item It does not read the postamble, so it can be started before TeX finishes. There is a  \texttt{--follow} switch that makes dvipng wait at end-of-file for further output, unless it finds the POST marker that indicates the end of the DVI;
          \item Interactive query of options. dvipng can read options interactively through stdin, and all options are usable. It is even possible to change the input file through this interface.
          \item Support for PK, VF, PostScript Type1, and TrueType fonts, colour specials, and inclusion of PostScript, PNG, JPEG or GIF images.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package README}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/dviware/dvipng/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/systems/doc/dvipng/dvipng.pdf}

          are commonly referred to the sources of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvitype}{dvitype} , 
          but that doesn't actually specify anything (merely tells you how the utility works).

          should do. The present ''level 0'' is as far as the effort got.

\section[\texttt{dvisvgm} -- Convert DVI, EPS, and PDF files to Scalable Vector Graphics \ldots]{\texttt{dvisvgm} -- Convert DVI, EPS, and PDF files to Scalable Vector Graphics format (SVG)}\label{pkg:dvisvgm}
\index{Package!dvisvgm}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvisvgm}
\item[name] \texttt{dvisvgm}
\item[caption] Convert DVI, EPS, and PDF files to Scalable Vector Graphics format (SVG)
\item[author] Gieseking, Martin
\index{Author!Gieseking, Martin}
\item[copyright] Martin Gieseking (2005-2025)
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[version] 3.6
\item[description] (no language specified) Dvisvgm is a command line utility that converts TeX DVI as well as EPS and PDF files to the XML-based 
          Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) format. It provides full font support including virtual fonts, font maps, 
          and sub-fonts. If necessary, dvisvgm vectorizes Metafont’s bitmap output in order to always create lossless 
          scalable output. The embedded SVG fonts can optionally be replaced with graphics paths so that applications 
          that do not support SVG fonts are enabled to render the graphics properly. Besides many other features, 
          dvisvgm also supports color, emTeX, tpic, papersize, PDF mapfile and PostScript specials. Users will 
          need a working TeX installation including the kpathsea library.

          For more detailed information, see the  \href{https://dvisvgm.de}{project page} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Manual page}: \url{https://dvisvgm.de/Manpage}

\section[\texttt{dviwin} -- MS-Windows DVI screen and printer driver]{\texttt{dviwin} -- MS-Windows DVI screen and printer driver}\label{pkg:dviwin}
\index{Package!dviwin}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/dviwin}
\item[name] \texttt{dviwin}
\item[caption] MS-Windows DVI screen and printer driver
\item[author] Sendoukas, Hippocrates
\index{Author!Sendoukas, Hippocrates}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[version] 2.9
\item[description] (no language specified) A screen and printer driver for TeX DVI files under 32-bit Windows. Its main features are: Fast previewing 
          (uses 386-specific code if it finds a 386/486); Painless support for graphics in TeX documents; Uses 
          any standard PK font files or FLI font libraries; Works with all displays and printers supported by Windows; 
          Automatic generation of missing fonts; Support for color printers; Native 32-bit versions for Windows 
          NT; Selectable measurement units; User-definable strings for easy adaptation to various languages (the 
          distribution contains strings for four different languages apart from English); graphics filters for 
          GIF and XPM files, etc. The required memory depends on the resolution that you use. It needs about 1.5M 
          free RAM to print on a 300dpi printer without swapping.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/dviware/dviwin/README}

\section[\texttt{dynamicnumber} -- Dynamically typeset numbers and values in LaTeX through “sym\ldots]{\texttt{dynamicnumber} -- Dynamically typeset numbers and values in LaTeX through “symbolic links”}\label{pkg:dynamicnumber}
\index{Package!dynamicnumber}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/dynamicnumber}
\item[name] \texttt{dynamicnumber}
\item[caption] Dynamically typeset numbers and values in LaTeX through “symbolic links”
\item[author] Pieters, Olivier
\index{Author!Pieters, Olivier}
\item[copyright] Olivier Pieters (2015)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version] 0.1.3
\item[description] (no language specified) This package dynamically typesets values generated by different kinds of scripts in LaTeX through the 
          use of ''symbolic links'' (which are not in any way related to the ''symbolic links'' used in UNIX systems!). 
          The aim is to reduce errors resulting from out-of-date numbers by directly setting them in the number 
          generating file and importing a ''symbolic link'' into the LaTeX source file.

          It can be used to import not only numerical values, but strings and pieces of code are also possible.

          Currently only MATLAB and Python are supported to produce Dynamic Number list files.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/dynamicnumber/dynamicnumber.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) EasyDTX is a variant of the DTX format which eliminates the need for all those pesky ''macrocode'' environments. 
          Any line introduced by a single comment counts as documentation, and documentation lines may be indented.

          An  \texttt{.edtx} file is converted to a \texttt{.dtx} by a little Perl script 
          called \texttt{edtx2dtx} . There is also a rudimentary Emacs mode, implemented in \texttt{easydoctex-mode.el} , 
          which takes care of fontification, indentation, and forward and inverse search.

\section[\texttt{easyfig} -- Simplifying the use of common figures]{\texttt{easyfig} -- Simplifying the use of common figures}\label{pkg:easyfig}
\index{Package!easyfig}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/easyfig}
\item[name] \texttt{easyfig}
\item[caption] Simplifying the use of common figures
\item[author] Scharrer, Martin
\index{Author!Scharrer, Martin}
\item[copyright] Martin Scharrer (2011-2018)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.2a (2018-03-30)
\item[last changes] 2018-03-30
\item[year] 2018
\index{Year!2018}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}Figure[<key=value>...]{\textbraceleft}<image 
          filename>{\textbraceright}} to simplify the business of including an image as figure in the 
          most common form (centred and with caption and label). Caption and label are set using the \texttt{caption} and \texttt{label} keys; 
          the label \texttt{fig:<image filename>} is used if none is given.

          If the  \texttt{here} key is given, the figure is not ‘floated’, and the user is responsible 
          for placement.

          The package uses the author’s package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/adjustbox}{adjustbox} to 
          centre an image and to simplify further modifications.

          As  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/adjustbox}{adjustbox} now provides keys to turn images 
          or other material into floats or non-floats, including captions, \texttt{easyfig} has become 
          quite redundant.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/easyfig/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/easyfig/easyfig.pdf}

\section[\texttt{ec} -- Computer modern fonts in T1 and TS1 encodings]{\texttt{ec} -- Computer modern fonts in T1 and TS1 encodings}\label{pkg:ec}
\index{Package!ec}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/ec}
\item[name] \texttt{ec}
\item[caption] Computer modern fonts in T1 and TS1 encodings
\item[author] Schwarz, Norbert
\index{Author!Schwarz, Norbert}
\item[author] Knappen, Jörg
\index{Author!Knappen, Jörg}
\item[license] other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
\index{License!other-free}
\index{License!Free license not otherwise listed}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The EC fonts are European Computer Modern Fonts, supporting the complete LaTeX T1 encoding defined at 
          the 1990 TUG conference hold at Cork/Ireland. These fonts are intended to be stable with no changes being 
          made to the tfm files. The set also contains a Text Companion Symbol font, called tc, featuring many 
          useful characters needed in text typesetting, for example oldstyle digits, currency symbols (including 
          the newly created Euro symbol), the permille sign, copyright, trade mark and servicemark as well as a 
          copyleft sign, and many others. Recent releases of LaTeX2e support the EC fonts. The EC fonts supersede 
          the preliminary version released as the DC fonts.

          The fonts are available in (traced) Adobe Type 1 format, as part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cm-super}{cm-super} bundle. 
          The other Computer Modern-style T1-encoded Type 1 set, \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/lm}{Latin 
          Modern} , is not actually a direct development of the EC set, and differs from the EC in a number 
          of particulars.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/ec/src/00readme.txt}

\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) Econometrics is a package that defines some commands that simplify mathematic notation in economic and 
          econometrics writing. The commands are related to the notation of

          \begin{itemize}
          \item vectors, matrices, sets, calligraphic and roman letters
          \item statistical distributions
          \item constants and symbols
          \item matrix operators and statistical operators.
          \end{itemize}
The package is based on "Notation in Econometrics: a proposal for a standard" by Karim Abadir and Jan 
          R. Magnus, The Econometrics Journal (2002), 5, 76-90.

\section[\texttt{eczar} -- A font family supporting Devanagari and Latin script]{\texttt{eczar} -- A font family supporting Devanagari and Latin script}\label{pkg:eczar}
\index{Package!eczar}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/eczar}
\item[name] \texttt{eczar}
\item[caption] A font family supporting Devanagari and Latin script
\item[author] निरंजन
\index{Author!निरंजन}
\item[license] ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
\index{License!ofl}
\index{License!The SIL Open Font License}
\item[version] 0.1
\item[description] (no language specified) रोझेटा संस्थेचा एग्झार हा युनिकोड आधारित मुक्त टंक आहे. ह्या टंकात ४५+३ भाषा लॅटिन व देवनागरी लिपीत पुरस्कृत 
          केल्या जातात. वैभव सिंह ह्यांनी ह्या टंकाचा अभिकल्प केला आहे व आज्ञावली तसेच निर्मिती डेव्हिड ब्रेझीना 
          ह्यांनी केली आहे.

          एग्ज़ार यह रोज़ेटा द्वारा प्रकाशित युनिकोड आधारित मुक्त टंक है। इस टंक द्वारा ४५+३ भाषाएँ लैटिन तथा देवनागरी 
          लिपि में पुरस्कृत की जाती है। वैभव सिंह ने इस का अभिकल्प किया है और आज्ञावलि तथा निर्मिति डेविड ब्रेज़ीना 
          द्वारा की गयी है।

          Eczar is an open-source type family published by Rosetta. The fonts support over 45+3 languages in Latin 
          and Devanagari scripts in 5 weights. These fonts were designed by Vaibhav Singh, code and production 
          are by David Březina.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/eczar/README.txt}

\section[\texttt{edmargin} -- Multiple series of endnotes for critical editions]{\texttt{edmargin} -- Multiple series of endnotes for critical editions}\label{pkg:edmargin}
\index{Package!edmargin}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[name] \texttt{edmargin}
\item[caption] Multiple series of endnotes for critical editions
\item[author] Burt, John
\index{Author!Burt, John}
\item[copyright] John Burt (2008)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) Edmargin provides a very simple scheme for endnote sections for critical editions. Endnotes can either 
          be marked in the text, or with marginal references to the page in the note sections where the note is 
          to be found. Notes can be set in individual paragraphs, or in block paragraph mode (where there are many 
          short notes). Note sections will have running headers of the form ''Textual notes to pp. xx--yy''. New 
          note sections can be created on the fly. There are predefined endnote sections for textual notes, emendations, 
          and explanatory notes.

\index{Package!edmaths}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/edmaths}
\item[name] \texttt{edmaths}
\item[caption] A report and thesis class file for the University of Edinburgh (UoE)
\item[author] Fogg, Josh
\index{Author!Fogg, Josh}
\item[copyright] Josh Fogg (2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.99
\item[description] (no language specified) A report and thesis class file for  \href{https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/}{The School of Mathematics, 
          Scotland} at the \href{https://www.ed.ac.uk/}{University of Edinburgh (UoE)} . When 
          working on a report or thesis, an easy way to implement the \href{https://www.ed.ac.uk/academic-services/students/thesis-submission}{University's 
          typesetting rules} in LaTeX is provided by \href{https://github.com/Foggalong/edinburgh-math-latex/blob/master/edmaths.sty}{edmaths.sty} . 
          It sets the page margins as required and defines commands to create the correct cover page and standard 
          declaration. A compiled version of the included example can be \href{https://foggalong.github.io/edinburgh-math-latex/example-report.pdf}{found 
          here} .

          It also loads the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsthm}{amsthm} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amscd}{amscd} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts}{amssymb} packages, which are required by almost 
          all mathematical publications. Through \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/setspace}{setspace} line 
          spacing settings are available that only affect the body text and not footnotes and captions. Additional 
          in-built options can be found in more detail in the project's documentation.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/edmaths/README.md}

\section[\texttt{eemeir} -- Adjust the gender of words in a document]{\texttt{eemeir} -- Adjust the gender of words in a document}\label{pkg:eemeir}
\index{Package!eemeir}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/eemeir}
\item[name] \texttt{eemeir}
\item[caption] Adjust the gender of words in a document
\item[author] Hansen, Mogens Lemvig
\index{Author!Hansen, Mogens Lemvig}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.1b
\item[description] (no language specified) Defines macros for third-person singular pronouns ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}E} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}Em} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}Eir} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}Eirs} ), 
          which expand differently according to a masculine/feminine switch. (If the switch is ‘masculine’, they 
          would expand to ‘he’, ‘him’, ‘his’ and ‘his’; if ‘feminine’, they would expand to ‘she’, ‘her’, ‘her’ 
          and ‘hers’. Apart from the pronouns, one can define ‘word pairs’, such as mother/father, daughter/son, 
          and so on.

          Gender may be defined once per document, as an environment, or may be flipped on the fly.
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/eemeir}
\item[on Mik\TeX] \texttt{eemeir}

          Developed with AI assistance, it offers multiple stone colors with full RGB customization, automatic 
          numbering systems with alternating colors, geometric transformations (rotations, mirrors), flexible board 
          display options with enhanced 2pt borders for publication quality, symbol placement, and full LuaLaTeX 
          compatibility. The package supports seven stone colors, border display, extended size presets with validation, 
          and advanced features for game analysis and problem presentation.

          and depends on \texttt{minimalist.sty} from the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/minimalist}{minimalist} package.

          The package name ''einfart'' is taken from the German word ''einfach'' (''simple''), combined with the 
          first three letters of ''Artikel'' (''article'').

\section[\texttt{eitl} -- Easy install of TeX Live]{\texttt{eitl} -- Easy install of TeX Live}\label{pkg:eitl}
\index{Package!eitl}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/eitl}
\item[name] \texttt{eitl}
\item[caption] Easy install of TeX Live
\item[author] Voß, Herbert
\index{Author!Voß, Herbert}
\item[author] Niepraschk, Rolf
\index{Author!Niepraschk, Rolf}
\item[copyright] Rolf Niepraschk, Herbert Voß (2012)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.04
\item[description] (no language specified) The script allows the easy install of a current TeX Live version over the net. It is tested with the 
          current Linux versions of OpenSUSE and Ubuntu. The script:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item looks for a fast server
          \item downloads the install script
          \item deletes an existing TeX Live version from Ubuntu (deb) or openSUSE (rpm)
          \item extracts and runs the install script
          \item installs a complete up-to-date TeX Live from  \texttt{tug.org} 
          \item installs the non free fonts from  \texttt{tug.org} which are not part of TeX Live, like arial, Luxi mono, etc.
          \item installs the GUIs TeXmaker and TeXworks
          \item creates files  \texttt{zzz-texlive.sh/csh} for \texttt{/etc/profile.d/} 
          \end{itemize}
If no directory is specified, TeX Live will be installed in the home directory  \texttt{{\textasciitilde}/texlive} . 
          For another directory, run the script with the directory name; e.g.:

          \texttt{./eitl.sh /usr/local/texlive} 

          for some actions the script needs to be root. In such cases it asks for the root password.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/texlive/eitl/README}

\section[\texttt{ekdosis} -- Typesetting TEI-xml compliant Critical Editions]{\texttt{ekdosis} -- Typesetting TEI-xml compliant Critical Editions}\label{pkg:ekdosis}
\index{Package!ekdosis}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/ekdosis}
\item[name] \texttt{ekdosis}
\item[caption] Typesetting TEI-xml compliant Critical Editions
\item[author] Alessi, Robert
\index{Author!Alessi, Robert}
\item[copyright] Robert Alessi (2020-2021)
\item[license] fdl = Free Documentation License (free)
\index{License!fdl}
\index{License!Free Documentation License}
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[version] 1.4 (2021-11-21)
\item[last changes] 2021-11-21
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) \texttt{ekdosis} is a LuaLaTeX package designed for multilingual critical editions. It can 
          be used to typeset texts and different layers of critical notes in any direction accepted by LuaTeX. 
          Texts can be arranged in running paragraphs or on facing pages, in any number of columns which in turn 
          can be synchronized or not. In addition to printed texts, ekdosis can convert \texttt{.tex} source 
          files so as to produce TEI xml-compliant critical editions. Database-driven encoding under LaTeX then 
          allows extraction of texts entered segment by segment according to various criteria: main edited text, 
          variant readings, translations or annotated borrowings between texts.

\index{Year!2017}
\item[description] (no language specified) A package for typesetting scholarly critical editions, replacing the established  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ledmac}{ledmac} package. 
          Ledmac itself was a LaTeX port of the plain TeX \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/edmac}{EDMAC} macros.

          The package supports indexing by page and by line numbers, and simple tabular- and array-style environments.

          The package is distributed with the related  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/eledpar}{eledpar} package. 
          The package is now superseded by \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/reledmac}{reledmac} .

\section[\texttt{elteiktdk} -- TDK-thesis template for Hungarian TDK conferences, Section o\ldots]{\texttt{elteiktdk} -- TDK-thesis template for Hungarian TDK conferences, Section of Computer Science}\label{pkg:elteiktdk}
\index{Package!elteiktdk}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/elteiktdk}
\item[name] \texttt{elteiktdk}
\item[caption] TDK-thesis template for Hungarian TDK conferences, Section of Computer Science
\item[author] Cserép, Máté
\index{Author!Cserép, Máté}
\item[copyright] Máté Cserép (2013-2024)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version] 2.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The National Conference of Scientific Students Associations (OTDK) of Hungary is the most significant 
          scientific event for Bachelor and Master students in the country, where students compete with their research 
          papers in all field of science. It is organized in every 2 years. The conference/competition has 2 rounds: 
          a university level and a country level (for the best papers).

          This class template enforces the required formatting rules for TDK theses and generates the cover and 
          title page given on the provided metadata. The formatting rules are defined to meet the requirements 
          for TDK theses submitted at the Eötvös Loránd University, Faculty of Informatics (Budapest, Hungary). 
          This also fits the formatting requirements of the Computer Science Section of the country level round. 
          With sufficient modifications the template could be usable for TDK theses at other national and faculty 
          level sections, too.

          The template supports producing both Hungarian and English theses.

\section[\texttt{emarks} -- Named mark registers with e-TeX]{\texttt{emarks} -- Named mark registers with e-TeX}\label{pkg:emarks}
\index{Package!emarks}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/emarks}
\item[name] \texttt{emarks}
\item[caption] Named mark registers with e-TeX
\item[author] Chervet, Florent
\index{Author!Chervet, Florent}
\item[copyright] Florent Chervet (2011)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etex}{E-TeX} provides 32 768 mark registers; using this facility 
          is far more comfortable than LaTeX tricks with \texttt{{\textbackslash}markright} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}markboth} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}leftmark} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}rightmark} .

          The package provides two commands for marking:  \texttt{{\textbackslash}marksthe} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}marksthecs} , 
          which have \texttt{*} forms which disable expansion; new mark registers are allocated as 
          needed. Syntax is closely modelled on the \texttt{{\textbackslash}marks} primitive.

          Four commands are provided for retrieving the marks registers’ content:  \texttt{{\textbackslash}thefirstmarks} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}thebotmarks} , \texttt{thetopmarks} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}getthemarks} ; 
          and the command \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifmarksequal} is available for comparing the 
          content of marks registers.

          The package requires an e-TeX-enabled engine, and the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etex}{etex} package.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/emarks/README}

          command for including color emoji such as 🏝 ({\textbackslash}emo{\textbraceleft}desert-island{\textbraceright}) 
          or 🦜 ({\textbackslash}emo{\textbraceleft}parrot{\textbraceright}) in your documents 
          independent of input encoding or LaTeX engine. The implementation uses the Noto color emoji font if the 
          engine supports it and includes PDF graphics otherwise. The latter are automatically derived from Noto’s 
          SVG sources, so the visual appearance is very similar.

          Emo may come in particularly handy when dealing with academic publishers that provide only minimal support 
          for non-Latin scripts.

\section[\texttt{emp} -- "Encapsulate" MetaPost figures in a document]{\texttt{emp} -- "Encapsulate" MetaPost figures in a document}\label{pkg:emp}
\index{Package!emp}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/emp}
\item[name] \texttt{emp}
\item[caption] "Encapsulate" MetaPost figures in a document
\item[author] Ohl, Thorsten
\index{Author!Ohl, Thorsten}
\item[copyright] Thorsten Ohl (1997)
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) Emp is a package for encapsulating  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/metapost}{MetaPost} figures 
          in LaTeX: the package provides environments where you can place MetaPost commands, and means of using 
          that code as fragments for building up figures to include in your document. So, with emp, the procedure 
          is to run your document with LaTeX, run MetaPost, and then complete running your document in the normal 
          way.

          Emp is therefore useful for keeping illustrations in synchrony with the text. It also frees you from 
          inventing descriptive names for PostScript files that fit into the confines of file system conventions.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/emp/README}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mathtools}{mathtools} bundle. 
          it provides a visual markup extension to \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} . 
          The user-friendly interface allows the user to put a set of equations inside a box thus enhancing the \texttt{{\textbackslash}boxed} feature 
          of amsmath. As a side effect it is also possible to add material on both sides of the equations thus 
          providing (and surpassing) the functionality of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cases}{cases} package. 
          Users of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ntheorem}{ntheorem} will probably want to have a 
          look at it as well, since the problem with end-of-theorem marks in \texttt{gather} and other 
          environments can be circumvented using \texttt{empheq} .

\item[description] (no language specified) The package supports the creation of hypertext links in support of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/endnotes}{endnotes} package. The package modifies the syntax of the \texttt{{\textbackslash}endnote} command:
          \begin{verbatim}
 \endnote*[<num>]{<text>}\label{<name>}.
          \end{verbatim}
When the \texttt{*} -option is used, no endnote mark is created, but the endnote itself is written. The \texttt{{\textbackslash}label} command appears at the end of the \texttt{{\textbackslash}endnote} and its arguments, rather than within the argument of the \verb|<text>| argument.

\index{License!lppl1.3}

\item[version] 1.8
\item[description] (no language specified) The package is a companion for the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem}{enumitem} package; 
          it makes it possible to reference any item in lists formatted by enumitem lists, viz., enumerated, itemize 
          and description lists, and any list defined (or customised) with \texttt{{\textbackslash}newlist} or \texttt{{\textbackslash}setlist} .

          References may be typeset differently with options/properties and even arbitrary text. With  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} , 
          anchors are added for each item to enable hyperlinks within the document or even to external documents.

          Three schemes are provided to make reference names (including the standard  \texttt{{\textbackslash}label} command).

          The package is currently broken, cf.  \href{https://tex.stackexchange.com/q/664886/1090}{https://tex.stackexchange.com/q/664886/1090}

\item[author] Robertson, Will

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}

\item[version] 0.3
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}collect@body} command (as in \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} ), 
          as well as a \texttt{{\textbackslash}long} version \texttt{{\textbackslash}Collect@Body} , 
          for collecting the body text of an environment.

          These commands are used to define a new author interface to creating new environments. For example,  \texttt{{\textbackslash}NewEnviron{\textbraceleft}test{\textbraceright}} , 
          wraps the entire environment body in square brackets, doing the right thing in ignoring leading and trailing 
          spaces.

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 2.5
\item[description] (no language specified) The package offers a group of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} -like environments:

          
          \begin{itemize}
          \item Equation, which is the standard equation environment, with an optional argument for a label name;
          \item Multiline, which is broadly similar to the amsmath multline environment, creating a pleasing layout for equations that run over several lines;
          \item System, for grouping a set of equations together within a left brace, with only one equation number; and
          \item EqSystem, similar to System, except that each equation has its own number.
          \end{itemize}
All the environments have ‘*’ forms, which don't generate equation numbers. The package also works on 
          the standard maths environments.

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bosisio}{bosisio} bundle.

\section[\texttt{eoldef} -- Define commands which absorb the whole source line as argume\ldots]{\texttt{eoldef} -- Define commands which absorb the whole source line as arguments}\label{pkg:eoldef}
\index{Package!eoldef}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/eoldef}
\item[name] \texttt{eoldef}
\item[caption] Define commands which absorb the whole source line as arguments
\item[author] plante
\index{Author!plante}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) This macro allows you to define commands that take the entire source line as arguments.

          Version 1.0\\Copyright (C) 2025 plante\\This file is relased under the LaTeX Project Public License 
          (LPPL) 1.3c.

          Usage:  \verb|\eoldef <control sequence> <parameter text> { <replacement text>}| defines a control sequence that is delimited by the end-of-line in addition to the specified parameter text.

          For instance,  \verb|\eoldef\test#1:#2{}| and

          {\textbackslash}test abc:def

          will give  \verb|#1| = \verb|abc| , \verb|#2| = \verb|def| .

          \verb|\eoldef| is the \verb|\global| variant to \verb|\eoldef| .

          Like  \verb|\verb|...|| , \verb|\eoldef| 'd commands may generally not be used as part of\\another command's argument as it changes catcodes.\\However, if you must use it in environments where catcodes are frozen, you\\may follow the command with a braced argument, eg. \verb|\test{#1:#2}| using the previous example.

          This package may be used in plain TeX or LaTeX by  \verb|\input{eoldef}| .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/eoldef/README.md}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/eoldef}

\item[description] (no language specified) ePiX is a collection of batch-oriented utilities for Unix-like systems. It creates mathematically accurate 
          line figures, plots, and movies using easy-to-learn syntax. LaTeX and dvips comprise the typographical 
          rendering engine, while ImageMagick is used to create bitmapped images and animations. The user interface 
          resembles that of LaTeX itself: you prepare a short scene description in a text editor, then ''compile'' 
          the input file into a picture. Default output formats are eepic (a plain text enhancement to the LaTeX 
          picture environment), eps, pdf, png, and mng.

\section[\texttt{epstopdf} -- Convert EPS to PDF using Ghostscript]{\texttt{epstopdf} -- Convert EPS to PDF using Ghostscript}\label{pkg:epstopdf}
\index{Package!epstopdf}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/epstopdf}
\item[name] \texttt{epstopdf}
\item[caption] Convert EPS to PDF using Ghostscript
\item[author] Oberdiek, Heiko
\index{Author!Oberdiek, Heiko}
\item[author] Wierda, Gerben
\index{Author!Wierda, Gerben}
\item[author] Rahtz, Sebastian
\index{Author!Rahtz, Sebastian}
\item[author] Berry, Karl
\index{Author!Berry, Karl}
\item[author] Esser, Thomas
\index{Author!Esser, Thomas}
\item[copyright] Sebastian Rahtz et al. (1998-2001)
\item[copyright] Karl Berry et al. (2009-2024)
\item[copyright] Gerben Wierda et al. (2002-2009)
\item[license] other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
\index{License!other-free}
\index{License!Free license not otherwise listed}
\item[version] 2.36 (2024-07-11)
\item[last changes] 2024-07-11
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) Epstopdf is a Perl script that converts an EPS file to an ‘encapsulated’ PDF file (a single page file 
          whose media box is the same as the original EPS’s bounding box). The resulting file suitable for inclusion 
          by pdfTeX as an image. The script is adapted to run both on Windows and on Unix-alike systems.

          The script makes use of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ghostscript}{Ghostscript} for the 
          actual conversion to PDF. It assumes Ghostscript version 6.51 or later, and (by default) suppresses its 
          automatic rotation of pages where most of the text is not horizontal.

          LaTeX users may make use of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/epstopdf-pkg}{epstopdf} package, 
          which will run the epstopdf script ''on the fly'', thus giving the illusion that pdfLaTeX is accepting 
          EPS graphic files.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Manual page}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/epstopdf/epstopdf.man1.pdf}

\section[\texttt{eq2db} -- Convert a quiz to one submitted to a server-side script]{\texttt{eq2db} -- Convert a quiz to one submitted to a server-side script}\label{pkg:eq2db}
\index{Package!eq2db}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/eq2db}
\item[name] \texttt{eq2db}
\item[caption] Convert a quiz to one submitted to a server-side script
\item[author] Story, Donald P.
\index{Author!Story, Donald P.}
\item[copyright] D. P. Story (1999-2016)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 2.0 (2016-01-02)
\item[last changes] 2016-01-02
\item[year] 2016
\index{Year!2016}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package permits to convert a self-contained  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/exerquiz}{exerquiz} quiz 
          to one that is submitted to a server-side script.

          \texttt{eq2db} is meant to be used with the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/exerquiz}{exerquiz} package, 
          one of the components of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/acrotex}{AcroTeX eDucation Bundle} . 
          The package redefines the ‘End Quiz’ button of the quiz environment appropriately so that when the user

\item[description] (no language specified) LaTeX users sometimes need to ensure that two or more blocks of text occupy the same amount of horizontal 
          space on the page. To that end, the eqparbox package defines a new command,  \texttt{{\textbackslash}eqparbox} , 
          which works just like \texttt{{\textbackslash}parbox} , except that instead of specifying 
          a width, one specifies a tag. All eqparboxes with the same tag—regardless of where they are in the document—will 
          stretch to fit the widest eqparbox with that tag. This simple, equal-width mechanism can be used for 
          a variety of alignment purposes, as is evidenced by the examples in eqparbox's documentation. Various 
          derivatives of \texttt{{\textbackslash}eqparbox} are also provided.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/eqparbox/eqparbox.pdf}

\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The ESK package allows to encapsulate Sketch files in LaTeX sources.

          This is very useful for keeping illustrations in sync with the text. It also frees the user from inventing 
          descriptive names for new files that fit into the confines of file system conventions. Sketch is a 3D 
          scene description language by Eugene K. Ressler and can generate TikZ and PSTricks code. ESK behaves 
          in a similar fashion to  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/emp}{EMP} (which encapsulates MetaPost 
          files), and was in fact developed from it.

\section[\texttt{esrelation} -- Provides a symbol set for describing relations between order\ldots]{\texttt{esrelation} -- Provides a symbol set for describing relations between ordered pairs}\label{pkg:esrelation}
\index{Package!esrelation}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/esrelation}
\item[name] \texttt{esrelation}
\item[caption] Provides a symbol set for describing relations between ordered pairs
\item[author] Reinfurt, David
\index{Author!Reinfurt, David}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version]  (2015-05-06)
\item[last changes] 2015-05-06
\item[year] 2015
\index{Year!2015}
\item[description] (no language specified) Around 2008, researcher Byron Cook and several colleagues began developing a new set of interrelated 
          algorithms capable of automatically reasoning about the behavior of computer programs and other systems 
          (such as biological systems, circuit designs, etc).

          At the center of these algorithms were new ideas about the relationships between structures expressable 
          as mathematical sets and relations. Using the language of mathematics and logic, the researchers communicated 
          these new results to others in their community via published papers, research talks, etc. Unfortunately, 
          they found the symbols already available for reasoning about relations lacking (in contrast to sets, 
          which have a long-ago developed and robust symbol vocabulary). Early presentations were unnecessarily 
          cluttered.

          To more elegantly express these ideas around relations, Cook recruited artist Tauba Auerbach to help 
          develop a set of symbols. This package provides an math symbol font for describing relations between 
          ordered pairs by using Metafont.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/esrelation/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/esrelation/esrelation.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./7711021434-esrelation.pdf|

\index{Package!e-tex (alias for etex)}
\index{Alias!e-tex (for etex)}
\item[name] \texttt{e-TeX}
\item[caption] An extended version of TeX, from the NTS project
\item[author] The TeX Live Team
\index{Author!The TeX Live Team}
\item[author] Breitenlohner, Peter
\index{Author!Breitenlohner, Peter}
\item[license] knuth = Knuth License (free)
\index{License!knuth}
\index{License!Knuth License}
\item[description] (no language specified) An extended version of TeX (capable of running as if it were unmodified TeX). E-TeX has been specified 
          by the LaTeX team as the base engine for LaTeX2e. Thus, LaTeX programmers may assume e-TeX functionality, 
          along with additional extensions.

          The  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex}{pdftex engine} and others directly incorporate 
          the e-TeX extensions. The \texttt{etex} program in most distributions is an incarnation of \texttt{pdftex} running 
          in DVI mode.

          The development source for e-TeX is the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/texlive-source}{TeX Live 
          source} repository, although further extensions have taken place in the \texttt{pdftex} and 
          other engine sources, keeping e-TeX stable.

\section[\texttt{etextools} -- e-TeX tools for LaTeX users and package writers]{\texttt{etextools} -- e-TeX tools for LaTeX users and package writers}\label{pkg:etextools}
\index{Package!etextools}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/etextools}
\item[name] \texttt{etextools}
\item[caption] e-TeX tools for LaTeX users and package writers
\item[author] Chervet, Florent
\index{Author!Chervet, Florent}
\item[copyright] Florent Chervet (2009)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 3.1415926
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides many (purely expandable) tools for LaTeX:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Extensive list management (csv lists, lists of single tokens/characters, etoolbox lists);
          \item purely expandable loops ( \texttt{csvloop} , \texttt{forcsvloop} , etc.);
          \item conversion ( \texttt{csvtolist} , etc.));
          \item addition/deletion ( \texttt{csvadd} , \texttt{listdel} , etc.);
          \item Expansion and group control:  \texttt{{\textbackslash}expandnext} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}ExpandAfterCmds} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}AfterGroup} …;
          \item Tests on tokens, characters and control sequences ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}iffirstchar} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifiscs} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifdefcount} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}@ifchar} …);
          \item Tests on strings ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifstrnum} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifuppercase} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}DeclareStringFilter} …);
          \item Purely expandable macros with options ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}FE@testopt} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}FE@ifstar} ) or modifiers ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}FE@modifiers} );
          \item Some purely expandable numerics ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}interval} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}locinterplin} ).
          \end{itemize}
The package is dependent on the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etex-pkg}{etex} and the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox}{etoolbox} packages.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/etextools/README}

\section[\texttt{etl} -- Expandable token list operations]{\texttt{etl} -- Expandable token list operations}\label{pkg:etl}
\index{Package!etl}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/etl}
\item[name] \texttt{etl}
\item[caption] Expandable token list operations
\item[author] Spratte, Jonathan P.
\index{Author!Spratte, Jonathan P.}
\item[copyright] Jonathan P. Spratte (2020-2021)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.3 (2021-11-07)
\item[last changes] 2021-11-07
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides expandable token list operations for which  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} ’s \texttt{l3tl} only 
          has unexpandable variants. These expandable versions are typically slower than the unexpandable code. 
          Unlike the \texttt{l3tl} versions, the functions in this module may contain braces and macro 
          parameter tokens in their arguments, but as a drawback they cannot distinguish some tokens and do not 
          consider the character code of group-begin and group-end tokens.

          Additionally a general map to token lists is provided, modelled after the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} internal \texttt{\_\_tl\_act:NNNn} but 
          with additional features.

          The package has no immediate use for document authors; it only contains  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} functions 
          intended for programmers.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/etl/README.md}

\item[description] (no language specified) With  \texttt{etoc} loaded, \texttt{{\textbackslash}tableofcontents} can 
          be used multiple times, and an added command \texttt{{\textbackslash}localtableofcontents} allows 
          to typeset ''local'' tables of contents, i.e. TOCs having their scope limited to the last sectioning 
          command encountered. Since release 1.2, also \texttt{{\textbackslash}locallistoffigures} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}locallistoftables} are 
          available.

          Loading  \texttt{etoc} per itself does not modify the ''contents lines'' inherited from the 
          class default or changed via other packages. But full usage of the package allows spectacular effects 
          such as displaying TOCs as trees or mind maps.

\section[\texttt{euenc} -- Unicode font encoding definitions for XeTeX]{\texttt{euenc} -- Unicode font encoding definitions for XeTeX}\label{pkg:euenc}
\index{Package!euenc}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/euenc}
\item[name] \texttt{EUenc}
\item[caption] Unicode font encoding definitions for XeTeX
\item[author] Hosny, Khaled
\index{Author!Hosny, Khaled}
\item[author] Robertson, Will
\index{Author!Robertson, Will}
\item[author] Roux, Élie
\index{Author!Roux, Élie}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.1h
\item[description] (no language specified) Font encoding definitions for unicode fonts loaded by LaTeX in XeTeX or LuaTeX. The package provides 
          two encodings:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item EU1, designed for use with XeTeX, which the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec}{fontspec} uses for unicode fonts which require no macro-level processing for accents, and
          \item EU2, which provides the same facilities for use with LuaTeX.
          \end{itemize}
Neither encoding places any restriction on the glyphs provided by a font; use of EU2 causes the package 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/euxunicode}{euxunicode} to be loaded (the package is part 
          of this distribution).

\section[\texttt{eulervm} -- Euler virtual math fonts]{\texttt{eulervm} -- Euler virtual math fonts}\label{pkg:eulervm}
\index{Package!eulervm}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/eulervm}
\item[name] \texttt{eulervm}
\item[caption] Euler virtual math fonts
\item[author] Schmidt, Walter A.
\index{Author!Schmidt, Walter A.}
\item[author] Harcombe, Keiran
\index{Author!Harcombe, Keiran}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 4.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The well-known Euler fonts are suitable for typsetting mathematics in conjunction with a variety of text 
          fonts which do not provide mathematical character sets of their own. Euler-VM is a set of  \emph{virtual} mathematics 
          fonts based on Euler and CM. This approach has several advantages over immediately using the \emph{real} Euler 
          fonts: Most noticeably, less TeX resources are consumed, the quality of various math symbols is improved 
          and a usable \texttt{{\textbackslash}hslash} symbol can be provided. The virtual fonts 
          are accompanied by a LaTeX package which makes them easy to use, particularly in conjunction with Type1 
          PostScript text fonts. They are compatible with \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} . 
          A package option allows the fonts to be loaded at 95\% of their nominal size, thus blending better 
          with certain text fonts, e.g., Minion.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/eulervm/README.eulervm}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/eulervm/doc/latex/eulervm/eulervm.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package overlays the five-circle EURion anti-photocopy constellation on document pages. It provides 
          three modes: scatter, for banknote-style tiling across every page; corner, for a single discreet mark 
          in a selected corner; and manual, for user placement with the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}eurion} command.

          The color, size, density, rotation, and random seed are configurable. The package provides a visual reproduction 
          only; it is not a real anti-counterfeiting feature.

\section[\texttt{eurofont} -- Provides a command that prints a euro symbol]{\texttt{eurofont} -- Provides a command that prints a euro symbol}\label{pkg:eurofont}
\index{Package!eurofont}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/eurofont}
\item[name] \texttt{eurofont}
\item[caption] Provides a command that prints a euro symbol
\item[author] McDonnell, Rowland
\index{Author!McDonnell, Rowland}
\item[copyright] Rowland McDonnell (1998)
\item[license] other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
\index{License!other-free}
\index{License!Free license not otherwise listed}
\item[version] 1.1.3
\item[description] (no language specified) The particular symbol printed by  \texttt{{\textbackslash}euro} will in general change 
          depending on the font family, weight, and shape in use at the time. This symbol can come from any source, 
          and the package user has complete control over which euro symbol is used in any given situation. The 
          package is pre-configured to behave sensibly with many common text fonts and available euro symbols. 
          The \texttt{{\textbackslash}euro} command can print ‘faked’ euro symbols from a C with 
          two lines across it when no suitable real euro symbol is available; the package also includes code for 
          printing fake bold euro symbols for use when no real bold symbol exists, as well as pre-configured support 
          for a faked italic version of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/marvosym}{marvosym} font. 
          Eurofont comes set up to use euro symbols from Adobe’s Eurofonts, the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/marvosym}{marvosym} font, 
          the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/eurosym}{Eurosym} font, and any available Text Companion 
          fonts. The selection between these can be done using options passed to the package. The eurofont package 
          also ‘knows’ about the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/china2e}{China2e} font’s euro symbol, 
          and can be configured to use it.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/eurofont/readme.txt}

\section[\texttt{europs} -- Access to Adobe’s Euro currency symbol fonts]{\texttt{europs} -- Access to Adobe’s Euro currency symbol fonts}\label{pkg:europs}
\index{Package!europs}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/europs}
\item[name] \texttt{europs}
\item[caption] Access to Adobe’s Euro currency symbol fonts
\item[author] Clausen, Jörn
\index{Author!Clausen, Jörn}
\item[copyright] Jörn Clausen (1998)
\item[license] noinfo = noinfo 
\index{License!noinfo}
\index{License!noinfo}
\item[version] 1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) Provides access to Adobe’s Euro currency symbol fonts from LaTeX. The fonts are named using Karl Berry’s 
          naming scheme, providing fd files and a style file to use the fonts directly, and providing four macros: 
          {\textbackslash}EURtm, {\textbackslash}EURhv, {\textbackslash}EURcr and {\textbackslash}EUR 
          (from  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/marvosym}{marvosym} ). The actual symbol they produce 
          depends on the currently active font, i.e., they follow font changes caused by {\textbackslash}text.. 
          and other NFSS commands.

          The fonts themselves are only available  \href{http://www.adobe.com/type/eurofont.html}{from 
          Adobe} (though the fonts are free of charge, the licence conditions prevent CTAN from distributing 
          them). Metrics and maps for using the fonts (at all) are available via the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/adobe-euro}{adobe-euro} package.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/europs//README}

\item[caption] Interface to Adobe’s sans-serif Euro font
\item[author] Schmidt, Walter A.
\index{Author!Schmidt, Walter A.}
\item[author] Harcombe, Keiran
\index{Author!Harcombe, Keiran}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 2.1
\item[description] (no language specified) Provides a convenient interface for using Adobe’s freely available Type 1 Euro fonts. Loading the package 
          defines a new command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}euro} which typesets a Euro symbol. 
          The symbol is always taken from the ‘EuroSans’ family, with the weight (medium or boldface) and shape 
          (normal or oblique) varying according to the font currently selected. This Euro symbol meets the official 
          design and matches most font families well enough, except for typewriter fonts.

          The fonts themselves are only available  \href{http://www.adobe.com/type/eurofont.html}{from 
          Adobe} (though the fonts are free of charge, the licence conditions prevent CTAN from distributing 
          them). Metrics and maps for using the fonts (at all) are available via the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/adobe-euro}{adobe-euro} package.

\section[\texttt{exam} -- Package for typesetting exam scripts]{\texttt{exam} -- Package for typesetting exam scripts}\label{pkg:exam}
\index{Package!exam}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/exam}
\item[name] \texttt{exam}
\item[caption] Package for typesetting exam scripts
\item[author] Hirschhorn, Philip S.
\index{Author!Hirschhorn, Philip S.}
\item[copyright] Philip S. Hirschhorn (1994,1997,2000,2004,2008,2011,2015,2017,2021,2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 2.704
\item[description] (no language specified) Provides a class  \texttt{exam.cls} , which eases production of exams, even by a LaTeX novice. 
          Simple commands are provided to:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item create questions, parts of questions, subparts of parts, and subsubparts of subparts, all with optional point values;
          \item create a grading table, indexed either by question number (listing each question and the total possible points for that question) or by page number (listing each page with points and the total possible points for that page);
          \item create headers and footers that are each specified in three parts: one part to be left justified, one part to be centered, and one part to be right justified, in the manner of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyhdr}{fancyhdr} .
          \end{itemize}
Headers and/or footers can be different on the first page of the exam, can be different on the last page 
          of the exam, and can vary depending on whether the page number is odd or even, or on whether the current 
          page continues a question from a previous page, or on whether the last question on the current page continues 
          onto the following page.

          Multiple line headers and/or footers are allowed, and it's easy to increase the part of the page devoted 
          to headers and/or footers to allow for this.

          Note that the bundle  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/exams}{exams} also provides a file \texttt{exam.cls} ; 
          the two bundles therefore clash, and should not be installed on the same system.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/exam/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/exam/examdoc.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./7307145371-examdoc.pdf|
\item[home page] \url{http://www-math.mit.edu/~psh/}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/exam}

\item[description] (no language specified) Although there are already several excellent exam packages or classes like  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/exam}{exam} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bhcexam}{bhcexam} , 
          these do not fit the Chinese style very well, or they cannot be customized easily for Chinese exams of 
          all types, like exams in primary school, junior high school, senior high school and even college. This 
          is the main reason why this package was created.

          This package provides a class  \texttt{exam-zh.cls} and several module packages like \texttt{exam-zh-question.sty} and \texttt{exam-zh-choices.sty} , 
          where these module packages can be used individually.

          Using  \texttt{exam-zh} you can

          \begin{itemize}
          \item separate the format and the content very well;
          \item use the  \texttt{choices} environment to typeset choice items easily and automatically;
          \item design the seal line easily;
          \item and more (see manual).
          \end{itemize}
