\section[\texttt{examdesign} -- LaTeX class for typesetting exams]{\texttt{examdesign} -- LaTeX class for typesetting exams}\label{pkg:examdesign}
\index{Package!examdesign}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/examdesign}
\item[name] \texttt{Exam design}
\item[caption] LaTeX class for typesetting exams
\item[author] Alexander, Jason
\index{Author!Alexander, Jason}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 1.101
\item[description] (no language specified) This bundle provides a class examdesign. The class provides several features useful for designing tests 
          or question sets:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item it allows for explicit markup of questions and answers;
          \item the class will, at the user’s request, automatically generate answer keys;
          \item multiple versions of the same test can be generated automatically, with the ordering of questions within each section randomly permuted so as to minimize cheating;
          \item the generated answer keys can be constructed either with or without the questions included;
          \item environments are provided to assist in constructing the most common types of test question: matching, true/false, multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, and short answer/essay questions.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/examdesign/examdesign.pdf}

\section[\texttt{examplep} -- Verbatim phrases and listings in LaTeX]{\texttt{examplep} -- Verbatim phrases and listings in LaTeX}\label{pkg:examplep}
\index{Package!examplep}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/examplep}
\item[name] \texttt{examplep}
\item[caption] Verbatim phrases and listings in LaTeX
\item[author] Szabó, Péter
\index{Author!Szabó, Péter}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 0.04
\item[description] (no language specified) Examplep provides sophisticated features for typesetting verbatim source code listings, including the 
          display of the source code and its compiled LaTeX or MetaPost output side-by-side, with automatic width 
          detection and enabled page breaks (in the source), without the need for specifying the source twice. 
          Special care is taken that section, page and footnote numbers do not interfere with the main document. 
          For typesetting short verbatim phrases, a replacement for the {\textbackslash}verb command is also 
          provided in the package, which can be used inside tables and moving arguments such as footnotes and section 
          titles. The  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/listings}{listings} package is used for syntax 
          highlighting.

          The accompanying codep package and the wrfiles.pl Perl script provide a convenient interface to the examplep 
          package for authors of manuals. With codep it is possible to generate the source code, the LaTeX or MetaPost 
          output and the compilable example file from a single source embedded into the appropriate place of the 
          .tex document file.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Article from EuroTeX 2005 talk}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/examplep/eurotex_2005_examplep.pdf}

\index{Package!exceltex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/exceltex}
\item[name] \texttt{Exceltex}
\item[caption] Get data from Excel files into LaTeX
\item[author] Doerr, Hans-Peter
\index{Author!Doerr, Hans-Peter}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 0.5.1
\item[description] (no language specified) Exceltex is a LaTeX package combined with a helper program written in Perl. It provides an easy to use 
          yet powerfull and flexible way to get data from Spreadsheets into LaTeX.

          In contrast to other solutions, exceltex does not seek to make the creation of tables in LaTeX easier, 
          but to get data from Spreadsheets into LaTeX as easily as possible.

          The Excel (TM) file format only acts as an interface between the spreadsheet application and exceltex 
          beacause it is easily accessible (via the  \texttt{Spreadsheet::ParseExcel} Perl module) 
          and because most spreadsheet applications are able to read and write Excel files.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Un*x-style man-page}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/exceltex/manpage.pdf}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[name] \texttt{excludeonly}
\item[caption] Prevent files being {\textbackslash}include-ed
\item[author] Arseneau, Donald
\index{Author!Arseneau, Donald}
\item[author] Luecking, Daniel H.
\index{Author!Luecking, Daniel H.}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The package defines an  \texttt{{\textbackslash}excludeonly} command, which is (in 
          effect) the opposite of \texttt{{\textbackslash}includeonly} . If both \texttt{{\textbackslash}includeonly} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}excludeonly} exist 
          in a document, only files ''allowed'' by both will be included.

          The package redefines the internal  \texttt{{\textbackslash}@include} command, so it 
          conflicts with packages that do the same. Examples are the classes \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/paper}{paper.cls} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/thesis}{thesis.cls} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/excludeonly/excludeonly.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) The package helps to typeset exercises or list of exercises within any document.

          Exercises, questions and sub-questions are automatically numbered. It is possible to put answers in the 
          same document, and display them immediatly, later in the document or not to print answers at all.

          The layout of exercises is fully customisable. It is possible to typeset long problems, short exercises, 
          questionnaires, etc.

          Usage of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} package is detected, but not fully 
          supported yet (only English and French are implemented).

          Since version 0.11 it has a regular and a beamer mode (selected depending on the documentclass used). 
          From version 0.16 on there is an embedded mode that allows using exercises in lecture notes etc. without 
          requiring page breaks. Since the package includes a loading mechanism for exercises from external files, 
          the same exercises can be reused in different contexts.

\section[\texttt{exesheet} -- Typesetting exercise or exam sheets]{\texttt{exesheet} -- Typesetting exercise or exam sheets}\label{pkg:exesheet}
\index{Package!exesheet}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/exesheet}
\item[name] \texttt{exesheet}
\item[caption] Typesetting exercise or exam sheets
\item[author] Missier, Antoine
\index{Author!Missier, Antoine}
\item[copyright] Antoine Missier (2020-2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 2.9 (2025-05-04)
\item[last changes] 2025-05-04
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) The exesheet package is designed for typesetting exercise or exam sheets. The primary advantage of exesheet 
          is its ability to display a detailed scoring guide and correction instructions as needed. This feature 
          is especially beneficial for grading papers with multiple graders.

          The exesheet package provides:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item macros for organizing exercises and subparts,
          \item specific settings for enumeration lists,
          \item environments for questions and answers, which can be displayed or hidden,
          \item macros for detailed comments and grading instructions in the margins which can be displayed or hidden.
          \end{itemize}
Additionally, the  \texttt{exesheet} class loads the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/schooldocs}{schooldocs} package 
          which manages the page layout, the main title, headers and footers.

\section[\texttt{expex-glossonly} -- Help gb4e, linguex, and covington users use the ExPex glossi\ldots]{\texttt{expex-glossonly} -- Help gb4e, linguex, and covington users use the ExPex glossing macros}\label{pkg:expex-glossonly}
\index{Package!expex-glossonly}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/expex-glossonly}
\item[name] \texttt{expex-glossonly}
\item[caption] Help gb4e, linguex, and covington users use the ExPex glossing macros
\item[author] Munn, Alan
\index{Author!Munn, Alan}
\item[copyright] Alan Munn (2016-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.9b (2024-02-14)
\item[last changes] 2024-02-14
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expex}{ExPex} package by John Frampton provides very 
          fine-grained control over glossing and example formatting, including unlimited gloss lines and various 
          ways of formatting multiline glosses. By contrast the \texttt{cgloss4e} glossing macros provided 
          with \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gb4e}{gb4e} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/linguex}{linguex} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/covington}{covington} , although very capable at basic 
          glossing, lack the degree of customization that is sometimes needed for more complex glossing.

          On the other hand, for those users who have heavily invested in using either  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gb4e}{gb4e} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/linguex}{linguex} , 
          or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/covington}{covington} , shifting to \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expex}{ExPex} can 
          be quite daunting and burdensome, especially since the basic syntax of the examples is quite different.

          This package is an attempt to have the best of both worlds: it allows  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gb4e}{gb4e} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/linguex}{linguex} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/covington}{covington} users 
          to keep using those packages for basic example numbering and formatting, but also allows them to use 
          the glossing macros that \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expex}{ExPex} provides.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/expex-glossonly/expex-glossonly.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./1624737634-expex-glossonly.pdf|

\section[\texttt{expkv-bundle} -- An expandable key=val implementation and friends]{\texttt{expkv-bundle} -- An expandable key=val implementation and friends}\label{pkg:expkv-bundle}
\index{Package!expkv-bundle}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/expkv-bundle}
\item[name] \texttt{expkv-bundle}
\item[caption] An expandable key=val implementation and friends
\item[author] Spratte, Jonathan P.
\index{Author!Spratte, Jonathan P.}
\item[copyright] Jonathan P. Spratte (2020-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version]  (2024-12-26)
\item[last changes] 2024-12-26
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This is a collection of different packages that provide  \texttt{key=value} functionality 
          in plainTeX, LaTeX, and ConTeXt.

          At the core, the  \texttt{expkv} package implements two expandable \texttt{key=value} parsers 
          that are somewhat fast and robust against common bugs in many \texttt{key=value} implementations 
          (no accidental brace stripping, no fragility for active commas or equals signs).

          \texttt{expkv-cs} enables users to define expandable \texttt{key=value} macros 
          in a comfortable and straightforward way.

          \texttt{expkv-def} provides an interface to define common key types for \texttt{expkv} similar 
          to the key defining interfaces of widespread \texttt{key=value} implementations.

          \texttt{expkv-opt} allows to parse package or class options in LaTeX via \texttt{expkv} .

          \texttt{expkv-pop} is a utility package to define prefix oriented parsers that allow a somewhat 
          natural formulation (it provides the core functionality for the key-defining front ends of both \texttt{expkv-cs} and \texttt{expkv-def} ).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/expkv-bundle/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/expkv-bundle/expkv-bundle.pdf}

\item[author] Niederberger, Clemens
\index{Author!Niederberger, Clemens}

\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the means to create exercises or questions and their corresponding solutions. The 
          questions may be divided into classes and/or topics and may be printed selectively. Meta-data to questions 
          can be added and recovered.

          The solutions may be printed where they are, or collected and printed at a later point in the document 
          all together, section-wise or selectively by ID.

          The package provides the means to selectively include questions from an external file, and to control 
          the style of headings of both questions and solutions.

          As of May 2017, this package has been superseded by its official successor  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xsim}{xsim} . \texttt{exsheets} itself 
          is now considered obsolete, but will stay alive, and will continue to receive bugfix releases. However, 
          new features will not be added any more.

\section[\texttt{exsol} -- Exercises and solutions from the same source, into a book]{\texttt{exsol} -- Exercises and solutions from the same source, into a book}\label{pkg:exsol}
\index{Package!exsol}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/exsol}
\item[name] \texttt{exsol}
\item[caption] Exercises and solutions from the same source, into a book
\item[author] Daems, Walter
\index{Author!Daems, Walter}
\item[copyright] Walter Daems (2012-2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}

\item[version] 1.7 (2025-02-14)
\item[last changes] 2025-02-14
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides macros to allow for embedding exercises and solutions in the LaTeX source of an 
          instructional text (e.g., a book or a course text) while generating the following separate documents:

          
          \begin{itemize}
          \item your original text that only contains the exercises, and
          \item a solution book that contains only the solutions to the exercises (optionally, the exercises themselves can also be copied to the solution book).
          \end{itemize}
The exercise data are generated when running LaTeX on your document; the first run also writes the solutions 
          to a secondary file that may be included in a simple document harness, may be processed by LaTeX, to 
          generate a nice solution book.

          The code of the package was derived (in large part) from  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyvrb}{fancyvrb} .

\section[\texttt{extract} -- Extract parts of a document and write to another document]{\texttt{extract} -- Extract parts of a document and write to another document}\label{pkg:extract}
\index{Package!extract}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/extract}
\item[name] \texttt{extract}
\item[caption] Extract parts of a document and write to another document
\item[author] Adriaens, Hendri
\index{Author!Adriaens, Hendri}
\item[copyright] Hendri Adriaens (2004-2019)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.9a
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the means to extract specific content from a source document and write that to a 
          target document. One could, for instance, use this to extract all exercises from lecture notes and generate 
          an exercises book on the fly.

          The package also provides an environment which writes its body entirely to the target file. Another environment 
          will write to the target file, but will also execute the body. This allows to share code (for instance, 
          a preamble) between the source document and the target file.

          Finally, the package provides an interface to conditionally extract content. With a single package option, 
          one can specify exactly which commands (counted from the start of the document) should be extracted and 
          which not. This might be useful for extracting specific slides from a presentation and use them in a 
          new file.

\section[\texttt{extractpdfmark} -- Extract page mode and named destinations as PDFmark from PDF\ldots]{\texttt{extractpdfmark} -- Extract page mode and named destinations as PDFmark from PDF}\label{pkg:extractpdfmark}
\index{Package!extractpdfmark}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/extractpdfmark}
\item[name] \texttt{extractpdfmark}
\item[caption] Extract page mode and named destinations as PDFmark from PDF
\item[author] Hosoda, Masamichi
\index{Author!Hosoda, Masamichi}
\item[copyright] Masamichi Hosoda (2016-2022)
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[version] 1.1.1 (2022-09-30)
\item[last changes] 2022-09-30
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) PDFmarks is a technique that accompanies PDF and that is used to store metadata such as author or title, 
          but also structural information such as bookmarks or hyperlinks.

          When Ghostscript reads the main PDF generated by the TeX system with embedded PDF files and outputs the 
          final PDF, the PDF page mode and name targets etc. are not preserved. Therefore, when you open the final 
          PDF, it is not displayed correctly. Also, remote PDF links do not work correctly.

          This program is able to extract the page mode and named targets as PDFmark from PDF. In this way, you 
          can obtain embedded PDF files that have kept this information.

          Usage:

          \begin{verbatim}
$ extractpdfmark TeX-System-Outputted.pdf > Extracted-PDFmark.ps
          \end{verbatim}

          \begin{verbatim}
$ gs -q -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dPDFDontUseFontObjectNum 
-sOutputFile=Final.pdf TeX-System-Outputted.pdf Extracted-PDFmark.ps
          \end{verbatim}
\item[documentation] \textit{Readme (Japanese)}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/extractpdfmark/README.ja.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/extractpdfmark/README.md}

          The class covers two areas:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item First, a title page is created with a detailed fax header;
          \item second, every page gets headers and footers so that the recipient can be sure that every page has been received and all pages are complete, and in the correct order.

          to 6,000 euros per calendar year (amount indexed annually) without having to pay tax or social security

\section[\texttt{fancyhandout} -- A LaTeX class for producing nice-looking handouts]{\texttt{fancyhandout} -- A LaTeX class for producing nice-looking handouts}\label{pkg:fancyhandout}
\index{Package!fancyhandout}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyhandout}
\item[name] \texttt{fancyhandout}
\item[caption] A LaTeX class for producing nice-looking handouts
\item[author] Friedl, Sebastian
\index{Author!Friedl, Sebastian}
\item[copyright] Sebastian Friedl (2017-2018)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version]  (2018-01-22)
\item[last changes] 2018-01-22
\item[year] 2018
\index{Year!2018}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package breaks with some of LaTeX’s principles and redefines basic LaTeX commands with the aim of 
          producing well-designed and clearly structured handouts: A sans-serif font is used by default; sections 
          are not numbered, but highlighted by underlining; head- and footline display document information; and 
          in order to avoid too much whitespace around the text the margin sizes are adjusted to smaller values.

          All in all,  \texttt{fancyhandout} provides a means of typesetting documents not exclusively 
          consisting of running text in a beautiful way.

          \texttt{fancyhandout} depends on the following other LaTeX packages: \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/csquotes}{csquotes} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem}{enumitem} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox}{etoolbox} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fancyhdr}{fancyhdr} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry}{geometry} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor}{xcolor} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fancyhandout/fancyhandout-doc.pdf}

\section[\texttt{fancytooltips} -- Include a wide range of material in PDF tooltips]{\texttt{fancytooltips} -- Include a wide range of material in PDF tooltips}\label{pkg:fancytooltips}
\index{Package!fancytooltips}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fancytooltips}
\item[name] \texttt{fancytooltips}
\item[caption] Include a wide range of material in PDF tooltips
\item[author] Mařík, Robert
\index{Author!Mařík, Robert}
\item[copyright] Robert Mařík (2007, 2009)
\item[license] lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.2}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2}
\item[version] 1.8
\item[description] (no language specified) The package was inspired by the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cooltooltips}{cooltooltips} package. 
          In contrast to cooltooltips, fancytooltips allows inclusion of tooltips which contain arbitrary TeX material 
          or a series of TeX materials (animated graphics) from an external PDF file. To see the tooltips, you

          All contributions are welcome: corrections of small errors, updating answers to questions, or adding 
          new questions!

          These files are made available on CTAN only to encourage reuse of this content, and to preserve a permanent 
          copy.

          Ce package contient les sources de la FAQ LaTeX francophone GUTenberg (groupe des utilisateurs francophones 
          de (La)TeX), actuellement maintenue à jour sous forme d’un dépôt Git ouvert à tous:  \href{https://gitlab.gutenberg-asso.fr}{https://gitlab.gutenberg-asso.fr} Si

\#\# Participer

          Ces fichiers ne sont mis à disposition sur le CTAN que pour encourager la réutilisation de ce contenu, 
          et pour en conserver une copie pérenne.

          \#\# Nous contacter

          Pour toutes questions et remarques: faq@gutenberg-asso.fr

\item[author] Suckale, Jakob
\index{Author!Suckale, Jakob}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version]  (2008-03-12)
\item[last changes] 2008-03-12
\item[year] 2008
\index{Year!2008}
\item[description] (no language specified) A BibTeX style file made with  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/custom-bib}{custom-bib} to 
          fit Frontiers in Bioscience requirements:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item all authors, no et al, full author names, initials abbreviated;
          \item only abbreviated journal name italicised, no abbreviation dots;
          \item only year, no month, at end of reference; and
          \item DOI excluded, ISSN excluded.
          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{fei} -- Class for academic works at FEI University Center — Brazil]{\texttt{fei} -- Class for academic works at FEI University Center — Brazil}\label{pkg:fei}
\index{Package!fei}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fei}
\item[name] \texttt{fei}
\item[caption] Class for academic works at FEI University Center — Brazil
\item[author] De Rizzo Meneghetti, Douglas
\index{Author!De Rizzo Meneghetti, Douglas}
\item[copyright] Douglas De Rizzo Meneghetti (2014-2022)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 4.10.4 (2022-12-23)
\item[last changes] 2022-12-23
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) \texttt{fei} is a class created by graduate students and LaTeX enthusiasts that allows students 
          from FEI University Center to create their academic works, be it a monograph, masters dissertation or 
          phd thesis, under the typographic rules of the institution.

          The class makes it possible to create a full academic work, supporting functionalities such as cover, 
          title page, catalog entry, dedication, summary, lists of figures, tables, algorithms, acronyms and symbols, 
          multiple authors, index, references, appendices and attachments.

          \texttt{fei} is loosely based in the Brazilian National Standards Organization (Associação 
          Brasileira de Normas Técnicas, ABNT) standards for the creation of academic works, such as ABNT NBR 10520:2002 
          (Citations) and ABNT NBR 6023:2002 (Bibliographic References).

\section[\texttt{fenixpar} -- One-shot changes to token registers such as {\textbackslash}everypar]{\texttt{fenixpar} -- One-shot changes to token registers such as {\textbackslash}everypar}\label{pkg:fenixpar}
\index{Package!fenixpar}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fenixpar}
\item[name] \texttt{fenixpar}
\item[caption] One-shot changes to token registers such as {\textbackslash}everypar
\item[author] Múgica de Rivera, Javier
\index{Author!Múgica de Rivera, Javier}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.92
\item[description] (no language specified) The bundle provides two packages, fenxitok and fenixpar.

          The fenixtok package provides user macros to add material to a token register; the material will be (automatically) 
          removed from the token register when the register is executed. Material may be added either to the left 
          or to the right, and care is taken not to override any redefinition that may be included in the token 
          register itself.

          The fenixpar package uses the macros of fenixtok to provide a user interface to manipulation of the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}everypar} token 
          register.

          The packages require the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etex}{e-TeX} extensions; with them, 
          they work either with Plain TeX or with LaTeX.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/fenixpar/README}

\section[\texttt{fetchcls} -- Fetch the current class name]{\texttt{fetchcls} -- Fetch the current class name}\label{pkg:fetchcls}
\index{Package!fetchcls}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fetchcls}
\item[name] \texttt{fetchcls}
\item[caption] Fetch the current class name
\item[author] Giannotti, Ruben
\index{Author!Giannotti, Ruben}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0 (2015-08-11)
\item[last changes] 2015-08-11
\item[year] 2015
\index{Year!2015}
\item[description] (no language specified) With standard LaTeX you are able to check for the class in use invoking the kernel command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}@ifclassloaded} . 
          However, doing so you cannot get the explicit class name, unless you want to loop over every possible 
          class name until \texttt{{\textbackslash}@ifclassloaded} returns true — don't do that!

          With the help of the present package you can obtain the name of the current class with significantly 
          less effort. Just load the package as usual:  \texttt{{\textbackslash}usepackage{\textbraceleft}fetchcls{\textbraceright}} ; 
          then, the control sequence \texttt{{\textbackslash}classname} will hold the name you 
          were looking for.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fetchcls/fetchcls.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) The ffslides ("freeform slides") class is intended to make it easier to place various types of content 
          freely on the page, and therefore easier to design documents with a strong visual component: presentations, 
          posters, research or lecture notes, and so on.

          The goal of the class is to be less rigid and less complex than some of the popular presentation-making 
          options. It is essentially a small set of macros added to the article class. A well-organized template 
          file is included, and the documentation is itself an extensive example of the class's capabilities.

\item[version] 0.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The FigSize package enables automatic sizing of graphics, especially when including graphics with the 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx}{graphicx} package. The user only has to specify 
          the number of graphics that should fit to a page or fraction there of and the package will dynamically 
          calculate the correct graphics sizes relative to the page size. Thus, graphics can be auto-sized to fill 
          a whole page or fraction and manual changes of graphic sizes are never needed when changing document 
          layouts. Finally, the package's dynamic lengths can be used to allow other document element sizes to 
          be dynamic.

\section[\texttt{filecontents} -- Create an external file from within a LaTeX document]{\texttt{filecontents} -- Create an external file from within a LaTeX document}\label{pkg:filecontents}
\index{Package!filecontents}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/filecontents}
\item[name] \texttt{filecontents}
\item[caption] Create an external file from within a LaTeX document
\item[author] Pakin, Scott
\index{Author!Pakin, Scott}
\item[copyright] Scott Pakin (2011-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.5a (2023-04-02)
\item[last changes] 2023-04-02
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) LaTeX2e’s  \texttt{filecontents} and \texttt{filecontents*} environments enable 
          a LaTeX source file to generate external files as it runs through LaTeX. However, there are two limitations 
          of these environments: they refuse to overwrite existing files, and they can only be used in the preamble 
          of a document. The filecontents package removes these limitations, letting you overwrite existing files 
          and letting you use \texttt{filecontents} / \texttt{filecontents*} anywhere.

          As of September 2019 the author tells us: ''This package is no longer necessary due to its functionality 
          having moved into recent LaTeX kernels. It’s probably better not to move the package to obsolete because 
          users may need it to rebuild old documents. Version 1.5 provides full functionality when run with an 
          older kernel but issues a warning message and disables itself when run with a newer kernel.''

          Supply the  \texttt{overwrite} option to LaTeX’s built-in \texttt{filecontents} environment 
          to mimic this package’s behavior:

          \verb|\begin{filecontents}[overwrite]{my-file}...\end{filecontents}|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/filecontents/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/filecontents/filecontents.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./9817241000-filecontents.pdf|

\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides two environments called  \texttt{filecontentsdef} and \texttt{filecontentshere} . 
          They are derived from the LaTeX \texttt{filecontents} environment as provided by Scott Pakin's \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/filecontents}{filecontents} package. 
          In addition to the file creation they either store the (verbatim) contents in a macro ( \texttt{filecontentsdef} ) 
          or typeset them (verbatim) on the spot ( \texttt{filecontentshere} ).

          The author developed the package to display TeX code verbatim in documentation and the same time produce 
          the corresponding files during the LaTeX run in order to embed them in the PDF as file attachment annotations 
          (by using Scott Pakin's package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/attachfile}{attachfile} ).

\item[name] \texttt{filemod}

\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides macros to read and compare the modification dates of files. The files may be  \texttt{.tex} files, 
          images or other files (as long as they can be found by LaTeX). It uses the \texttt{{\textbackslash}pdffilemoddate} primitive 
          of pdfLaTeX to find the file modification date as PDF date string, parses the string and returns the 
          value to the user. The package will also work for \texttt{DVI} output with recent versions 
          of the LaTeX compiler which uses pdfLaTeX in \texttt{DVI} mode. The functionality is provided 
          by purely expandable macros or by faster but non-expandable ones.

\item[description] (no language specified) Finomaton is a TCL program that allows users to comfortably draw and typeset finite state machines (automata). 
          The resulting graphs can be exported to plain MetaPost and subsequently be included in TeX and LaTeX 
          documents for excellent typesetting quality. In contrast to many other packages, the mouse can be used 
          to interactively move objects around. States are magnetic to facilitate connection, and any TeX command 
          can be embedded in the labels of states and lines.

\section[\texttt{fitr} -- Set a rectangular destination and jump to it]{\texttt{fitr} -- Set a rectangular destination and jump to it}\label{pkg:fitr}
\index{Package!fitr}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fitr}
\item[name] \texttt{FitR}
\item[caption] Set a rectangular destination and jump to it
\item[author] Story, Donald P.
\index{Author!Story, Donald P.}
\item[copyright] D. P. Story (2012-2020)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.3.2 (2020-07-09)
\item[last changes] 2020-07-09
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package is an implementation of the FitR view-type destination as described in the PDF Reference; 
          it defines one new command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}jdRect} . The command (optionally) 
          sets a jump to and/or sets a destination of a FitR (Rectangle). (Can you see where \texttt{{\textbackslash}jdRect} comes 
          from?).

          The package requires  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/eforms}{eforms} (part of the AeB) and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/collectbox}{collectbox} (by 
          Martin Scharrer). Drivers supported are dvips and dvipsone (using Adobe Distiller as the PDF creator); 
          pdfTeX (including LuaTeX); and dvipdfm, dvipdfmx, and XeTeX.

          The package was developed in response to a user of the AeB Bundle who was interested in developing documents 
          for students with low vision; the idea is to magnify regions of the document so the student can read 
          more comfortably. Optional special effects are included (JavaScript functions) to help focus one the 
          rectangle as it is magnified, and as the previous view is restored.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Code documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fitr/docs/fitr.pdf}

\section[\texttt{fixmath} -- Make maths comply with ISO 31-0:1992 to ISO 31-13:1992]{\texttt{fixmath} -- Make maths comply with ISO 31-0:1992 to ISO 31-13:1992}\label{pkg:fixmath}
\index{Package!fixmath}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fixmath}
\item[name] \texttt{fixmath}
\item[caption] Make maths comply with ISO 31-0:1992 to ISO 31-13:1992
\item[author] Schmidt, Walter A.
\index{Author!Schmidt, Walter A.}
\item[author] Harcombe, Keiran
\index{Author!Harcombe, Keiran}
\item[copyright] Keiran Harcombe (2022)
\item[copyright] Walter Schmidt (2000-2003)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.9.1 (2022-10-06)
\item[last changes] 2022-10-06
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) LaTeX’s default style of typesetting mathematics does not comply with the International Standards ISO 
          31-0:1992 to ISO 31-13:1992 which require that uppercase Greek letters always be typset upright, as opposed 
          to italic (even though they usually represent variables) and allow for typsetting of variables in a boldface 
          italic style (even though the required fonts are available). This package ensures that uppercase Greek 
          be typeset in italic style, that upright  \texttt{\${\textbackslash}Delta\$} and \texttt{\${\textbackslash}Omega\$} symbols 
          are available through the commands \texttt{{\textbackslash}upDelta} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}upOmega} ; 
          and provides a new math alphabet \texttt{{\textbackslash}mathbold} for boldface italic 
          letters, including Greek.

          This package used to be part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/was}{was} bundle, but 
          has now become a package in its own right.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fixmath/fixmath.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5554927200-fixmath.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Bundle readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fixmath/README}
\item[contact] \textit{repository}: \url{https://gitlab.com/kjhtex/fixmath}
\index{Contact!repository}

\section[\texttt{fixme} -- Collaborative annotation tool for LaTeX]{\texttt{fixme} -- Collaborative annotation tool for LaTeX}\label{pkg:fixme}
\index{Package!fixme}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fixme}
\item[name] \texttt{FiXme}
\item[caption] Collaborative annotation tool for LaTeX
\item[author] Verna, Didier
\index{Author!Verna, Didier}
\item[copyright] Didier Verna (1998-2002, 2004-2007, 2009, 2013, 2017-2019)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 4.5 (2019-01-03)
\item[last changes] 2019-01-03
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) FiXme is a collaborative annotation tool for LaTeX documents. Annotating a document here refers to inserting 
          meta-notes, that is, notes that do not belong to the document itself, but rather to its development or 
          reviewing process. Such notes may involve things of different importance levels, ranging from simple 
          ''fix the spelling'' flags to critical ''this paragraph is a lie'' mentions. Annotations like this should 
          be visible during the development or reviewing phase, but should normally disappear in the final version 
          of the document.

          FiXme is designed to ease and automate the process of managing collaborative annotations, by offering 
          a set of predefined note levels and layouts, the possibility to register multiple authors, to reference 
          annotations by listing and indexing etc. FiXme is extensible, giving you the possibility to create new 
          layouts or even complete ''themes'', and also comes with support for AUCTeX.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fixme/fixme.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./9580217689-fixme.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fixme/README.md}
\item[home page] \url{https://www.lrde.epita.fr/~didier/software/latex.php#fixme}
\item[contact] \textit{repository}: \url{https://github.com/didierverna/fixme}
\index{Contact!repository}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fixme}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides utility functions in  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} and 
          LaTeX2e syntax for setting tounicode mappings for 7/8 bit fonts. The package provides a unified interface 
          which enables mappings for both \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex}{pdfTeX} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/luatex}{LuaTeX} .

          The aim is to make it easier to make legacy (text) symbol packages, which often use arbitary glyph names 
          and encodings, accessible for the two engines currently capable of producing accessible PDFs.

          The package provides a limited workaround for LuaTeX 1.22 and earlier, which make the provision of such 
          mappings more challenging.

          Full support requires pdfTeX or LuaTeX 1.24 or later.

\section[\texttt{fldigigal} -- Create a Flash slide show of digital photos]{\texttt{fldigigal} -- Create a Flash slide show of digital photos}\label{pkg:fldigigal}
\index{Package!fldigigal}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fldigigal}
\item[name] \texttt{fldigigal}
\item[caption] Create a Flash slide show of digital photos
\item[author] Story, Donald P.
\index{Author!Story, Donald P.}
\item[copyright] D. P. Story (2010-2020)
\item[license] lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
\index{License!lppl1}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1}
\item[version] 0.6 (2020-08-08)
\item[last changes] 2020-08-08
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package uses the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/rmannot}{rmannot} package (thus requiring 
          an Adobe Distiller workflow) to create what the author calls ''an AcroTeX Flash Digital Gallery''; that 
          is, a Flash slide show that displays a series of digital images (PNG, JPG or GIF formats). The document 
          author describes the digital images (path and caption) from the LaTeX source; on compilation, fldigigal 
          writes an XML file, which Distiller embeds in the PDF. The digital images may be embedded in the PDF, 
          or be accessed remotely (reducing filesize). Three layouts are offered: vertical thumbnails, horizontal 
          thumbnails, or no thumbnails.

          This package has become obsolete after December 2020. Since December 2020, Adobe no longer supports Flash 
          player (SWF, FLV). This package uses a custom SWF file ( \texttt{fdg\_ht1.swf} , eg); 
          as a result this package will no longer function in Adobe Acrobat Reader DC. The package will continue 
          to produce PDFs as designed, but only if built using Acrobat XI (or a version Acrobat prior to 2021) 
          and viewed in Adobe Acrobat Reader XI (or a version of Reader prior 2021).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/macros/latex/contrib/fldigigal/doc/fdg_man.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5253628097-fdg_man.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/obsolete/macros/latex/contrib/fldigigal/README.md}

\section[\texttt{flowframtk} -- Vector graphics application with support for flowfram.sty]{\texttt{flowframtk} -- Vector graphics application with support for flowfram.sty}\label{pkg:flowframtk}
\index{Package!flowframtk}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/flowframtk}
\item[Alias] \texttt{jpgfdraw}
\index{Package!jpgfdraw (alias for flowframtk)}
\index{Alias!jpgfdraw (for flowframtk)}
\item[name] \texttt{FlowframTk}
\item[caption] Vector graphics application with support for flowfram.sty
\item[author] Talbot, Nicola
\index{Author!Talbot, Nicola}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 0.8.4
\item[description] (no language specified) FlowframTk is a graphics application written in Java designed for use with  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/flowfram}{flowfram} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{pgf} , 
          but can also be used to create standalone image files.

          You can use FlowframTk to:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Construct frames for use with the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/flowfram}{flowfram} package.
          \item Construct shapes using lines, moves and cubic Bezier segments.
          \item Edit shapes by changing the defining control points.
          \item Add symmetry to shapes.
          \item Convert shapes into patterns (rotational, scaled, spiral).
          \item Incorporate text and bitmap images (for annotation and background effects).
          \item Display text along a shape.
          \item Extract the parameters for TeX’s  \texttt{{\textbackslash}parshape} command and for \texttt{{\textbackslash}shapepar} (defined in the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/shapepar}{shapepar} package).
          \end{itemize}
Pictures can be saved in FlowframTk’s native binary format (JDR) or native ascii format (AJR) or can 
          be exported as:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item a  \texttt{pgfpicture} environment for use in LaTeX documents with the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{pgf} package;
          \item a LaTeX class or package that loads the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/flowfram}{flowfram} package;
          \item a PostScript file;
          \item a PDF file;
          \item a PNG image file; or
          \item an SVG image file.
          \end{itemize}
Alternative text can be specified to use when exporting to a LaTeX file (e.g. if the text contains symbols 
          or if it should be set in maths mode).

          Mappings can be used to specify what LaTeX font declarations should be used when exporting to a LaTeX 
          file.

          To install, download and run the installer application  \texttt{flowframtk-}  \emph{version}  \texttt{-installer.jar} (where \emph{version} is 
          the version number).

          This application replaces the now obsolete JpgfDraw.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{User manual}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/flowframtk/flowframtk-en-GB.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./1863283820-flowframtk-en-GB.pdf|

\item[version] 1.1a
\item[description] (no language specified) The package defines two macros which decide to typeset a number either as an Arabic number or as a word 
          (or words) for the number. If the number is between zero and twelve (including zero and twelve) then 
          words will be used; if the number is outside that range, it will be typeset using the package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/numprint}{numprint} 

          Words for English representation of numbers are generated within the package, while those for German 
          are generated using the package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/zahl2string}{zahl2string} .

\index{Package!foliono}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/foliono}
\item[name] \texttt{foliono}
\item[caption] Use folio numbers to replace page numbers
\item[author] Syrjänen, Tommi
\index{Author!Syrjänen, Tommi}
\item[copyright] Tommy Syrjänen (2021)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)

\item[version] 1.000 (2021-03-25)
\item[last changes] 2021-03-25
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package adds functionality to create several styles of folio numbers. Folio numbering preceded the 
          modern page numbering convention and was in common use until the 18th century. In folio numbering the 
          numbers are placed only on odd (right-side) pages and the numbers typically comprise of two parts: quire 
          and folio numbers.

          The intended use for this package is to help creating old-style books.

\section[\texttt{font-change-xetex} -- Macros to change text and mathematics fonts in plain XeTeX]{\texttt{font-change-xetex} -- Macros to change text and mathematics fonts in plain XeTeX}\label{pkg:font-change-xetex}
\index{Package!font-change-xetex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/font-change-xetex}
\item[name] \texttt{font-change-xetex}
\item[caption] Macros to change text and mathematics fonts in plain XeTeX
\item[author] Dhawan, Amit Raj
\index{Author!Dhawan, Amit Raj}
\item[license] other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
\index{License!other-free}
\index{License!Free license not otherwise listed}
\item[version] 2016.1
\item[description] (no language specified) This package consists of macros that can be used to typeset ''plain'' XeTeX documents using any OpenType 
          or TrueType font installed on the computer system.

          The macros allow the user to change the text mode fonts and some math mode fonts. For any declared font 
          family, various font style, weight, and size variants like bold, italics, small caps, etc., are available 
          through standard and custom TeX control statements. Using the optional argument of the macros, the available 
          XeTeX font features and OpenType tags can be accessed.

          Other features of the package include activating and deactivating hanging punctuation, and support for 
          special Unicode characters.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/xetex/plain/font-change-xetex/doc/font-change-xetex.pdf}

\section[\texttt{fontch} -- Changing fonts, sizes and encodings in Plain TeX]{\texttt{fontch} -- Changing fonts, sizes and encodings in Plain TeX}\label{pkg:fontch}
\index{Package!fontch}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontch}
\item[name] \texttt{fontch}
\item[caption] Changing fonts, sizes and encodings in Plain TeX
\item[author] Medina, Rodrigo
\index{Author!Medina, Rodrigo}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 2.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The fontch macros allow the user to change font size and family anywhere in a plain TeX document. Sizes 
          of 8, 10, 12, 14, 20 and 24 points are available. A sans serif family ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}sf} ) 
          is defined in addition to the families already defined in plain TeX. Optional support for Latin Modern 
          T1 and TS1 fonts is given. There are macros for non-latin1 letters and for most TS1 symbols. Math mode 
          always uses CM fonts.

          A command for producing doubled-spaced documents is also provided.

          The present version of the package is designed to deal with the latest release of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/lm}{Latin 
          Modern fonts} version 1.106. Unfortunately, it can no longer support earlier versions of the fonts, 
          so an \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/old-fontch}{obsolete version of the package} is retained 
          for users who don't yet have access to the latest version of the fonts.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme and usage details}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/fontch/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/fontch/fontch.pdf}

\item[caption] Help with installing fonts for TeX and LaTeX
\item[author] Jeffrey, Alan
\index{Author!Jeffrey, Alan}
\item[author] Rahtz, Sebastian
\index{Author!Rahtz, Sebastian}
\item[author] Vieth, Ulrik
\index{Author!Vieth, Ulrik}

\index{Author!Hellström, Lars}

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.933
\item[description] (no language specified) TeX macros for converting Adobe Font Metric files to TeX metric and virtual font format. Fontinst helps 
          mainly with the number crunching and shovelling parts of font installation. This means in practice that 
          it creates a number of files which give the TeX metrics (and related information) for a font family that 
          (La)TeX needs to do any typesetting in these fonts. Fontinst furthermore makes it easy to create fonts 
          containing glyphs from more than one base font, taking advantage of (e.g.) ''expert'' font sets.

          Fontinst cannot examine files to see if they contain any useful information, nor automatically search 
          for files or work with binary file formats; those tasks must normally be done manually or with the help 
          of some other tool, such as the pltotf and vptovf programs.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package introduction}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/fontinst/doc/manual/intro98.pdf}

\section[\texttt{fontools} -- Tools to simplify using fonts (especially TT/OTF ones)]{\texttt{fontools} -- Tools to simplify using fonts (especially TT/OTF ones)}\label{pkg:fontools}
\index{Package!fontools}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontools}
\item[Alias] \texttt{autoinst}
\index{Package!autoinst (alias for fontools)}
\index{Alias!autoinst (for fontools)}
\item[name] \texttt{fontools}
\item[caption] Tools to simplify using fonts (especially TT/OTF ones)
\item[author] Penninga, Marc
\index{Author!Penninga, Marc}
\item[copyright] Marc Penninga (2005-2026)
\item[license] gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
\index{License!gpl2}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 2}
\item[version]  (2026-04-22)
\item[last changes] 2026-04-22
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides tools to simplify using OpenType fonts with LaTeX.

          By far the most important program in this bundle is autoinst:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{autoinst} – a wrapper script around Eddie Kohler’s LCDF TypeTools. Autoinst aims to automate the installation of OpenType fonts in LaTeX by calling the LCDF TypeTools (with the correct options) for all fonts you wish to install, and generating the necessary \texttt{.fd} and \texttt{.sty} files.
          \end{itemize}
In addition, this bundle contains a few other, less important utilities:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{afm2afm} – re-encode \texttt{.afm} files,
          \item  \texttt{ot2kpx} – extract kerning pairs from OpenType fonts,
          \item  \texttt{splitttc} – split an OpenType Collection file ( \texttt{ttc} or \texttt{otc} ) into individual fonts.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{autoinst documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/utilities/fontools/doc/autoinst.pdf}

\item[author] Domenjoud, Eric
\index{Author!Domenjoud, Eric}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 2.0.7
\item[description] (no language specified) The package makes bibliographic references appear as footnotes. It defines a command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}footcite} which 
          is similar to the LaTeX \texttt{{\textbackslash}cite} command but the references cited 
          in this way appear at the bottom of the pages. This ‘foot bibliography’ does not conflict with the standard 
          one and both may exist simultaneously in a document. The command \texttt{{\textbackslash}cite} may 
          still be used to produce the standard bibliography.

          The foot bibliography uses its own style and bibliographic database which may be specified independently 
          of the standard one. Any standard bibliography style may be used.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/footbib/README}

\section[\texttt{footmisc} -- A range of footnote options]{\texttt{footmisc} -- A range of footnote options}\label{pkg:footmisc}
\index{Package!footmisc}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/footmisc}
\item[name] \texttt{footmisc}
\item[caption] A range of footnote options
\item[author] Fairbairns, Robin
\index{Author!Fairbairns, Robin}
\item[author] Mittelbach, Frank
\index{Author!Mittelbach, Frank}
\item[copyright] Frank Mittelbach (2018-2025)
\item[copyright] Robin Fairbairns (1995-2011)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 7.0b (2025-05-09)
\item[last changes] 2025-05-09
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) A collection of ways to change the typesetting of footnotes. The package provides means of changing the 
          layout of the footnotes themselves (including setting them in ‘paragraphs’ — the  \texttt{para} option), 
          a way to number footnotes per page (the \texttt{perpage} option), to make footnotes disappear 
          in a ‘moving’ argument ( \texttt{stable} option) and to deal with multiple references to 
          footnotes from the same place ( \texttt{multiple} option). The package also has a range of 
          techniques for labelling footnotes with symbols rather than numbers.

          Some of the functions of the package are overlap with the functionality of other packages. The  \texttt{para} option 
          is also provided by the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/manyfoot}{manyfoot} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bigfoot}{bigfoot} packages, 
          though those are both also portmanteau packages. (Don’t be seduced by \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fnpara}{fnpara} , 
          whose implementation is improved by the present package.) The \texttt{perpage} option is 
          also offered by \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/footnpag}{footnpag} and by the rather more 
          general-purpose \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/perpage}{perpage}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/footmisc/README.md}

\item[description] (no language specified) The footnote package provides commands for handling footnotes rather more fluently than LaTeX manages. 
          Several LaTeX commands and environments (for example,  \texttt{{\textbackslash}parbox} , \texttt{minipage} and \texttt{tabular} ) 
          ''trap'' footnotes. The footnote package provides an environment \texttt{savenotes} , that 
          can be wrapped around a command or environment; at \texttt{{\textbackslash}end{\textbraceleft}savenotes{\textbraceright}} all 
          the footnotes within will emerge. The command \texttt{{\textbackslash}makesavenoteenv} will 
          generate environments that behave as if they've been wrapped in a savenotes environment.

          The package also provides  \texttt{footnote} and \texttt{footnotetext} environments 
          which you can put verbatim inside.

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mdwtools}{mdwtools} bundle.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/mdwtools/README}

\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the environments  \texttt{footnoterange} and \texttt{footnoterange*} . 
          Multiple footnotes inside these environments are not referenced as (e.g.) ''1 2 3'' but as ''1-3'', i.e., 
          the range (from first to last referred footnote at that place) is given. If the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} package 
          is loaded with enabled \texttt{hyperfootnotes} -option, then the references are hyperlinked. 
          (References to footnotes in \texttt{footnoterange*} environments are never hyperlinked.)

\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides functionality for processing lists and array structures in  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex}{LaTeX} . 
          Arrays can contain characters as well as TeX and LaTeX commands, nesting of arrays is possible, and arrays 
          are processed within the same brace level as their surrounding environment. Array levels can be delimited 
          by characters or control sequences defined by the user. Practical uses of this package include data management, 
          construction of lists and tables, and calculations based on the contents of lists and arrays.

\index{Package!forest}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/forest}
\item[name] \texttt{forest}
\item[caption] Drawing (linguistic) trees
\item[author] Živanović, Sašo
\index{Author!Živanović, Sašo}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 2.1.5 (2017-07-14)
\item[last changes] 2017-07-14
\item[year] 2017
\index{Year!2017}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides a PGF/TikZ-based mechanism for drawing linguistic (and other kinds of) trees. Its 
          main features are:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item a packing algorithm which can produce very compact trees;
          \item a user-friendly interface consisting of the familiar bracket encoding of trees plus the key-value interface to option-setting;
          \item many tree-formatting options, with control over option values of individual nodes and mechanisms for their manipulation;
          \item the possibility to decorate the tree using the full power of PGF/TikZ; and
          \item an externalization mechanism sensitive to code-changes.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/forest/README}

\section[\texttt{forms16be} -- Initialize form properties using big-endian encoding]{\texttt{forms16be} -- Initialize form properties using big-endian encoding}\label{pkg:forms16be}
\index{Package!forms16be}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/forms16be}
\item[name] \texttt{forms16be}
\item[caption] Initialize form properties using big-endian encoding
\item[author] Story, Donald P.
\index{Author!Story, Donald P.}
\item[copyright] D. P. Story (2017-2019)
\item[license] lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.2}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2}
\item[version] 1.3 (2019-03-20)
\item[last changes] 2019-03-20
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides support for UTF-16BE Unicode character encoding (called a big-endian character 
          string) for the text string type (PDF Reference, version 1.7, beginning on page 158). Text strings are 
          used in ''text annotations, bookmark names, article threads, document information, and so forth'' (to 
          partially quote page 158). The particular application is to set property values of form fields, at least 
          those properties that take the text strings as its value.

          The package contains support for Basic Latin plus the ability to enter any unicode character using the 
          notation  \texttt{{\textbackslash}uXXXX} , where \texttt{XXXX} are four 
          hex digits.

          The Package works for dvips/Distiller, pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, and XeLaTeX.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/forms16be/README.md}

\item[name] \texttt{fpl}
\item[caption] SC and OsF fonts for URW Palladio L
\item[author] Stubner, Ralf
\index{Author!Stubner, Ralf}
\item[copyright] Ralf Stubner (2004, 2005)
\item[license] gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
\index{License!gpl2}

\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.003 (2018-12-11)
\item[last changes] 2018-12-11
\item[year] 2018
\index{Year!2018}
\item[description] (no language specified) The FPL Fonts provide a set of SC/OsF fonts for URW Palladio L which are compatible with respect to metrics 
          with the Palatino SC/OsF fonts from Adobe. Note that it is not my aim to exactly reproduce the outlines 
          of the original Adobe fonts. The SC and OsF in the FPL Fonts were designed with the glyphs from URW Palladio 
          L as starting point. For some glyphs (e.g. ‘o’) I got the best result by scaling and boldening. For others 
          (e.g. ‘h’) shifting selected portions of the character gave more satisfying results. All this was done 
          using the free  \href{http://fontforge.github.io/}{font editor FontForge} . The kerning 
          data in these fonts comes from Walter Schmidt’s improved Palatino metrics.

          LaTeX use is enabled by the mathpazo package, which is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/psnfss}{psnfss} distribution.

\section[\texttt{fragoli} -- Macros for constructing complex semantic derivations]{\texttt{fragoli} -- Macros for constructing complex semantic derivations}\label{pkg:fragoli}
\index{Package!fragoli}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fragoli}
\item[name] \texttt{FraGoLi}
\item[caption] Macros for constructing complex semantic derivations
\item[author] Koenig, Paul Eduard
\index{Author!Koenig, Paul Eduard}
\item[copyright] Paul Eduard Koenig (2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.2.3 (2025-06-11)
\item[last changes] 2025-06-11
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) The primary goal of this package is to provide a minimal and user-friendly syntax for constructing large 
          and complex  \emph{semantic derivations} , following the specific notational style used at 
          Goethe University Frankfurt. It includes a comprehensive set of commands for text formatting and various 
          types of bracketing, ensuring a consistent style — particularly when distinguishing between meta-language 
          and object-language within a single derivation or formula. Formula-Style is losely based on the accompanying 
          material to an introductory course to linguistic semantics by Prof. Dr. Thomas Ede Zimmermann.

          The package brings together and refines a collection of LaTeX commands and concepts developed over the 
          years within the  \href{https://www.linguistik-in-frankfurt.de/}{Department of Linguistics} at 
          the Goethe-Universität at Frankfurt am Main. In the process of preparing research papers, assignments, 
          and examinations, numerous custom LaTeX headers and commands were shared within the department — some 
          mutually compatible, others not.

          Note: The package name is an abbreviation of ''Frankfurt Goethe Linguistic''.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/fragoli/fragoli_doc.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) The package creates three environments:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{framed} , which puts an ordinary frame box around the region,
          \item  \texttt{shaded} , which shades the region, and
          \item  \texttt{leftbar} , which places a line at the left side. The environments allow a break at their start (the \texttt{{\textbackslash}FrameCommand} enables creation of a title that is ''attached'' to the environment); breaks are also allowed in the course of the framed/shaded matter.
          \end{itemize}
There is also a command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}MakeFramed} to make your own framed-style 
          environments.

\section[\texttt{freemath} -- LaTeX maths without backslashes]{\texttt{freemath} -- LaTeX maths without backslashes}\label{pkg:freemath}
\index{Package!freemath}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/freemath}
\item[name] \texttt{freemath}
\item[caption] LaTeX maths without backslashes
\item[author] plante
\index{Author!plante}
\item[copyright] plante (2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) This package allows for the omission of backslashes from most math mode commands. Specifically, any consecutive 
          string of at least two (Latin) letters appearing in math mode will automatically be turned into the control 
          sequence with the same name, if it exists.

          The package provides the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}freemathon} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}freemathoff} commands 
          which respectively activate and deactivate this behaviour. It is \emph{disabled} by default 
          upon loading.

          Regular commands initiated by a backslash may of course still be used when freemath is active, and can 
          furthermore be freely mixed with backslash-free commands.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/freemath/README.md}

\section[\texttt{frege} -- Typeset fregean Begriffsschrift]{\texttt{frege} -- Typeset fregean Begriffsschrift}\label{pkg:frege}
\index{Package!frege}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/frege}
\item[name] \texttt{frege}
\item[caption] Typeset fregean Begriffsschrift
\item[author] Pamp, Quirin
\index{Author!Pamp, Quirin}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 1.3
\item[description] (no language specified) The package defines a number of new commands for typesetting fregean Begriffsschrift in LaTeX.

          It is loosely based on the package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/begriff}{begriff} , and 
          offers a number of improvements including better relative lengths of the content stroke with respect 
          to other strokes, content strokes that point at the middle of lines rather than the bottom, a greater 
          width for the assertion stroke as compared to the content stroke, a more intuitive structure for the 
          conditional, greater care taken to allow for the linewidth in the spacing of formulas.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frege/README}

\item[version] 1.0.0
\item[description] (no language specified) This LuaLaTeX package provides batch generation of scale and chord diagrams for plucked string instruments, 
          such as the guitar.

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \textbf{Flexible and Automated:} Highly customizable and automatable via simple, powerful file formats for describing fretboard diagrams. Easily generate batches of diagrams.
          \item  \textbf{Attractive Defaults:} Comes with sensible, visually appealing default settings.
          \item  \textbf{Music Theory Aware:} Includes easy-to-use LaTeX macros that understand music theory. Render guitar scale diagrams by specifying the musical scale or scale type via built-in macros or directly via degree, pitch class, or interval formulae.
          \end{itemize}

\item[last changes] 2024-12-18
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides an intuitive functional programming interface for LaTeX2, which is an alternative 
          choice to expl3 or LuaTeX, if you want to do programming in LaTeX.

          Although there are functions in LaTeX3 programming layer (expl3), the evaluation of them is from outside 
          to inside. With this package, the evaluation of functions is from inside to outside, which is the same 
          as other programming languages such as Lua. In this way, it is rather easy to debug code too.

\index{Package!fundus}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus}
\item[name] \texttt{fundus}
\item[caption] Providing LaTeX access to various font families
\item[author] Neugebauer, Gerd
\index{Author!Neugebauer, Gerd}
\item[license] collection = collection 
\index{License!collection}
\index{License!collection}
\item[version]  (2012-04-17)
\item[last changes] 2012-04-17
\item[year] 2012
\index{Year!2012}
\item[description] (no language specified) Fonts supported are

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Peter Vanroose’s  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/calligra}{calligra} font (package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-calligra}{fundus-calligra} );
          \item the emulation of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/script-font}{Peter Vanroose’s handwriting} (package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-pvscript}{fundus-script} ;
          \item the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/wncyr}{Washington University cyrillic} fonts (package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-cyr}{fundus-cyr} );
          \item the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/la}{ \emph{la} and \emph{lla} children's handwriting fonts} (package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-la}{fundus-la} );
          \item the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cmoutlines}{Computer Modern outline fonts} (package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-outline}{fundus-outline} );
          \item a group of ‘Startrek’ fonts (package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-startrek}{fundus-startrek} , which contains the fonts it supports;
          \item the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/sueterlin}{Sütterlin} font (package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-sueterlin}{fundus-sueterlin} );
          \item the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/twcal}{twcal} calligraphic fonts (package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-twcal}{fundus-twcal} ); and
          \item the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/va}{ \emph{va} } handwriting font (package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fundus-va}{fundus-va} ).
          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{gamebooklib} -- Macros for setting numbered entries in shuffled order]{\texttt{gamebooklib} -- Macros for setting numbered entries in shuffled order}\label{pkg:gamebooklib}
\index{Package!gamebooklib}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/gamebooklib}
\item[name] \texttt{Gamebooklib}
\item[caption] Macros for setting numbered entries in shuffled order
\item[author] Lee, Robert J
\index{Author!Lee, Robert J}
\item[copyright] Robert J Lee (2021-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.4 (2023-07-28)
\item[last changes] 2023-07-28
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides macros and environments to allow the user to typeset a series of cross-referenced, 
          numbered ''entries'', shuffled into random order, to produce an interactive novel or ''gamebook''.

          This allows entries to be written in natural order and shuffled automatically into a repeatable non-linear 
          order.

          Limited support is provided for footnotes to appear at the natural position: the end of each entry, or 
          the end of each page, whichever is closest to the footnote mark.

          This is unrelated to the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gamebook}{gamebook} package which 
          is more concerned with the formatting of entries rather than their order. The two packages can be used 
          together or separately.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/gamebooklib/gamebooklib.pdf}

\item[last changes] 2024-04-23
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) Garamond Libre is a free and open-source old-style font family. It is a ''true Garamond,'' i.e., it is 
          based off the designs of 16th-century French engraver Claude Garamond (also spelled Garamont).

          The Roman design is Garamond’s; the italics are from a design by Robert Granjon. The upright Greek font 
          is after a design by Firmin Didot; the ''italic'' Greek font is after a design by Alexander Wilson.

          The font family includes support for Latin, Greek (monotonic and polytonic) and Cyrillic scripts, as 
          well as small capitals, old-style figures, superior and inferior figures, historical ligatures, Byzantine 
          musical symbols, the IPA and swash capitals.
