\section[\texttt{gates} -- Support for writing modular and customisable code]{\texttt{gates} -- Support for writing modular and customisable code}\label{pkg:gates}
\index{Package!gates}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/gates}
\item[name] \texttt{gates}
\item[caption] Support for writing modular and customisable code
\item[author] Robbers, Yuri
\index{Author!Robbers, Yuri}
\item[author] Isambert, Paul
\index{Author!Isambert, Paul}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the means of writing code in a modular fashion: big macros or functions are divided 
          into small chunks (called gates) with names, which can be externally controlled (e.g. they can be disabled, 
          subjected to conditionals, loops...) and/or augmented with new chunks.

          Thus complex code may easily be customised without having to rewrite it, or even understand its implementation: 
          the behavior of existing gates can be modified, and new ones can be added, without endangering the whole 
          design. This allows code to be hacked in ways the original authors might have never envisioned.

          The gates package is implemented independently for both TeX and Lua. The TeX implementation, running 
          in any current environment, requires the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/texapi}{texapi} package,

\section[\texttt{gatherenum} -- A crossover of align* and enumerate]{\texttt{gatherenum} -- A crossover of align* and enumerate}\label{pkg:gatherenum}
\index{Package!gatherenum}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/gatherenum}
\item[name] \texttt{gatherenum}
\item[caption] A crossover of align* and enumerate
\item[author] Rivaud, Julien
\index{Author!Rivaud, Julien}
\item[copyright] Julien RIVAUD (2016-2019)
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[version] 1.8 (2019-09-29)
\item[last changes] 2019-09-29
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package (ab)uses the inline enumeration capabilities of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem}{enumitem} to 
          add a ''displayed'' enumeration mode, triggered by adding ‘ \texttt{gathered} ’ to the key-value 
          option list of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/enumerate}{enumerate} environment. The 
          end result is similar to a regular \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/enumerate}{enumerate} environment 
          wrapped in a \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/multicol}{multicols} environment, with the following 
          advantages:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Gathered enumerate can pack items depending on their actual width rather than a fixed, constant number per line.
          \item Gathered enumeration fills items in a line-major order (instead of column-major order), which my students found less confusing. YMMV.
          \end{itemize}
The package depends on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem}{enumitem} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse}{xparse} ,
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/gatherenum/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/gatherenum/gatherenum.pdf}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[caption] LaTeX-like markup for writing XML documents
\item[author] Hammond, William F.
\index{Author!Hammond, William F.}
\item[copyright] William F. Hammond (2001-2006)
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 0.8.4.1
\item[description] (no language specified) GELLMU is an acronym for ''Generalized Extensible LaTeX-Like MarkUp''. With GELLMU one may use LaTeX-like 
          markup to write consciously for SGML document types such as HTML, DocBook, TEI, or GELLMU's own LaTeX-like 
          document type ‘article’.

          The package provides a syntactic translator, which is the project layer for all document types.

          The article document type is very much like LaTeX with a tightly enforced syntax and vocabulary. For 
          article, the package provides translators to classic HTML, regular LaTeX and the XML form of HTML extended 
          by MathML (XHTML). The latter form provides optimal online content that is ‘accessible’ and in the author's 
          opinion superior to PDF for web presentation.

\section[\texttt{genealogytree} -- Pedigree and genealogical tree diagrams]{\texttt{genealogytree} -- Pedigree and genealogical tree diagrams}\label{pkg:genealogytree}
\index{Package!genealogytree}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/genealogytree}
\item[name] \texttt{genealogytree}
\item[caption] Pedigree and genealogical tree diagrams
\item[author] Sturm, Thomas F.
\index{Author!Sturm, Thomas F.}
\item[copyright] Prof. Dr. Dr. Thomas F. Sturm (2013-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 2.3.0 (2023-03-09)
\item[last changes] 2023-03-09
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) Pedigree and genealogical tree diagrams are proven tools to visualize genetic and relational connections 
          between individuals. The naming (''tree'') derives from historical family diagrams. However, even the 
          smallest family entity consisting of two parents and several children is hardly a ‘mathematical’ tree 
          — it is a more general graph.

          The package provides a set of tools to typeset genealogical trees (i.e., to typeset a set of special 
          graphs for the description of family-like structures). The package uses an autolayout algorithm which 
          can be customized, e.​g., to prioritize certain paths.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/genealogytree/genealogytree.pdf}

\section[\texttt{gensymb} -- Generic symbols for both text and math mode]{\texttt{gensymb} -- Generic symbols for both text and math mode}\label{pkg:gensymb}
\index{Package!gensymb}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/gensymb}
\item[name] \texttt{gensymb}
\item[caption] Generic symbols for both text and math mode
\item[author] Schmidt, Walter A.
\index{Author!Schmidt, Walter A.}
\item[author] Harcombe, Keiran
\index{Author!Harcombe, Keiran}
\item[copyright] Walter Schmidt (2003-2022)
\item[copyright] Keiran Harcombe (2022)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.0.2
\item[description] (no language specified) Provides generic commands  \texttt{{\textbackslash}degree} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}celsius} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}perthousand} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}micro} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}ohm} which 
          work both in text and maths mode. Various means are provided to fake the symbols or take them from particular 
          symbol fonts, if they are not available in the default fonts used in the document. This should be perfectly 
          transparent at user level, so that one can apply the same notation for units of measurement in text and 
          math mode and with arbitrary typefaces. Note that the package has been designed to work in conjunction 
          with \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/units}{units.sty} .

\item[license] ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
\index{License!ofl}

\item[version] 6.200
\item[description] (no language specified) This is a redistribution of the original Gentium release from SIL, not altered in any way.

          \href{https://software.sil.org/gentium/}{Gentium} is a typeface family designed to enable 
          the diverse ethnic groups around the world who use the Latin, Cyrillic and Greek scripts to produce readable, 
          high-quality publications.

          The Gentium family includes a complete Greek font, supporting both monotonic and polytonic forms. While 
          some Greek characters do closely resemble Latin ones, it is a separate design that embraces the robust, 
          distinctive character of the Greek script, but does so within the design context of the whole typeface. 
          As a result, the two scripts can be successfully mixed in a paragraph or page of text.

\section[\texttt{geometry} -- Flexible and complete interface to document dimensions]{\texttt{geometry} -- Flexible and complete interface to document dimensions}\label{pkg:geometry}
\index{Package!geometry}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry}
\item[name] \texttt{geometry}
\item[caption] Flexible and complete interface to document dimensions
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[author] Umeki, Hideo
\index{Author!Umeki, Hideo}
\item[author] Carlisle, David
\index{Author!Carlisle, David}
\item[copyright] Hideo Umeki, David Carlisle (2018-2026)
\item[copyright] Hideo Umeki (1996-2010)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 6.0 (2026-03-07)
\item[last changes] 2026-03-07
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides an easy and flexible user interface to customize page layout, implementing auto-centering 
          and auto-balancing mechanisms so that the users have only to give the least description for the page 
          layout. For example, if you want to set each margin 2cm without header space, what you need is just  \texttt{{\textbackslash}usepackage[margin=2cm,nohead]{\textbraceleft}geometry{\textbraceright}} .

          The package knows about all the standard paper sizes, so that the user need not know what the nominal 
          ‘real’ dimensions of the paper are, just its standard name (such as  \texttt{a4} , \texttt{letter} , 
          etc.).

          An important feature is the package’s ability to communicate the paper size it’s set up to the output 
          (whether via DVI  \texttt{{\textbackslash}special} s or via direct interaction with 
          pdf(La)TeX).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/geometry/README.md}
\item[documentation] \textit{Package documentation (German)}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/geometry/geometry-de.pdf}

\section[\texttt{getargs} -- A flexible list-parsing macro with configurable parsing char\ldots]{\texttt{getargs} -- A flexible list-parsing macro with configurable parsing character}\label{pkg:getargs}
\index{Package!getargs}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/getargs}
\item[name] \texttt{getargs}
\item[caption] A flexible list-parsing macro with configurable parsing character
\item[author] Segletes, Steven B.
\index{Author!Segletes, Steven B.}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.01 (2016-05-20)
\item[last changes] 2016-05-20
\item[year] 2016
\index{Year!2016}
\item[description] (no language specified) This short package provides a flexible list-parsing macro with the ability to configure the parsing character, 
          as well as the macro names in which the parsed list items are placed. The name of the parsing macro is 
          \texttt{{\textbackslash}getargs} .

          It is a significant improvement over similarly named macros in the same author’s  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/stringstrings}{stringstrings} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/readarray}{readarray} packages. 
          It is the author’s intent to eventually have the parsers of those other packages point to this package, 
          to achieve a measure of uniformity.

          Note: This package has been withdrawn by its author in July 2016. It will be replaced by the forthcoming

\index{Package!gfs}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/gfs}
\item[name] \texttt{GFS}
\item[caption] The GFS font collection
\item[author] Tsolomitis, Antonis
\index{Author!Tsolomitis, Antonis}
\item[author] The Greek Font Society
\index{Author!The Greek Font Society}
\item[author] Matthiopoulos, George D.
\index{Author!Matthiopoulos, George D.}
\item[license] other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
\index{License!other-free}
\index{License!Free license not otherwise listed}
\item[description] (no language specified) The Greek Font Society has made a large number of fonts publicly available, and this collection reflects 
          those that have been adapted, by Tsolomitis and others, for use with LaTeX. The collection comprises:

          
          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsartemisia}{GFS Artemisia} , a relatively modern general-purpose font;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsbaskerville}{GFS Baskerville} , based on Baskerville’s classic font;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsbodoni}{GFS Bodoni} , based on Bodoni’s 19th century work;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsdidot}{GFS Didot} , based on Didot’s 1805 font;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsneohellenic}{GFS Neo-Hellenic} , a version of a font developed in Britain in the early 20th century; and
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsporson}{GFS Porson} , developed from the early 19th century font based on Porson’s writing.
          \end{itemize}
The fonts, except Baskerville and Porson, support the Latin alphabet as well as the Greek alphabet. Neo 
          Hellenic has been matched to the existing  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cmbright}{CM bright} set 
          of mathematics fonts.

          new set of majuscules.

\section[\texttt{gfsdidot} -- A Greek font based on Didot’s work]{\texttt{gfsdidot} -- A Greek font based on Didot’s work}\label{pkg:gfsdidot}
\index{Package!gfsdidot}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/gfsdidot}
\item[name] \texttt{GFSDidot}
\item[caption] A Greek font based on Didot’s work
\item[author] Aubord, Alain
\index{Author!Aubord, Alain}
\item[author] The Greek Font Society
\index{Author!The Greek Font Society}
\item[author] Matthiopoulos, George D.
\index{Author!Matthiopoulos, George D.}

\item[version]  (2023-12-13)
\item[last changes] 2023-12-13
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) The design of Didot’s 1805 Greek typeface was influenced by the neoclassical ideals of the late 18th 
          century. The font was brought to Greece at the time of the 1821 Greek Revolution, by Didot’s son, and 
          was very widely used. The present version is provided by the  \href{https://greekfontsociety-gfs.gr/}{Greek 
          Font Society} .

          The font supports the Greek alphabet, and is accompanied by a matching Latin alphabet based on Zapf’s 
          Palatino. LaTeX support is provided, using the OT1, T1, TS1, and LGR encodings.

\item[description] (no language specified) The GFSNeohellenic font, a historic font first designed by Victor Scholderer, and digitized by George 
          Matthiopoulos of the Greek Font Society (GFS), now has native support for Mathematics.

          The project was commissioned to GFS by the Department of Mathematics of the University of the Aegean, 
          Samos, Greece. The Math Table was constructed by the Mathematics Professor A. Tsolomitis. A useful application 
          is in beamer documents since this is a Sans Math font.

          text and math) under the OFL license.

\item[description] (no language specified) The package builds on the standard LaTeX packages  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics}{graphics} and/or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx}{graphicx} and 
          allows external LaTeX source files to be included, in the same way as graphic files, by \texttt{{\textbackslash}includegraphics} . 
          In effect, then package adds support for the \texttt{.tex} extension.

          Some of the lower level operations like clipping and trimming are implemented using the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/adjustbox}{adjustbox} package 
          which includes native pdfLaTeX support and uses the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{pgf} package 
          for other output formats.

\item[author] Harders, Harald
\index{Author!Harders, Harald}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) If the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/inputenc}{inputenc} is used and German umlauts are 
          input directly, they are converted to the LICR representation \texttt{{\textbackslash}"a} (etc.). 
          This breaks the sort algorithm of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex}{makeindex} , 
          for instance. Ginpenc converts umlauts and the sharp-s to the short forms defined by \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} , 
          e.g., \texttt{"a} instead, if the text is typeset in German.

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/gladtex}
\item[name] \texttt{GladTeX}
\item[caption] LaTeX equations in HTML
\item[author] Humenda, Sebastian
\index{Author!Humenda, Sebastian}
\item[author] Gulbrandsen, Martin G.
\index{Author!Gulbrandsen, Martin G.}
\item[copyright] Sebastian Humenda (2013-2016)
\item[copyright] Jonathan Daugherty (2011-2013)
\item[copyright] Martin G. Gulbrandsen (1999-2010)
\item[license] lgpl3 = GNU Lesser General Public License 3 (free)
\index{License!lgpl3}
\index{License!GNU Lesser General Public License 3}
\item[version] 3.0.0
\item[description] (no language specified) GladTeX is a utility that enables LaTeX equations within HTML code. You write HTML code as usual, but 
          in addition you can include equations within the special tags  \texttt{<EQ>..</EQ>} , as 
          if within \texttt{\$\$..\$\$} in LaTeX. Then you run gladtex, which replaces 
          the equations by images. Features include image alignment (baseline of equations agree with baseline 
          of text), GIF and PNG support, transparent backgrounds and antialiasing.

          Additionally, GladTeX can aid the creation of accessible documents for the blind by providing the LaTeX 
          equation in the  \texttt{alt} attribute of an image. It also comes with a library which allows 
          embedding GladTeX into other applications.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/gladtex/README.md}

\section[\texttt{glosmathtools} -- Mathematical nomenclature tools based on the glossaries pack\ldots]{\texttt{glosmathtools} -- Mathematical nomenclature tools based on the glossaries package}\label{pkg:glosmathtools}
\index{Package!glosmathtools}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/glosmathtools}
\item[name] \texttt{glosmathtools}
\item[caption] Mathematical nomenclature tools based on the glossaries package
\item[author] Gagnon, Francis
\index{Author!Gagnon, Francis}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0.0 (2020-03-26)
\item[last changes] 2020-03-26
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package can be used to generate a mathematical nomenclature (also called ''list of symbols'' or 
          ''notation''). It is based on the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries}{glossaries} package.

          Its main features are:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item symbol categories (e.g.: latin, greek)
          \item automatic but customizable symbol sorting
          \item easy subscript management
          \item easy accentuation management
          \item abbreviation support (with first use definition)
          \item bilingual nomenclatures (for bilingual documents)
          \item bilingual abbreviations
          \end{itemize}
The documentation is based on the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ulthese}{ulthese} class.

          The package itself depends on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries}{glossaries} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts}{amsfonts} ,

\section[\texttt{glossaries} -- Create glossaries and lists of acronyms]{\texttt{glossaries} -- Create glossaries and lists of acronyms}\label{pkg:glossaries}
\index{Package!glossaries}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries}
\item[name] \texttt{glossaries}
\item[caption] Create glossaries and lists of acronyms
\item[author] Talbot, Nicola
\index{Author!Talbot, Nicola}
\item[copyright] Nicola Talbot (2007-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 5.1 (2026-04-21)
\item[last changes] 2026-04-21
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) The glossaries package supports acronyms and multiple glossaries, and has provision for operation in 
          several languages (using the facilities of either  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia}{polyglossia} ). 
          New entries are defined to have a name and description (and optionally an associated symbol). Support 
          for multiple languages is offered, and plural forms of terms may be specified. An additional package, \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries-accsupp}{glossaries-accsupp} , 
          can make use of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/accsupp}{accsupp} package mechanisms for 
          accessibility support for PDF files containing glossaries.

          The user may define new glossary styles, and preambles and postambles can be specified. There is provision 
          for loading a database of terms, but only terms used in the text will be added to the relevant glossary.

          The package uses an indexing program to provide the actual glossary; either  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex}{makeindex} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xindy}{xindy} may 
          serve this purpose, and a Perl script is provided to serve as interface.

          This package requires the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mfirstuc}{mfirstuc} package.

          The package supersedes the author’s  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/glossary}{glossary} package 
          (which is now obsolete).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/glossaries/README.md}

\section[\texttt{gmdoc} -- Documentation of LaTeX packages]{\texttt{gmdoc} -- Documentation of LaTeX packages}\label{pkg:gmdoc}
\index{Package!gmdoc}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/gmdoc}
\item[name] \texttt{gmdoc}
\item[caption] Documentation of LaTeX packages
\item[author] Murzynowski, Grzegorz

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.993
\item[description] (no language specified) A LaTeX package and an example class for documenting (La)TeX packages, document classes, .dtx etc., providing 
          hyperlinks. The package is believed to be compatible with  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/doc}{doc} and 
          permits minimal markup of code (the macrocode environment is no longer necessary). The package provides 
          automatic detection of definitions (detecting such things as \texttt{{\textbackslash}def} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}newcommand} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}DeclareOption} etc.).

          The package needs  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} and the author’s three 
          ‘basic’ packages: \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gmutils}{gmutils} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gmverb}{gmverb} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gmiflink}{gmiflink} .

          As a bonus (and as an example of doc compatibility) driver files are provided that may be used to typeset 
          the LaTeX Base.

\item[description] (no language specified) Changing the size of the typeset area is well-known to be a dangerous operation in TeX documents. This 
          package identifies the circumstances where the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}geometry} command 
          of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/geometry}{geometry} package may safely be used, (other, 
          of course, than in the preamble of a document) and provides a mechanism for using it.

          The package makes use of the author’s  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gmutils}{gmutils} package.

\item[description] (no language specified) Miscellaneous macros used by others of the author’s packages.

          Contents of the package:  \texttt{{\textbackslash}newgif} and other globals; \texttt{{\textbackslash}@ifnextcat} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}@ifXeTeX} ; \texttt{{\textbackslash}(Re)storeMacro(s)} to 
          override redefinitions; \texttt{{\textbackslash}afterfi} and friends; commands from \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/relsize}{relsize} ,

\index{License!gpl2}

\item[version] 0.9.5
\item[description] (no language specified) This package allows you to include  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gnuplot}{Gnuplot} graphs 
          in your LaTeX documents.

          The gnuplot code is extracted from the document and written to  \texttt{.gnuplot} files. 
          Then, if shell escape is used, the graph files are automatically processed to graphics or LaTeX code 
          files which will then be included in the document. If shell escape isn't used, the user will have to 
          manually convert the files by running gnuplot on the extracted \texttt{.gnuplot} files.

\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) The LaTeX package  \texttt{gobble} includes several gobble macros not included in the LaTeX 
          kernel. These macros remove a number of arguments after them, a feature regulary used inside other macros. 
          This includes gobble macros for optional arguments.

          The LaTeX package  \texttt{gobble-user} provides these macros at the user level, i.e. using 
          names without \texttt{@} so that these can be used without \texttt{{\textbackslash}makeatletter} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}makeatother} .

          The same macros are provided inside  \texttt{.tex} files for use with plain-TeX or other 
          TeX formats. However, the gobble macros for optional macros require \texttt{{\textbackslash}@ifnextchar} to 
          be defined.

\item[description] (no language specified) This package combines the tools of the graphic, subfigure and float packages in a way that makes their 
          use simpler and more robust. The  \texttt{Figure} environment (capitalized) differs from 
          the standard LaTeX figure environment by the addition of a mandatory argument to specify the caption 
          and an optional argument to be used as a label. These ensure that the \texttt{{\textbackslash}label} command 
          appears after the \texttt{{\textbackslash}caption} command to avoid the common labelling 
          error. The commands \texttt{{\textbackslash}graphfig} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}graphfig*} have 
          the additional advantage that the image will be automatically centered horizontally.

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bosisio}{bosisio} bundle.

          many earlier packages used in LaTeX 2.09. The package aims to give a consistent interface to including 
          the file types that are understood in your output, by use of ‘printer drivers’ (now known, simply, as 
          ‘drivers’). The distribution of the package contains several drivers, but others (for example,  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex-def}{pdfTeX} )

          of inserting them into a document (for example, rotation and scaling).

\section[\texttt{graphicscache} -- Cache includegraphics calls]{\texttt{graphicscache} -- Cache includegraphics calls}\label{pkg:graphicscache}
\index{Package!graphicscache}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicscache}
\item[name] \texttt{graphicscache}
\item[caption] Cache includegraphics calls
\item[author] Schwarz, Max
\index{Author!Schwarz, Max}
\item[copyright] Max Schwarz (2018-2021)
\item[license] bsd3 = 3-clause BSD License (free)
\index{License!bsd3}
\index{License!3-clause BSD License}
\item[version] 0.4 (2022-12-20)
\item[last changes] 2022-12-20
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) This LaTeX package provides caching of  \texttt{{\textbackslash}includegraphics} calls, 
          with several useful effects:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Recompilations are much faster (10x speedup observed).
          \item Images can be postprocessed with  \texttt{ghostscript} before inclusion, thus:
          \begin{itemize}
          \item Automatic downscaling to specified DPI
          \item Automatic JPEG compression with configurable quality
          \item Much smaller files (e.g. 10MB instead of 150MB)!
          \end{itemize}

          \end{itemize}
Note: Due to the one-by-one invocation of  \texttt{pdflatex} and \texttt{ghostscript} for 
          each graphics element, the first compilation is typically slower than usual.

          Note:  \texttt{graphicscache} needs the \texttt{{\textbackslash}write18} call 
          (also called shell escape). This is a security risk if you have untrusted TeX sources.

          \texttt{graphicscache} supports pdfLaTeX and LuaLaTeX; XeLaTeX is not supported.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/graphicscache/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/graphicscache/graphicscache.pdf}

\index{Package!graphicx-psmin}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[name] \texttt{graphicx-psmin}
\item[caption] Reduce size of PostScript files by not repeating images
\item[author] Adriaens, Hendri
\index{Author!Adriaens, Hendri}
\item[copyright] Hendri Adriaens (2004-2020)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The package is an extension of the standard  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-graphics}{latex-graphics} bundle 
          and provides a way to include repeated PostScript graphics (ps, eps) only once in a PostScript document. 
          This leads to smaller PostScript documents when having, for instance, a logo on every page. The package 
          only works when post-processed with \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipsk}{dvips} , which 
          should be version 5.95b or later.

          The difference for a resulting distilled PDF file is minimal (as Ghostscript and Adobe Distiller only 
          include a single copy of each graphics file, anyway).

\item[caption] Produce ‘gray hints’ to a variable text field
\item[author] Story, Donald P.
\index{Author!Story, Donald P.}
\item[license] lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.2}

\item[version]  (2018-11-01)
\item[last changes] 2018-11-01
\item[year] 2018
\index{Year!2018}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides JavaScript code snippets to create ‘gray hints’. Gray hints, as the author terms 
          them, are text that appears initially in a text field that gives a short hint as to what the contents 
          of the text field should be. For example, a text field might contain the hint ‘First Name’, or a date 
          field might read ‘yyyy/mm/dd’. As soon as the field comes into focus, the hint disappears. It reappears 
          when the field is blurred and the user did not enter any text into the field.

          The package works for dvips/Distiller, pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, and XeLaTeX.

\section[\texttt{greektonoi} -- Facilitates writing/editing of multiaccented greek]{\texttt{greektonoi} -- Facilitates writing/editing of multiaccented greek}\label{pkg:greektonoi}
\index{Package!greektonoi}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/greektonoi}
\item[name] \texttt{greektonoi}
\item[caption] Facilitates writing/editing of multiaccented greek
\item[author] Cornaros, Charalampos
\index{Author!Cornaros, Charalampos}
\item[license] lgpl3 = GNU Lesser General Public License 3 (free)
\index{License!lgpl3}
\index{License!GNU Lesser General Public License 3}
\item[version]  (2016-01-01)
\item[last changes] 2016-01-01
\item[year] 2016
\index{Year!2016}
\item[description] (no language specified) The greektonoi mapping extends the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/betababel}{betababel} package 
          or the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} polutonikogreek option to provide a simple 
          way to insert ancient Greek texts with diacritical characters into your document using a similar method 
          to the commonly used Beta Code transliteration, but with much more freedom. It is designed especially 
          for the XeTeX engine and it could also be used for fast and easy modification of monotonic greek texts 
          to polytonic. The output text is natively encoded in Unicode, so it can be reused in any possible way. 
          The \texttt{greektonoi} package provides, in addition to inserting greek accents and breathings, 
          many other symbols used in greek numbers and arithmetic or in the greek archaic period. It could be used 
          with greektonoi mapping or indepedently.
\item[documentation] \textit{Package documentation (Greek)}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/greek/greektonoi/greektonoi.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) Grid setting — also known as strict in-register setting — is something, that should be done for a lot 
          of documents but is not easy using LaTeX. The package helps to get the information needed for grid setting. 
          It does not implement auto grid setting, but there is a command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}vskipnextgrid} , 
          that moves to the next grid position. This may be enough under some circumstances, but in other circumstances 
          it may fail. Thus gridset is only one more step for grid setting, not a complete solution.

\section[\texttt{gtex-letter} -- A Gnome assistant to ease the writing of LaTeX letters]{\texttt{gtex-letter} -- A Gnome assistant to ease the writing of LaTeX letters}\label{pkg:gtex-letter}
\index{Package!gtex-letter}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/gtex-letter}
\item[name] \texttt{gtex-letter}
\item[caption] A Gnome assistant to ease the writing of LaTeX letters
\item[author] Folini, Christian
\index{Author!Folini, Christian}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) A good looking interface, based on the gnome-desktop. Serial letters are supported. Multiple letter headers 
          can be accessed from within the application. Standard openings and default closings can be configured. 
          These openings can be configured to adopt to the sex of the addressee automatically.

          You can choose from three different user interfaces. Novice is very easy for the beginner, intermediate 
          is the standard way, expert is straight forward, all on one big page.

          The application can swallow text you pipe into it, being it the address or the text of the letter. A 
          special non-interactive mode lets you produce standard-letters in an extremely efficient way.

          gtex-letter connects to the gnome-address-book from the gnome-pim package.

          gtex-letter is implemented in python and based on gnome.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/gtex-letter/manual/html/index.html}

          seul, en autodidacte. C’est pourquoi j’ai réuni toutes mes connaissances actuelles sur LaTeX dans ce

          more handsome documents. Lots of examples are provided all along this guide.

          into four lessons and it has been written for people without any previous knowledge of LaTeX. It has 
          been successfully tested on Windows and *nix platforms.

          The class  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/guitbeamer}{guitbeamer} is needed to run the presentations. 
          Documentation is only available in Italian.
\item[description] (Italian) Viene qui presentato il materiale realizzato per il corso ''Introduzione al mondo di LaTeX'' tenuto dai 
          membri del Gruppo Utilizzatori Italiani di TeX e destinato a chiunque abbia in animo di organizzare un 
          corso ma non trovi il tempo e/o la voglia necessaria per allestire tutto il materiale. Il corso è articolato 
          in quattro lezioni ed è rivolto a discenti senza alcuna conoscenza pregressa di LaTeX e/o linguaggi di 
          programmazione. Esso può essere svolto sia per piattaforme Windows che *nix, essendo stato sperimentato 
          con successo su entrambi i sistemi.

          Le presentazioni a video sono realizzate sulla base della classe  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/guitbeamer}{guitbeamer} sviluppata 
          da Emiliano Giovanni Vavassori e disponibile su CTAN.

          Likewise, commands are provided that simplify the writing of the GuIT acronym’s complete expansion, of 
          the addresses of the group’s internet site and public forum, and the meeting ‘GuITmeeting’ and the magazine 
          Ars TeXnica’s logo.

          Optionally, using  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} , the outputs of the 
          above cited commands can become hyperlinks to the group’s website \href{https://www.guitex.org}{https://www.guitex.org} .

          The Documentation is available in Italian only.

\item[last changes] 2024-03-09

\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This bundle provides two classes and BibLaTeX styles for the French journal  \href{http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/Gazette/}{''La 
          Gazette des Mathématiciens''} :

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{gzt} for the complete issues of the journal, aimed at the Gazette’s team,
          \item  \texttt{gztarticle} , intended for authors who wish to publish an article in the Gazette. This class’s goals are to
          \begin{itemize}
          \item faithfully reproduce the layout of the Gazette, thus enabling the authors to be able to work their document in actual conditions, and
          \item provide a number of tools (commands and environments) to facilitate the drafting of documents, in particular those containing mathematical formulas.
          \end{itemize}

          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{har2nat} -- Replace the harvard package with natbib]{\texttt{har2nat} -- Replace the harvard package with natbib}\label{pkg:har2nat}
\index{Package!har2nat}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/har2nat}
\item[name] \texttt{har2nat}
\item[caption] Replace the harvard package with natbib
\item[author] Straathof, Bas
\index{Author!Straathof, Bas}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) This small package allows a LaTeX document containing the citation commands provided by the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/harvard}{Harvard} package 
          to be compiled using the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/natbib}{natbib} package. Migration 
          from harvard to natbib thus can be achieved simply by replacing

          \begin{verbatim}
\usepackage{harvard}
          \end{verbatim}
with

          \begin{verbatim}
usepackage{natbib}
usepackage{har2nat}
          \end{verbatim}
It is important that har2nat be loaded after natbib, since it modifies natbib commands.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/har2nat/har2nat.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./6336765370-har2nat.pdf|

\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/har2nat}

\section[\texttt{harvard} -- Harvard citation package for use with LaTeX 2e]{\texttt{harvard} -- Harvard citation package for use with LaTeX 2e}\label{pkg:harvard}
\index{Package!harvard}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/harvard}
\item[name] \texttt{harvard}
\item[caption] Harvard citation package for use with LaTeX 2e
\item[author] Williams, Peter
\index{Author!Williams, Peter}
\item[author] Schnier, Thorsten
\index{Author!Schnier, Thorsten}
\item[copyright] Peter Williams (1994)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 2.0.5
\item[description] (no language specified) This is a re-implementation, for LaTeX 2e, of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/harvard-obsolete}{original 
          Harvard package} . The bundle contains the LaTeX package, several BibTeX styles, and a ‘Perl package’ 
          for use with \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex2html}{LaTeX2HTML} .

          Harvard is an author-year citation style (all but the first author are suppressed in second and subsequent 
          citations of the same entry); the package defines several variant styles:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{apsr.bst} for the American Political Science Review;
          \item  \texttt{agsm.bst} for Australian Government publications;
          \item  \texttt{dcu.bst} from the Design Computing Unit of the University of Sydney;
          \item  \texttt{kluwer.bst} which aims at the format preferred in Kluwer publications;
          \item  \texttt{nederlands.bst} which deals with sorting Dutch names with prefixes (such as \texttt{van} ) according to Dutch rules,
          \item together with several styles whose authors offer no description of their behaviour.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/harvard/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/harvard/harvard.pdf}

\index{Package!hecthese}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/hecthese}
\item[name] \texttt{hecthese}
\item[caption] A class for dissertations and theses at HEC Montréal
\item[author] Hamel, Benoit
\index{Author!Hamel, Benoit}
\item[copyright] HEC Montreal (2017-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}

\item[version] 3.0 (2026-04-20)
\item[last changes] 2026-04-20
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides the  \texttt{hecthese} class, a class based on \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/memoir}{memoir} and 
          compatible with LaTeX.

          Using this class, postgraduate students at HEC Montréal will be able to write their dissertation or thesis 
          while complying with all the presentation standards required by the University.

          This class is meant to be as flexible as possible; in particular, there are very few hardcoded features 
          except those that take care of the document’s layout.

          Dissertations and theses at HEC Montréal can be written on a per-chapter or per-article basis. Documents 
          that are written on a per-article basis require a bibliography for each of the included articles and 
          a general bibliography for the entire document. The  \texttt{hecthese} class takes care of 
          these requirements.

\section[\texttt{helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation} -- Beautiful in-line microtonal just intonation accidentals]{\texttt{helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation} -- Beautiful in-line microtonal just intonation accidentals}\label{pkg:helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation}
\index{Package!helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation}
\item[name] \texttt{helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation}
\item[caption] Beautiful in-line microtonal just intonation accidentals
\item[author] Nicholson, Thomas
\index{Author!Nicholson, Thomas}
\item[copyright] Thomas Nicholson (2020)
\item[license] cc-by-4 = CC BY 4.0 (free)
\index{License!cc-by-4}
\index{License!CC BY 4.0}
\item[version] 1.1 (2020-05-19)
\item[last changes] 2020-05-19
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) The Helmholtz-Ellis JI Pitch Notation (HEJI), devised in the early 2000s by Marc Sabat and Wolfgang von 
          Schweinitz, explicitly notates the raising and lowering of the  \emph{untempered} diatonic 
          Pythagorean notes by specific microtonal ratios defined for each prime. It provides visually distinctive 
          ''logos'' distinguishing families of justly tuned intervals that relate to the harmonic series. These 
          take the form of strings of additional accidental symbols based on historical precedents, extending the 
          traditional sharps and flats. Since its 2020 update, HEJI ver. 2 (''HEJI2'') provides unique microtonal 
          symbols through the 47-limit.

          This package is a simple LaTeX implementation of HEJI2 that allows for in-line typesetting of microtonal 
          accidentals for use within theoretical texts, program notes, symbol legends, etc.

          Documents must be compiled using  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xetex}{XeLaTeX} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./1523872656-helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation/README.md}
\item[home page] \url{http://plainsound.org/}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/helmholtz-ellis-ji-notation}

\item[description] (no language specified) Hepnames provides a pair of LaTeX packages, heppennames and hepnicenames, providing a large set of pre-defined 
          high energy physics particle names built with the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hepparticles}{hepparticles} package. 
          The packages are based on \texttt{pennames.sty} by Michel Goosens and Eric van Herwijnen.

          Heppennames re-implements the particle names in pennames.sty, with some additions and alterations and 
          greater flexibility and robustness due to the hepparticles structures, which were written for this purpose.

          Hepnicenames provides the main non-resonant particle names from heppennames with more ''friendly'' names.

\section[\texttt{hepparticles} -- Macros for typesetting high energy physics particle names]{\texttt{hepparticles} -- Macros for typesetting high energy physics particle names}\label{pkg:hepparticles}
\index{Package!hepparticles}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/hepparticles}
\item[name] \texttt{HEPparticles}
\item[caption] Macros for typesetting high energy physics particle names
\item[author] Buckley, Andy
\index{Author!Buckley, Andy}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 2.0
\item[description] (no language specified) HEPparticles is a set of macros for typesetting high energy particle names, to meet the following criteria:

          1. The main particle name is a Roman or Greek symbol, to be typeset in upright font in normal contexts.

          2. Additionally a superscript and/or subscript may follow the main symbol.

          3. Particle resonances may also have a resonance specifier which is typeset in parentheses following 
          the main symbol. In general the parentheses may also be followed by sub- and superscripts.

          4. The particle names are expected to be used both in and out of mathematical contexts.

          5. If the surrounding text is bold or italic then the particle name should adapt to that context as best 
          as possible (this may not be possible for Greek symbols).

          A consequence of point 5 is that the well-known problems with boldness of particle names in section titles, 
          headers and tables of contents automatically disappear if these macros are used.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hepparticles/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hepparticles/hepparticles.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./4358153215-hepparticles.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hepparticles}

\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}

\item[description] (no language specified) Hepthesis is a LaTeX class for typesetting large academic reports, in particular PhD theses. It was originally 
          developed for typesetting the author’s high-energy physics PhD thesis and includes some features specifically 
          tailored to such an application. In particular, hepthesis offers:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Attractive semantic environments for various rubric sections;
          \item Extensive options for draft production, screen viewing and binding-ready output;
          \item Helpful extensions of existing environments, including equation and tabular; and
          \item Support for quotations at the start of the thesis and each chapter.
          \end{itemize}
The class is based on scrbook, from the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script}{KOMA-Script} bundle.

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)

\item[version] 2.0.0

\item[description] (no language specified) The command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}hhline} produces a line like \texttt{{\textbackslash}hline} , 
          or a double line like \texttt{{\textbackslash}hline{\textbackslash}hline} , except 
          for its interaction with vertical lines. The command takes a preamble (rather like the preamble of a 
          tabular environment), and this specifies whether there are to be one or two horizontal lines, and what 
          happens when the horizontal line meets a vertical one.

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools}{latex-tools} bundle 
          in the LaTeX \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/required}{required} distribution.

\item[author] Wintz, Paul

\item[copyright] pwintz (2025)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) This package introduces an alternate proof environment,  \texttt{proof*} , which conditionally 
          hides or shows its contents based on the document mode ( \texttt{draft} , \texttt{final} , 
          or default). This is useful for omitting formal proofs from draft versions while retaining them in final 
          documents.

          The motivation for this package is to reduce the clutter in large files by omitting long proofs, allowing 
          authors to focus their attention on results or proofs that are currently works in progress.

\item[version] 1.5
\item[description] (no language specified) The hieroglf bundle provides a Type 1 renidition of some of the ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs. Hieroglyphic 
          writing was used between about 3000 BC and 400 AD.

          The bundle is based on Serge Rosmorduc's comprehensive  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hieroglyph}{hieroglyph} package, 
          but only provides about one tenth of his 650-odd hieroglyphs. Sufficient glyphs are provided for writing 
          a few names like Cleopatra or Ptolomeny (together with cartouches) and some numbers, but the package 
          is not for serious Egyptologists.

          The bundle is part of a  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/archaic}{set of archaic fonts} , 
          and requires use of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/oands}{oands} fonts from that set.

\section[\texttt{hitex} -- A TeX extension writing HINT output for on-screen reading]{\texttt{hitex} -- A TeX extension writing HINT output for on-screen reading}\label{pkg:hitex}
\index{Package!hitex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/hitex}
\item[Alias] \texttt{HINT}
\index{Package!HINT (alias for hitex)}
\index{Alias!HINT (for hitex)}
\item[name] \texttt{hitex}
\item[caption] A TeX extension writing HINT output for on-screen reading
\item[author] Ruckert, Martin
\index{Author!Ruckert, Martin}
\item[copyright] Martin Ruckert (null)
\item[license] x11 = X11 License (free)
\index{License!x11}
\index{License!X11 License}
\item[description] (no language specified) An extension of TeX which generates HINT output.

          The HINT file format is an alternative to the DVI and PDF formats which was designed specifically for 
          on-screen reading of documents. Especially on mobile devices, reading DVI or PDF documents can be cumbersome. 
          Mobile devices are available in a large variety of sizes but typically are not large enough to display 
          documents formated for a4/letter-size paper. To compensate for the limitations of a small screen, users 
          are used to alternating between landscape (few long lines) and portrait (more short lines) mode.

          The HINT format supports variable and varying screen sizes, leveraging the ability of TeX to format a 
          document for nearly-arbitrary values of  \texttt{{\textbackslash}hsize} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}vsize} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{HiTeX documentation, in both PDF and HINT formats}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/systems/doc/hitex}

\item[last changes] 2025-04-07

\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package allows for typing in Hittite cuneiform in LaTeX documents, using relatively simple commands 
          based on the Latin transcriptions of the various signs. It also includes some formatting commands designed 
          to allow for easy formatting of heterographic compounds, as well as shorthands for symbols commonly used 
          in transcriptions.

          The  \texttt{UllikummiA.ttf} , \texttt{UllikummiB.ttf} , and \texttt{UllikummiC.ttf} files 
          comprise the Ullikummi Hittite cuneiform fonts developed by Dr Sylvie Vanséveren, distributed with written 
          permission from Dr Vanséveren, available on Hethitologie Portal Mainz at \href{https://www.hethport.uni-wuerzburg.de/cuneifont/}{https://www.hethport.uni-wuerzburg.de/cuneifont/} .

          defined a mechanism for concatenating multiple files into a single file for faster loading.

          The disadvantage is that it introduces hard dependencies between the source files that are included and 
          complicates distribution and updates.

          It was principally used with  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} but is not 
          currently used in any standard packages in TeX Live.

          The packages are still distributed as simple stubs that reference the included packages via  \texttt{{\textbackslash}RequirePackage} rather 
          than copying their source.

          The documented source of the original packages is available at  \href{https://github.com/ho-tex/hobsub}{github} , 
          but is not distributed to CTAN.

\item[author] XU, Jinwen

\item[version]  (2024-09-30)
\item[last changes] 2024-09-30

\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The current document class is for writing homework. It has the following features.

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Simple and clear interface.
          \item Built-in support for many theorem-type environments, already configured and ready to use.
          \item Multilingual support.
          \item Page numbers are of the form ''Page [current] of [total]'', which can help you ensure that there are no missing pages when you print your homework for submission.
          \item Support writing problem statements and solutions (or proofs) in different colors.
          \item Every statement and solution has its own QED symbol, in hollow or solid shape, respectively.
          \item You can mark the unfinished parts, and a report shall be generated at the end of your document for reminding.
          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{hook-pre-commit-pkg} -- Pre-commit git hook for LaTeX package developpers]{\texttt{hook-pre-commit-pkg} -- Pre-commit git hook for LaTeX package developpers}\label{pkg:hook-pre-commit-pkg}
\index{Package!hook-pre-commit-pkg}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/hook-pre-commit-pkg}
\item[name] \texttt{hook-pre-commit-pkg}
\item[caption] Pre-commit git hook for LaTeX package developpers
\item[author] Rouquette, Maïeul
\index{Author!Rouquette, Maïeul}
\item[copyright] Maïeul Rouquette (2014-2016)
\item[license] gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
\index{License!gpl3}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3}
\item[version] 1.1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a pre-commit git hook to check basic LaTeX syntax for the use of package developers.

          It is installed by copying it into the  \texttt{.git/.hooks} file.

          It then checks the following file types:  \texttt{.sty} , \texttt{.dtx} , \texttt{.bbx} , \texttt{.cbx} , 
          and \texttt{.lbx} .

          List of performed checks:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Each line must be terminated by a  \texttt{\%} , without a space before it. Empty lines are allowed, but not lines with nothing but spaces in them.
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}macro{\textbraceright}} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}end{\textbraceleft}macro{\textbraceright}} must be paired.
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}macrocode{\textbraceright}} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}end{\textbraceleft}macrocode{\textbraceright}} must be paired.
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}macro{\textbraceright}} must have a second argument.
          \item One space must be printed between  \texttt{\%} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}macro{\textbraceright}} or \texttt{{\textbackslash}end{\textbraceleft}macro{\textbraceright}} . \texttt{\%} must be the first character in the line.
          \item Four spaces must be printed between  \texttt{\%} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}macrocode{\textbraceright}} or \texttt{{\textbackslash}end{\textbraceleft}macrocode{\textbraceright}} .
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}cs} argument must not start with a backslash.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation] \textit{Tutorial (French)}: \url{http://geekographie.maieul.net/Hook-de-pre-commit-pour-fichier}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/hook-pre-commit-pkg/README}
\item[contact] \textit{repository}: \url{https://github.com/maieul/git-hooks}
\index{Contact!repository}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/hook-pre-commit-pkg}
\item[on \TeX Live] \texttt{hook-pre-commit-pkg}
\item[keyword] \texttt{package-devel} (support for package development)

\index{Package!hrefhide}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/hrefhide}
\item[name] \texttt{hrefhide}
\item[caption] Suppress hyper links when printing
\item[author] Münch, Hans-Martin
\index{Author!Münch, Hans-Martin}
\item[copyright] H.-Martin Münch (2010-2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.1b (2025-01-27)
\item[last changes] 2025-01-27
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides the command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}hrefdisplayonly} (additionally 
          to \texttt{{\textbackslash}href} provided by the hyperref package). While the (hyperlinked) 
          text appears like an ordinary \texttt{{\textbackslash}href} in the compiled pdf-file, 
          the same text will be ''hidden'' when printing the text. Hiding is actually achieved by making the text 
          the same colour as the background, thus preserving the layout of the rest of the text.

          Further the commands  \texttt{{\textbackslash}hycon} and {\textbackslash}hycoff 
          (hyper-colour-on/off) can be used to simulate switching option \texttt{ocgcolorlinks} of 
          the hyperref package on and off.

          This package is possibly obsolete, see section 3: ''Alternatives'' in the documentation.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hrefhide/hrefhide.pdf}

\item[name] \texttt{huaz}
\item[caption] Automatic definite articles for Hungarian
\item[author] Tómács, Tibor
\index{Author!Tómács, Tibor}
\item[copyright] Tibor Tómács (2022-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}

\item[version] 2.1 (2024-05-05)
\item[last changes] 2024-05-05
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) In Hungarian there are two definite articles, ''a'' and ''az'', which are determined by the pronunciation 
          of the subsequent word. The definite article is ''az'', if the first phoneme of the pronounced word is 
          a vowel, otherwise it is ''a''. The  \texttt{huaz} package helps the user to insert automatically 
          the correct definite article for cross-references and other commands containing text.

          It is commonly used for demonstrating the textual elements of a document template.

          \emph{Lórum ipse} is a Hungarian variation of \emph{Lorem ipsum} . ( \emph{Lórum} is 
          a Hungarian card game, and \emph{ipse} is a Hungarian slang word meaning \emph{bloke} .) 
          With this package you can typeset 150 paragraphs of \emph{Lórum ipse} .

          All paragraphs are taken with permission from  \href{http://www.lorumipse.hu}{http://www.lorumipse.hu} . 
          Thanks to \emph{Lórum Ipse Lab} (Viktor Nagy and Dávid Takács) for their work.

\index{License!lppl}

\item[description] (no language specified) Definitions of horizontal and vertical dashed lines for the array and tabular environment. Instead of 
          building partial horizontal dashed lines using Isozaki's {\textbackslash}cline{\textbraceleft}2-3{\textbraceright}, 
          {\textbackslash}hdashline fills the full width. The proportion of the dashed line is defined by 
          the two parameters: {\textbackslash}hdashlinewidth=2pt and {\textbackslash}hdashlinegap=2pt, 
          where the former defines the width of the dash and the latter sets their gap.

          Note that this functionality has been re-implemented, for current LaTeX, in the package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/arydshln}{arydshln} .

\item[description] (no language specified) This package defines a macro to place objects (tables and figures) and their captions in different positions 
          with different rotating angles within a float. All objects and captions can be framed. The main command 
          is  \texttt{{\textbackslash}hvFloat{\textbraceleft}float type{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}floating 
          object{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}caption{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}label{\textbraceright}} ; 
          a simple example is \texttt{{\textbackslash}hvFloat{\textbraceleft}figure{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}includegraphics{\textbraceleft}rose{\textbraceright}{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}Caption{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}fig:0{\textbraceright}} . 
          Options are provided to place captions to the right or left, and rotated. Setting nonFloat=true results 
          in placing the float here.

\section[\texttt{hwkatakana} -- Half-width katakana fonts]{\texttt{hwkatakana} -- Half-width katakana fonts}\label{pkg:hwkatakana}
\index{Package!hwkatakana}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/hwkatakana}
\item[name] \texttt{hwkatakana}
\item[caption] Half-width katakana fonts
\item[author] Hassenpflug, Gernot
\index{Author!Hassenpflug, Gernot}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) Half-width katakana Type 1 fonts in SJIS encoding are provided to integrate with the Wadalab fonts for 
          use with, for example, the CJK package. Auxiliary files to use the font with Unicode UTF8 encoding are 
          also provided. The origin of the font is the Wadalab gothic font katakana glyphs, which have been modified 
          to make up the JIS X 0201 set of half-width katakana characters using Fontforge. The  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/wadalab}{Wadalab} fonts 
          need to be available for this package to work.

\item[description] (no language specified) The package offers a solution to the problem that when you link to a float using  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} , 
          the link anchors to below the float’s caption, rather than the beginning of the float.

          Hypcap defines a separate  \texttt{{\textbackslash}capstart} command, which you put 
          where you want links to end; you should have a \texttt{{\textbackslash}capstart} command 
          for each \texttt{{\textbackslash}caption} command. Package options can be used to auto-insert 
          a \texttt{{\textbackslash}capstart} at the start of a float environment.

\item[description] (no language specified) HyperLaTeX defines a form of LaTeX that may be processed in the ordinary way with a  \texttt{latex} command, 
          for printed output. However, HyperLaTeX documents may also be processed by the program \texttt{hyperlatex} to 
          produce good-quality HTML.

          HyperLaTeX is not a LaTeX to HTML converter (see, for example,  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tth}{tth} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex2html}{latex2html} for 
          that). Rather, HyperLaTeX provides an environment where the author can prepare a document that may be 
          converted to either print or HTML output.

          defined for HyperTeX DVI processors; for embedded \texttt{pdfmark} commands for processing 
          by Acrobat Distiller ( \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvips}{dvips} and Y\&amp;Y’s dvipsone);

          for \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tex4ht}{TeX4ht} ; and for VTeX’s pdf and HTML backends.

          The package is distributed with the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/backref}{backref} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/nameref}{nameref} packages, 
          which make use of the facilities of hyperref.

\section[\texttt{hyperxmp} -- Embed XMP metadata within a LaTeX document]{\texttt{hyperxmp} -- Embed XMP metadata within a LaTeX document}\label{pkg:hyperxmp}
\index{Package!hyperxmp}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperxmp}
\item[name] \texttt{hyperxmp}
\item[caption] Embed XMP metadata within a LaTeX document
\item[author] Pakin, Scott
\index{Author!Pakin, Scott}
\item[copyright] Scott Pakin (2011-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 5.13
\item[description] (no language specified) XMP (eXtensible Metadata Platform) is a mechanism proposed by Adobe for embedding document metadata within 
          the document itself. The metadata is designed to be easy to extract, even by programs that are oblivious 
          to the document's file format. Most of Adobe's applications store  \texttt{XMP} metadata 
          when saving files. Now, with the hyperxmp package, it is trivial for LaTeX document authors to store \texttt{XMP} metadata 
          in their documents as well.

          The package integrates seamlessly with  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} and 
          requires virtually no modifications to documents that already exploit hyperref's mechanisms for specifying 
          PDF metadata. The current version of hyperxmp can embed the following metadata as \texttt{XMP} : 
          title, authors, primary author's title or position, metadata writer, subject/summary, keywords, copyright, 
          license URL, document base URL, document identifier and instance identifier, language, source file name, 
          PDF generating tool, PDF version, and contact telephone number/postal address/email address/URL. Hyperxmp 
          currently embeds \texttt{XMP} only within PDF documents; it is compatible with pdfLaTeX, 
          XeLaTeX, LaTeX+dvipdfm, and LaTeX+dvips+ps2pdf.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/hyperxmp/hyperxmp.pdf}

\section[\texttt{hyph-utf8} -- Hyphenation patterns expressed in UTF-8]{\texttt{hyph-utf8} -- Hyphenation patterns expressed in UTF-8}\label{pkg:hyph-utf8}
\index{Package!hyph-utf8}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyph-utf8}
\item[name] \texttt{hyph-utf8}
\item[caption] Hyphenation patterns expressed in UTF-8
\item[author] Rosendahl, Arthur
\index{Author!Rosendahl, Arthur}
\item[author] Hosny, Khaled
\index{Author!Hosny, Khaled}
\item[author] Miklavec, Mojca
\index{Author!Miklavec, Mojca}
\item[author] Roux, Élie
\index{Author!Roux, Élie}
\item[author] Pégourié-Gonnard, Manuel
\index{Author!Pégourié-Gonnard, Manuel}
\item[copyright] TeX Users Group (2008-2025)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version]  (2025-01-20)
\item[last changes] 2025-01-20
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) Modern native UTF-8 engines such as XeTeX and LuaTeX need hyphenation patterns in UTF-8 format, whereas 
          older systems require hyphenation patterns in the 8-bit encoding of the font in use (such encodings are 
          codified in the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/encguide}{LaTeX scheme} with names like OT1, 
          T2A, TS1, OML, LY1, etc).

          The present package offers a collection of conversions of existing patterns to UTF-8 format, together 
          with converters for use with 8-bit fonts in older systems. Since hyphenation patterns for Knuthian-style 
          TeX systems are only read at iniTeX time, it is hoped that the UTF-8 patterns, with their converters, 
          will completely supplant the older patterns.
\item[documentation]  (English) \textit{Main documentation for hyph-utf8}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/hyph-utf8/doc/hyph-utf8.pdf}

\item[caption] A document class for IACR journal publications
\item[author] McCurley, Kevin
\index{Author!McCurley, Kevin}
\item[copyright] Joppe W. Bos; Kevin S. McCurley (2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.9.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The iacrj document class is used to produce publications for three IACR journals. It is intended as an 
          eventual replacement for iacrcc.cls and iacrtrans.cls. It can be used to produce publications for IACR 
          Communications in Cryptology, IACR Transactions on Symmetric Cryptology, and IACR Transactions on Cryptographic 
          Hardware and Embedded Systems.

          iacrj.cls is part of a larger set of tools for implementing a journal publishing workflow, and it depends 
          on the metacapture.sty package. There is also a companion open source implementation of a publishing 
          workflow written in Python that is used for this journal and provides a simplified workflow for copy 
          editing and production. Further information on this workflow can be found in two articles that were published 
          by the authors:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10424}{Lowering the Cost of Diamond Open Access Journals} ,
          \item  \href{https://tug.org/TUGboat/tb46-3/tb144bos-workflow.html}{A LaTeX publishing workflow} 
          \end{itemize}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package allows you to check whether a string is contained within another set of strings, and perform 
          an action if it is not. This is done by using the  \texttt{allfalse} environment and passing 
          in a string and an action to be performed if the string is not contained in the set. Then, passing in 
          a string to the \texttt{{\textbackslash}orcheck} macro inside the respective \texttt{allfalse} environment 
          adds that to the set of strings.

\item[last changes] 2016-05-16

\item[description] (no language specified) The package defines commands that switch according to the prevailing ‘draft’ or ‘final’ options; each 
          command takes two arguments, the first for the ‘true’, the second for the ‘false’ case. Commands are:

          
          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifdraft} determines whether we're operating in draft (‘true’) or final mode;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifoptiondraft} determines whether a ‘draft’ option has been given; and
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifoptionfinal} determines whether a ‘final’ option has been given.
          \end{itemize}

\item[caption] Utility macro: peek ahead without ignoring spaces
\item[author] Lück, Uwe

\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.3
\item[description] (no language specified) The package deals with the behaviour of the LaTeX internal command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}@ifnextchar} , 
          which skips blank spaces. This has the potential to surprise users, since it can produce really unwanted 
          effects. A common example occurs with brackets starting a line following \texttt{{\textbackslash}{\textbackslash}} : 
          the command looks for an optional argument, whereas the user wants the brackets to be printed.

          The package offers commands and options for modifying this behaviour, maybe limited to certain parts 
          of the document source.

          (Unix environment over a windows system).

          Booleans provided are:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifwindows} ,
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}iflinux} ,
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifmacosx} and
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifcygwin} .
          \end{itemize}
The package also preserves the output of  \texttt{uname} on a Unix-like system, which may 
          be used to distinguish between various classes of Unix systems.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ifplatform/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ifplatform/ifplatform.pdf}

\item[version] 0.62
\item[description] (no language specified) This package is based on the package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/go}{go} written in 1991 
          by Hanna Kołodziejska which provides typesetting facilities for Go games and positions. Although igo 
          contains roughly the same commands as the original package and uses the fonts created by Kołodziejska, 
          it has been improved in a number of ways. It uses command names less likely to conflict with standard 
          AMS packages. It allows different board sizes to be used. It understands a standardized notation for 
          board coordinates. And it provides a facility to work on more than one board. Moreover, a few commands 
          were reworked to define positions or game sequences more conveniently.

\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/iitem}
\item[name] \texttt{iitem}
\item[caption] Multiple level of lists in one list-like environment
\item[author] Vitecek, Ben
\index{Author!Vitecek, Ben}
\item[copyright] Ben Vitecek (2013)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The package defines multiple level lists within one list-like environment. instead of writing 
          \begin{verbatim}
\begin{enumerate}
\item 1
\begin{enumerate}
\item 2
\begin{enumerate}
\item 3
\begin{enumerate}
\item 4
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\item 2.1
\end{enumerate}
\item 1.1
\begin{enumerate}
\item 2
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
          \end{verbatim}
this package allows you to write
          \begin{verbatim}
\begin{enumerate}
\item 1
\iitem 2
\iiitem 3
\ivtem 4
\iitem 2.1
\item 1.1
\iitem 2
\end{enumerate}
          \end{verbatim}

\item[last changes] 2025-02-06

\item[description] (no language specified) This is a reimplementation of LaTeX’s indexing macros to provide better support for indexing. For example, 
          it supports multiple indexes in a single document and provides a more robust  \texttt{{\textbackslash}index} command. 
          It supplies short hand notations for the \texttt{{\textbackslash}index} command ( \texttt{{\textasciicircum}{\textbraceleft}word{\textbraceright}} ) 
          and a \texttt{*} variation of \texttt{{\textbackslash}index} (abbreviated \texttt{\_{\textbraceleft}word{\textbraceright}} ) 
          that prints the word being indexed, as well as creating an index entry for it.

\item[last changes] 2023-10-14
