\item[description] (no language specified) This package enables the user to produce and typeset one or more indices simultaneously.

          The package is known to work in LaTeX documents processed with pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX. If  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex}{makeindex} is 
          used for processing the index entries, no particular setup is needed when TeX Live is used. Using \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xindy}{xindy} or 
          other programs, it is necessary to enable shell escape. Shell escape is also needed if \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/splitindex}{splitindex} is 
          used.

          This is a fork of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/imakeidx}{imakeidx} , with new features 
          and fixed bugs.

\item[description] (no language specified) Adobe Type 1 version of public Metafont fonts (from CTAN) for 10 Indic scripts: Devanagari, Sanskrit, 
          Gurmukhi/Punjabi, Bangla, Tamil, Sinhala, Malayalam, Kannada, Telugu, Tibetan.

          The fonts derive from an accurate analytic conversion to outlines using MetaPost output, with subsequent 
          optimization and autohinting with FontForge.

          The package contains the PFB and map files for 122 fonts, the copies of the TFM files have been also 
          included to allow testing the fonts without the original packages.

          For font tables, proofsheet files and other information see the package home page.

\section[\texttt{inlinedef} -- Inline expansions within definitions]{\texttt{inlinedef} -- Inline expansions within definitions}\label{pkg:inlinedef}
\index{Package!inlinedef}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/inlinedef}
\item[name] \texttt{inlinedef}
\item[caption] Inline expansions within definitions
\item[author] Hicks, Stephen
\index{Author!Hicks, Stephen}
\item[copyright] Stephen D. Hicks (2008)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides a macro  \texttt{{\textbackslash}Inline} that precedes a \texttt{{\textbackslash}def} or \texttt{{\textbackslash}gdef} . 
          Within the definition text of an inlined definition, keywords such as \texttt{{\textbackslash}Expand} may 
          be used to selectively inline certain expansions at definition-time. This eases the process of redefining 
          macros in terms of the original definition, as well as definitions in which the token that must be expanded 
          is deep within, where \texttt{{\textbackslash}expandafter} would be difficult and \texttt{{\textbackslash}edef} is 
          not suitable. Another application is as an easier version of \texttt{{\textbackslash}aftergroup} , 
          by defining a macro in terms of expanded local variables, then ending the group with \texttt{{\textbackslash}expandafter{\textbackslash}endgroup{\textbackslash}macro} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/inlinedef/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/inlinedef/inlinedef.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package optionally modifies four aspects of TeX’s automatic math formatting to improve typesetting: 
          (1) it adds extra space around relation and operation symbols in superscripts and subscripts; (2) it 
          removes extra space around  \texttt{{\textbackslash}left} - \texttt{{\textbackslash}right} delimiter 
          pairs; (3) it adds extra space after right delimiters in certain situations; and (4) it forces \texttt{{\textbackslash}left} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}right} delimiters

          Using these fonts with XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX is easy using the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec}{fontspec} package; 
          we refer to the documentation of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec}{fontspec} for more 
          information.

          The present package provides a way of using them with LaTeX and pdfLaTeX: it provides two style files, 
          \texttt{InriaSerif.sty} and \texttt{InriaSans.sty} , together with the PostScript 
          version of the fonts and their associated files. These were created using autoinst.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/inriafonts/README}

\item[author] Isambert, Paul
\index{Author!Isambert, Paul}
\item[author] Robbers, Yuri
\index{Author!Robbers, Yuri}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The package preprocesses input files to a Lua(La)TeX run, on the fly.

          The user defines Lua regular expressions to search for patterns and modify input lines (or entire paragraphs) 
          accordingly, before TeX reads the material. In this way, documents may be prepared in a non-TeX language 
          (e.g., some lightweight markup language) and turned into ‘proper’ TeX for processing.

          The source of the documentation is typed in such a lightweight language and is thus easily readable in 
          a text editor (the PDF file is also available, of course); the transformation to TeX syntax via Interpreter’s 
          functions is explained in the documentation itself.

          Interpreter is implemented using the author’s  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/gates}{gates} (lua 
          version), and works for plain TeX and LaTeX, but not ConTeXt.

\section[\texttt{interval} -- Format mathematical intervals, ensuring proper spacing]{\texttt{interval} -- Format mathematical intervals, ensuring proper spacing}\label{pkg:interval}
\index{Package!interval}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/interval}
\item[name] \texttt{interval}
\item[caption] Format mathematical intervals, ensuring proper spacing
\item[author] Madsen, Lars
\index{Author!Madsen, Lars}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.4 (2019-03-06)
\item[last changes] 2019-03-06
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) When typing an open interval as  \texttt{\$]a,b[\$} , a closing bracket is being 
          used in place of an opening fence and vice versa. This leads to the wrong spacing in, say, \texttt{\$]-a,b[\$ 
          or \$A{\textbackslash}in]a,b[=B\$} . The package attempts to solve this using:\\ \texttt{{\textbackslash}interval{\textbraceleft}a{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}b{\textbraceright}} -> \texttt{[a,b]} \\ \texttt{{\textbackslash}interval[open]{\textbraceleft}a{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}b{\textbraceright}} -> \texttt{]a,b[} \\ \texttt{{\textbackslash}interval[open 
          left]{\textbraceleft}a{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}b{\textbraceright}} -> \texttt{]a,b]} 

          The package also supports fence scaling and ensures that the enclosing fences will end up having the 
          proper closing and opening types. TeX maths does not do this job properly.

          The package depends on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgfkeys}{pgfkeys} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/interval/interval.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./7434102523-interval.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/interval/README}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/interval}
\item[on Mik\TeX] \texttt{interval}
\item[on \TeX Live] \texttt{interval}

\item[caption] A LaTeX package for typesetting integrals
\item[author] Dao, Valentin

\item[last changes] 2026-01-02
\item[year] 2026

\item[description] (no language specified) Typesetting integrals, although common in LaTeX, is not particularly practical. The way in which the 
          different parts are managed often generates unreadable source code, making modifications laborious. The 
          package therefore follows a simple philosophy: focus on the essential element of an integral, the integrand. 
          Everything else (limits, differentials, symbols) can be modified using keys. These keys are designed 
          to allow you to easily and quickly change the style of an integral. Additionally, the package provides 
          various auxiliary macros to support some keys which can have lengthy inputs.

\section[\texttt{ionumbers} -- Restyle numbers in maths mode]{\texttt{ionumbers} -- Restyle numbers in maths mode}\label{pkg:ionumbers}
\index{Package!ionumbers}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/ionumbers}
\item[name] \texttt{ionumbers}
\item[caption] Restyle numbers in maths mode
\item[author] Schneider, Christian
\index{Author!Schneider, Christian}
\item[copyright] Christian Schneider (2007-2009, 2011, 2012, 2014)
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 0.3.3 (2014-04-06)
\item[last changes] 2014-04-06
\item[year] 2014
\index{Year!2014}
\item[description] (no language specified) ‘ \texttt{ionumbers} ’ stands for ‘input/output numbers’.

          The package restyles numbers in maths mode. If a number in the input file is written, e.g., as  \texttt{\$3,231.44\$} as 
          commonly used in English texts, the package is able to restyle it to be output as \texttt{\$3{\textbackslash},231{\textbraceleft},{\textbraceright}44\$} as 
          commonly used in German texts (and vice versa). This may be useful, for example, if you have a large 
          table and want to include it in texts with different output conventions without the need to change the 
          table.

          The package can also automatically group digits left of the decimal separator (thousands) and right of 
          the decimal separator (thousandths) in triplets without the need of specifing commas (English) or points 
          (German) as separators. E.g., the input  \texttt{\$1234.567890\$} can be output as \texttt{\$1{\textbackslash},234.{\textbackslash},567{\textbackslash},890\$} .

          Finally, an  \texttt{e} starts the exponent of the number. For example, \texttt{\$21e6\$} may 
          be output as \texttt{\$26{\textbackslash}times10{\textbackslash},{\textasciicircum}{\textbraceleft}6{\textbraceright}\$} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ionumbers/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ionumbers/ionumbers.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5339961535-ionumbers.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ionumbers}
\item[on Mik\TeX] \texttt{ionumbers}

\section[\texttt{iran-bibtex} -- Iran Manual of Style Citation Guide for BibTeX]{\texttt{iran-bibtex} -- Iran Manual of Style Citation Guide for BibTeX}\label{pkg:iran-bibtex}
\index{Package!iran-bibtex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/iran-bibtex}
\item[name] \texttt{iran-bibtex}
\item[caption] Iran Manual of Style Citation Guide for BibTeX
\item[author] Rasuli, Farshad
\index{Author!Rasuli, Farshad}
\item[copyright] Farshad Rasuli (2023-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.4.3
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \texttt{iran-bibtex package} , designed for LaTeX, provides BibTeX styles in accordance 
          with the guidelines outlined in the \href{https://imos.irandoc.ac.ir}{Iran Manual of Style} (1st 
          edn., 2016)—citation guide to Persian, and English information sources.

          A collection of illustrative examples showcasing the usage of this package has been meticulously prepared 
          and is accessible in  \href{https://github.com/farshadrasuli/iran-bibtex}{the package’s GitHub 
          repository} under the ‘examples’ sub-directory.

          To facilitate alphabetical sorting of references, prioritizing Persian/Farsi items ahead of English/Latin 
          ones, a dedicated file named  \texttt{iran-bibtex-cp1256fa.csf} is provided for use with 
          this package. This file, derived from the \href{https://mirrors.ctan.org/biblio/bibtex/bibtex-x/csf/ascii.csf}{ascii.csf} file, 
          serves the purpose of arranging references in the desired order.

          It is important to note that this package relies on the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/natbib}{natbib} package, 
          which is automatically loaded.
\item[documentation]  (Persian) \textit{User guide}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/bibtex/contrib/iran-bibtex/iran-bibtex-userguide-fa.pdf}

\section[\texttt{isodate} -- Tune the output format of dates according to language]{\texttt{isodate} -- Tune the output format of dates according to language}\label{pkg:isodate}
\index{Package!isodate}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/isodate}
\item[name] \texttt{isodate}
\item[caption] Tune the output format of dates according to language
\item[author] Harders, Harald
\index{Author!Harders, Harald}
\item[copyright] Harald Harders (2000-2005)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 2.28
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides ten output formats of the commands  \texttt{{\textbackslash}today} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}printdate} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}printdateTeX} , 
          and \texttt{{\textbackslash}daterange} (partly language dependent).

          Formats available are: ISO (yyyy-mm-dd), numeric (e.g. dd.{\textbackslash},mm.{\textasciitilde}yyyy), 
          short (e.g. dd.{\textbackslash},mm.{\textbackslash},yy), TeX (yyyy/mm/dd), original (e.g. 
          dd. mmm yyyy), short original (e.g. dd. mmm yy), as well as numerical formats with Roman numerals for 
          the month.

          The commands  \texttt{{\textbackslash}printdate} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}printdateTeX} print 
          any date. The command \texttt{{\textbackslash}daterange} prints a date range and leaves 
          out unnecessary year or month entries.

          This package supports German (old and new rules), Austrian, US English, British English, French, Danish, 
          Swedish, and Norwegian.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/isodate/isodate.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./1934303133-isodate.pdf|

\item[license] noinfo = noinfo 
\index{License!noinfo}
\index{License!noinfo}
\item[version] 0.9
\item[description] (no language specified) The package represents an outdated mechanism for reading ISO Latin-1 (ISO/IEC 8859-1) by means of setting 
          the printing glyphs in the upper half of the character set to category code ''active'', and defining 
          them all.

          While this mechanism is broadly that employed by the standard LaTeX  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/inputenc}{inputenc} package, 
          the standard package has several advantages, including a more satisfactory approach to undefined character 
          codes, better integration with other input encodings and generally improved robustness.

\section[\texttt{issuulinks} -- Produce external links instead of internal ones]{\texttt{issuulinks} -- Produce external links instead of internal ones}\label{pkg:issuulinks}
\index{Package!issuulinks}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/issuulinks}
\item[name] \texttt{issuulinks}
\item[caption] Produce external links instead of internal ones
\item[author] Veytsman, Boris
\index{Author!Veytsman, Boris}
\item[copyright] Boris Veytsman (2012)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The PDF visualizer  \texttt{http://issuu.com/ISSUU} is a popular service which shows PDF 
          documents ''a page a time''. Due to the way it is implemented, internal links in these documents are 
          not allowed. Instead, they must be converted to external ones in the form \texttt{http://issuu.com/action/page?page=PAGENUMBER} .

          The package patches hyperref to produce external links in the required form instead of internal links 
          created by  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ref} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}cite} and 
          other commands.

          Since the package redefines the internals of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} , 
          it must be loaded it AFTER hyperref.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/issuulinks/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/issuulinks/issuulinks.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5182603353-issuulinks.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/issuulinks}

\item[description] (no language specified) This LaTeX package provides macros based on TikZ to draw a game tree. The main idea underlying its core 
          macros is the completion of a whole tree by using a sequence of simple ‘parent-child’ tree structures, 
          with no longer nested relations involved (like the use of ‘grandchildren’ or ‘great-grandchildren’).

          Using this package you can draw a game tree as easily as drawing a game tree with pen and paper.

          This package depends on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse}{xparse} .

          The ‘ist’ prefix stands for ''it’s a simple tree'' or ''In-Sung’s simple tree.''

          produces ‘IVD-DVI’ files which extend DVI files with ‘reflection’ commands for horizontal reversal of 
          text. In general, IVD-DVI files cannot be processed by an ordinary DVI processor; \texttt{ivd2dvi} will 
          convert such a file to DVI so that it can be processed by a normal DVI driver.

\section[\texttt{iwona} -- A two-element sans-serif font]{\texttt{iwona} -- A two-element sans-serif font}\label{pkg:iwona}
\index{Package!iwona}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/iwona}

\item[caption] A two-element sans-serif font
\item[author] Nowacki, Janusz Marian
\index{Author!Nowacki, Janusz Marian}

\item[license] gfl = The GUST Font License (GFL) (free)
\index{License!gfl}
\index{License!The GUST Font License (GFL)}
\item[version] 0.995b
\item[description] (no language specified) Iwona is a two-element sans-serif typeface. It was created as an alternative version of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/kurier}{Kurier} typeface, 
          which was designed in 1975 for a diploma in typeface design at the Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts under 
          the supervision of Roman Tomaszewski.

          This distribution contains a significantly extended set of characters covering the following modern alphabets: 
          latin (including Vietnamese), Cyrillic and Greek as well as a number of additional symbols (including 
          mathematical symbols). The fonts are prepared in Type 1 and OpenType formats. For use with TeX the following 
          encoding files have been prepared: T1 (ec), T2 (abc), and OT2—Cyrillic, T5 (Vietnamese), OT4, QX, texansi 
          and nonstandard (IL2 for the Czech fonts), as well as supporting macros and files defining fonts for 
          LaTeX.

\section[\texttt{jabref} -- Graphical frontend to manage BibTeX databases]{\texttt{jabref} -- Graphical frontend to manage BibTeX databases}\label{pkg:jabref}
\index{Package!jabref}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/jabref}
\item[name] \texttt{jabref}
\item[caption] Graphical frontend to manage BibTeX databases
\item[author] Alver, Morten
\index{Author!Alver, Morten}
\item[author] Kopp, Oliver
\index{Author!Kopp, Oliver}
\item[author] The JabRef Project
\index{Author!The JabRef Project}
\item[author] Batada, Nizar
\index{Author!Batada, Nizar}
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version] 5.10
\item[description] (no language specified) JabRef is a graphical frontend to manage  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} (and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} ) 
          databases having \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} as internal format. It offers 
          quality checks for entries; fetching complete bibliographic information based on ISBN, DOI, PubMed-ID 
          and arXiv-ID; searching across many online scientific catalogues such as CiteSeer, CrossRef, Google Scholar, 
          IEEEXplore, INSPIRE-HEP, Medline PubMed, MathSciNet, Springer, arXiv, and zbMATH.

          It allows for grouping entries (and storing the group information in the  \texttt{.bib} file 
          itself), advancing searching and filtering, finding duplicate entries, attaching and renaming PDFs (e.g., 
          according to the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} key), and generating \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} keys.

          Since JabRef fully relies on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bibtex}{BibTeX} , additional 
          information such as ranking, priority, printed-flag, and quality-assured-flag are stored in the BibTeX 
          entry in the \texttt{.bib} file itself.
\item[home page] \url{https://www.jabref.org/}

\section[\texttt{jeopardy} -- Build a jeopardy game in LaTeX]{\texttt{jeopardy} -- Build a jeopardy game in LaTeX}\label{pkg:jeopardy}
\index{Package!jeopardy}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/jeopardy}
\item[name] \texttt{jeopardy}
\item[caption] Build a jeopardy game in LaTeX
\item[author] Mařík, Robert
\index{Author!Mařík, Robert}
\item[copyright] Robert Mařík (2004)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.1a
\item[description] (no language specified) The jeopardy package allows to build a jeopardy game with pdfLaTeX. It is based on the  \href{http://www.math.uakron.edu/{\textasciitilde}dpstory/jj\_game.html}{jj-game} class 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/exerquiz}{exerquiz} package, written by D. P. Story. The 
          author of the game can use multichoice questions or fill-in questions. The answer for fill-in questions 
          is either a mathematical formula or text string (see the documentation of exerquiz and \texttt{{\textbackslash}RespBoxMath} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}RespBoxTxt} commands 
          to learn more about the capabilities). JavaScripts are written to record the score. If the score is greater 
          than a given value, a hidden string is shown. The user should use the style with some screen presentation 
          package, such as \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/acrotex-web}{web} .

          The package is distributed with some example games, including both 1- and 2-player games.

\item[description] (no language specified) This program provides functionality to process data files (JFM and VF) that form logical fonts used in 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ptex}{(u)pTeX} . The functions currently available include:

          
          \begin{itemize}
          \item The mutual conversion between Japanese virtual fonts (pairs of VF and JFM) and files in the ''ZVP format'', which is an original text format representing data in virtual fonts. This function can be seen as a counterpart to the  \texttt{vftovp} / \texttt{vptovf} programs.
          \item The mutual conversion between VF files alone and files in the ''ZVP0 format'', which is a subset of the ZVP format.
          \end{itemize}

\item[description] (no language specified) The class defines a Jeopardy-like game; question answers may be multiple choice, or text or mathematics 
          ‘fill-ins’.

          The basic game can be constructed using dvipsone,  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvips}{dvips} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex}{pdftex} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipdfm}{dvipdfm} . 
          The ‘pro’ option of the game works with dvipsone or dvips only, and requires Adobe Acrobat Pro 7.0 (or 
          later), with its distiller.

          The game requires the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/acrotex}{AcroTeX education bundle} , 
          and (for the pro option) \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/aeb-pro}{AeB pro} .

          Also, the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/eforms}{eforms} package dated 2016-08-29 or later 
          is required.

          Samples of sources for games are provided.

\index{License!gpl}

\item[version] 188
\item[description] (no language specified) JLM is an advanced LaTeX mode for the  \href{http://www.jedsoft.org/jed}{Jed} editor. 
          Its aim is to help the user by taking over annoying and stupid things that need to be done, like adding 
          {\textbackslash}usepackage when you add a command or environment from this package, or placing 
          dollar signs around mathematical commands and move the cursor to an appropriate point.

          JLM does not think for you. If you want a tabular but insert an itemize, JLM doesn't prevent this. So, 
          you should be familiar with LaTeX and know what environments and commands are, and where to place them 
          in a document; JLM is there to help writing them.

\item[description] (no language specified) The jmlr bundle provides a class for authors ( \texttt{jmlr} ) and a class for production 
          editors ( \texttt{jmlrbook} ).

          The  \texttt{jmlrbook} class can be used to combine articles written using the jmlr class 
          into a book. The class uses the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/combine}{combine} class and 
          the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} package to produce either a colour 
          hyperlinked book for on-line viewing or a greyscale nonhyperlinked book for printing.

          Production editors can use  \href{http://www.dickimaw-books.com/software/makejmlrbookgui}{makejmlrbookgui} to 
          help build the proceedings from the articles.

\section[\texttt{jmsdelim} -- A package for compositional delimiter sizing]{\texttt{jmsdelim} -- A package for compositional delimiter sizing}\label{pkg:jmsdelim}
\index{Package!jmsdelim}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/jmsdelim}
\item[name] \texttt{jmsdelim}
\item[caption] A package for compositional delimiter sizing
\item[author] Sterling, Jonathan
\index{Author!Sterling, Jonathan}
\item[copyright] Jonathan Sterling (2022)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.2.0
\item[description] (no language specified) Correctly sizing delimiters is very difficult, particularly in well-architected documents: a correctly 
          engineered mathematical document will include macros for all operations, and these macros necessarily 
          will include delimiters (such as parentheses). However, the correct size for the delimiter cannot be 
          chosen ahead of time, because it will depend on the arguments; two options are available:

          \begin{enumerate}
          \item Provide optional arguments to each notation macro for choosing delimiter sizes. This is nearly intractable to do in practice.
          \item Ignore delimiter sizes.
          \end{enumerate}
With jmsdelim we offer an alternative: the correct delimiter sizes can be set at the leaf nodes of a 
          mathematical expression, and magically bubble upward through the delimiters.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/jmsdelim/jmsdelim.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./8733702062-jmsdelim.pdf|

\section[\texttt{jourcl} -- Cover letter for journal submissions]{\texttt{jourcl} -- Cover letter for journal submissions}\label{pkg:jourcl}

\item[description] (no language specified) Paper submissions to journals are usually accompanied by a cover letter. This package provides a LaTeX 
          class and a template for such a cover letter with the following main features:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Minimalistic design.
          \item Custom image.
          \item Pre-defined commands for journal name, author, date, etc.
          \item Many macros contained in this package speed up the process of preparing the necessary ingredients for the cover letter.
          \item Macros for recommending up to three reviewers and/or editors.
          \item ORCID logo and link to the submitting author’s ORCID page.
          \item Controls for adding a ''Conflict of interest'' statement and declaration.
          \item Custom greeting (e.g., ''Dear Editor'' for a regular submission, ''Dear Editor-in-Chief'' for a submission to a journal’s special issue, etc.)
          \item Predefined valedictions for different types of submissions (e.g., Yours sincerely, Yours faithfully, Best regards, etc.)
          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{jourrr} -- A LaTeX template for journal rebuttal letters]{\texttt{jourrr} -- A LaTeX template for journal rebuttal letters}\label{pkg:jourrr}
\index{Package!jourrr}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/jourrr}
\item[name] \texttt{jourrr}
\item[caption] A LaTeX template for journal rebuttal letters
\item[author] Kukovec, Rok
\index{Author!Kukovec, Rok}
\item[license] cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
\index{License!cc-by-sa-4}
\index{License!CC BY-SA 4.0}
\item[version]  (2023-10-14)
\item[last changes] 2023-10-14
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides an elegant LaTeX template designed for crafting professional rebuttal letters in 
          response to editors or reviewers.

          It consists of a LaTeX class and a template, fine-tuned to support your publishing journey with several 
          pre-defined commands that drastically speed up the process of preparing letters during the revision process.

          The repository hosts a template for writing responses to editors/reviewers comments for journal submissions 
          written in LaTeX that is minimalistic in one way while pre-defined with several commands that drastically 
          speed up the process of preparing letters during the revision process.

          Main Features of this template:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item With front page included
          \item  \textbf{Response ticks} to mark as completed
          \item Custom response color
          \item Minimalistic design
          \item Everything is customizable
          \item Predefined commands for a journal name, submission ID, author, editor, associate editor, date, etc.
          \item Many macros included
          \item Predefined different valedictions for different types of submissions (e.g., Yours sincerely, Yours faithfully, Best regards, etc.)
          \item Custom greeting (e.g., ''Dear Editor'' or bDear Editor-in-Chief'' for regular submission, etc.)
          \item (Optional) Table of contents, jump to the reply you wish to address
          \item Option to add custom Signature (i.e. an image of your hand-written signature)
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/jourrr/README.md}

\item[description] (no language specified) This distribution makes the full text of the most recent reprint of the second edition of ''The Joy of

          ''Joy'' is the user documentation for \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amstex}{AMS-TeX} . (Please

          the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amstex}{AMS-TeX} macro package, by M. D. Spivak. This

\section[\texttt{jpeg2ps} -- Convert JPEG files to PostScript Level 2 or 3 EPS]{\texttt{jpeg2ps} -- Convert JPEG files to PostScript Level 2 or 3 EPS}\label{pkg:jpeg2ps}
\index{Package!jpeg2ps}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/jpeg2ps}
\item[name] \texttt{jpeg2ps}
\item[caption] Convert JPEG files to PostScript Level 2 or 3 EPS
\item[author] Merz, Thomas
\index{Author!Merz, Thomas}
\item[copyright] Thomas Merz (1994-1999)
\item[license] nosell = Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement (not free)
\index{License!nosell}
\index{License!Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement}
\item[version] 1.8
\item[description] (no language specified) Converts JPEG files to PostScript Level 2 or 3 EPS. In fact, jpeg2ps is not really a converter but a 
          ''wrapper'': it reads the image parameters (width, height, number of color components) in a JPEG file, 
          writes the according EPS header and then copies the compressed JPEG data to the output file. Decompression 
          is done by the PostScript interpreter (only PostScript Level 2 and 3 interpreters support JPEG compression 
          and decompression).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/jpeg2ps/jpeg2ps.txt}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/jslectureplanner}
\item[name] \texttt{jslectureplanner}
\item[caption] Creation and management of university course material
\item[author] Spitzmüller, Jürgen
\index{Author!Spitzmüller, Jürgen}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.15 (2025-10-02)
\item[last changes] 2025-10-02
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \texttt{jslectureplanner} package facilitates the generation and management of university 
          course material. It provides an interface to set up and access centralized course data that can be reused 
          in all course documents. Furthermore, the package is able to calculate the session dates of a whole semester 
          and generate course programs, if the course is held weekly and the date of the first lecture is specified. 
          Moreover, the package can be used to generate a sectioned course bibliography via \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} .

          The bundle also includes a package  \texttt{jsmembertable.sty} that helps in generating course 
          member and presence lists.

\item[version] 1.0.2 (2026-01-31)
\item[last changes] 2026-01-31
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) A minimal LuaLaTeX package for rendering  \href{https://jsonresume.org/}{JSON Resume} data 
          into clean, professional resumes.

          \textbf{Features} 

          \begin{description}
          \item[Full JSON Resume Schema Support]All 12 sections (basics, work, volunteer, education, awards, certificates, publications, skills, languages, interests, references, projects)
          \item[Load from File or URL]Local JSON files or remote URLs
          \item[Schema Validation]Strict mode warns about schema violations
          \item[Clean FAANG-style Formatting]Professional typography with no distracting design elements
          \item[Customizable Section Titles]Override default section headers
          \end{description}

 \textbf{Requirements} 

          \begin{description}
          \item[LuaLaTeX]Part of TeX Live or MiKTeX
          \item[curl]For URL loading, pre-installed on most systems
          \end{description}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package enables automated citation with BibTeX for legal studies and the humanities. In addition, 
          the package provides commands for specifying editors in a commentary in a convenient way. Simplified 
          formatting of the citation as well as the bibliography entry is also provided. It is possible to display 
          the (short) title of a work only if an authors is cited with multiple works. Giving a full citation in 
          the text, conforming to the bibliography entry, is supported. Several options are provided which might 
          be of special interest for those outside legal studies—for instance, displaying multiple full citations. 
          In addition, the format of last names and first names of authors may be changed easily. Cross references 
          to other footnotes are possible. Language dependent handling of bibliography entries is possible by the 
          special language field.

\item[description] (no language specified) JustFontIt TeX Edition for Win32 is a tool for TeX users. It helps installing fonts in Type1 Binary (PFB), 
          Type1 ASCII (PFA), TrueType and OpenType/CFF to use with TeX.

          The major features of JustFontIt TeX Edition are:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Functionality of the pltotf, tftopl, vftovp, vptovf tools, all developed by Prof. D. E. Knuth;
          \item Direct production of TFM and PL TeX metric files from various sources (PFA, PFB, TTF, OTF, AFM, PFM), including reencoding;
          \item Support for response files and recursive directory search;
          \item Clear command-line interface; and
          \item High performance.
          \end{itemize}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a LaTeX environment  \texttt{listing} , an alternative to the built-in \texttt{verbatim} environment. 
          The \texttt{listing} environment is tailored for including listings of computer program source 
          code into documents.

          The main advantages over the original  \texttt{verbatim} environment are:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item environments automatically fixes leading whitespace so that the environment and program listing can be indented with the rest of the document source, and;
          \item  \texttt{listing} environments may easily be customised and extended.

          dates in classical Latin given days on the Julian or Gregorian calendars, using the same syntax used 
          by ancient Roman authors. The format of these dates may be customised either in the package options or

\item[author] Zahumensky, Adam

\item[license] bsd = BSD Style License (free)
\index{License!bsd}
\index{License!BSD Style License}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides a kana parser for LuaTeX. It is a set of 4 macros that handle transliteration of 
          text:

          \begin{enumerate}
          \item from hiragana and katakana to Latin
          \item from Latin and katakana to hiragana
          \item from Latin and hiragana to katakana
          \end{enumerate}
It can be used to write kana directly using only the ASCII character set or for education purposes. The 
          package has support for obsolete and rarely used syllables, some only accessible via the provided toggle 
          macro.

\item[version] 0.6.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The problem this class solves is  \href{https://kdp.amazon.com/en\_US/help/topic/G201953020}{the 
          necessity} to change the size of the cover PDF according to the number of pages in the book — the 
          bigger the book, the larger the spine of the book must be. The provided class makes the necessary calculations 
          on-the-fly, using the \texttt{qpdf} tool. Obviously, you need to have it installed. Also, 
          you must run \texttt{pdflatex} with the \texttt{--shell-escape} option, in order 
          to allow LaTeX to run \texttt{qpdf} .

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.32
\item[description] (no language specified) This class makes it easy to generate tables that show many different kerning pairs of an arbitrary font, 
          usable by LaTeX. It shows the kerning values that are used in the font by default.

          In addition, this class enables the user to alter the kernings and to observe the results. Kerning pairs 
          can be defined for groups of similar glyphs at the same time. An mtx file is generated automatically. 
          The mtx file may then be loaded by  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontinst}{fontinst} to 
          introduce the user-made kernings into the virtual font for later use in LaTeX.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/kerntest/README}

\item[description] (no language specified) KeTCindy combines a plugin to Cinderella with free mathematical software (R, Maxima, …) to produce high-quality 
          LaTeX graphics.

          Using Cinderella to generate graphics in an interactive environment, the generated image can be fine-tuned 
          using KeTCindy commands embedded into CindyScript, the scripting language of Cinderella.

          KeTCindy can be regarded as a prominent scheme to establish an effective linkage between visualization 
          tools and editing tools. Moreover, KeTCindy enables the importation of data calculated or simulated using 
          other mathematical software such as Maxima, Fricas, Risa/Asir and R, and to combine them with the graphical 
          data, so that an extremely wide range of mathematical objects can be presented.

\section[\texttt{keyfloat} -- Provides a key/value interface for generating floats]{\texttt{keyfloat} -- Provides a key/value interface for generating floats}\label{pkg:keyfloat}
\index{Package!keyfloat}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/keyfloat}
\item[name] \texttt{keyfloat}
\item[caption] Provides a key/value interface for generating floats
\item[author] Dunn, Brian
\index{Author!Dunn, Brian}
\item[copyright] Brian Dunn (2016-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 2.09
\item[description] (no language specified) The keyfloat package provides a key/value user interface for quickly creating figures with a single image 
          each, figures with arbitrary contents, tables, subfloats, rows of floats, floats located [H]ere, floats 
          in the [M]argin, and floats with text [W]rapped around them. 

          Key/value combinations may specify 
          a caption and label, a width proportional to {\textbackslash}linewidth, a fixed width and/or height, 
          rotation, scaling, a tight or loose frame, an {\textbackslash}arraystretch, a continued float, 
          additional supplemental text, and an artist/author's name with automatic index entry. When used with 
          the tocdata package, the name also appears in the List of Figures.

          Floats may be placed into 
          a row environment, and are typeset to fit within the given number of columns, continuing to the next 
          row if necessary. Nested sub-rows may be used to generate layouts such as two small figures placed vertically 
          next to one larger figure.

          Subfloats are supported by two environments.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/keyfloat/README.txt}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/keyfloat/keyfloat.pdf}

\index{Package!knuth-hint}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/knuth-hint}
\item[name] \texttt{knuth-hint}
\item[caption] HINT collection of typeset C/WEB sources in TeX Live
\item[author] Scherer, Andreas
\index{Author!Scherer, Andreas}
\item[license] knuth = Knuth License (free)
\index{License!knuth}
\index{License!Knuth License}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[version] 2.5 (2024-08-12)
\item[last changes] 2024-08-12
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \texttt{knuth-hint} package contains the large collection of HINT documents for many 
          of the CWEB amd WEB sources of programs in the TeX Live distribution (and, for technical reasons, a PDF 
          document for XeTeX). Each program is presented in its original form as written by the respective authors, 
          and in the ''changed'' form as used in TeX Live. Care has been taken to keep the section numbering intact, 
          so that you can study the codes and the changes in parallel. Also included are the ''errata'' for Donald 
          Knuth’s ''Computers \& Typesetting''.

          HINT is the dynamic document format created by Martin Ruckert’s HiTeX engine that was added to TeX Live 
          2022. The HINT files can be viewed on Linux, Windows, and Android with the hintview application. The 
          \texttt{knuth-hint} package is a showcase of HiTeX’s capabilities.

\item[version] 2.5 (2024-08-12)
\item[last changes] 2024-08-12

\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) Here you find a large collection of PDF documents for many C/WEB programs in TeX Live, both in their 
          original form as written by their respective authors, and in the changed form as they are actually used 
          in the TeX Live system. Care has been taken to keep the section numbering intact, so that you can study 
          the sources and their changes in parallel. Also included is the collection of ''errata'' for Donald Knuth’s 
          ''Computers \& Typesetting series''.

          Although not all the texts here are written or maintained by Donald Knuth, it is more convenient for 
          everything to be collected in one place for reading and searching. They all stem from the system that 
          Knuth created. The central entry point is the ''index'' file, with links to the individual documents, 
          either in HTML or in PDF format.

\section[\texttt{koma-script} -- A bundle of versatile classes and packages]{\texttt{koma-script} -- A bundle of versatile classes and packages}\label{pkg:koma-script}
\index{Package!koma-script}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script}
\item[name] \texttt{koma-script}
\item[caption] A bundle of versatile classes and packages
\item[author] Kohm, Markus
\index{Author!Kohm, Markus}
\item[copyright] Markus Kohm (1994-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 3.43 (2024-10-24)
\item[last changes] 2024-10-24
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The KOMA-Script bundle provides replacements for the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/scrartcl}{article} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/scrreprt}{report} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/scrbook}{book} classes with emphasis on typography and 
          versatility. There is also a \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/scrlttr2}{letter class} .

          The bundle also offers:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item a  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/typearea}{package for calculating type areas} in the way laid down by the typographer Jan Tschichold,
          \item packages for easily changing and defining page styles,
          \item a package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/scrdate}{scrdate} for getting not only the current date but also the name of the day, and
          \item a package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/scrtime}{scrtime} for getting the current time.
          \end{itemize}
All these packages may be used not only with KOMA-Script classes but also with the standard classes.

          Since every package has its own version number, the version number quoted only refers to the version 
          of  \texttt{scrbook} , \texttt{scrreprt} , \texttt{scrartcl} , \texttt{scrlttr2} and \texttt{typearea} (which 
          are the main parts of the bundle).
\item[documentation] \textit{English documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/koma-script/doc/scrguide-en.pdf}

\section[\texttt{komacv-rg} -- LaTeX packages that aid in creating CVs based on the komacv \ldots]{\texttt{komacv-rg} -- LaTeX packages that aid in creating CVs based on the komacv class and creating related documents}\label{pkg:komacv-rg}
\index{Package!komacv-rg}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/komacv-rg}
\item[name] \texttt{komacv-rg}
\item[caption] LaTeX packages that aid in creating CVs based on the komacv class and creating related documents
\item[author] Grewe, Richard
\index{Author!Grewe, Richard}
\item[copyright] Richard Grewe (2016-2018)
\item[license] lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.2}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2}
\item[version] 0.9.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The komacv-rg bundle provides packages that aid in creating CVs based on the komacv class and creating 
          related documents, such as cover letters and cover sheets for job applications. Concretely, the bundle 
          consists of three packages: komacv-addons, komacv-lco, and komacv-multilang.

          \begin{itemize}
          \item komacv-addons is a small collection of add-ons and fixes for the komacv class;
          \item komacv-lco enables the use of letter class options from scrlttr2 also in komacv-based and other non-scrlttr2-based documents;
          \item komacv-multilang enables the provisioning of CVs in multiple languages and the selection of a language via babel or polyglossia.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation komacv-multilang}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/komacv-rg/komacv-multilang.pdf}

\section[\texttt{konwerter} -- A program for automatic numbering of compounds in chemical p\ldots]{\texttt{konwerter} -- A program for automatic numbering of compounds in chemical publications}\label{pkg:konwerter}
\index{Package!konwerter}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/konwerter}
\item[name] \texttt{konwerter}
\item[caption] A program for automatic numbering of compounds in chemical publications
\item[author] Wawrzyniak, Piotr
\index{Author!Wawrzyniak, Piotr}
\item[license] gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
\index{License!gpl2}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 2}
\item[version] 0.2.4
\item[description] (no language specified) Konwerter automatically numbers compounds in chemical publications created by  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex}{LaTeX} . 
          It is written in C++ and works both in Unix and Windows operating systems. It works similar to LaTeX \texttt{{\textbackslash}label} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}ref} commands. 
          Instead of giving number to every compound you give them labels and then refer to the structure in the 
          text using the same label. The konwerter is able to resolve labels to numbers both in the eps files and 
          in the text.

\item[author] Caignaert, Christophe
\index{Author!Caignaert, Christophe}

\item[last changes] 2024-10-27
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The family contains text fonts in roman, sans-serif and monospaced shapes, with true small caps and old-style 
          numbers; the package offers full support of the textcomp package. The mathematics fonts include all the 
          AMS fonts, in both normal and bold weights.

          Each of the font types is available in two main versions: default and ‘light’. Each version is available 
          in four variants: default; oldstyle numbers; oldstyle numbers with old ligatures such as ct and st, and 
          long-tailed capital Q; and veryoldstyle with long s. Other variants include small caps as default or 
          ‘large small caps’, and for mathematics both upright and slanted shapes for Greek letters, as well as 
          default and narrow versions of multiple integrals.

          The fonts were originally derived from URW Palladio (with URW’s agreement) though the fonts are very 
          clearly different in appearance from their parent.

\item[description] (no language specified) This bundle provides OpenType versions of the Type1 Kp-fonts designed by Christophe Caignaert. It is 
          usable with LuaTeX or XeTeX engines only.

          It consists of sixteen Text fonts (eight Serif, four Sans-Serif, four Monotype) and six Math fonts.

          Serif and Sans-Serif families have small caps available in two sizes (SmallCaps and PetitesCaps), upper 
          and lowercase digits, real superscripts and subscripts; ancient ligatures (ct and st), ancient long-s 
          and a long-tailed capital Q are available via font features.

          Math fonts cover all usual symbols including AMS’; a full list of available symbols is provided, see 
          the ‘List of glyphs’.

\section[\texttt{ktbox} -- Framework for semantic color, structured highlighting, and s\ldots]{\texttt{ktbox} -- Framework for semantic color, structured highlighting, and scholarly communication }\label{pkg:ktbox}
\index{Package!ktbox}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/ktbox}
\item[name] \texttt{KTBox}
\item[caption] Framework for semantic color, structured highlighting, and scholarly communication
\item[author] Mangal, Bhaskar
\index{Author!Mangal, Bhaskar}
\item[copyright] Bhaskar Mangal (2025)
\item[license] apache2 = Apache License, version 2.0 (free)
\index{License!apache2}
\index{License!Apache License, version 2.0}
\item[version] 0.0.1
\item[description] (no language specified) KTBox is a modular LaTeX framework that introduces semantic color palettes, structured highlight boxes, 
          and ORCID-linked author utilities for scholarly writing. The package is composed of three lightweight 
          and independent style files:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \textbf{ktbox.sty} – defines highlight boxes (standard, numbered, wide) with semantic theming.
          \item  \textbf{ktcolor.sty} – provides semantic color palettes with light and dark modes.
          \item  \textbf{ktorcid.sty} – adds ORCID-linked author commands and icons.
          \end{itemize}
The framework separates structure from style, ensuring compatibility with major classes such as  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ieeetran}{IEEEtran} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/acmart}{acmart} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/article}{article} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/beamer}{beamer} , 
          and ICLR. Features include numbered key-takeaway boxes, wide-format environments for emphasis, multi-column 
          layouts, and dual light/dark themes. KTBox aims to improve clarity, portability, and reproducibility 
          in academic publishing across articles, posters, and presentations.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ktbox/doc/ktbox.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./8047895656-ktbox.pdf|

\index{License!gfl}

\item[description] (no language specified) Kurier is a two-element sans-serif typeface. It was designed for a diploma in typeface design at the 
          Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts under the supervision of Roman Tomaszewski.

          This distribution contains a significantly extended set of characters covering the following modern alphabets: 
          latin (including Vietnamese), Cyrillic and Greek as well as a number of additional symbols (including 
          mathematical symbols). The fonts are prepared in Type 1 and OpenType formats. For use with TeX the following 
          encoding files have been prepared: T1 (ec), T2 (abc), and OT2—Cyrillic, T5 (Vietnamese), OT4, QX, texansi 
          and—nonstandard (IL2 for the Czech fonts), as well as supporting macros and files defining fonts for 
          LaTeX.

\item[description] (no language specified) The l3experimental packages are a collection of experimental implementations for aspects of the LaTeX3 
          kernel, dealing with higher-level ideas such as the Designer Interface. Some of them work as stand alone 
          packages, providing new functionality, and can be used on top of LaTeX2e with no changes to the existing 
          kernel.

          The present release includes:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{l3draw} , a code-level interface for constructing drawings;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xcoffins}{xcoffins} , which allows the alignment of boxes using a series of ‘handle’ positions, supplementing the simple TeX reference point;
          \end{itemize}

\item[caption] Regular expression facilities for LaTeX
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team

\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)

\item[last changes] 2024-12-09
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides regular expression testing, extraction of submatches, splitting, and replacement, 
          all acting on token lists. The syntax of regular expressions is mostly a subset of the PCRE syntax (and 
          is very close to Posix), with some additions arising from the fact that TeX manipulates tokens rather 
          than characters.

          For performance reasons, only a limited set of features are implemented. Notably, back-references are 
          not supported.

          The package is currently distributed as part of the LaTeX3  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel}{l3kernel} bundle.

\section[\texttt{l3sys-query} -- System queries for LaTeX using Lua]{\texttt{l3sys-query} -- System queries for LaTeX using Lua}\label{pkg:l3sys-query}
\index{Package!l3sys-query}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3sys-query}
\item[name] \texttt{l3sys-query}
\item[caption] System queries for LaTeX using Lua
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[copyright] The LaTeX3 Project (2024)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version]  (2024-04-08)
\item[last changes] 2024-04-08
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \texttt{l3sys-query} script provides a method for TeX runs to obtain system information 
          via shell escape to Lua. The facilities are more limited than the similar Java script \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/texosquery}{texosquery} , 
          but since it uses Lua, \texttt{l3sys-query} can be used out of the box; with any installed 
          TeX system.

          The script is written taking account of TeX Live security requirements; it is therefore suitable for 
          use with restricted shell escape, the standard setting when installing a TeX system.

          The supported queries are

          \begin{description}
          \item[ \texttt{ls} ]Directory listing supporting a range of options
          \item[ \texttt{pwd} ]Obtaining details of the current working directory
          \end{description}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/l3sys-query/README.md}

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}eachlabelcase} , which distinguishes whether a set of labels is defined, and for each label either queues action accordingly, or appends the action to a macro; and
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}lotlabelcase} , which takes a comma-separated list of label names, and distinguishes the resulting action on whether all were defined, whether none were defined, whether not all were defined, or whether the lest is empty (again, the action resulting from \texttt{{\textbackslash}lotlabelcase} may be written to a macro).

\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 3.1
\item[description] (no language specified) These are patterns for the Latin language mainly in modern spelling (u when u is needed and v when v 
          is needed); medieval spelling with the ligatures {\textbackslash}ae and {\textbackslash}oe 
          and the (uncial) lowercase ‘v’ written as a ‘u’ is also supported; apparently there is no conflict between 
          the patterns of modern Latin and those of medieval Latin.

          The patterns support the restricted character set of the OT1-encoding (obviously without the ligature 
          characters), as well as T1-encoded usage.

\section[\texttt{lametex} -- A PostScript translator for a subset of LaTeX]{\texttt{lametex} -- A PostScript translator for a subset of LaTeX}\label{pkg:lametex}
\index{Package!lametex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/lametex}
\item[name] \texttt{lametex}
\item[caption] A PostScript translator for a subset of LaTeX
\item[author] Monsarrat, Jonathan
\index{Author!Monsarrat, Jonathan}
\item[copyright] Jonathan Monsarrat (1992)
\item[license] nosell = Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement (not free)
\index{License!nosell}
\index{License!Do Not Sell Except by Arrangement}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) LameTeX is a direct PostScript generator for a (very limited) subset of LaTeX. One of its original design 
          goals, the inclusion of PostScript commands directly in a LaTeX document, has been superseded by  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base}{PSTricks} . 
          However, one of the side effects of a special-purpose translator for LaTeX is the ability of that translator 
          to produce different kinds of output, including plain ASCII.

          The system only understands a subset of LaTeX, and is not set up to use Type 1 fonts; however, it is

\section[\texttt{lapdf} -- PDF drawing directly in TeX documents]{\texttt{lapdf} -- PDF drawing directly in TeX documents}\label{pkg:lapdf}
\index{Package!lapdf}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/lapdf}
\item[name] \texttt{lapdf}
\item[caption] PDF drawing directly in TeX documents
\item[author] Reimers, Detlef
\index{Author!Reimers, Detlef}
\item[copyright] Detlef Reimers (2006-2011)
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the means to use PDF drawing primitives to produce high quality, colored graphics. 
          It

          \begin{itemize}
          \item uses Bézier curves (integral and rational) from degree one to seven,
          \item allows TeX typesetting in the graphic,
          \item offers most of the standard math functions,
          \item allows plotting normal, parametric and polar functions.
          \end{itemize}
The package has linear, logx, logy, logxy and polar grids with many specs;

          \begin{itemize}
          \item it can rotate, clip and do many nice things easily
          \item it has two looping commands for programming and many instructive example files.
          \end{itemize}
The package requires  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex}{pdfTeX} but otherwise only depends 
          on the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/calc}{calc} package.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/lapdf/lapdf.pdf}

          2.09} , and superseded the older system in June 1994. The basic distribution is catalogued separately, 
          at \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-base}{latex-base} ; apart from a large set of contributed 
          packages and third-party documentation (elsewhere on the archive), the distribution includes:

          – a bunch of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/required}{required packages} , which LaTeX authors 
          are ''entitled to assume'' will be present on any system running LaTeX; and\\– a minimal set of documentation 
          detailing differences from the ‘old’ version of LaTeX in the areas of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/usrguide}{user 
          commands} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fntguide}{font selection and control} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/clsguide}{class

          options} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/modguide}{modification of LaTeX} .

\item[caption] AMS mathematical facilities for LaTeX
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[copyright] LaTeX3 Project and American Mathematical Society (2016-2023)
\item[copyright] American Mathematical Society (2001-2004, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2011, 2013)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 2024-11-01a
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the principal packages in the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amslatex}{AMS-LaTeX} distribution. 
          It adapts for use in LaTeX most of the mathematical features found in \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amstex}{AMS-TeX} ; 
          it is highly recommended as an adjunct to serious mathematical typesetting in LaTeX.

          When amsmath is loaded, AMS-LaTeX packages  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsbsy}{amsbsy} (for 
          bold symbols), \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsopn}{amsopn} (for operator names) and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amstext}{amstext} (for 
          text embedded in mathematics) are also loaded.

          amsmath is part of the LaTeX required distribution; however, several contributed packages add still further 
          to its appeal; examples are  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/empheq}{empheq} , which provides 
          functions for decorating and highlighting mathematics, and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ntheorem}{ntheorem} , 
          for specifying theorem (and similar) definitions.

\item[description] (no language specified) This is a collection of fonts for use with standard LaTeX packages and classes. It includes ‘invisible’ 
          fonts (for use with the slides class), line and circle fonts (for use in the picture environment) and 
          ‘LaTeX symbol’ fonts.

          For full support of a LaTeX installation, some Computer Modern font variants cmbsy(6-9), cmcsc(8,9), 
          cmex(7-9) and cmmib(5-9) from the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts}{amsfonts} distribution, 
          are also necessary.

          The fonts are available as Metafont source, and metric (tfm) files are also provided. Most of the fonts 
          are also available in Adobe Type 1 format, in the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts}{amsfonts} distribution.

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-indexer}
\item[name] \texttt{latex-indexer}
\item[caption] Automate index generation for LaTeX documents
\item[author] Degenhardt, David
\index{Author!Degenhardt, David}
\item[license] gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
\index{License!gpl3}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3}
\item[version] 1.0.0 (2025-06-13)
\item[last changes] 2025-06-13
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This is a free, open-source, platform-independent tool designed to automate the generation of indexes 
          for LaTeX documents. It extracts words from  \texttt{.tex} files, generates frequency distributions 
          using \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgfplots}{PGFplots} , allows users to select and tag 
          terms (including variants and sub-variants), and compiles the indexed document with \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/makeindex}{MakeIndex} . 
          Released under GPL-3, it saves approximately 80\% of indexing time, making document creation more 
          efficient.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/indexing/latex-indexer/README.md}

          so that there can be intermediate releases not affecting the production use of LaTeX.

\section[\texttt{latex-make} -- Easy compiling of complex (and simple) LaTeX documents]{\texttt{latex-make} -- Easy compiling of complex (and simple) LaTeX documents}\label{pkg:latex-make}
\index{Package!latex-make}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-make}
\item[name] \texttt{latex-make}
\item[caption] Easy compiling of complex (and simple) LaTeX documents
\item[author] Danjean, Vincent
\index{Author!Danjean, Vincent}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 2.4.3
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides several tools that aim to simplify the compilation of LaTeX documents:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item LaTeX.mk: a Makefile snippet to help compiling LaTeX documents in DVI, PDF, PS, … format. Dependencies are automatically tracked: one should be able to compile documents with a one-line Makefile containing 'include LaTeX.mk'. Complex documents (with multiple bibliographies, indexes, glossaries, …) should be correctly managed.
          \item figlatex.sty: a LaTeX package to easily insert xfig figures (with {\textbackslash}includegraphics{\textbraceleft}file.fig{\textbraceright}). It can interact with LaTeX.mk so that the latter automatically invokes transfig if needed.
          \item And various helper tools for LaTeX.mk
          \end{itemize}
This package  \emph{requires} GNUmake (>= 3.81).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/latex-make/README}

\section[\texttt{latex2man} -- Translate LaTeX-based manual pages into Unix man format]{\texttt{latex2man} -- Translate LaTeX-based manual pages into Unix man format}\label{pkg:latex2man}
\index{Package!latex2man}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex2man}
\item[name] \texttt{latex2man}
\item[caption] Translate LaTeX-based manual pages into Unix man format
\item[author] Vollmer, Jürgen
\index{Author!Vollmer, Jürgen}
\item[license] lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
\index{License!lppl1}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1}
\item[version] 1.30 (2026-01-16)
\item[last changes] 2026-01-16
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) Latex2man is a tool to translate UNIX manual pages written with LaTeX into the troff format understood 
          by the UNIX  \texttt{man(1)} command. Alternatively HTML, Texinfo, or LaTeX code can be produced 
          too. Output of parts of the text may be suppressed using the conditional text feature (for this, LaTeX 
          generation may be used).

          There is a LaTeX package ( \texttt{latex2man.sty} ) for writing the \texttt{man} page 
          and a Perl script ( \texttt{latex2man} ) that does the actual translation.

\section[\texttt{latex2nemeth} -- Convert LaTeX source to Braille with math in Nemeth]{\texttt{latex2nemeth} -- Convert LaTeX source to Braille with math in Nemeth}\label{pkg:latex2nemeth}
\index{Package!latex2nemeth}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex2nemeth}
\item[name] \texttt{Latex2Nemeth}
\item[caption] Convert LaTeX source to Braille with math in Nemeth
\item[author] Tsolomitis, Antonis
\index{Author!Tsolomitis, Antonis}
\item[author] Papasalouros, Andreas
\index{Author!Papasalouros, Andreas}
\item[copyright] Andreas Papasalοuros, Antonis Tsolomitis (2016-2022)
\item[license] gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
\index{License!gpl3}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3}
\item[version] 1.1.3
\item[description] (no language specified) After many failed attempts to transcribe real math notes and books to Braille/Nemeth in order to deal 
          with a real situation (blind student in Math Dept.), we decided to develop a new program that follows 
          a direct, from LaTeX to Braille/Nemeth, approach.

          Our main target was the Greek language which is only Braille level 1, but English at level 1 is supported 
          as well. Simple pictures in  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base}{PSTricks} are 
          also supported in order to produce tactile graphics with specialized equipment.

          Note that embossing will need LibreOffice and  \texttt{odt2braille} as this project does 
          not deal with embossers’ drivers.

          What’s new in version 1.1

          In this version, the support of the user level commands of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} package 
          was added, as described in its user guide, with the exception of commutative diagrams ( \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amscd}{amscd} package) 
          as well as structures that are irrelevant to visually impared persons.

          Also, the Unicode mathematics symbols of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/unicode-math}{unicode-math} package 
          that are represented by the Nemeth code are now supported by latex2nemeth.

          We would like to acknowledge support by the TUGfund for this project (TUGfund project 33).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{HowTo videos on youtube}: \url{https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLcBOch-MEQ5o1_7Qd474I3dK_T1lKuvqq}

\section[\texttt{latexalpha2} -- Embed Mathematica code and plots into LaTeX]{\texttt{latexalpha2} -- Embed Mathematica code and plots into LaTeX}\label{pkg:latexalpha2}
\index{Package!latexalpha2}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/latexalpha2}
\item[name] \texttt{latexalpha2}
\item[caption] Embed Mathematica code and plots into LaTeX
\item[author] Liu, Yi
\index{Author!Liu, Yi}
\item[copyright] Yi Liu (2019)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0 (2019-03-02)
\item[last changes] 2019-03-02
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) This LaTeX package allows you to embed and execute your Wolfram Language (Mathematica) source code in 
          a LaTeX document. When the document is compiled, the computation results will be inserted into the compiled 
          file. In addition to general Wolfram Language computations it is also quite easy to generate plots or 
          animations with this package. Moreover, all the embedded code can be executed either locally (via locally 
          installed Mathematica) or on the cloud (via Wolfram Cloud).

          The main features of this package are somewhat similar to  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/sagetex}{SageTeX} , 
          but here we use Wolfram Language (Mathematica) instead of Sage.

          The package is heavily inspired by  \href{https://github.com/Akollek/LaTeX-Alpha}{LaTeX-Alpha} , 
          which also explains the name ''latexalpha2''. Unfortunately, LaTeX-Alpha has been down for a while. The 
          objective of \texttt{latexalpha2} is to replace LaTeX-Alpha and at the same time provide 
          various new features.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/latexalpha2/latexalpha2.pdf}

          issues.

          Notable features:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Automated transition from Bangla to English and vice versa.
          \item Patch for the unproportionate whitespace issue in popular Bangla fonts.
          \item Full support for all the common commands and environments.

\item[version]  (2026-01-02)
\item[last changes] 2026-01-02
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) Latexdiff is a Perl script for visual mark up and revision of significant differences between two LaTeX 
          files. Various options are available for visual markup using standard LaTeX packages such as  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/color}{color} . 
          Changes not directly affecting visible text, for example in formatting commands, are still marked in 
          the LaTeX source. A rudimentary revision facility is provided by another Perl script, latexrevise, which 
          accepts or rejects all changes. Manual editing of the difference file can be used to override this default 
          behaviour and accept or reject selected changes only.

\index{Package!latexmk}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/latexmk}
\item[name] \texttt{latexmk}
\item[caption] Fully automated LaTeX document generation
\item[author] Collins, John
\index{Author!Collins, John}
\item[author] McLean, Evan
\index{Author!McLean, Evan}
\item[author] Musliner, David J.
\index{Author!Musliner, David J.}
\item[copyright] John Collins (1998-2025)
\item[license] gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
\index{License!gpl2}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 2}
\item[version] 4.88 (2026-03-09)
\item[last changes] 2026-03-09
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) Latexmk completely automates the process of generating a LaTeX document. Given the source files for a 
          document, latexmk issues the appropriate sequence of commands to generate a  \texttt{.dvi} , \texttt{.ps} , \texttt{.pdf} or 
          hardcopy version of the document.

          An important feature is the ''preview continuous mode'', where the script watches all of the source files 
          (primary file and included TeX and graphics files), and reruns LaTeX, etc., whenever a source file has 
          changed. Thus a previewer can offer a display of the document’s latest state.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Manual page, PDF}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/latexmk/latexmk.pdf}
