\section[\texttt{mnttex} -- Tools for the "The Secret History of the Mongols"]{\texttt{mnttex} -- Tools for the "The Secret History of the Mongols"}\label{pkg:mnttex}
\index{Package!mnttex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/mnttex}
\item[name] \texttt{mnttex}
\item[caption] Tools for the "The Secret History of the Mongols"
\item[author] Corff, Oliver
\index{Author!Corff, Oliver}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.3
\item[description] (no language specified) The Secret History of the Mongols (Monggol-un niguca tobciyan→MNT) is the oldest work of Mongolian literature 
          surviving today. Though the language of the text is Middle Mongolian, the text was written entirely in 
          Chinese characters which were used to render Mongolian phonetically.

          Modern tools for typing, editing and typesetting Chinese do not easily lend themselves for preparing 
          research documentation due to pecularities of the historical source.

          The MNTTeX package assists the scholar typesetting the complex Chinese material by accessing all characters 
          either by number or pronounciation as well as offering convenient access to small or combined characters.

          The MNTTeX package relies on an existing environment for processing Chinese characters and assumes that 
          the package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cjk}{CJK} is installed. It is further required 
          to have a recent inputenc package with ucs support from the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/unicode}{unicode} package. 
          Without these, MNTTeX is not likely to work. Furthermore it is required to use the font zysong.ttf or 
          a similar font in Song style. Since not all characters used in the MNT are provided by modern fonts they 
          had to be made for this package. Being closely modelled according to Song style, these especially made 
          characters would stand out in stark contrast from e.g. Kaiti style character sets. Limited in number, 
          these individual characters were coded as scalable vector images, rather than as font. No difference 
          between these characters and ordinary characters can be perceived in print even though the on-screen 
          display may appear hardly intelligible.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/mongolian/MNT/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/mongolian/MNT/doc/mnttex.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./4896453835-mnttex.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/mongolian/MNT}
\item[keyword] \texttt{mongolian} (support for typesetting Mongolian)
\index{Topic!mongolian}
\item[language(s)] no language specified
\index{Language in description/documentation!no language specified}
\item[year] without year
\index{Year!without year}
\item[last access] 2025-02-07
\end{labeling}

\section[\texttt{modernruler} -- Flexible ruler and annotation commands with key-value suppor\ldots]{\texttt{modernruler} -- Flexible ruler and annotation commands with key-value support and vertical writing compatibility}\label{pkg:modernruler}
\index{Package!modernruler}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/modernruler}
\item[name] \texttt{modernruler}
\item[caption] Flexible ruler and annotation commands with key-value support and vertical writing compatibility
\item[author] KKTeX
\index{Author!KKTeX}
\item[copyright] Kosei Kawaguchi (2025-2026)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version] 2.1.6 (2026-02-07)
\item[last changes] 2026-02-07
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a versatile set of commands for drawing rules and creating annotations in LaTeX. 
          While standard LaTeX rules can be rigid, this package introduces more flexible alternatives:  \texttt{{\textbackslash}mruleth} (horizontal 
          rules), \texttt{{\textbackslash}mruletv} (vertical rules), and \texttt{{\textbackslash}undernote} (underlined 
          annotations).

          Key Features:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Key-Value Interface: All commands support a consistent key-value syntax for adjust dimensions (width, height, depth), colors, and dash patterns (dash, dash-len, gap-len).
          \item Underline Annotations: The  \texttt{{\textbackslash}undernote} command allows users to attach descriptive notes to underlined text. It automatically handles positioning, spacing between multiple notes, and provides options for various border styles (solid or dashed boxes).
          \item Vertical Writing Compatibility: Designed with multilingual typesetting in mind, the package is compatible with vertical writing modes, ensuring that rules and notes are oriented correctly.
          \item Customization: Users can update package-wide dfaults at any point in the document using a dedicated set of  \texttt{{\textbackslash}SetUNote…} commands.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/modernruler/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/modernruler/modernruler-doc.pdf}

          of dihydrogen would be written as:

          \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}MOdiagram{\textbraceright}} \\ \texttt{{\textbackslash}atom{\textbraceleft}left{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft} 
          1s = {\textbraceleft}0;up{\textbraceright} {\textbraceright}} \\ \texttt{{\textbackslash}atom{\textbraceleft}right{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft} 
          1s = {\textbraceleft}0;up{\textbraceright} {\textbraceright}} \\ \texttt{{\textbackslash}molecule{\textbraceleft} 
          1sMO = {\textbraceleft}1;pair, {\textbraceright} {\textbraceright}} \\ \texttt{{\textbackslash}end{\textbraceleft}MOdiagram{\textbraceright}} 

          The package also needs the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel}{l3kernel} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3packages}{l3packages} bundles 
          from the LaTeX 3 experimental distribution.

\item[version] 1
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides only two macros viz.  \texttt{{\textbackslash}modromannumeral} which 
          writes the number given as argument in lower case roman numeral with a ‘j’ instead of a ‘i’ as the final 
          letter of numbers greater than 1 and \texttt{{\textbackslash}modroman{\textbraceleft}MyCounter{\textbraceright}} which 
          writes the value of a counter in the same way. You use the first in the same way as the TeX primitive \texttt{{\textbackslash}romannumeral} and 
          the second as LaTeX command \texttt{{\textbackslash}roman} . The default option is 
          ‘vpourv’ with which 5 is ‘translated’ as ‘v’ and option ‘upourv’ whith which the same 5 is given as ‘u’.

\item[description] (no language specified) LaTeX sections have absolute depth, e.g.  \texttt{{\textbackslash}section} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}subsection} , 
          etc. When composing modular documents, we want \emph{relative} depths.

          The  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/coseoul}{coseoul} package provides relative headings, 
          but does not get things right when composing a document modularly from multiple parts. This package provides 
          the missing piece.

          \texttt{modular} relies on \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/coseoul}{coseoul} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/import}{import} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ifthen}{ifthen} .

\section[\texttt{montex} -- Mongolian LaTeX]{\texttt{montex} -- Mongolian LaTeX}\label{pkg:montex}
\index{Package!montex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/montex}
\item[name] \texttt{montex}
\item[caption] Mongolian LaTeX
\item[author] Corff, Oliver
\index{Author!Corff, Oliver}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] IVu.04.092
\item[description] (no language specified) MonTeX provides Mongolian and Manju support for the TeX/LaTeX community.

          Mongolian is a language spoken in North East Asia, namely Mongolia and the Inner Mongol Autonomous Region 
          of China. Today, it is written in an extended Cyrillic alphabet in Mongolia whereas the Uighur writing 
          continues to be in use in Inner Mongolia, though it is also, legally speaking, the official writing system 
          of Mongolia.

          Manju is another language of North East Asia, belonging to the Tungusic branch of the Altaic languages. 
          Though it is hardly spoken nowadays, it survives in written form as Manju was the native language of 
          the rulers of the Qing dynasty (1644–1911) in China. Large quantities of documents of the Imperial Archives 
          survive, as well as some of the finest dictionaries ever compiled in Asia, like the Pentaglot, a dictionary 
          comprising Manju, Tibetan, Mongolian, Uighur and Chinese. MonTeX provides all necessary characters for 
          writing standard Mongolian in Cyrillic and Classical (aka Traditional or Uighur) writing, and Manju as 
          well as transliterated Tibetan texts, for which purpose a number of additional characters was created.

          In MonTeX, both Mongolian and Manju are entered in romanized form. The retransliteration (from Latin 
          input to Mongolian and Manju output) is completely realized in TeX/Metafont so that no external preprocessor 
          is required.

          Please note that most of the enhanced functions of MonTeX require a working e-LaTeX environment. This 
          is especially true when compiling documents with Mongolian or Manju as the main document language. It 
          is recommended to choose pdfelatex as the resulting PDF files are truly portable. Vertical text generated 
          by MonTeX is not supported in DVI.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/mongolian/montex/doc/montex.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./7731006575-montex.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/mongolian/montex/README}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/mongolian/montex}

\item[description] (no language specified) Montserrat is a geometric sans-serif typeface designed by Julieta Ulanovsky, inspired by posters and 
          signage from her historical Buenos Aires neighborhood of the same name. It is rather close in spirit 
          to Gotham and Proxima Nova, but has its own individual appearance — more informal, less extended, and 
          more idiosyncratic.

          It is provided in a total of nine different weights, each having eight figure styles and small caps in 
          both upright and italic shapes.

          There are two quite different versions that don’t fit into the usual LaTeX classifications. The version 
          having the appellation ''Alternates'' has letter shapes that are much more rounded than the default version, 
          reflecting the signage in the neighborhood of Montserrat.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/montserrat/doc/montserrat-doc.pdf}

\section[\texttt{moreenum} -- More enumeration options]{\texttt{moreenum} -- More enumeration options}\label{pkg:moreenum}
\index{Package!moreenum}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/moreenum}
\item[name] \texttt{moreenum}
\item[caption] More enumeration options
\item[author] Bradley, Seamus
\index{Author!Bradley, Seamus}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.03
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the following new enumerate styles:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}greek} for lowercase Greek letters;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}Greek} for uppercase Greek letters;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}enumHex} for uppercase hexadecimal enumeration;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}enumhex} for lowercase hexadecimal enumeration;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}enumbinary} for binary enumeration;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}enumoctal} for octal enumeration;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}levelnth} for ''1st'', ''2nd'', ''3rd'' etc., with the ''nth''s on the baseline;
          \item  \texttt{raisenth} for ''1st'', ''2nd'', ''3rd'' etc., with the ''nth''s raised;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}nthwords} for ''first'', ''second'', ''third'' etc.;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}Nthwords} for ''First'', ''Second'', ''Third'' etc.;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}NTHWORDS} for ''FIRST'', ''SECOND'', ''THIRD'' etc.;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}nwords} for ''one'', ''two'', ''three'' etc.;
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}Nwords} for ''One'', ''Two'', ''Three'' etc.; and
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}NWORDS} for ''ONE'', ''TWO'', ''THREE'' etc.
          \end{itemize}
Each of these works with  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem}{enumitem} ’s ''starred 
          variant'' feature. So \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}enumerate{\textbraceright}[label={\textbackslash}enumhex*]} will 
          output a hex enumerated list. Enumitem provides a \texttt{start=0} option for starting your 
          enumerations at 0.

          The package requires  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/alphalph}{alphalph} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/enumitem}{enumitem} (of 
          course), \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/binhex}{binhex} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/nth}{nth} , 
          all of which are widely available.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/moreenum/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/moreenum/moreenum-doc.pdf}

\section[\texttt{moremath} -- Additional commands for typesetting maths]{\texttt{moremath} -- Additional commands for typesetting maths}\label{pkg:moremath}
\index{Package!moremath}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/moremath}
\item[name] \texttt{moremath}
\item[caption] Additional commands for typesetting maths
\item[author] Ilg, Marcel
\index{Author!Ilg, Marcel}
\item[copyright] Marcel Ilg (2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.5.0 (2024-08-20)
\item[last changes] 2024-08-20
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides several document level commands to ease typesetting of maths with LaTeX.

          This package provides complementary commands to all operators defined by  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} which 
          typeset the operators together with delimiters (which can be scaled manually, automatically or not at 
          all). These commands also accept optional sub- and superscripts.

          Additionally, this package provides several commands to typeset gradient, divergence, curl, Laplace, 
          and d’Alembert operators. Those commands also accept an optional subscript and their appearance can be 
          modified using key-value options.

          Furthermore several commands for producing row and column vectors, as well as (anti-)diagonal matrices 
          and identity matrices, utilizing  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mathtools}{mathtools} ’ \texttt{matrix*} family 
          of environments, are provided.

          Most of the document level commands defined by this package can also be disabled using a package load-time 
          option to avoid clashes with commands defined by other packages.

          The package depends on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mathtools}{mathtools} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bm}{bm} (optional), 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsfonts}{amssymb} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/moremath/README.md}

\item[last changes] 2024-02-02
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package aims to solve the error ''No room for a new  \texttt{{\textbackslash}write} '', 
          which occurs when the user, or when the user’s packages have ‘allocated too many streams’ using \texttt{{\textbackslash}newwrite} (TeX 
          has a fixed maximum number – 16 – such streams built-in to its code). The package hooks into TeX primitive 
          commands associated with writing to files; it should be loaded near the beginning of the sequence of 
          loading packages for a document.

          The package uses the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel}{l3kernel} bundle.

          Option ‘autoplay’ causes the media clip to be started right after the page has loaded. This is useful

\item[description] (no language specified) The Computer Modern fonts are available in Type 1 format, but these renditions are somewhat thin and 
          spindly, and produce much lighter results than the originals. It is alternatively possible to use Metafont 
          bitmaps, but this has its disadvantages in comparison with vector fonts.

          These fonts are conversions to Type 3 fonts, done entirely in MetaPost; they are vector fonts which are 
          a direct conversion from the original Metafont files, so they are the design most authentic to the originals.

          However, these fonts, because they are PostScript Type 3 fonts, are not suitable for on-screen reading, 
          and should probably only be used for printing.

          Note: do NOT add the map file to updmap!

          with only and only one run of LaTeX, pdfLaTeX or XeLaTeX (no separate runs of mpost).

          feature of current TeX distributions, so that the whole process is automatic and the end user is saved

\index{Package!mptopdf}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\index{Package!pdf-mps-supp (alias for mptopdf)}
\index{Alias!pdf-mps-supp (for mptopdf)}
\item[name] \texttt{mptopdf}
\item[caption] Direct MetaPost graphics support in PDF
\item[author] Hagen, Hans
\index{Author!Hagen, Hans}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a set of macros and a script for MetaPost graphics support. All files are maintained 
          as part of the ConTeXt distribution.

          The macros provide support for the use of MetaPost graphics output directly in pdfTeX, either in ConTeXt 
          or using the LaTeX  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics}{graphics} package under pdfTeX.

\section[\texttt{msx2msa} -- Simulate msxm and msym fonts using msam and msbm]{\texttt{msx2msa} -- Simulate msxm and msym fonts using msam and msbm}\label{pkg:msx2msa}

\item[license] noinfo = noinfo 
\index{License!noinfo}
\index{License!noinfo}
\item[version]  (1992-08-16)
\item[last changes] 1992-08-16
\item[year] 1992
\index{Year!1992}
\item[description] (no language specified) In the deeps of time, the AMS distributed mathematical symbol fonts called  \texttt{msxm} and \texttt{msym} ; 
          these fonts were designed using the original (SAIL) version of Metafont and for a long time after the 
          demise of that system were only available as 300 dpi bitmaps.

          Eventually, the symbols were re-implemented using ‘modern’ Metafont in fonts called  \texttt{msam} and \texttt{msbm} . 
          The virtual fonts of this bundle implement the encoding of the old fonts using the glyphs of the new 
          fonts, and can be used as drop-in replacements in documents (and even when processing DVI files).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/vf-files/msx2msa/README}

\section[\texttt{multi-sudoku} -- Create and customise Sudoku grids of various sizes]{\texttt{multi-sudoku} -- Create and customise Sudoku grids of various sizes}\label{pkg:multi-sudoku}
\index{Package!multi-sudoku}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/multi-sudoku}
\item[name] \texttt{multi-sudoku}
\item[caption] Create and customise Sudoku grids of various sizes
\item[author] Bartolo Alegre, Luis F.
\index{Author!Bartolo Alegre, Luis F.}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.00
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides tools for typesetting Sudoku grids of various sizes in LaTeX. Unlike other Sudoku 
          packages which are typically limited to the standard 9×9 layout, this package supports a broad range 
          of grid sizes – from trivial 1×1 puzzles to extended 49×49 Sudokus – that’s the limit for now! Grids 
          are drawn with our sudoku environment, which is based on using LaTeX’s native tabular environment. We 
          include intuitive options to control dimensions, font size, and grid thickness. Entries in the grid are 
          inserted as in a regular table, thus making it simple to create, customise, and fill Sudoku puzzles manually.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/multi-sudoku/multi-sudoku-documentation.pdf}

\section[\texttt{multicol} -- Intermix single and multiple columns]{\texttt{multicol} -- Intermix single and multiple columns}\label{pkg:multicol}
\index{Package!multicol}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/multicol}
\item[name] \texttt{multicol}
\item[caption] Intermix single and multiple columns
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[author] Mittelbach, Frank
\index{Author!Mittelbach, Frank}
\item[copyright] Frank Mittelbach (1989-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 2.0b (2025-10-21)
\item[last changes] 2025-10-21
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) Multicol defines a multicols environment which typesets text in multiple columns (up to a maximum of 
          10), and (by default) balances the end of each column at the end of the environment. The package enables 
          you to switch between any (permitted) number of columns at will: there is no imposed ''clear page'' operation, 
          as there is in unadorned LaTeX at a switch between {\textbackslash}onecolumn and {\textbackslash}twocolumn 
          sections. The multicolumn environment can also be used inside a box, thus allowing multicolumned insets 
          in text.

          Multicol patches the output routine, and may clash with other packages that do the same (e.g.,  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable}{longtable} ); 
          furthermore, there is no provision for single column floats inside a multicolumn environment, so figures 
          and tables must be coded in-line (using, for example, the H modifier of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/float}{float} package).

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools}{latex-tools} bundle 
          in the LaTeX \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/required}{required} distribution.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/multicol.pdf}

\item[version]  (2024-03-24)
\item[last changes] 2024-03-24

\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides several commands for generating footnotes which correspond to multiple footnote 
          numbers (resp. marks).

          In some cases, you may wish for certain footnotes to correspond to several places in your text. The traditional 
          solution usually involves writing the same footnote mark multiple times at the corresponding places. 
          However, this approach makes it difficult to see at once how many times a footnote has been referred 
          to. Therefore, the current package proposes another method: writing the footnote marks in linear order, 
          and allowing a footnote text to match several of these marks.

          macros and environments. These wrappers allow one to clearly specify multiple translations for the arguments

\item[description] (no language specified) The package redefines  \texttt{{\textbackslash}makeindex} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}index} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}printindex} commands 
          to deal with multiple indexes. In each case, the command gains a (first) argument specifying the index 
          in question: the name used there is used as a name for the index files, so one then uses the command\\ \texttt{makeindex 
          <index file>} \\for each index, separately.

          The package does not work in documents using  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amscls}{AMS classes} ; 
          the AMS provide a replacement package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmidx}{amsmidx} , 
          which is based on multind.

\item[description] (no language specified) MusiXTeX provides a set of macros, based on the earlier  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/musictex}{MusicTeX} , 
          for typesetting music with TeX. To produce optimal spacing, MusiXTeX is a three-pass system: \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etex}{etex} , \texttt{musixflx} , 
          and \texttt{etex} again. ( \texttt{Musixflx} is a \texttt{lua} script 
          that is provided in the bundle.) The three-pass process, optionally followed by processing for printed 
          output, is automated by the \texttt{musixtex} wrapper script.

          The package uses its own  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/musixtex-fonts}{specialised fonts} , 
          which must be available on the system for musixtex to run.

          This version of MusiXTeX builds upon work by  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/musixtex-egler}{Andreas 
          Egler} , whose own version is no longer being developed.

          The MusiXTeX macros are universally acknowledged to be challenging to use directly: the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pmx}{pmx} preprocessor 
          compiles a simpler input language to MusiXTeX macros..

\section[\texttt{musixtnt} -- A MusiXTeX extension library that enables transformations of\ldots]{\texttt{musixtnt} -- A MusiXTeX extension library that enables transformations of the effect of notes commands}\label{pkg:musixtnt}
\index{Package!musixtnt}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/musixtnt}
\item[name] \texttt{musixtnt}
\item[caption] A MusiXTeX extension library that enables transformations of the effect of notes commands
\item[author] Tennent, Bob
\index{Author!Tennent, Bob}
\item[copyright] Bob Tennent (2015-2016)
\item[license] gpl2 = GNU General Public License, version 2 (free)
\index{License!gpl2}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 2}
\item[version]  (2016-01-30)
\item[last changes] 2016-01-30
\item[year] 2016
\index{Year!2016}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package includes an archive containing a MusiXTeX extension library  \texttt{musixtnt} and 
          C source code, binaries for Windows (32 bit and 64 bit) and MacOSX, and documentation for two programs: 
          fixmsxpart and msxlint.

          musixtnt.tex provides a macro  \texttt{{\textbackslash}TransformNotes} that enables 
          transformations of the effect of notes commands such as \texttt{{\textbackslash}notes} . 
          In general, the effect of \texttt{{\textbackslash}TransformNotes{\textbraceleft}input{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}output{\textbraceright}} is 
          that notes commands in the source will expect their arguments to match the input pattern, but the notes 
          will be typeset according to the output pattern. An example is extracting single-instrument parts from 
          a multi-instrument score.

          fixmsxpart corrects note spacing in a single-part MusiXTeX source (possibly derived from a multi-instrument 
          score and as a result having irregular note spacing).

          msxlint detects incorrectly formatted notes lines in a MusiXTeX source file. This should be used before 
          using  \texttt{{\textbackslash}TransformNotes} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/musixtnt/doc/msxlint.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./6534622661-msxlint.pdf|

\item[description] (no language specified) mwcls is a set of document classes for LaTeX 2e designed with Polish typographical tradition in mind. 
          Classes include: ‘ \texttt{mwart} ’ (which is a replacement for ‘ \texttt{article} ’), 
          ‘ \texttt{mwrep} ’ (replacing ‘ \texttt{report} ’), and ‘ \texttt{mwbk} ’ 
          (replacing ‘ \texttt{book} ’). Most features present in standard classes work with mwcls 
          classes. Some extensions/exceptions include: sectioning commands allow for second optional argument (it 
          is possible to state different texts for running head and for TOC), new environments ‘ \texttt{itemize*} ’ 
          and ‘ \texttt{enumerate*} ’ for lists with long items, page styles have variants for normal, 
          opening, closing, and blank pages.

\item[author] Tennent, Bob

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version]  (2020-01-23)
\item[last changes] 2020-01-23
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) Many font families available for use with LaTeX are available at multiple weights. Many Type 1-oriented 
          support packages for such fonts re-define the standard  \texttt{{\textbackslash}mddefault} or \texttt{{\textbackslash}bfdefault} macros. 
          This can create difficulties if the weight desired for one font family isn’t available for another font 
          family, or if it differs from the weight desired for another font family.

          The package provides a solution to these difficulties.

\item[last changes] 2020-10-23

\item[description] (no language specified) The file  \texttt{mylatex.ltx} permits you to create a format that pre-loads a set of package 
          files (and/or other macros) that you regularly use. In some circumstances, this can be a great advantage 
          (though on an ordinarily fast modern computer on the desktop, gains will be limited).

          The general scheme is to initialise your usage by a command of the form:\\ \texttt{latex -ini 
          mylatex.ltx <document>} \\whick will create a format file \texttt{mylatex.fmt} , 
          which you then use as:\\ \texttt{latex -fmt=mylatex <document>}

\section[\texttt{namedef} -- TeX definitions with named parameters]{\texttt{namedef} -- TeX definitions with named parameters}\label{pkg:namedef}
\index{Package!namedef}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/namedef}
\item[name] \texttt{namedef}
\item[caption] TeX definitions with named parameters
\item[author] Oleinik, Phelype
\index{Author!Oleinik, Phelype}
\item[copyright] Phelype Oleinik (2019-2020)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0 (2020-06-20)
\item[last changes] 2020-06-20
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a prefix  \texttt{{\textbackslash}named} to be used in TeX definitions 
          so that parameters can be identified by their name rather than by number, giving parameters a semantic 
          rather than syntactic meaning, making it easy to understand long definitions.

          A usual definition reads:

          \begin{verbatim}
\def\SayHello#1{Hello, #1!}
          \end{verbatim}
but with  \texttt{namedef} you can replace \texttt{\#1} by, say, \texttt{\#[person]} :

          
          \begin{verbatim}
\named\def\SayHello#[person]{Hello, #[person]!}
          \end{verbatim}
and  \texttt{{\textbackslash}named} will figure out the numbering of the parameters 
          for you.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/namedef/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/namedef/namedef.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./9651357191-namedef.pdf|

\item[author] Marvan, Michal
\index{Author!Marvan, Michal}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) Nath is a LaTeX (both 2e and 2.09) style to separate presentation and content in mathematical typography. 
          The style delivers a particular context-dependent presentation on the basis of a rather coarse context-independent 
          notation. Highlighted features: depending on the context, the command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}frac} produces 
          either built-up or case or solidus fractions, with parentheses added whenever required for preservation 
          of the mathematical meaning; delimiters adapt their size to the material enclosed, rendering \texttt{{\textbackslash}left} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}right} almost 
          obsolete.

\item[description] (no language specified) Navigator implements PDF features for all formats (with some limitations in ConTeXt) with pdfTeX, LuaTeX 
          and XeTeX (i.e. xdvipdfmx). Features include:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Customizable outlines (i.e. bookmarks);
          \item Anchors;
          \item Links and actions (e.g. JavaScript or user-defined PDF actions);
          \item File embedding (not in ConTeXt);
          \item Document information and PDF viewer's display (not in ConTeXt); and
          \item Commands to create and use raw PDF objects.
          \end{itemize}
Navigator requires  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/texapi}{texapi} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/yax}{yax} , 
          both version at least 1.03.

\section[\texttt{nccsect} -- A re-implementation of sections, captions and tocs]{\texttt{nccsect} -- A re-implementation of sections, captions and tocs}\label{pkg:nccsect}
\index{Package!nccsect}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/nccsect}
\item[name] \texttt{nccsect}
\item[caption] A re-implementation of sections, captions and tocs
\item[author] Rozhenko, Alexander I.
\index{Author!Rozhenko, Alexander I.}
\item[copyright] Alexander I. Rozhenko (2002-2006)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.5
\item[description] (no language specified) The package user has section control commands that mirror the internal controls used in LaTeX. In particular, 
          the user may express the section level explicitly in a {\textbackslash}startsection command, rather 
          than by name (as in {\textbackslash}section, {\textbackslash}subsection, etc., in LaTeX itself, 
          defined in terms of an internal command). By using this {\textbackslash}startsection, the user 
          may have astounding depths of sections, which is sometimes useful in extreme typesetting applications. 
          A {\textbackslash}sectionstyle command controls the appearance of predefined, or user-defined sections, 
          and {\textbackslash}DeclareSection allows the user to create sectioning or caption commands, or 
          to modify existing ones.

          The package also extends user control of the appearance of tables of contents, etc., using a command 
          {\textbackslash}DeclareTOCEntry.

          This package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ncctools}{ncctools} bundle.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Bundle readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ncctools/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ncctools/doc/nccsect.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5727714057-nccsect.pdf|

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) This package's theorems have two distinguishing characteristics. First, theorem numbering uses dynamic 
          counters (specified by using the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dcounter}{dcounter} package, 
          which gives the user considerable flexibility in counting styles. Second, the environment isn't defined 
          as a trivlist (as LaTeX theorems are), which gives extra flexibility in using the environment. In addition, 
          parameter definition is explicit and well-organised, and there is a QED-symbol-placing command.

          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/nccfancyhdr}{improvements to fancy headers} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/nccfloats}{float ''styles'', mini floats, side floats} ;

          Updated (2022) North Dakota State University LaTeX thesis class features several functionalities, including

          nesting left and right quotes that properly change between double and single quotes according to their 
          nesting level. For example, the input \texttt{{\textbackslash}nlq Foo {\textbackslash}nlq 
          bar{\textbackslash}nrq{\textbackslash} bletch{\textbackslash}nrq} will be typeset 
          as if it had been entered as ''Foo ‘bar’ bletch''.

\section[\texttt{newclude} -- Reimplemented {\textbackslash}include system for LaTeX]{\texttt{newclude} -- Reimplemented {\textbackslash}include system for LaTeX}\label{pkg:newclude}
\index{Package!newclude}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/newclude}
\item[name] \texttt{newclude}
\item[caption] Reimplemented {\textbackslash}include system for LaTeX
\item[author] Swift, Matt
\index{Author!Swift, Matt}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 2
\item[description] (no language specified) A LaTeX package providing a backwards-compatible reimplementation of  \texttt{{\textbackslash}include} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}includeonly} . 
          The principal new features are:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item the restriction that  \texttt{{\textbackslash}clearpage} s must surround an included file is removed,
          \item the restriction that  \texttt{{\textbackslash}include} s cannot be nested is removed, and
          \item the provision of hooks to be executed before and after the contents of an included file.
          \end{itemize}
Newclude accomplishes the first two by using a single  \texttt{.aux} file instead of many. 
          Newclude also provides the experimental functionality of the unsupported package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/includex}{includex} , 
          which allows you to include partial contents of independent LaTeX files that can also be processed on 
          their own (that is, files that contain \texttt{{\textbackslash}documentclass} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}document{\textbraceright}} , 
          etc.).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Bundle README}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frankenstein/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/frankenstein/newclude.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./1386094956-newclude.pdf|

\index{Package!newtx}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/newtx}
\item[name] \texttt{newtx}
\item[caption] Alternative uses of the TX fonts, with improved metrics
\item[author] Sharpe, Michael
\index{Author!Sharpe, Michael}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.756 (2025-01-09)
\item[last changes] 2025-01-09
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) The bundle splits  \texttt{txfonts.sty} (from the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/txfonts}{TX 
          fonts} distribution) into two independent packages, \texttt{newtxtext.sty} and \texttt{newtxmath.sty} , 
          each with fixes and enhancements.

          \texttt{newtxmath} ’s metrics have been re-evaluated to provide a less tight appearance, 
          and to provide a \texttt{libertine} option that substitutes \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/libertineotf}{Libertine} italic 
          and Greek letter for the existing math italic and Greek glyphs, making a mathematics package that matches 
          Libertine text quite well.

          \texttt{newtxmath} can also use the maths italic font provided with the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/garamondx}{garamondx} package, 
          thus offering a garamond-alike text-with-maths combination.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Notes concerning math fonts}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/newtx/doc/mathnotes.pdf}

          or by XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX. The command provided is

          \texttt{{\textbackslash}newunicodechar{\textbraceleft}<char>{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}<code>{\textbraceright}}

          its replacement.

\item[description] (no language specified) The package allows the definition of  \texttt{{\textbackslash}verb} variants which 
          add TeX code before and after the verbatim text (e.g., quotes or surrounding \texttt{{\textbackslash}fbox{\textbraceleft}{\textbraceright}} ). 
          When used together with the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/shortvrb}{shortvrb} package it 
          allows the definition of short verbatim characters which use this package’s variant instead of the normal \texttt{{\textbackslash}verb} .

          In addition, it is possible to collect an argument verbatim to either typeset or write it into a file.

          The  \texttt{{\textbackslash}Verbdef} command defines verbatim text to a macro which 
          can later be used to write the verbatim text to a file.

\section[\texttt{nicematrix} -- Improve the typesetting of matrices and tabulars with PGF]{\texttt{nicematrix} -- Improve the typesetting of matrices and tabulars with PGF}\label{pkg:nicematrix}
\index{Package!nicematrix}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/nicematrix}
\item[name] \texttt{nicematrix}
\item[caption] Improve the typesetting of matrices and tabulars with PGF
\item[author] Pantigny, François
\index{Author!Pantigny, François}
\item[copyright] F. Pantigny (2018-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 7.8 (2026-03-11)
\item[last changes] 2026-03-11
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package is based on the package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/array}{array} . It creates \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{PGF/TikZ} nodes 
          under the cells of the array and uses these nodes to provide functionalities to construct tabulars, arrays 
          and matrices.

          Among the features :

          \begin{itemize}
          \item continuous dotted lines for the mathematical matrices;
          \item exterior rows and columns (so-called border matrices);
          \item control of the width of the columns;
          \item tools to color rows and columns with a good PDF result;
          \item blocks of cells;
          \item tabular notes;
          \item etc.
          \end{itemize}
The package requires and loads  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/array}{array} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{pgfcore} , 
          and the module \texttt{shapes} of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{PGF} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/nicematrix/nicematrix.pdf}

\section[\texttt{nicetext} -- Minimal markup for simple text (Wikipedia style) and documen\ldots]{\texttt{nicetext} -- Minimal markup for simple text (Wikipedia style) and documentation}\label{pkg:nicetext}
\index{Package!nicetext}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/nicetext}
\item[name] \texttt{nicetext}
\item[caption] Minimal markup for simple text (Wikipedia style) and documentation
\item[author] Lück, Uwe
\index{Author!Lück, Uwe}
\item[copyright] Uwe Lück (2009-2015)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] r0.67
\item[description] (no language specified) The bundle offers ''minimal'' markup syntax for various simple kinds of text. The user will typically 
          involve little more than is printed, and will still get LaTeX quality.

          The bundle provides four packages:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/wiki}{wiki} addresses general texts, marked up in the simple style used on Wikipedia;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/niceverb}{niceverb} is yet another means of documenting LaTeX packages: it offers syntax-aware typesetting of meta-variables (macro arguments) and for referring to commands (and their syntax) in footnotes, section titles etc.;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fifinddo}{fifinddo} aims to parse plain text or (La)TeX files using TeX, and to write the results to an external file; the package is used by another member of the bundle:
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/makedoc}{makedoc} , which provides the means to produce typeset documentation direct from package files.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Niceverb documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/nicetext/doc/niceverb.pdf}

\item[version]  (2016-01-22)
\item[last changes] 2016-01-22
\item[year] 2016
\index{Year!2016}
\item[description] (no language specified) This LaTeX document class tries to adhere to the Biographical Sketch formatting requirements outlined 
          in NIH Notice [NOT-OD-15-032] (http://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/notice-files/NOT-OD-15-032.html). This 
          new format is required for applications submitted for due dates on or after May 25, 2015.

          The package tries to mimic the example documents provided on the [SF 424 (R\&R) Forms and Applications 
          page] (http://grants.nih.gov/grants/funding/424/index.htm\#format) as closely as possible. The author 
          has used this class for his own grant submissions; however he offers no guarantee of conformity to NIH 
          requirements.

\item[last changes] 2022-02-13
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package carefully selects and defines 9 colors for 13 hues each. All colors with the same suffix 
          number have equal luminance level. Also the color black is of level 0, and the color white is of level 
          10.

          By simply choosing two colors in the above list, which differ in level by at least 5, as foreground and 
          background colors, you will get proper WCAG Color Contrast.

\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 0.03
\item[description] (no language specified) This is a compatible rewrite of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latexdb}{LaTeXDB} (by Hans-Georg 
          Eßer) or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ratexdb}{ratexdb} (by this package's author) in C\#/.Net. 
          It works under Mono, too.

          It is a preprocessor which performs SQL queries on a database and creates LaTeX code for the resulting 
          rows. Ratexdb implements a few improvements, e.g. regexp postprocessing, command-line options, some protection 
          against SQL injection, replacement of LaTeX reserved characters.

\section[\texttt{non-decimal-units} -- Display and manipulate historical non-decimal units]{\texttt{non-decimal-units} -- Display and manipulate historical non-decimal units}\label{pkg:non-decimal-units}
\index{Package!non-decimal-units}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/non-decimal-units}
\item[name] \texttt{non-decimal-units}
\item[caption] Display and manipulate historical non-decimal units
\item[author] Eriksen, Mikkel Eide
\index{Author!Eriksen, Mikkel Eide}
\item[license] cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
\index{License!cc-by-sa-4}
\index{License!CC BY-SA 4.0}
\item[version]  (2024-01-25)
\item[last changes] 2024-01-25
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) Many historical unit systems were non-decimal. For example, the Danish rigsdaler — where 1 rigsdaler 
          consists of 6 mark, each again consisting of 16 skilling for a total of 96 skilling per rigsdaler — was 
          used from 1625 to 1875, when currency was decimalised to the current system of 1 krone = 100 øre.

          Units for such measures as length, area, weight, and so on were also often non-decimal, and in fact remain 
          so in the few places of the world that have not made the change to the metric system.

          The non-decimal numbers were chosen due to their larger number of division factors, which simplified 
          mental arithmetic, eg. when sharing an amount of money or dividing goods.

          This package enables creation and configuration of such units to facilitate their presentation in textual 
          and tabular contexts, as well as simple arithmetic.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/non-decimal-units/docs/non-decimal-units.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./9331479190-non-decimal-units.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/non-decimal-units/README.md}
\item[contact] \textit{bugs}: \url{https://github.com/mikkelee/latex-units/issues}
\index{Contact!bugs}
\item[contact] \textit{repository}: \url{https://github.com/mikkelee/latex-units}
\index{Contact!repository}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/non-decimal-units}

          than ‘plain’ on the opening pages you must use \texttt{{\textbackslash}thispagestyle} on

\index{Package!noprot}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/noprot}
\item[name] \texttt{noprot}
\item[caption] Avoid the need for protection
\item[author] Sozuer, Sami
\index{Author!Sozuer, Sami}
\item[license] noinfo = noinfo 
\index{License!noinfo}
\index{License!noinfo}
\item[version]  (2004-08-16)
\item[last changes] 2004-08-16
\item[year] 2004
\index{Year!2004}
\item[description] (no language specified) An approach to reducing the need for  \texttt{{\textbackslash}protect} . The package 
          re-writes the \texttt{{\textbackslash}thanks} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}caption} and 
          sectioning commands ( \texttt{{\textbackslash}chapter} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}section} , 
          …), \texttt{{\textbackslash}addcontentsline} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}addtocontents} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}bibitem} , 
          to suppress the expansion of their arguments when those arguments are written to the \texttt{.aux} file.

          The mechanism is not entirely satisfactory: there is still a problem with things written with the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}mark*} commands, 
          and one loses the facility of making direct reference to the current page (i.e., one must use \texttt{{\textbackslash}pageref} for 
          such things).
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex209/contrib/misc/noprot.sty}

\section[\texttt{notes2bib} -- Integrating notes into the bibliography]{\texttt{notes2bib} -- Integrating notes into the bibliography}\label{pkg:notes2bib}
\index{Package!notes2bib}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/notes2bib}
\item[name] \texttt{notes2bib}
\item[caption] Integrating notes into the bibliography
\item[author] Wright, Joseph
\index{Author!Wright, Joseph}
\item[copyright] Joseph Wright (2007-2013, 2016, 2019)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 2.0m (2019-09-28)
\item[last changes] 2019-09-28
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package defines a new type of note, bibnote, which will always be added to the bibliography. The 
          package allows footnotes and endnotes to be moved into the bibliography in the same way. The package 
          can be used with natbib and BibLaTeX as well as plain LaTeX citations. Both sorted and unsorted bibliography 
          styles are supported.

          The package uses the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel}{LaTeX 3} macros and the associated \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3packages}{xpackages 
          bundle} . It also makes use of the e-TeX extensions (any post-2005 LaTeX distribution will provide 
          these by default, but users of older systems may need to use an \texttt{elatex} command or 
          equivalent).

          The package relies on LaTeX 3 support from the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3kernel}{l3kernel} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3packages}{l3packages} bundles.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/notes2bib/README.md}

\section[\texttt{notoccite} -- Prevent trouble from citations in table of contents, etc]{\texttt{notoccite} -- Prevent trouble from citations in table of contents, etc}\label{pkg:notoccite}
\index{Package!notoccite}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/notoccite}
\item[name] \texttt{notoccite}
\item[caption] Prevent trouble from citations in table of contents, etc
\item[author] Arseneau, Donald
\index{Author!Arseneau, Donald}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[description] (no language specified) If you have  \texttt{{\textbackslash}cite} commands in \texttt{{\textbackslash}section} -like 
          commands, or in \texttt{{\textbackslash}caption} , the citation will also appear in 
          the table of contents, or list of whatever. If you are also using an unsrt-like bibliography style, these 
          citations will come at the very start of the bibliography, which is confusing. This package suppresses 
          the effect.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/notoccite/notoccite.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./7484781491-notoccite.pdf|

\section[\texttt{noweb} -- A simple extensible literate programming tool]{\texttt{noweb} -- A simple extensible literate programming tool}\label{pkg:noweb}
\index{Package!noweb}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/noweb}
\item[name] \texttt{noweb}
\item[caption] A simple extensible literate programming tool
\item[author] Ramsey, Norman
\index{Author!Ramsey, Norman}
\item[copyright] Norman Ramsey (1989-2018)
\item[license] other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
\index{License!other-free}
\index{License!Free license not otherwise listed}
\item[license] bsd2 = Simplified BSD License (free)
\index{License!bsd2}
\index{License!Simplified BSD License}
\item[version] 2.12 (2018-06-20)
\item[last changes] 2018-06-20
\item[year] 2018
\index{Year!2018}
\item[description] (no language specified) Noweb is designed to meet the needs of literate programmers while remaining as simple as possible. Its 
          primary advantages are simplicity, extensibility, and language-independence. Noweb uses 5 control sequences 
          to WEB’s 27. The noweb manual is only 4 and a bit pages; an additional page explains how to customize 
          its LaTeX output. Noweb works ''out of the box'' with any programming language, and supports TeX, LaTeX, 
          and HTML back ends. A back end to support full hypertext or indexing takes about 250 lines; a simpler 
          one can be written in 40 lines of awk. Noweb does not prettyprint natively, but supports prettyprinting 
          through such third-party filters as pretzel and dpp.
\item[documentation]  (English) \textit{Frequently asked questions}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/web/noweb/src/FAQ.html}

          \begin{enumerate}
          \item A plugin for Notepad++ that implements, for the ConTeXt document processing system, 
          \begin{enumerate}
          \item a language lexer for semantic highlighting of TeX, LuaTeX, and ConTeXt commands;
          \item autocompletion of commands with full support for calltips (set in columns);
          \item tagging and insertion of markup and templates, with support for mnemonic keys.
          \end{enumerate}

\index{Package!numberpt}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/numberpt}
\item[name] \texttt{numberpt}
\item[caption] Counters spelled out in Portuguese
\item[author] Frasson, Miguel Vinícius Santini
\index{Author!Frasson, Miguel Vinícius Santini}
\item[copyright] Miguel V. S. Frasson (2019)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0 (2019-07-13)
\item[last changes] 2019-07-13
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) This packages defines commands to display counters spelled out in Portuguese.

          The styles are

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}numberpt} for ''all lowercase''
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}Numberpt} for ''First word capitalized''
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}NumberPt} for ''All Capitalized''
          \item  \texttt{{\textbackslash}NUMBERPT} for ''ALL UPPERCASE''
          \end{itemize}
For example,  \texttt{{\textbackslash}renewcommand{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}thechapter{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}NumberPt{\textbraceleft}chapter{\textbraceright}{\textbraceright}} makes 
          chapter titles to be rendered as ''Capítulo Um'', ''Capítulo Dois'' etc.

          Options are offered to select variations in the spelling of ''14'', or Brazilian vs. European Portuguese 
          forms in the spelling of ''16'', ''17'', and ''19''.

          The package requires  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse}{xparse} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/numberpt/numberpt.pdf}

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.39
\item[description] (no language specified) The package numprint prints numbers with a separator every three digits and converts numbers given as 
          12345.6e789 to 12{\textbackslash},345,6{\textbackslash}cdot 10{\textasciicircum}{\textbraceleft}789{\textbraceright}. 
          Numbers are printed in the current mode (text or math) in order to use the correct font.

          Many things, including the decimal sign, the thousand separator, as well as the product sign can be changed 
          by the user, e.g., to reach 12,345.6{\textbackslash}times 10{\textasciicircum}{\textbraceleft}789{\textbraceright}.

          If an optional argument is given it is printed upright as unit. Numbers can be rounded to a given number 
          of digits. The package supports an automatic, language-dependent change of the number format.

          Tabular alignment using the tabular(*), array, tabularx, and longtable environments (similar to the dcolumn 
          and rccol packages) is supported using all features of numprint. Additional text can be added before 
          and after the formatted number.

\index{Package!nwejm}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/nwejm}
\item[name] \texttt{nwejm}
\item[caption] Support for the journal “North-Western European Journal of Mathematics”
\item[author] Bitouzé, Denis
\index{Author!Bitouzé, Denis}
\item[copyright] Denis Bitouzé (2015-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0.6 (2024-02-08)
\item[last changes] 2024-02-08
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The bundle includes LaTeX classes and BibLaTeX styles files dedicated to the new journal  \href{http://math.univ-lille1.fr/{\textasciitilde}nwejm/}{''North-Western 
          European Journal of Mathematics''} :

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{nwejm} for the complete issues of the journal, aimed at the NWEJM’s team,
          \item  \texttt{nwejmart} , intended for the authors who wish to publish an article in the NWEJM. This class’s goal is to:
          \begin{itemize}
          \item faithfully reproduce the layout of the nwejm, thus enabling the authors to be able to work their document in actual conditions,
          \item provide a number of tools (commands and environments) to facilitate the drafting of documents, in particular those containing mathematical formulas.
          \end{itemize}

          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme.md}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/nwejm/README.md}

          based on KOMA-Script \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/scrreprt}{scrreprt} ; a letter class

          glyph. All components can be adapted for use at other institutions.

\index{Package!oberdiek}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/oberdiek}
\item[name] \texttt{oberdiek}
\item[caption] A bundle of packages submitted by Heiko Oberdiek
\item[author] Oberdiek, Heiko
\index{Author!Oberdiek, Heiko}
\item[copyright] Heiko Oberdiek (2007, 2009-2011)
\item[copyright] Oberdiek Package Support Group (2016-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version]  (2026-03-06)
\item[last changes] 2026-03-06
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) The bundle comprises packages to provide:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/bmpsize}{bmpsize} : get bitmap size and resolution data;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/centernot}{centernot} : a horizontally-centred \texttt{{\textbackslash}not} symbol;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/chemarr}{chemarr} : extensible chemists’ reaction arrows;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/classlist}{classlist} : record information about document class(es) used;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/colonequals}{colonequals} : poor man’s mathematical relation symbols;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvipscol}{dvipscol} : dvips colour stack management;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/engord}{engord} : define counter-printing operations producing English ordinals;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/eolgrab}{eolgrab} : collect arguments delimited by end of line;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/flags}{flags} : setting and clearing flags in bit fields and converting the bit field into a decimal number;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/holtxdoc}{holtxdoc} : extra documentation macros;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hypbmsec}{hypbmsec} : bookmarks in sectioning commands;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hypgotoe}{hypgotoe} : experimental package for links to embedded files;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyphsubst}{hyphsubst} : substitute hyphenation patterns;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ifdraft}{ifdraft} : switch for option draft;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/iflang}{iflang} : provides expandable checks for the current language;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdfcolparallel}{pdfcolparallel} : fixes colour problems in package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/parallel}{parallel} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdfcolparcolumns}{pdfcolparcolumns} : fixes colour problems in package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/parcolumns}{parcolumns} ;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdfcrypt}{pdfcrypt} : setting PDF encryption;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/protecteddef}{protecteddef} : define a command that protected against expansion;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/resizegather}{resizegather} : automatically resize overly large equations;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/rotchiffre}{rotchiffre} : performs simple rotation cyphers;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/scrindex}{scrindex} : redefines environment ‘theindex’ of package ‘index’, if a class from KOMA-Script is loaded;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/setouterhbox}{setouterhbox} : set \texttt{{\textbackslash}hbox} in outer horizontal mode;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/settobox}{settobox} : getting box sizes;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/stackrel}{stackrel} : extensions of the \texttt{{\textbackslash}stackrel} command;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/stampinclude}{stampinclude} : selects the files for {\textbackslash}include by inspecting the timestamp of the .aux file(s);
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tabularht}{tabularht} : tabulars with height specification;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tabularkv}{tabularkv} : key value interface for tabular parameters;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/thepdfnumber}{thepdfnumber} : canonical numbers for use in PDF files and elsewhere;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/twoopt}{twoopt} : commands with two optional arguments;
          \end{itemize}
Each of the packages is represented by two files, a  \texttt{.dtx} (documented source) and 
          a PDF file; the \texttt{.ins} file necessary for installation is extracted by running the \texttt{.dtx} file 
          with Plain TeX.

\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the means to insert OGC (Optional Group Content, commonly known as layers) into 
          PDF presentations. This allows the user to insert any TeX material into separate layers in a PDF document 
          and also insert links which toggle these layers on and off. Parts of the PDF document, such as formatted 
          text, tables, maths formulas or graphics may be switched to visible or invisible state by clicking active 
          links or buttons.

          The documentation discusses the package’s relation to various apparently similar packages.

\section[\texttt{ocgx} -- Use OCGs within a PDF document without JavaScript]{\texttt{ocgx} -- Use OCGs within a PDF document without JavaScript}\label{pkg:ocgx}
\index{Package!ocgx}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/ocgx}
\item[name] \texttt{ocgx}
\item[caption] Use OCGs within a PDF document without JavaScript
\item[author] Gaborit, Paul
\index{Author!Gaborit, Paul}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.5
\item[description] (no language specified) The package extends the  \texttt{ocg} package, which allows you to create OCGs ( \emph{Optional 
          Content Group} s) in PDF documents. (The \texttt{ocg} package is distributed as part 
          of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/asymptote}{Asymptote} .)

          Every OCG includes TeX material into a layer of the PDF file. Each of these layers can be displayed or 
          not. Links can enable or disable the display of OCGs.

          The ocgx package does not use Javascript embedded in the PDF document to enable (to show) or disable 
          (to hide) OCGs.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package demo}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ocgx/demo-ocgx.pdf}

\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package serves as a drop-in replacement for the packages  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ocgx}{ocgx} by 
          Paul Gaborit and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ocg-p}{ocg-p} by Werner Moshammer for the 
          creation of PDF Layers.

          It re-implements the functionality of the  \texttt{ocg} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ocgx}{ocgx} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ocg-p}{ocg-p} packages and adds support for all known 
          engines and back-ends including:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item LaTeX → dvips → ps2pdf/Distiller
          \item (Xe)LaTeX(x) → dvipdfmx
          \item pdfLaTeX and LuaLaTeX .
          \end{itemize}
It also ensures compatibility with the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/media9}{media9} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/animate}{animate} packages.

\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The octavo class is a modification of the standard LaTeX book class. Its purpose is to typeset books 
          following classical design and layout principles, with the express intention of encouraging the making 
          of beautiful books by anyone with access to a good printer and with an inclination towards venerable 
          crafts, e.g., bookbinding.

          The octavo class differs from the book class by implementing many of the proposals and insights of respected 
          experts, especially Jan Tschichold and Hugh Williamson.

          The documentation discusses methods to organise and print out any text into signatures, which can then 
          be gathered, folded and sewn into a book.

\index{Package!odesandpdes}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/odesandpdes}
\item[name] \texttt{odesandpdes}
\item[caption] Optimizing workflow involving odes and pdes
\item[author] McMullen-Diermayr, Anakin J.
\index{Author!McMullen-Diermayr, Anakin J.}
\item[copyright] Anakin McMullen-Diermayr (2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0.0 (2024-01-17)
\item[last changes] 2024-01-17
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package is the solution no one asked for, to a problem nobody had.

          Have you ever thought to yourself "wow, I sure do dislike having to remember multiple macros for my odes 
          and pdes" and the author of this package has to agree, wholeheartedly. In the modern world of "tik-toking" 
          and "family guy surfing" our brains have rotted beyond salvage for even basic levels of cognitive recall. 
          This package aims to fix this, through two macros that have been set to each have an identical form and 
          function with an emphasis on intuitive use. Through setting options, the multiple common notational style 
          are easily swapped between, all by a single option.

          You're Welcome.

\section[\texttt{ofs} -- Macros for managing large font collections]{\texttt{ofs} -- Macros for managing large font collections}\label{pkg:ofs}
\index{Package!ofs}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/ofs}
\item[name] \texttt{ofs}
\item[caption] Macros for managing large font collections
\item[author] Olšák, Petr
\index{Author!Olšák, Petr}
\item[license] knuth = Knuth License (free)
\index{License!knuth}
\index{License!Knuth License}
\item[version]  (2004-05-31)
\item[last changes] 2004-05-31
\item[year] 2004
\index{Year!2004}
\item[description] (no language specified) OFS (Olsak's Font System) is a set of Plain TeX and LaTeX macros for managing large font collections; 
          it has been used by Czech/Slovak users for many years. Main features include:\\

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Mapping from long names of fonts to the metric file name. The user can specify only exact long names in documents.
          \item Support for many font encodings.
          \item Printing of catalogues of fonts and test samples of font families; the interactive macro {\textbackslash}showfonts shows all font families you have installed via OFS.
          \item The user interface is the same for Plain TeX and for LaTeX, but the implementation differs: the LaTeX variant of OFS uses NFSS, but the Plain variant implements its own font management (which may even be better than NFSS)
          \item Support for math fonts including TX fonts.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (English) \textit{EuroTeX paper}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/ofs/doc/papers/eurotex2003-ofs.pdf}

\item[version] 2.7a (2024-03-04)
\item[last changes] 2024-03-04
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) Old Standard is designed to reproduce the actual printing style of the early 20th century, reviving a 
          specific type of Modern (classicist) style of serif typefaces, very commonly used in various editions 
          of the late 19th and early 20th century, but almost completely abandoned later.

          The font supports typesetting of Old and Middle English, Old Icelandic, Cyrillic (with historical characters, 
          extensions for Old Slavonic and localised forms), Gothic transliterations, critical editions of Classical 
          Greek and Latin, and many more.

          This package works with TeX engines that directly support OpenType features, such as XeTeX and LuaTeX, 
          as well as traditional engines such as TeX and pdfTeX.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/oldstandard/doc/oldstandard.pdf}

\section[\texttt{olsak-misc} -- Collection of plain TeX macros written by Petr Olšák]{\texttt{olsak-misc} -- Collection of plain TeX macros written by Petr Olšák}\label{pkg:olsak-misc}
\index{Package!olsak-misc}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/olsak-misc}
\item[name] \texttt{olsak-misc}
\item[caption] Collection of plain TeX macros written by Petr Olšák
\item[author] Olšák, Petr
\index{Author!Olšák, Petr}
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[version] Aug. 2022
\item[description] (no language specified) This is a collection of various single-file plain TeX macros written by Petr Olšák.

          The documentation is included in each file separately.

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{booklet.tex} : re-orders PDF pages and collects them for booklet printing
          \item  \texttt{cnv.tex} : conversion of texts
          \item  \texttt{cnv-pu.tex} : example of usage of cnv.tex --- pdf outlines in Unicode
          \item  \texttt{cnv-word.tex} : example of usage of cnv.tex --- word to word conversion
          \item  \texttt{eparam.tex} : Full expansion during parameter scanning
          \item  \texttt{fun-coffee.tex} : generates splotches in the document
          \item  \texttt{openclose.tex} : repairs balanced text between {\textbackslash}Open ...{\textbackslash}Close pair
          \item  \texttt{qrcode.tex} : QR code generated at TeX level
          \item  \texttt{scanbase.tex} : parser of text-style mysql outputs
          \item  \texttt{scancsv.tex} : parser of CSV format
          \item  \texttt{seplist.tex} : macros with alternative separators of a parameter

          \begin{itemize}
          \item a plain letter layout

          customers: documents are submitted digitally, and the service handles printing, enveloping, franking, 
          and postal delivery.

          with this LaTeX class.
