\index{Package!rvwrite}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/rvwrite}
\item[name] \texttt{rvwrite}
\item[caption] Increase the number of available output streams in LaTeX
\item[author] Radhakrishnan, C. V.
\index{Author!Radhakrishnan, C. V.}
\item[copyright] C. V. Radhakrishnan (2010)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The package addresses, for LaTeX documents, the severe limitation on the number of output streams that 
          TeX provides.

          The package uses a single TeX output stream, and writes ''marked-up'' output to this stream. The user 
          may then post-process the marked-up output file, using LaTeX, and the document’s output appears as separate 
          files, according to the calls made to the package.

          The output to be post-processed uses macros from the widely-available  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/protex}{ProTeX} package.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/rvwrite/rvwrite-doc.pdf}

\section[\texttt{sam2p} -- Convert bitmap formats to compact PS/PDF]{\texttt{sam2p} -- Convert bitmap formats to compact PS/PDF}\label{pkg:sam2p}
\index{Package!sam2p}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/sam2p}
\item[name] \texttt{sam2p}
\item[caption] Convert bitmap formats to compact PS/PDF
\item[author] Szabó, Péter
\index{Author!Szabó, Péter}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 0.49.4
\item[description] (no language specified) Sam2p is a UNIX command line utility written in ANSI C++ that converts many raster (bitmap) image formats 
          into Adobe PostScript or PDF files and several other formats. The images are not vectorized. sam2p gives 
          full control to the user to specify standards-compliance, compression, and bit depths. In some cases 
          sam2p can compress an image 100 times smaller than the PostScript output of many other common image converters. 
          Sam2p provides ZIP, RLE and LZW (de)compression filters even on output destined for PostScript Level 
          1 devices.

          The author provides a script bundle,  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/a2ping}{a2ping} , that 
          uses sam2p as part of a generic format conversion mechanism.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/sam2p/README}

\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/sam2p}

          friends with pdfLaTeX.

          pdfLaTeX.

\item[name] \texttt{savesym}
\item[caption] Redefine symbols where names conflict
\item[author] Göbel, Jürgen
\index{Author!Göbel, Jürgen}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.2 (2013-09-02)
\item[last changes] 2013-09-02
\item[year] 2013
\index{Year!2013}
\item[description] (no language specified) There are a number of symbols (e.g.,  \texttt{{\textbackslash}Square} ) that are defined 
          by several packages. In order to typeset all the variants in a document, we have to give the glyph a 
          unique name. To do that, we define \texttt{{\textbackslash}savesymbol{\textbraceleft}XXX{\textbraceright}} , 
          which renames a symbol from \texttt{{\textbackslash}XXX} to \texttt{{\textbackslash}origXXX} , 
          and \texttt{{\textbackslash}restoresymbols{\textbraceleft}yyy{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}XXX{\textbraceright}} , 
          which renames \texttt{{\textbackslash}origXXX} back to \texttt{{\textbackslash}XXX} and 
          defines a new command, \texttt{{\textbackslash}yyyXXX} , which corresponds to the most 
          recently loaded version of \texttt{{\textbackslash}XXX} .

\item[last changes] 2016-04-14
\item[year] 2016
\index{Year!2016}
\item[description] (no language specified) The goal of the savetrees package is to pack as much text as possible onto each page of a LaTeX document. 
          Admittedly, this makes the document far less attractive. Nevertheless, savetrees is a simple way to save 
          paper when printing draft copies of a document. It can also be useful when trying to meet a tight page-length 
          requirement for a conference or journal submission.

          Most of the package options cover specific modifications to typesetting rules, but there are also options 
          \texttt{subtle} , \texttt{moderate} and \texttt{extreme} options 
          for the ''broad brush'' approach.

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) \texttt{{\textbackslash}scalefont{\textbraceleft}2{\textbraceright}} selects 
          the current font in twice the current size. \texttt{{\textbackslash}scalefont{\textbraceleft}.75{\textbraceright}} reduces 
          the current font size by three quarters.

          Note that the effectiveness of such operations depends on the LaTeX font selection for that font; it 
          will typically work well for ordinary Type 1 fonts, but Metafont fonts are usually set up to work only 
          at a discrete set of sizes.

          The package is distributed as part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/carlisle}{carlisle} bundle.

\section[\texttt{sciposter} -- Make posters of ISO A3 size and larger]{\texttt{sciposter} -- Make posters of ISO A3 size and larger}\label{pkg:sciposter}
\index{Package!sciposter}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/sciposter}
\item[name] \texttt{sciposter}
\item[caption] Make posters of ISO A3 size and larger
\item[author] Wilkinson, Michael
\index{Author!Wilkinson, Michael}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.18
\item[description] (no language specified) This collection of files contains LaTeX packages for posters of ISO A3 size and larger (ISO A0 is the 
          default size). American paper sizes and custom paper are supported. In particular, sciposter.cls defines 
          a document class which allows cutting and pasting most of an article to a poster without any editing 
          (save reducing the size) — see the manual.

          Sciposter does work for LaTeX, not just pdfLaTeX. However, xdvi produces strange results, though a recent 
          version of dvips does create good ps-files from the dvi files.

          Also note that logos must either be put in the current working directory or in the directories of your 
          LaTeX distribution. For some reason graphicspath settings are ignored.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sciposter/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package manual}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sciposter/scipostermanual.pdf}

\section[\texttt{scrambledenvs} -- Create and print scrambled environments]{\texttt{scrambledenvs} -- Create and print scrambled environments}\label{pkg:scrambledenvs}
\index{Package!scrambledenvs}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/scrambledenvs}
\item[name] \texttt{scrambledenvs}
\item[caption] Create and print scrambled environments
\item[author] Chen, Dennis
\index{Author!Chen, Dennis}
\item[copyright] Dennis Chen (2021)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.1.0 (2021-09-26)
\item[last changes] 2021-09-26
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package allows you to create and print scrambled environments for purposes such as randomized hint 
          environments. You can mark a location with a series of hints, and then print the hints at the end in 
          a pseudo-random order.

          The general structure follows: there is an outer environment which creates the label, an inner environment 
          that creates the references, and a print command that prints out all of the hints.

          This generalizes beyond hints; one can create scrambled solutions as well, etc.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/scrambledenvs/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/scrambledenvs/scrambledenvs.pdf}

          other classes and packages.

\item[version] 3.42 (2024-09-04)
\item[last changes] 2024-09-04
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) Up to version 3.41, the scrhack package was part of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script}{KOMA-Script} . 
          It was originally intended to improve the compatibility of third-party packages with KOMA-Script. However, 
          most of the so-called hacks also added additional functionality to the corresponding third-party package. 
          On the other hand, it was sometimes urgent to react to a change in such a third-party package, which 
          was difficult to do from within a large collection like KOMA-Script. Therefore, the scrhack part of KOMA-Script 
          was split into several independent packages. And the scrhack spin-off was made to emulate the former 
          KOMA-Script package of the same name.

\section[\texttt{sdaps} -- LaTeX support files for SDAPS]{\texttt{sdaps} -- LaTeX support files for SDAPS}\label{pkg:sdaps}
\index{Package!sdaps}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/sdaps}
\item[name] \texttt{sdaps}
\item[caption] LaTeX support files for SDAPS
\item[author] Berg, Benjamin
\index{Author!Berg, Benjamin}
\item[copyright] Benjamin Berg (2019-2021)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.9.10
\item[description] (no language specified) This bundle contains LaTeX classes and packages to create machine readable questionnaires. Metadata is 
          generated for the whole document and it is possible to process created forms fully automatically using 
          the SDAPS main program.

          Features include:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item PDF Form generation
          \item Advanced array like layouting 
          \begin{itemize}
          \item Can flow over multiple pages and repeats the header automatically
          \item Optional document wide alignment of array environments
          \item Has complex layout features like rotating the headers to safe space
          \item Ability to exchange rows and columns on the fly
          \end{itemize}

          \item Different question types: 
          \begin{itemize}
          \item Freeform text
          \item Single/multiple choice questions
          \item Range questions
          \end{itemize}

          \item Layouting questions in rows or columns
          \item Possibility to pre-fill questionnaires from LaTeX
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sdaps/sdaps.html}

          and provides several additions and customizations to these classes. While the class provides some basic 
          settings, mostly regrading the type area, fonts, and the title page, it still provides large degrees 
          of freedom to its users. However, the package’s documentation also provides recommendations regarding 
          several aspects, for example, recommending \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} for 
          bibliographies.

\item[description] (no language specified) Defines a command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}outputonly} , whose argument is a list of

\section[\texttt{selnolig} -- Selectively disable typographic ligatures]{\texttt{selnolig} -- Selectively disable typographic ligatures}\label{pkg:selnolig}
\index{Package!selnolig}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/selnolig}
\item[name] \texttt{selnolig}
\item[caption] Selectively disable typographic ligatures
\item[author] Loretan, Mico
\index{Author!Loretan, Mico}
\item[copyright] Mico Loretan (2013-2015)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.302 (2015-10-26)
\item[last changes] 2015-10-26
\item[year] 2015
\index{Year!2015}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package suppresses typographic ligatures selectively, i.e., based on predefined search patterns. 
          The search patterns focus on ligatures deemed inappropriate because they span morpheme boundaries. For 
          example, the word  \texttt{shelfful} , which is mentioned in the TeXbook as a word for which 
          the \texttt{ff} ligature might be inappropriate, is automatically typeset as \texttt{shelf{\textbackslash}/ful} rather 
          than as \texttt{shel{\textbraceleft}ff{\textbraceright}ul} .

          For English and German language documents, the package provides extensive rules for the selective suppression 
          of so-called ''common'' ligatures. These comprise the  \texttt{ff} , \texttt{fi} , \texttt{fl} , \texttt{ffi} , 
          and \texttt{ffl} ligatures as well as the \texttt{ft} and \texttt{fft} ligatures. 
          Other f-ligatures, such as \texttt{fb} , \texttt{fh} , \texttt{fj} and \texttt{fk} , 
          are suppressed globally, while exceptions are made for names and words of non-English/German origin, 
          such as \texttt{Kafka} and \texttt{fjord} .

          For English language documents, the package further provides ligature suppression macros for a number 
          of so-called ''discretionary'' or ''rare'' ligatures such as  \texttt{ct} , \texttt{st} , 
          and \texttt{sp} .

          The package requires use of a recent LuaLaTeX format (for example those from TeX Live 2012 or 2013, or 
          MiKTeX 2.9).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/selnolig/selnolig.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./4614671846-selnolig.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/selnolig/README}
\item[contact] \textit{repository}: \url{https://github.com/micoloretan/selnolig}
\index{Contact!repository}

\section[\texttt{semantex} -- Semantic, keyval-based mathematics]{\texttt{semantex} -- Semantic, keyval-based mathematics}\label{pkg:semantex}
\index{Package!semantex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/semantex}
\item[name] \texttt{SemanTeX}
\item[caption] Semantic, keyval-based mathematics
\item[author] Ørsted, Sebastian
\index{Author!Ørsted, Sebastian}

\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}

\item[version] 0.525 (2023-01-23)
\item[last changes] 2023-01-23
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) The SemanTeX package for LaTeX delivers a more semantic, systematized way of writing mathematics, compared 
          to the classical math syntax in LaTeX. The system uses keyval syntax, and the user can define their own 
          keys and customize the system down to the last detail. At the same time, care has been taken to make 
          the syntax as simple, natural, practical, and lightweight as possible.

          Furthermore, the package has a companion package, called stripsemantex, which allows you to completely 
          strip your documents of SemanTeX markup to prepare them e.g. for publication.

          The package is still in beta, but is considered feature-complete and more or less stable, so using it 
          at this point should be safe. Still, suggestions, ideas, and bug reports are more than welcome!

\section[\texttt{semantic-markup} -- Meaningful semantic markup in the spirit of the Text Encodin\ldots]{\texttt{semantic-markup} -- Meaningful semantic markup in the spirit of the Text Encoding Initiative}\label{pkg:semantic-markup}
\index{Package!semantic-markup}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/semantic-markup}
\item[name] \texttt{semantic-markup}
\item[caption] Meaningful semantic markup in the spirit of the Text Encoding Initiative
\item[author] Cashner, Andrew A.
\index{Author!Cashner, Andrew A.}
\item[copyright] Andrew A. Cashner (2020)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version]  (2020-01-29)
\item[last changes] 2020-01-29
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides simple commands to allow authors (especially scholars in the humanities) to write 
          with a focus on content rather than presentation. The commands are inspired by the XML elements of the 
          \href{http://www.tei-c.org}{Text Encoding Initiative} . Commands like \texttt{{\textbackslash}term} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}foreign} are 
          aliases for \texttt{{\textbackslash}emph} . \texttt{{\textbackslash}quoted} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}soCalled} are 
          aliases for quoting commands. These commands could be easily redefined for different formats.

          The package also provides a footnote environment so that long footnotes can be more cleanly separated 
          from the main text.

          Because the author is a music scholar, the package also includes some macros for musical symbols and 
          other basic notations for musical analysis.

\item[version] 0.45 (2020-10-03)
\item[last changes] 2020-10-03
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package is a small LaTeX package that adds a collection of simple macros for parentheses and bullets. 
          It exists for one purpose only: To be loaded by documents which were originally typeset using the package 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/semantex}{SemanTeX} , but which have been stripped of SemanTeX 
          markup using the package \texttt{stripsemantex} which is part of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/semantex}{SemanTeX} . 
          Therefore, unless your document is one of those, simply \textbf{don't use this package} .

          And even if your document is one of those, there is a good chance you will not have to load it after 
          all. In most cases, you will be able to replace the macros it provides by macros from other packages.

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.1
\item[description] (no language specified) When one needs to type long sequences of letters (such as in base-sequences in genes) or of numbers (such 
          as calculations of transcendental numbers), there's no obvious break points to be found. The package 
          provides a command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}seqsplit} , which makes its argument splittable 
          anywhere, and then leaves the TeX paragraph-maker to do the splitting.

          While the package may obviously be used to typeset DNA sequences, the user may consider the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dnaseq}{dnaseq} as 
          a rather more powerful alternative.

\item[author] Osborne, Martin J.
\index{Author!Osborne, Martin J.}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 2.15
\item[description] (no language specified) Formats strategic games. For a 2x2 game, for example, the input:\\
          \begin{verbatim}
\begin{game}{2}{2}
&$L$ &$M$\\
$T$ &$2,2$ &$2,0$\\
$B$ &$3,0$ &$0,9$
\end{game}
          \end{verbatim}
produces output with (a) boxes around the payoffs, (b) payoff columns of equal width, and (c) payoffs vertically centered within the boxes.

          Note that the game environment will not work in the argument of another command.

\index{Author!Hefferon, Jim}

\item[description] (no language specified) Extends the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}newtheorem} command. If you say \texttt{{\textbackslash}newshadetheorem{\textbraceleft}theorem{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}Theorem{\textbraceright}} in 
          the preamble then your regular \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}theorem{\textbraceright} 
          .. {\textbackslash}end{\textbraceleft}theorem{\textbraceright}} will produce a 
          theorem statement in a shaded box. It supports all the options of \texttt{{\textbackslash}newtheorem} , 
          including forms \texttt{{\textbackslash}newshadetheorem{\textbraceleft}..{\textbraceright}[..]{\textbraceleft}..{\textbraceright}} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}newshadetheorem{\textbraceleft}..{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}..{\textbraceright}[..]} .

          Environments declared using the package require their body to remain on one page; the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mdframed}{mdframed} package 
          can frame and shade theorems, and \emph{its} environments break at the end of a page; users 
          are generally recommended, therefore, to use \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mdframed}{mdframed} .

          In the same spirit, the author told us in January 2020: ''These materials are obsolete. There are a number 
          of more recent, more powerful packages that have capabilities that greatly extend the simple ones here. 
          A new project should use one of those. These files only continue to be available to help people who are 
          working with an old project.''

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[name] \texttt{shapepar}
\item[caption] A macro to typeset paragraphs in specific shapes
\item[author] Arseneau, Donald
\index{Author!Arseneau, Donald}

\item[license] other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
\index{License!other-free}
\index{License!Free license not otherwise listed}
\item[version] 2.2
\item[description] (no language specified) {\textbackslash}shapepar is a macro to typeset paragraphs in a specific shape. The size is adjusted 
          automatically so that the entire shape is filled with text. There may not be displayed maths or ‘ \texttt{{\textbackslash}vadjust} ’ 
          material (no \texttt{{\textbackslash}vspace} ) in the argument of \texttt{{\textbackslash}shapepar} . 
          The macros work for both LaTeX and plain TeX. For LaTeX, specify \texttt{{\textbackslash}usepackage{\textbraceleft}shapepar{\textbraceright}} ; 
          for Plain, \texttt{{\textbackslash}input shapepar.sty} .

          \texttt{{\textbackslash}shapepar} works in terms of user-defined shapes, though the 
          package does provide some predefined shapes: so you can form any paragraph into the form of a heart by 
          putting \texttt{{\textbackslash}heartpar{\textbraceleft}sometext...{\textbraceright}} inside 
          your document. The tedium of creating these polygon definitions may be alleviated by using the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/shapepatch}{shapepatch} extension 
          to \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/transfig}{transfig} which will convert xfig output to \texttt{{\textbackslash}shapepar} polygon 
          form.

\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) ShapePatch is a patch against  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/transfig}{Transfig} , which 
          adds the capability to export \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xfig}{XFig} figures to shape 
          definitions for \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/shapepar}{shapepar} . Shapepar itself will 
          form a paragraph into a specified shape, and the size of the shape is automatically adjusted so that 
          the given paragraph completely fills the shape. ShapePatch effort: one simply draws the required shape 
          with XFig and then convert it to a shape definition for shapepar, either by calling fig2dev manually 
          or by choosing ''Export/Shape'' in XFig (if you install the additional XFig patch).

\section[\texttt{shipunov} -- A collection of LaTeX packages and classes]{\texttt{shipunov} -- A collection of LaTeX packages and classes}\label{pkg:shipunov}
\index{Package!shipunov}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/shipunov}
\item[name] \texttt{shipunov}
\item[caption] A collection of LaTeX packages and classes
\item[author] Shipunov, Alexey
\index{Author!Shipunov, Alexey}
\item[copyright] Alexey Shipunov (2010-2019)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The bundle collects packages and classes, along with one bibliography style and examples and scripts 
          for converting TeX files. Many of the files in the collection are designed to support field biologists 
          and/or Russian writers, while others have wider application.

          The collection includes:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item add2 – Save trees. Quick way to fit as many as possible into one page.  Good for handouts.
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/altverse}{altverse} – Typesetting verses. Straightforward typesetting, using the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xtab}{xtab} package to aid layout.
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/autolist}{autolist} – More lists. A means to define various sorts of list.
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biokey}{biokey} – Flexible identification key tables in LaTeX. The package provides straightforward macros to typeset sets of biological identification keys. Layout is flexible, and the macros will be useful in other disciplines.
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biolist}{biolist} – List observed species. Pretty formatting of species lists of flora and fauna.
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/boldline}{boldline} – Heavier lines in tables. The package provides commands replacing \texttt{{\textbackslash}hline} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}cline} , as well as a table preamble element that generates heavy lines.
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cassette-shipunov}{cassete} (with one ‘t’) – Print labels for audio cassettes.  This is a LaTeX2e class file (the only other cassette package on CTAN is \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cassette}{cassette} (with two ‘t’), written for Plain TeX).
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/classif2}{classif2} – Biological classification tables. The package defines an environment classif that simplifies the process of typesetting classification tables.
          \item dline – Double line on the left of text.
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/drcaps}{drcaps} – Simple dropped capitals. The package offers simple macros for dropped capitals, in a couple of forms.
          \item etiketka – Class for typesetting business-card-sized information (including business cards).
          \item flower – Typesetting lists of flower formulas.
          \item isyntax – Interactively check LaTeX file syntax.
          \item numerus – Spell numbers in Russian words.
          \item punct – Within italicized text, punctuation is still straight, this is typographically more aesthetic.
          \item qqru – Universal quotation marks, for Russian and English. It is able also to convert uniform typewriter ''quotes'' into left or right typographic quotes.
          \item rusnat – Bibliography style file, now deprecated.
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/sltables}{sltables} – Simplified tables for LaTeX. These macros develop the concepts of the stables, which are designed to offer table macros whose use is ''as simple as one might hope''. Some would claim that LaTeX’s built-in table specifications are as simple as one might hope, but this package offers many short-cuts and optimization of the mechanisms of tables.
          \item starfn – Stars as footnote marks.
          \item textfrac – Simple slanted fractions.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (English) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/shipunov/doc/README}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/shipunov}

\item[description] (no language specified) This script permits centralization of the many program calls necessary to completely compile a LaTeX 
          document. In particular, the multiple calls of the LaTeX command necessary in order to create a table 
          of contents, a bibliography or an index are carried out automatically. Are also managed the calls of 
          the programs BibTeX and makeindex as well as the vizualisation of the resulting file (in DVI, PostScript 
          or PDF format) by calling an external program. It is possible to stress characters in documents wich 
          use the {\textbackslash}input and {\textbackslash}include commands to make references to 
          some external files, and that in a transparent way by compiling only the main source file. Available 
          in English and French languages.

\section[\texttt{shobhika} -- An OpenType Devanāgarī font designed for scholars]{\texttt{shobhika} -- An OpenType Devanāgarī font designed for scholars}\label{pkg:shobhika}
\index{Package!shobhika}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/shobhika}
\item[name] \texttt{shobhika}
\item[caption] An OpenType Devanāgarī font designed for scholars
\item[author] Kolachana, Aditya
\index{Author!Kolachana, Aditya}
\item[license] ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
\index{License!ofl}
\index{License!The SIL Open Font License}
\item[version] 1.05
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a free, open source, Unicode compliant, OpenType font with support for Devanāgarī, 
          Latin, and Cyrillic scripts. It is available in two weights—regular and bold. The font is designed with 
          over 1600 Devanāgarī glyphs, including support for over 1100 conjunct consonants, as well as vedic accents.

          The Latin component of the font not only supports a wide range of characters required for Roman transliteration 
          of Sanskrit, but also provides a subset of regularly used mathematical symbols for scholars working with 
          scientific and technical documents.

          The project has been launched under the auspices of the Science and Heritage Initiative (SandHI) at  \href{http://www.iitb.ac.in}{IIT 
          Bombay} , and builds upon the following two fonts for its Devanāgarī and Latin components respectively: 
          (i) \href{https://github.com/RajyaMarathiVikasSanstha/Yashomudra}{Yashomudra} by \href{https://rmvs.marathi.gov.in/}{Rājya 
          Marāṭhī Vikās Saṃsthā} , and (ii) \href{https://fonts.google.com/specimen/PT+Serif}{PT 
          Serif} by \href{http://www.paratype.com}{ParaType} . We would like to thank both 
          these organisations for releasing their fonts under the SIL Open Font Licence, which has enabled us to 
          create Shobhika.

          the text \texttt{|stuff|} has the same effect as \texttt{{\textbackslash}verb|stuff|} .

\section[\texttt{sidenotesplus} -- Place referenced notes, alerts, figures and tables into the \ldots]{\texttt{sidenotesplus} -- Place referenced notes, alerts, figures and tables into the document margin}\label{pkg:sidenotesplus}
\index{Package!sidenotesplus}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/sidenotesplus}
\item[name] \texttt{sidenotesplus}
\item[caption] Place referenced notes, alerts, figures and tables into the document margin
\item[author] Vrba, Anton
\index{Author!Vrba, Anton}
\item[copyright] Anton Vrba (2022-2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.05 (2025-02-18)
\item[last changes] 2025-02-18
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) Sidenotesplus is a comprehensive package for placing labeled or referenced notes, temporary alerts, bibliography 
          references, figures and tables into the margin. Marginals can be either floated or at fixed positions 
          relative to the text. Twoside symmetry is preserved. For BibLaTeX users, macros for side references are 
          provided.

          Three margin styles are provided. Two-page symmetric layouts either as (i) Ragged outer with note reverences 
          in the margin separator or (ii) justified with last line ragged outer. And (iii) a classic look, justified 
          with last line ragged right and note reference to the left of the note, but two-page symmetry is lost.

          The command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}sidenote} mimics the \texttt{{\textbackslash}footnote} command 
          and provides labelled (numbers, alphabetic, roman) references. However, un-numbered and custom symbols 
          can also be specified.

          Temporary sidealerts are rendered only if the package option  \texttt{alerton} is specified. 
          Alerts are useful as to do reminders during document development.

          Furthermore, captions for figures and tables can also be placed into margin. Also, full width environments 
          for figures, tables and text are provided. The text environment can be partially widened, suitable if 
          that extra space for an equation is required.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sidenotesplus/README.txt}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sidenotesplus/sidenotesplus.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./8083497875-sidenotesplus.pdf|
\item[contact] \textit{repository}: \url{https://github.com/anton-vrba/sidenotesplus}
\index{Contact!repository}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sidenotesplus}

\section[\texttt{simplebnf} -- A simple package to format Backus-Naur form (BNF)]{\texttt{simplebnf} -- A simple package to format Backus-Naur form (BNF)}\label{pkg:simplebnf}
\index{Package!simplebnf}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/simplebnf}
\item[name] \texttt{simplebnf}
\item[caption] A simple package to format Backus-Naur form (BNF)
\item[author] Lee, Jay
\index{Author!Lee, Jay}
\item[copyright] Jay Lee (2019-2023)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version] 1.0.0 (2023-11-25)
\item[last changes] 2023-11-25
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a simple way for typesetting grammars in Backus-Naur form (BNF). The included  \texttt{bnf} environment 
          parses BNF expressions (possibly annotated), so users can write readable BNF expressions in their documents. 
          It features a flexible configuration system, allowing for the customization of the domain-specific language 
          (DSL) used in typesetting the grammar. Additionally, the package comes with sensible defaults.

          The package requires  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse}{xparse} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/mathtools}{mathtools} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tabularray}{tabularray.} .

\item[description] (no language specified) This is a LaTeX macro package for generating simple node-based flow graphs or diagrams built upon the 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} package. The package provides two basic commands, 
          one to generate a node and one to create links between nodes. The positioning of the nodes is not handled 
          by the package itself but is preferably done in a tabular environment.

          In total, four simple node types are defined, loosely based on the nomenclature and color patterns of 
          the popular Java script  \href{https://getbootstrap.com/}{Bootstrap} .

\section[\texttt{simpler-wick} -- Simpler Wick contractions]{\texttt{simpler-wick} -- Simpler Wick contractions}\label{pkg:simpler-wick}
\index{Package!simpler-wick}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/simpler-wick}
\item[name] \texttt{simpler-wick}
\item[caption] Simpler Wick contractions
\item[author] Ellis, Joshua
\index{Author!Ellis, Joshua}
\item[copyright] Joshua Ellis (2014-2015)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.0.0 (2015-12-11)
\item[last changes] 2015-12-11
\item[year] 2015
\index{Year!2015}
\item[description] (no language specified) In every quantum field theory course, there will be a chapter about Wick’s theorem and how it can be 
          used to convert a very large product of many creation and annihilation operators into something more 
          tractable and normal ordered.

          The contractions are denoted with a square bracket over the operators which are being contracted, which 
          used to be rather annoying to typeset in LaTeX as the only other package available was  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/simplewick}{simplewick} , 
          which is rather unwieldy.

          This package provides a simpler syntax for Wick contractions.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/simpler-wick/simpler-wick.pdf}

\section[\texttt{simplesystemtex} -- An automated file {\&} block management system for large-scale \ldots]{\texttt{simplesystemtex} -- An automated file {\&} block management system for large-scale LaTeX}\label{pkg:simplesystemtex}
\index{Package!simplesystemtex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/simplesystemtex}
\item[name] \texttt{SimpleSystemTeX}
\item[caption] An automated file {\&} block management system for large-scale LaTeX
\item[author] Zhou, KeXin
\index{Author!Zhou, KeXin}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0.0 (2026-03-24)
\item[last changes] 2026-03-24
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This LaTeX3 package has been specifically designed for large-scale, integrated typesetting tasks such 
          as books, theses, or extensive lecture notes.

          The core design philosophy of this package is to maximize the separation of content and structure. It 
          provides an automated file and block management system that frees content creators from constantly managing 
          global document structure and stylistic details.

          Key features include:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Automated subfile management: Section files are automatically added to the TOC upon import.
          \item A flexible Block System for theorems, definitions, and proofs.
          \item Dynamic cross-referencing that generates and manages anchors automatically.
          \item Automated generation of block indexes (e.g., List of Theorems).
          \item Highly customizable styling via dynamic display arguments and conditional statements.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/simplesystemtex/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/simplesystemtex/simplesystemtex.doc.pdf}
\item[contact] \textit{bugs}: \url{https://github.com/JokerXin2025/SimpleSystemTeX/issues}
\index{Contact!bugs}

\section[\texttt{siunitx} -- A comprehensive (SI) units package]{\texttt{siunitx} -- A comprehensive (SI) units package}\label{pkg:siunitx}
\index{Package!siunitx}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/siunitx}
\item[name] \texttt{siunitx}
\item[caption] A comprehensive (SI) units package
\item[author] Wright, Joseph
\index{Author!Wright, Joseph}
\item[copyright] Joseph Wright (2008-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 3.5.4 (2026-04-15)
\item[last changes] 2026-04-15
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) Physical quantities have both numbers and units, and each physical quantity should be expressed as the 
          product of a number and a unit. Typesetting physical quantities requires care to ensure that the combined 
          mathematical meaning of the number-unit combination is clear. In particular, the SI units system lays 
          down a consistent set of units with rules on how these are to be used.

          However, different countries and publishers have differing conventions on the exact appearance of numbers 
          (and units). The  \texttt{siunitx} package provides a set of tools for authors to typeset 
          quantities in a consistent way. The package has an extended set of configuration options which make it 
          possible to follow varying typographic conventions with the same input syntax. The package includes automated 
          processing of numbers and units, and the ability to control tabular alignment of numbers.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{User manual}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/siunitx/siunitx.pdf}

\section[\texttt{skak} -- Fonts and macros for typesetting chess games]{\texttt{skak} -- Fonts and macros for typesetting chess games}\label{pkg:skak}
\index{Package!skak}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/skak}
\item[name] \texttt{skak}
\item[caption] Fonts and macros for typesetting chess games
\item[author] Hoffmann, Torben
\index{Author!Hoffmann, Torben}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.5.3
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides macros and fonts in Metafont format which can be used to typeset chess games using 
          PGN, and to show diagrams of the current board in a document. The package builds on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/chess}{work 
          by Piet Tutelaers} — the main novelty is the use of PGN for input instead of the more cumbersome 
          coordinate notation ( \texttt{g1f3} becomes the more readable \texttt{Nf3} in 
          PGN).

          An Adobe Type 1 implementation of skak's fonts is available as package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/skaknew}{skaknew} ; 
          an alternative chess notational scheme is available in package \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/texmate}{texmate} , 
          and a general mechanism for selecting chess fonts is provided in \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/chessfss}{chessfss} .

\section[\texttt{skb} -- Tools for a repository of long-living documents]{\texttt{skb} -- Tools for a repository of long-living documents}\label{pkg:skb}
\index{Package!skb}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/skb}
\item[name] \texttt{skb}
\item[caption] Tools for a repository of long-living documents
\item[author] van der Meer, Sven
\index{Author!van der Meer, Sven}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.52
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides macros that help to build a document repository for long living documents. It focuses 
          on structure and re-use of text, code, figures etc. The basic concept is first to separate structure 
          from content (i.e., text about a topic from the structure it is presented by) and then separating the 
          content from the actual published document, thus enabling easy re-use of text blocks in different publications 
          (i.e., text about a protocol in a short article about this protocol as well as in a book about many protocols); 
          all without constantly copying or changing text.

          As a side effect, using the document classes provided, it hides a lot of LaTeX from someone who just 
          wants to write articles and books.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/skb/README}

\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 0.2
\item[description] (no language specified) Sketch is a small, simple system for producing line drawings of two- or three-dimensional objects and 
          scenes. It began as a way to make illustrations for a textbook after we could find no suitable tool for 
          this purpose. Existing scene processors emphasized GUIs and/or photo-realism, neither of which was useful 
          to us. We wanted to produce finely wrought, mathematically-based illustrations with no extraneous detail.

          The input language is reminiscent of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base}{PSTricks} , 
          so will be easy for current PSTricks users to learn; output is for use either by \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base}{pstricks} itself, 
          or by \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{pgf} .

\item[description] (no language specified) This package attempts to make it easy for even a LaTeX novice to prepare proficiency tests, especially 
          in combination with the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/exam}{exam} document class. Thus, 
          almost all command names are very similar.

          After defining skills in the preamble or in an external file, they are declared using labels, and can 
          optionally be set as global skills. A skills table is generated to summarize the evaluated competencies 
          and to allow for writing down the resulting proficiency level.

          A user’s guide attempts to explain all of the possibilities in a readable way, with many examples.

\section[\texttt{smartref} -- Extend LaTeX's {\textbackslash}ref capability]{\texttt{smartref} -- Extend LaTeX's {\textbackslash}ref capability}\label{pkg:smartref}
\index{Package!smartref}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/smartref}
\item[name] \texttt{smartref}
\item[caption] Extend LaTeX's {\textbackslash}ref capability
\item[author] Bilotta, Giuseppe
\index{Author!Bilotta, Giuseppe}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.9
\item[description] (no language specified) The package extends the LaTeX labelling system: whenever a label is set, the values of counters (selected 
          by the user) are recorded, along with the label. The value of these counters can be recalled with a command 
          similar to  \texttt{{\textbackslash}pageref} .

          The package also adds commands  \texttt{{\textbackslash}s[name]ref} (for each counter \texttt{[name]} that 
          the user has selected); these commands display something only if the value of the \texttt{[name]} counter 
          is changed from when the label was set. Many commands are provided to serve as a macro programming environment 
          for using the extended labels.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme and command details}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/smartref/README}

\section[\texttt{snapshot} -- List the external dependencies of a LaTeX document]{\texttt{snapshot} -- List the external dependencies of a LaTeX document}\label{pkg:snapshot}
\index{Package!snapshot}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/snapshot}
\item[name] \texttt{snapshot}
\item[caption] List the external dependencies of a LaTeX document
\item[author] Downes, Michael J.
\index{Author!Downes, Michael J.}
\item[author] The American Mathematical Society
\index{Author!The American Mathematical Society}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 2.14
\item[description] (no language specified) The snapshot package helps the owner of a LaTeX document obtain a list of the external dependencies of 
          the document, in a form that can be embedded at the top of the document. It provides a snapshot of the 
          current processing context of the document, insofar as it can be determined from inside LaTeX. If a document 
          contains such a dependency list, then it becomes possible to arrange that the document be processed always 
          with the same versions of everything, in order to ensure the same output. This could be useful for someone 
          wanting to keep a LaTeX document on hand and consistently reproduce an identical DVI file from it, on 
          the fly; or for someone wanting to shield a document during the final stages of its production cycle 
          from unexpected side effects of routine upgrades to the TeX system.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/snapshot/snapshot.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5627982424-snapshot.pdf|

\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/snapshot}

\index{Alias!softmaker-freefont (for softmakerfreefont)}
\item[name] \texttt{softmakerfreefont}
\item[caption] Support files for SoftMaker free fonts
\item[author] Kleber, Josef

\item[copyright] Josef Kleber (2010)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) In June 2009  \href{http://www.freefont.de}{SoftMaker} offered a handwriting font for 
          free download: The Softmaker Stone Handwriting. As handwriting fonts are a quite limited resource in 
          the LaTeX world, the author decided to create support files for the font. Since then, the author has 
          added support files for the fonts Alte Schwabacher, Artistic (regular), Baskerville-Nova (regular + bold 
          + italic + bold italic), Bonita (regular), Broadway (regular + engraved), Canossa (regular + bold + light), 
          Congress (regular + bold + italic), Delano-Caps, Digital (regular + bold + italic + bold italic), EgyptienneStd 
          (light + bold + light italic + bold italic), Flagstaff (regular), Grenoble(regular + bold + italic + 
          bold italic), Helium (regular + bold), Heliumtwo (regular + bold + shadow), Henderson (regular), Iceberg 
          (regular + bold), Inverserif (regular), Jugendstil (regular), Marseille (regular + bold + italic + bold 
          italic), Moab (regular), Nevada (regular + bold), Newcastle (regular + demibold + bold), Old Blackletter, 
          Quadrat (regular + bold + italic + bold italic), Stone Handwriting, Sunset (regular + bold), Tampa (regular), 
          VAGRounded (regular), Velo (regular), Veracruz (regular + bold + italic + bold italic).

          This is the base package for all other softmakerfreefont packages, namely:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/softmaker-alteschwabacher}{Alte Schwabacher}

          input file: ''words and chords'' books for the musicians to play from, ''words only'' songbooks for the 
          congregation to sing from, and overhead transparency masters for congregational use. The package will

          \begin{itemize}
          \item a very easy chord-entry syntax;
          \item multiple modes (words-only; words+chords; slides; handouts);
          \item measure bars;
          \item guitar tablatures;
          \item automatic transposition;
          \item scripture quotations;

\index{Year!2009}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex}{LaTeX} system is provided as a large number of 
          separate modules. The interested user may process each module separately, to produce formatted documentation. 
          Formatted documentation of the entire system, however, is a more substantial undertaking; \texttt{source2e.tex} provides 
          what the user needs to produce a complete listing of the LaTeX kernel. It not only includes the relevant 
          modules in the ‘correct’ order, but it also guides the user through the rather complex compilation process 
          (by writing messages to the terminal and log).

          The document also includes a command index.

          A formatted copy of source2e is provided in the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tds}{latex-tds} bundle; 
          the file itself is part of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-base}{LaTeX base} distribution.

\section[\texttt{spalign} -- Typeset matrices and arrays with spaces and semicolons as de\ldots]{\texttt{spalign} -- Typeset matrices and arrays with spaces and semicolons as delimiters}\label{pkg:spalign}
\index{Package!spalign}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/spalign}
\item[name] \texttt{spalign}
\item[caption] Typeset matrices and arrays with spaces and semicolons as delimiters
\item[author] Rabinoff, Joseph
\index{Author!Rabinoff, Joseph}
\item[copyright] Joseph Rabinoff (2016)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version]  (2016-10-05)
\item[last changes] 2016-10-05
\item[year] 2016
\index{Year!2016}
\item[description] (no language specified) Typeset matrices and arrays with spaces and semicolons as delimiters.

          The purpose of this package is to decrease the number of keystrokes needed to typeset small amounts of 
          aligned material (matrices, arrays, etc.). It provides a facility for typing alignment environments and 
          macros with spaces as the alignment delimiter and semicolons (by default) as the end-of-row indicator. 
          For instance, typeset a matrix using {\textbackslash}spalignmat{\textbraceleft}1 12 -3; 24 
          -2 2; 0 0 1{\textbraceright}, or a vector using {\textbackslash}spalignvector{\textbraceleft}22 
          {\textbackslash}frac{\textbraceleft}1{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}2{\textbraceright} 
          -14{\textbraceright}.

          This package also contains utility macros for typesetting augmented matrices, vectors, arrays, systems 
          of equations, and more, and is easily extendable to other situations that use alignments.

          People who have to typeset a large number of matrices (like linear algebra teachers) should find this 
          package to be a real time saver.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spalign/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spalign/spalign.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5638252674-spalign.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spalign}

\section[\texttt{spanish-mx} -- Typeset Spanish as in Mexico]{\texttt{spanish-mx} -- Typeset Spanish as in Mexico}\label{pkg:spanish-mx}
\index{Package!spanish-mx}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/spanish-mx}
\item[name] \texttt{spanish-mx}
\item[caption] Typeset Spanish as in Mexico
\item[author] Rivera, Luis
\index{Author!Rivera, Luis}
\item[copyright] J. Luis Rivera N. (2008)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.1a
\item[description] (no language specified) The bundle provides files to support typesetting of texts in Spanish according to Mexican current practices, 
          using  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} . The files merge earlier work on a \texttt{mexican.ldf} , 
          or may be used to define a configuration that will typeset all documents (that request babel’s \texttt{spanish} option) 
          to use the Mexican language facilities. (Note that this facility is only available with version >=4.2b 
          releases of the Spanish option.)

          release of a chapter on sparklines. A PHP implementation may be found at \href{http://sparkline.sourceforge.net/}{SourceForge} .

\section[\texttt{spectralsequences} -- Print spectral sequence diagrams using PGF/TikZ]{\texttt{spectralsequences} -- Print spectral sequence diagrams using PGF/TikZ}\label{pkg:spectralsequences}
\index{Package!spectralsequences}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/spectralsequences}
\item[name] \texttt{spectralsequences}
\item[caption] Print spectral sequence diagrams using PGF/TikZ
\item[author] Chatham, Hood
\index{Author!Chatham, Hood}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.3.3 (2023-01-28)
\item[last changes] 2023-01-28
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package is a specialized tool built on top of PGF/TikZ for drawing spectral sequences. It provides 
          a powerful, concise syntax for specifying the data of a spectral sequence, and then allows the user to 
          print various pages of spectral sequences, automatically choosing which subset of the classes, differentials, 
          and structure lines to display on each page. It also handles most of the details of the layout.

          At the same time, it is extremely flexible.  \texttt{spectralsequences} is closely integrated 
          with TikZ to ensure that users can take advantage of as much as possible of its expressive power. It 
          is possible to turn off most of the automated layout features and draw replacements using TikZ commands. 
          The package also provides a carefully designed error reporting system intended to ensure that it is as 
          clear as possible what is going wrong.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/spectralsequences/README.md}

\section[\texttt{spelatex} -- Create PDF documents with hyperlinks to audiofragments]{\texttt{spelatex} -- Create PDF documents with hyperlinks to audiofragments}\label{pkg:spelatex}
\index{Package!spelatex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/spelatex}
\item[name] \texttt{SpeLaTeX}
\item[caption] Create PDF documents with hyperlinks to audiofragments
\item[author] Daems, Walter
\index{Author!Daems, Walter}
\item[copyright] Walter Daems and Paul Levrie (2024-2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.95 (2025-01-31)
\item[last changes] 2025-01-31
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package equips the PDF that is generated with LaTeX with hyperlinks to audio files that contain 
          the spoken equivalent of the original text, equations, figures and tables.

          The audio files can be automatically generated using a Perl-script called  \texttt{spel-wizard.pl} (part 
          of the \texttt{SpeL::Wizard} module available on CPAN). This script interfaces with locally 
          installed text-to-speech software or with online available (paying) cloud services to generate the audio 
          files. To this end, the LaTeX chunks of your text are parsed and translated to ''natural language''.

          SpeLaTeX is babel-enabled such that your text is read with the correct pronunciation corresponding to 
          your language. So far, it provides the languages English and Dutch, but it will be extended in the future.

          You can package your PDF together with the audio-files (in your favorite archive format) and make it 
          available to your users, such that the only requirements to read your text and listen to the audio are 
          a suited PDF reader and media player.

          For the text-to-speech conversion, one can use free options (festival, balabolka, ...) or paying services 
          (e.g. AWS polly).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spelatex/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spelatex/spelatex.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./9269323380-spelatex.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spelatex}

\item[license] other-free = Free license not otherwise listed (free)
\index{License!other-free}
\index{License!Free license not otherwise listed}
\item[description] (no language specified) Spidery WEB is built around the tool Spider, that reads a description of a programming language, and 
          writes source code for a Weave and a Tangle which support that language. The base sources derive from 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/cweb}{CWEB} , so that the resulting programs inherit some 
          properties of that system (e.g., the ability to read multiple files). Spider itself is written in Awk, 
          and the Weave and Tangle output is in C.

          Spidery WEB is no longer supported: its author used lessons learned from the development to produce the 
          still more compact  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/noweb}{noweb} system.

          information that is located somewhere else), in a human-readable format (no need to know SpiX to understand

\item[description] (no language specified) SplitIndex consists of a LaTeX package,  \texttt{splitidx} , and a small program, \texttt{splitindex} . 
          The package may be used to produce one index or several indexes. Without splitindex (for example, using 
          the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/index}{index} package), the number of indexes is limited 
          by the number of TeX’s output streams. But using the program you may use even more than 16 indexes: splitidx 
          outputs only a single file \texttt{{\textbackslash}jobname.idx} and the program splits 
          that file into several raw index files and calls your favorite index processor for each of the files.

\section[\texttt{spverbatim} -- Allow line breaks within {\textbackslash}verb and verbatim output]{\texttt{spverbatim} -- Allow line breaks within {\textbackslash}verb and verbatim output}\label{pkg:spverbatim}
\index{Package!spverbatim}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/spverbatim}
\item[name] \texttt{spverbatim}
\item[caption] Allow line breaks within {\textbackslash}verb and verbatim output
\item[author] Pakin, Scott
\index{Author!Pakin, Scott}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) LaTeX's  \texttt{{\textbackslash}verb} macro treats its argument as an unbreakable 
          unit of text. This can lead to poor typesetting, especially when the argument is long. The spverbatim 
          package provides an \texttt{{\textbackslash}spverb} macro that is analogous to \texttt{{\textbackslash}verb} and 
          an \texttt{spverbatim} environment that is analogous to \texttt{verbatim} with 
          the difference being that \texttt{{\textbackslash}spverb} and \texttt{spverbatim} allow 
          LaTeX to break lines at space characters.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/spverbatim/README}

\section[\texttt{sqltex} -- An SQL Preprocessor for LaTeX]{\texttt{sqltex} -- An SQL Preprocessor for LaTeX}\label{pkg:sqltex}
\index{Package!sqltex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/sqltex}
\item[name] \texttt{SQLTeX}
\item[caption] An SQL Preprocessor for LaTeX
\item[author] van Eijk, Oscar
\index{Author!van Eijk, Oscar}
\item[copyright] Oscar van Eijk (2001-2024)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 3.0 (2024-09-20)
\item[last changes] 2024-09-20
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) SQLTeX is a preprocessor that enables the use of SQL statements in LaTeX. The SQLTeX perl script reads 
          an input file containing the LaTeX source with SQL commands, and writes a LaTeX file in which the SQL 
          commands have been replaced by the values from their execution. It is possible to select a field for 
          substitution in your LaTeX document, or to be used as input in another SQL command. (When an SQL command 
          returns multiple fields and/or rows, the values can only be used within the document.)

          The default is to use MySQL databases, but Pg, Sybase, Oracle, Ingres, mSQL and PostgreSQL are also supported.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package README}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/support/sqltex/README.md}

\section[\texttt{sshrc-insight} -- A LaTeX class for SSHRC Insight Grant proposals]{\texttt{sshrc-insight} -- A LaTeX class for SSHRC Insight Grant proposals}\label{pkg:sshrc-insight}
\index{Package!sshrc-insight}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/sshrc-insight}
\item[name] \texttt{sshrc-insight}
\item[caption] A LaTeX class for SSHRC Insight Grant proposals
\item[author] Miller, Tristan
\index{Author!Miller, Tristan}
\item[copyright] Tristan Miller (2024)
\item[copyright] Steven B. Segletes (2021)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 2024.1.0 (2024-10-21)
\item[last changes] 2024-10-21
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The sshrc-insight LaTeX class facilitates the preparation of funding proposals for the Insight Grants 
          program of Canada’s Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC). It has the following key 
          features:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Formats the proposal according to the SSHRC’s specifications.
          \item Allows parts of the proposal to be compiled into separate PDFs to attach to the appropriate places in the online application form.
          \item Alternatively, allows the proposal to be compiled into a single PDF in order to facilitate the writing and pre-submission reviewing process.
          \item Ensures that citation numbering remains consistent regardless whether the proposal is compiled as separate PDFs or a single PDF.
          \item Provides character counts for long-answer form fields.
          \item Supports preparation of proposals in either English or French.
          \item Compatible with pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX, and LuaLaTeX.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sshrc-insight/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Example of use}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sshrc-insight/insight_proposal.pdf}

\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/sshrc-insight/sshrc-insight.pdf}

          or as part of a main document. Special support for pictures with beamer overlays is also provided.

          The package is used in the main document and skips extra preambles in sub-files. The class may be used 
          to simplify the preamble in sub-files. By default the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/preview}{preview} package 
          is used to display the typeset code without margins.

          The behaviour in standalone mode may adjusted using a configuration file  \texttt{standalone.cfg} to 
          redefine the \texttt{standalone} environment.

\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a convenient way to create customizable theorem and proposition boxes using  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tcolorbox}{tcolorbox} .

          Its most distinctive feature is the automatic Preview and Recall mechanism. By using a single command 
          ({\textbackslash}refcallsp), you can display a statement box anywhere in your document. The package 
          automatically determines its position relative to the main definition: if placed before, it generates 
          a ''Preview'' box; if placed after, it generates a ''Recall'' box. Both automatically include hyperlinks 
          jumping directly to the main definition.

          functions (increasing or decreasing, in frequency or absolute count domain), from the counts of individual 
          values, or ranges, or even the raw value list with repetitions.

          It can also compute and draw a bar diagram in case of individual values, or, when the data repartition 
          is known from ranges, an histogram or the continuous cumulative distribution function.

\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)

\item[version] 1.1 (2022-11-07)
\item[last changes] 2022-11-07
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) This little package is mainly meant to be used when there is a (TrueType or OpenType) font that does 
          not provide real small capitals. As a workaround, this package helps to borrow, or ''steal'', the small 
          capitals from another font. This might also be useful in the rare case that someone does not like the 
          present small capitals, and wants to change them, or likes those from another font better.

          To achieve the borrowing, one only needs to load the package and specify the name of the target font 
          via the  \texttt{from} option.

          Package dependencies:  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgfopts}{pgfopts} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/iftex}{iftex} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec}{fontspec} .

\section[\texttt{stellenbosch} -- Stellenbosch thesis bundle (legacy version)]{\texttt{stellenbosch} -- Stellenbosch thesis bundle (legacy version)}\label{pkg:stellenbosch}
\index{Package!stellenbosch}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/stellenbosch}
\item[name] \texttt{stellenbosch}
\item[caption] Stellenbosch thesis bundle (legacy version)
\item[author] Els, Daniel
\index{Author!Els, Daniel}
\item[copyright] Danie Els (2003-2015)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 11a
\item[description] (no language specified) Note: This bundle should only be used for typesetting legacy documents. For new documents, its successor 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/stellenbosch-2}{stellenbosch-2} is available.

          The usthesis class/style files are provided to typeset reports, theses and dissertations that conform 
          to the requirements of the Engineering Faculty of the University of Stellenbosch.

          The class file  \texttt{usthesis.cls} is based on the standard LaTeX book class, while \texttt{usthesis.sty} is 
          a style file to be loaded on top of the very powerful \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/memoir}{memoir} class. 
          Both options give identical output, but the benefit of the using memoir is that it has many additional 
          command and environments for formatting and processing of a document.

          Usthesis is primarily concerned with the formatting of the front matter such as the title page, abstract, 
          etc. and a decent page layout on A4 paper. It also works together with the babel package to provide language 
          options to typeset documents in Afrikaans or in English.

          Additional packages are provided for bibliographic matter, note title pages, lists of symbols, as well 
          as various graphic files for logos.
\item[documentation]  (English) \textit{USnomencl package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/stellenbosch/doc/USnomencl-1.1.pdf}

\item[last changes] 2017-03-27
\item[year] 2017
\index{Year!2017}
\item[description] (no language specified) The stfloats package provides:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item commands to control  \texttt{{\textbackslash}baselineskip} , that actually permit stretch and shrink, allowing a different value for use within floats;
          \item commands to control whether footnotes will appear above (as standard) or below a bottom float;
          \item a command that declares that double floats should be placed at the bottom (rather than the top) of a page.
          \end{itemize}
The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/sttools}{sttools} bundle.

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[caption] Type1 versions of the STIX Two OpenType fonts
\item[author] The STI Pub Companies
\index{Author!The STI Pub Companies}
\item[author] Jones, David M.
\index{Author!Jones, David M.}
\item[copyright] STI Pub Companies (2001-2018, 2021)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}

\item[license] ofl = The SIL Open Font License (free)
\index{License!ofl}
\index{License!The SIL Open Font License}
\item[version] 2.0.2
\item[description] (no language specified) The stix2 package provides minimal support for using the STIX Two fonts with versions of TeX that are 
          limited to TFM files, Type 1 PostScript fonts, and 8-bit font encodings.

          Version 2.0.0 of the STIX fonts are being released in this format in hopes of easing the transition from 
          legacy TeX engines to modern fully Unicode-compatible systems.

          The Type 1 versions are merely a repackaging of the original OpenType versions and should not be viewed 
          as independent entities. Some glyphs that are traditionally available in TeX math fonts are not yet available 
          in the STIX Two OpenType fonts. In such cases, we have chosen to omit them from the stix2 package rather 
          than create incompatibilities between the OpenType and Type 1 versions. In addition, while development 
          of the OpenType versions is ongoing, no further updates are planned to the Type 1 versions of the fonts.

\section[\texttt{stricttex} -- Strictly balanced brackets and numbers in command names]{\texttt{stricttex} -- Strictly balanced brackets and numbers in command names}\label{pkg:stricttex}
\index{Package!stricttex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/stricttex}
\item[name] \texttt{stricttex}
\item[caption] Strictly balanced brackets and numbers in command names
\item[author] Ørsted, Sebastian
\index{Author!Ørsted, Sebastian}
\item[copyright] Sebastian Ørsted (2020)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.2beta
\item[description] (no language specified) This is a small, LuaLaTeX-only package providing you with three, sometimes useful features:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item It allows you to make brackets  \texttt{[...]} ''strict'', meaning that each \texttt{[} must be balanced by a \texttt{]} .
          \item It allows you to use numbers in command names, so that you can do stuff like  \texttt{{\textbackslash}newcommand{\textbackslash}pi12{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}pi\_{\textbraceleft}12{\textbraceright}{\textbraceright}} .
          \item It allows you to use numbers  \emph{and} primes in command names, so that you can do stuff like \texttt{{\textbackslash}newcommand{\textbackslash}pi'12{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}pi '\_{\textbraceleft}12{\textbraceright}{\textbraceright}} .
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/stricttex/stricttex.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./8025416446-stricttex.pdf|

\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/luatex/latex/stricttex}

\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.24
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides a large and sundry set of macros for the manipulation of strings. The macros are 
          developed not merely for cosmetic application (such as changing the case of letters and string substitution), 
          but also for programming applications such as character look-ahead, argument parsing, conditional tests 
          on various string conditions, etc.

          The macros were designed all to be expandable (note that things such as  \texttt{{\textbackslash}uppercase} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}lowercase} are 
          not expandable), so that the macros may be strung together sequentially and nested (after a fashion) 
          to achieve rather complex manipulations.

          (using  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pict2e}{pict2e} for preference).

\item[description] (no language specified) This package can be used to generate a single master document that contains a set of individual student 
          handouts. The package has two main functions.

          First, it provides a simple framework for organizing handout source code, and supplies a set of import 
          management tools for selectively importing a subset of the handouts into the master document. Selective 
          import is convenient when compilation of all of the handouts is unnecessary, for example when working 
          on a new handout.

          As a secondary feature, the package defines a basic visual style for handouts. This style can be easily 
          changed.
