\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tib}
\item[name] \texttt{tib}
\item[caption] A bibliographic preprocessor
\item[author] Kolb, Hans-Peter
\index{Author!Kolb, Hans-Peter}
\item[author] Alexander, James
\index{Author!Alexander, James}
\item[author] Kremer, Sebastian
\index{Author!Kremer, Sebastian}
\item[license] noinfo = noinfo 
\index{License!noinfo}
\index{License!noinfo}
\item[version]  (1989-12-11)
\item[last changes] 1989-12-11
\item[year] 1989
\index{Year!1989}
\item[description] (no language specified) Tib is a collection of four programs for making citations and reference lists in TeX documents. The main 
          program, Tib, operates on a TeX file with incomplete or keyed citations, looks up the reference in a 
          database, makes the complete citation and on command, makes a list of the references. The citations in 
          the source document are enclosed in (non-TeX) escape characters which Tib recognizes. The output of Tib 
          is another TeX file with complete citations and reference list formatted with a number of TeX control 
          sequences and with definitions for these control sequences, ready to be processed by Plain TeX, LaTeX, 
          or whatever.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/biblio/tib/README.1st}

\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides straightforward ways to define three-dimensional coordinate frames through which 
          to plot in TikZ. The user can specify the orientation of the main coordinate frame, and use standard 
          TikZ commands and coordinates to render their tikzfigure. A secondary coordinate frame is provided to 
          allow rotations and translations with respect to the main coordinate frame. In addition, the package 
          can also handle plotting user-specified functions in spherical polar coordinates, where both the radius 
          and fill color can be expressed as parametric functions of polar angles.

\item[description] (no language specified) The built-in determination of the bounding box in TikZ is not entirely accurate. This is because, for 
          Bezier curves, it is the smallest box that contains all control points, which is in general larger than 
          the box that just contains the curve. This library determines the exact bounding box of the curve.

\section[\texttt{tikz-feynhand} -- Feynman diagrams with TikZ]{\texttt{tikz-feynhand} -- Feynman diagrams with TikZ}\label{pkg:tikz-feynhand}
\index{Package!tikz-feynhand}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tikz-feynhand}
\item[name] \texttt{TikZ-FeynHand}
\item[caption] Feynman diagrams with TikZ
\item[author] Dohse, Max
\index{Author!Dohse, Max}
\item[copyright] Max Dohse (2019)
\item[copyright] Joshua Ellis (2016)
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[version] 1.1.0 (2019-08-19)
\item[last changes] 2019-08-19
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package lets you draw Feynman diagrams using TikZ.

          It is a low-end modification of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tikz-feynman}{TikZ-Feynman} package, 
          one of whose principal advantages is the automatic generation of diagrams, for which it needs \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/luatex}{LuaTex} . 
          TikZ-FeynHand only provides the manual mode and hence runs in LaTeX without any reference to \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/luatex}{LuaTeX} .

          In addition it provides some new styles for vertices and propagators, alternative shorter keywords in 
          addition to  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tikz-feynman}{TikZ-Feynman} ’s longer ones, some 
          shortcut commands for quickly customizing the diagrams’ look, and the new feature of putting one propagator 
          ''on top'' of another.

          It also includes a quick user guide for getting started, with many examples and a 5-minute introduction 
          to  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/tikz-feynhand/tikz-feynhand.userguide.pdf}

\section[\texttt{tikz-karnaugh} -- Typeset Karnaugh maps using TikZ]{\texttt{tikz-karnaugh} -- Typeset Karnaugh maps using TikZ}\label{pkg:tikz-karnaugh}
\index{Package!tikz-karnaugh}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tikz-karnaugh}
\item[name] \texttt{tikz-karnaugh}
\item[caption] Typeset Karnaugh maps using TikZ
\item[author] Laus, Luís Paulo
\index{Author!Laus, Luís Paulo}
\item[copyright] Luis Paulo Laus (2017-2022)
\item[license] lppl1 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1 (free)
\index{License!lppl1}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1}
\item[version] 1.5 (2022-02-15)
\item[last changes] 2022-02-15
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \texttt{tikz-karnaugh} package is a LaTeX package used to draw Karnaugh maps. It uses 
          TikZ to produce high quality graph from 1 to 12 variables, but this upper limit depends on the TeX memory 
          usage and can be different for you. It is very good for presentation since TikZ allows for a better control 
          over the final appearance of the map. You can control colour, styles and distances.

          It can be considered as an upgrade and extension of Andreas W. Wieland's  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/karnaugh}{karnaugh} package 
          towards TikZ supporting. Upgrade because uses TikZ for more option on typesetting and overall higher 
          quality. Extension because it also supports American style and inputting the values as they would appear 
          in the map or in the truth table. Complex maps with solution (implicants) pointed out can be generated 
          with external java software (see documentation for details).

          It supports both American and traditional (simplified labels) styles and from version 1.3 on American 
          style is natively supported, therefore, no more addition work is required to typeset Gray coded labels, 
          variable names etc. From version 1.4, two new macros allow typesetting a map much more similarly as it 
          should appear. Original order, as the values appear in the truth table, still being supported.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/tikz-karnaugh/README.txt}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/tikz-karnaugh/doc/tikz-karnaugh-doc.pdf}

          The following styles are supported:

          \begin{itemize}

          \item ens: ensemble

          \item inhibt: inhibitory connection

          \item rect: rectification ensemble
          \item recurrent: recurrent connection

\item[description] (no language specified) This package allows for drawing a map of a particle accelerator just by giving a list of elements — similar 
          to lattice files for simulation software. The package includes 12 common element types like dipoles, 
          quadrupoles, cavities, or screens, as well as automatic labels with element names, a legend, a rule, 
          and an environment to fade out parts of the accelerator.

          The coordinate of any element can be saved and used for custom TikZ drawings or annotations. Thereby, 
          lattices can be connected to draw injection/extraction or even a complete accelerator facility.

          the easy syntax of Alexis Dimitriadis’ \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/qtree}{Qtree} . It 
          improves on TikZ’s standard tree-drawing facility by laying out tree nodes without collisions; it improves 
          on Qtree by adding lots of features from TikZ (for example, edge labels, arrows between nodes); and it

\index{License!lppl1.3c}

\item[version] 2.0
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} library for working with 
          tiles, tilings, and tessellations. Using it, one can define tiles, place tiles, deform tiles, and — in 
          some cases — apply replacement rules to generate tessellations. It has pre-defined tiles for most of 
          the Penrose tile sets and the aperiodical polykite tiles.

          This is a replacement for the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/penrose}{penrose} package, 
          renamed as it now deals with more extensive tiles than just the Penrose tile sets.

\section[\texttt{tipauni} -- Producing Unicode characters with TIPA commands]{\texttt{tipauni} -- Producing Unicode characters with TIPA commands}\label{pkg:tipauni}
\index{Package!tipauni}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tipauni}
\item[name] \texttt{tipauni}
\item[caption] Producing Unicode characters with TIPA commands
\item[author] निरंजन
\index{Author!निरंजन}
\item[copyright] निरंजन (2021-2023)
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[license] fdl = Free Documentation License (free)
\index{License!fdl}
\index{License!Free Documentation License}
\item[version] 0.7a (2023-02-13)
\item[last changes] 2023-02-13
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) Package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tipa}{TIPA} uses the T3 encoding for producing IPA 
          characters. The package is widely used in the field of linguistics, but because of the old encoding, 
          the output documents are less productive than Unicode-based documents.

          This package redefines most of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tipa}{TIPA} -commands 
          for outputting Unicode characters. Users can now use their beloved TIPA shortcuts with the benefits of 
          Unicode, i.e. searchability, copy-pasting, changing the font and many more.

          As this package needs the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec}{fontspec} package for 
          loading an IPA font, it needs to be compiled with XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX.

          This package can also be viewed as an ASCII-based input method for producing IPA characters in Unicode.

          It needs the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/newcomputermodern}{New Computer Modern} font 
          for printing IPA characters.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Example of use}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/unicodetex/latex/tipauni/tipauni-example.pdf}

\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package is intended for setting rich text into titling capitals (in which the first character of 
          words are capitalized). It automatically accounts for diacritical marks (like umlauts), national symbols 
          (like ''ae''), punctuation, and font changing commands that alter the appearance or size of the text. 
          It allows a list of predesignated words to be protected as lower-cased, and also allows for titling exceptions 
          of various sorts.

\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 3.10c
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a library written in Lua, allowing to make all the necessary calculations to define 
          the objects of a Euclidean geometry figure. You need to compile with LuaLaTeX. The definitions and calculations 
          are only done with Lua.

          The main possibility of programmation proposed is oriented ''object programming'' with object classes 
          like point, line, triangle, circle and ellipse. For the moment, once the calculations are done, it is 
          \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tkz-euclide}{tkz-euclide} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf}{TikZ} which 
          allows the drawings.

\section[\texttt{tocdata} -- Adds names to chapters, sections, figures in the TOC and LOF\ldots]{\texttt{tocdata} -- Adds names to chapters, sections, figures in the TOC and LOF}\label{pkg:tocdata}
\index{Package!tocdata}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tocdata}
\item[name] \texttt{tocdata}
\item[caption] Adds names to chapters, sections, figures in the TOC and LOF
\item[author] Dunn, Brian
\index{Author!Dunn, Brian}
\item[copyright] Brian Dunn (2016-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 2.07 (2024-01-20)
\item[last changes] 2024-01-20
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The tocdata package may be used to add a small amount of data to an entry in the table of contents or 
          list of figures, between the section or caption name and the page number. The typical use would be to 
          add the name of an author or artist of a chapter or section, such as in an anthology or a collection 
          of papers.

          Additionally, user-level macros are provided which add the author’s name to a chapter or section, along 
          with an optional prefix and/or suffix, and add to a figure the artist’s name, prefix, and suffix, plus 
          optional additional text. Author and artist names are also added to the index. Additional user-level 
          macros control formatting.

          tocdata works with the TOC/LOF formatting of the default LaTeX classes, memoir, koma-script, and with 
          titletoc, tocloft, tocbasic, and tocstyle.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tocdata/tocdata.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./9356122951-tocdata.pdf|

\section[\texttt{tokcycle} -- Build tools to process tokens from an input stream]{\texttt{tokcycle} -- Build tools to process tokens from an input stream}\label{pkg:tokcycle}
\index{Package!tokcycle}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tokcycle}
\item[name] \texttt{tokcycle}
\item[caption] Build tools to process tokens from an input stream
\item[author] Segletes, Steven B.
\index{Author!Segletes, Steven B.}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.42 (2021-08-25)
\item[last changes] 2021-08-25
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) The tokcycle package helps one to build tools to process tokens from an input stream. If a macro to process 
          an arbitrary single token can be built, then tokcycle can provide a wrapper for cycling through an input 
          stream (including macros, spaces, and groups) on a token-by-token basis, using the provided macro on 
          each successive character.

          tokcycle characterizes each successive token in the input stream as a Character, a Group, a Macro, or 
          a Space. Each of these token categories are processed with a unique directive, to bring about the desired 
          effect of the token cycle. If condition flags are provided to identify active, implicit, and catcode-6 
          tokens as they are digested. The package provides a number of options for handling groups.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Examples of use}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/tokcycle/tokcycle-examples.pdf}

\index{License!lppl}

\item[version] 1.1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) A tokenizer for LaTeX.  \texttt{{\textbackslash}GetTokens{\textbraceleft}Target1{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}Target2{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}Source{\textbraceright}} splits 
          source into two tokens at the first encounter of a comma. The first token is saved in a newly created 
          command with the name passed as \texttt{<Target1>} and the second token likewise. A package 
          option ‘ \texttt{trim} ’ causes leading and trailing space to be removed from each token; 
          with this option, the \texttt{{\textbackslash}TrimSpaces} command is defined, which 
          removes leading and trailing spaces from its argument.

\section[\texttt{tokmap} -- Iterate over a token list expandably, without dropping space\ldots]{\texttt{tokmap} -- Iterate over a token list expandably, without dropping spaces or braced groups}\label{pkg:tokmap}
\index{Package!tokmap}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tokmap}
\item[name] \texttt{tokmap}
\item[caption] Iterate over a token list expandably, without dropping spaces or braced groups
\item[author] plante
\index{Author!plante}
\item[copyright] plante (2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0
\item[description] (no language specified) Usage:  \verb|\tokmap <command> { <tokens> }| applies \texttt{command} over the token list tokens. Space tokens, left and right braces are replaced with the marker tokens \texttt{{\textbackslash}tokmap@space} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}tokmap@bgroup} , and \texttt{{\textbackslash}tokmap@egroup} respectively (which are \texttt{{\textbackslash}ifx} -equal to themselves exclusively). For convenience, \texttt{command} may contain multiple tokens. It is assumed that \texttt{{\textbraceleft}} and \texttt{{\textbraceright}} are the only characters with category codes 1 (beginning of group) and 2 (end of group) respectively. Expandable.

          This package may be used in LaTeX by  \verb|\usepackage{tokmap}| , or in plain TeX and other formats by \verb|\input{tokmap}| .

          See the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/visualtoks}{visualtoks} package for an example application.

\section[\texttt{tokstools} -- Tools for manipulating tokens]{\texttt{tokstools} -- Tools for manipulating tokens}\label{pkg:tokstools}
\index{Package!tokstools}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tokstools}
\item[name] \texttt{tokstools}
\item[caption] Tools for manipulating tokens
\item[author] Tellechea, Christian
\index{Author!Tellechea, Christian}
\item[copyright] Christian Tellechea (2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.2
\item[description] (no language specified) This package is still in the experimental stage. Therefore, its behavior is not guaranteed to match the 
          description in the manual, and bugs of varying severity may occur.

          Additionally, some features, as well as their syntax, may be subject to change.

          It requires any modern engine that supports etex primitives and can therefore be used with either TeX 
          or LaTeX.

          The tokstools package provides tools for manipulating tokens and implements ''PEG''-style grammars in 
          TeX. Predefined elementary patterns can be combined to form grammars that search for matches within tokens.

          Two categories of macros are provided: 
          \begin{itemize}
          \item those operating on individual tokens ( \verb|\toksdo| , \verb|\tokscount| , and \verb|\printtoks| );
          \item those operating on tokens that have matched a grammar ( \verb|\ifpegmatch| , \verb|\pegcount| , and \verb|\pegreplace| )
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (English) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/tokstools/tokstools-en.pdf}

\item[version] 2.0
\item[description] (no language specified) The virtual fonts in this package allow the user to easily write English, Quenya and Sindarin in several 
          modes with J.R.R. Tolkien's tengwar, cirth, sarati and valmaric scripts, using freely available TrueType 
          fonts found on the internet.

          Support is at very nearly the highest possible level; the point of this package was to avoid bizarre 
          spellings or lots of special commands.

          Fonts supported are Tengwar Annatar, Cirth Erebor, Sarati and Valmaric Eldamar, and (with a little more 
          work) Tengwar Parmaite, Eldamar, Noldor, Quenya and Sindarin.

\section[\texttt{topiclongtable} -- Extend longtable with cells that merge hierarchically]{\texttt{topiclongtable} -- Extend longtable with cells that merge hierarchically}\label{pkg:topiclongtable}
\index{Package!topiclongtable}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/topiclongtable}
\item[name] \texttt{topiclongtable}
\item[caption] Extend longtable with cells that merge hierarchically
\item[author] Brasolin, Paolo
\index{Author!Brasolin, Paolo}
\item[copyright] Paolo Brasolin (2017-2020)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version] 1.3.2 (2020-04-12)
\item[last changes] 2020-04-12
\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) This LaTeX package extends  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable}{longtable} implementing 
          cells that:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item merge with the one above if it has the same content,
          \item do not merge with the one above unless the ones on the left are merged,
          \item are well behaved with respect to longtable chunking on page breaks,
          \item and automatically draw the correct separation lines.
          \end{itemize}
The typical use case is a table spanning multiple pages that contains a list of hierarchically organized 
          topics (hence the package name).

          The package depends on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/array}{array} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/longtable}{longtable} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/multirow}{multirow} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xparse}{xparse} , 
          and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/oberdiek}{zref-abspage} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/topiclongtable/README.md}

          infix strings may be selected and specified at will by means of a configuration file, so as to customize

          the bundle is suited for multilanguage theses that are becoming more and more frequent thanks to the

\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 0.6
\item[description] (no language specified) This package aims to improve of font readability in presentations, especially with maths. The standard 
          cm maths fonts at large design sizes are difficult to read from far away, especially at low resolutions 
          and low contrast color choice. Using this package leads to much better overall readability of some font 
          combinations. The package offers a couple of ‘harmonising’ combinations of text and maths fonts from 
          the (distant) relatives of computer modern fonts, with a couple of extras for optimising readability. 
          Text fonts from computer modern roman, computer modern sans serif, SliTeX computer modern sans serif, 
          computer modern bright, or concrete roman are available, in addition to maths fonts from computer modern 
          maths, computer modern bright maths, or Euler fonts.

          The package is part of the TeXPower bundle.

\index{Package!tpx}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[name] \texttt{TpX}
\item[caption] A drawing tool for Windows
\item[author] Tsyplakov, Alexander
\index{Author!Tsyplakov, Alexander}
\item[license] gpl = GNU General Public License (free)
\index{License!gpl}
\index{License!GNU General Public License}
\item[version] 1.5
\item[description] (no language specified) TpX is a lightweight, easy-to-use graphical editor for Windows platform for creating drawings and including 
          them into TeX files in publication-ready form. It can also be used as a stand-alone editor for vector 
          graphics.

          The output is a file (with extension .TpX) containing the drawing as TeX code or as an {\textbackslash}includegraphics 
          link to an external file created by the program. The user can choose between several output formats. 
          TpX saves its own data in TeX file comments so that the drawing can be loaded into TpX and edited again. 
          This internal TpX format is based on XML and can easily be understood and edited.

          TpX can import EMF/WMF pictures created by other Windows applications, including many applications producing 
          scientific graphs. In most cases the result is nice, though sometimes the imported picture needs some 
          manual editing. So TpX can be used as an EMF-to-any converter.

\index{Package!trace}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/trace}
\item[name] \texttt{trace}
\item[caption] Make sensible use of TeX tracing in LaTeX
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[author] Mittelbach, Frank
\index{Author!Mittelbach, Frank}
\item[copyright] The LaTeX Project (1993-2023)
\item[copyright] Frank Mittelbach (1999-2019)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.1f (2021-04-18)
\item[last changes] 2021-04-18
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the means to suppress excessive (and usually unnecessary) tracing inside some particularly 
          verbose parts of LaTeX (such as the font selection routines, or the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/calc}{calc} package's 
          parsing of expressions).

          The package therefore redefines a number of key commands to turn off tracing while they execute (those 
          the author finds most annoying and noisy). Since it potentially modifies the content of other packages, 
          the package should be loaded last in a document's preamble.

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools}{latex-tools} bundle 
          in the LaTeX \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/required}{required} distribution.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/trace.pdf}

\section[\texttt{tracking} -- Adjust tracking of strings]{\texttt{tracking} -- Adjust tracking of strings}\label{pkg:tracking}
\index{Package!tracking}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tracking}
\item[name] \texttt{tracking}
\item[caption] Adjust tracking of strings
\item[author] Glazkov, Dmitry A.
\index{Author!Glazkov, Dmitry A.}
\item[license] other-nonfree = License that prevents distribution (not free)
\index{License!other-nonfree}
\index{License!License that prevents distribution}
\item[description] (no language specified) Automatically adjust spaces between symbols in words or phrases to fit them into a specified length. 
          Any chain of symbols (including spaces) in the current font may be treated.

          Commands  \texttt{{\textbackslash}track{\textbraceleft}<length>{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}<string>{\textbraceright}} (add 
          space \texttt{<length>} , which may be <0, after each symbol of \texttt{<string>} ), \texttt{{\textbackslash}fittrack{\textbraceleft}<length>{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}<string>{\textbraceright}} (make \texttt{<string>} fit 
          into width \texttt{<length>} , which may be smaller than the original width) and \texttt{{\textbackslash}ratiotrack{\textbraceleft}<ratio>{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}<string>{\textbraceright}} (as \texttt{{\textbackslash}fittrack} , 
          with \texttt{<length>} replaced by \texttt{<ratio>} of the natural length of \texttt{<string>} ).
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tracking/tracking.sty}
\item[keyword] \texttt{letterspace} (change space between characters)
\index{Topic!letterspace}

\item[see also] see section~\ref{pkg:letterspacing} on page~\pageref{pkg:letterspacing}: (\texttt{letterspacing} -- Letter spacing)

\section[\texttt{transparent-io} -- Show for approval the filenames used in {\textbackslash}input, {\textbackslash}openin, or \ldots]{\texttt{transparent-io} -- Show for approval the filenames used in {\textbackslash}input, {\textbackslash}openin, or {\textbackslash}openout}\label{pkg:transparent-io}
\index{Package!transparent-io}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/transparent-io}
\item[name] \texttt{Transparent-IO}
\item[caption] Show for approval the filenames used in {\textbackslash}input, {\textbackslash}openin, or {\textbackslash}openout
\item[author] Wermuth, Udo
\index{Author!Wermuth, Udo}
\item[copyright] Udo Wermuth (2022)
\item[license] gpl3 = GNU General Public License, version 3 (free)
\index{License!gpl3}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3}
\item[version]  (2022-04-30)
\item[last changes] 2022-04-30
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides macros to make the file I/O in plain TeX more transparent. That is, every  \verb|\input| , \verb|\openin| , and \verb|\openout| operation by TeX is presented to the user who must check carefully if the file name of the source is acceptable. The user must sometimes enter additional text and has to specify the file name that the TeX operation should use.

          The macros require a complex installation procedure; the package contains  \texttt{sed} and \texttt{bash} scripts 
          to do this on a UNIX-like operating system. Every installation is different from any other as password-protected 
          macro names and private messages have to be chosen by the installer. Therefore, the files in the package 
          cannot be used directly. The files carry the extension \texttt{.org} , and only after the 
          user has performed an individual customization for a private installation the changed files are renamed 
          and have the extension \texttt{.tex} . For details see the manual.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/transparent-io/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/transparent-io/Transparent-IO-doc.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./7233650778-Transparent-IO-doc.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/plain/contrib/transparent-io}

\section[\texttt{trig} -- Simple trigonometric functions]{\texttt{trig} -- Simple trigonometric functions}\label{pkg:trig}
\index{Package!trig}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/trig}
\item[name] \texttt{trig}
\item[caption] Simple trigonometric functions
\item[author] Carlisle, David
\index{Author!Carlisle, David}
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[copyright] David Carlisle, LaTeX3 Project (2000-2021)
\item[copyright] David Carlisle (1993-1997, 1999)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.11 (2023-12-02)
\item[last changes] 2023-12-02
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) Provides the trigonometric functions  \texttt{sin} , \texttt{cos} and \texttt{tan} , 
          for use in the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/graphics}{graphics} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/graphicx}{graphicx} packages.

          Before any trigonometric value is used, it must be pre-calculated, so a usage sequence might be  \texttt{{\textbackslash}CalculateSin{\textbraceleft}22.5{\textbraceright} 
          ... {\textbackslash}UseSin{\textbraceleft}22.5{\textbraceright}} ; the argument 
          may also be a LaTeX count, as in \texttt{{\textbackslash}UseTan{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}value{\textbraceleft}mycounter{\textbraceright}{\textbraceright}} , 
          or a count register, as in \texttt{{\textbackslash}CalculateCos{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}count@{\textbraceright}} .

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-graphics}{latex-graphics} bundle, 
          which is one of the collections in the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/required}{LaTeX ‘required’} set 
          of packages.

\section[\texttt{tudscr} -- Corporate Design of Technische Universität Dresden]{\texttt{tudscr} -- Corporate Design of Technische Universität Dresden}\label{pkg:tudscr}
\index{Package!tudscr}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tudscr}
\item[name] \texttt{tudscr}
\item[caption] Corporate Design of Technische Universität Dresden
\item[author] Hanisch, Falk
\index{Author!Hanisch, Falk}
\item[copyright] Falk Hanisch (2012-2022)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 2.06o (2022-08-09)
\item[last changes] 2022-08-09
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) The TUD-Script bundle provides both classes and packages in order to create LaTeX documents in the corporate 
          design of the Technische Universität Dresden. It bases on the KOMA-Script bundle, which must necessarily 
          be present.

          For questions, problems and comments, please refer to either the  \href{https://latex.wcms-file3.tu-dresden.de/phpBB3/}{LaTeX 
          forum of the Dresden University of Technology} or the \href{https://github.com/tud-cd/tudscr/issues}{GitHub 
          ''tudscr'' repository} .

          The bundle offers:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item the three document classes  \texttt{tudscrartcl} , \texttt{tudscrreprt} , and \texttt{tudscrbook} which serve as wrapper classes for \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script}{scrartcl} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script}{scrreprt} , and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/koma-script}{scrbook} ,
          \item the class  \texttt{tudscrposter} for creating posters,
          \item the package  \texttt{tudscrsupervisor} providing environments and macros to create tasks, evaluations and notices for scientific theses,
          \item the package  \texttt{tudscrfonts} , which makes the corporate design fonts of the Technische Universität Dresden available for LaTeX standard classes and KOMA-Script classes,
          \item the package  \texttt{fix-tudscrfonts} , which provides the same fonts to additional corporate design classes not related to TUD-Script,
          \item the package  \texttt{tudscrcomp} , which simplifies the switch to TUD-Script from external corporate design classes,
          \item the package  \texttt{mathswap} for swapping math delimiters within numbers (similar to \texttt{ionumbers} ),
          \item the package  \texttt{twocolfix} for fixing the positioning bug of headings in twocolumn layout, and
          \item a comprehensive user documentation as well as several tutorials.
          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{tuple} -- Expandable operations for tuples of numbers]{\texttt{tuple} -- Expandable operations for tuples of numbers}\label{pkg:tuple}
\index{Package!tuple}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tuple}
\item[name] \texttt{tuple}
\item[caption] Expandable operations for tuples of numbers
\item[author] Tellechea, Christian
\index{Author!Tellechea, Christian}
\item[copyright] Christian Tellechea (2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.2 (2024-12-20)
\item[last changes] 2024-12-20
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides  \emph{expandable} operations for tuples of numbers:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item len, sum, min, max, mean, med, quantile, standard deviation, get item, position of item
          \item sort, add or set(*) items, filter, operations, composition(*), split(*), formatting and display
          \end{itemize}
All with a concise syntax that is easy and intuitive to use :

          \begin{verbatim}
      object.method1.method2...
          \end{verbatim}
(*): unexpandable method

          -----------------------------------------------------------------------

          Cette extension met à disposition des opérations  \emph{développables} pour les tuples de 
          nombres :

          \begin{itemize}
          \item len, sum, min, max, mean, med, quantile, écart type, get item, position d’un élément
          \item tri, ajout ou modification(*) d’éléments, filtre, opérations, composition(*), coupure(*), formattage et affichage
          \end{itemize}
Le tout avec une syntaxe concise et d'un usage facile et intuitif :

          \begin{verbatim}
              object.methode1.methode2...
          \end{verbatim}
(*) : méthode non développable

\section[\texttt{tuzuk} -- Turkish bylaws and regulations document class]{\texttt{tuzuk} -- Turkish bylaws and regulations document class}\label{pkg:tuzuk}
\index{Package!tuzuk}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/tuzuk}
\item[name] \texttt{tuzuk}
\item[caption] Turkish bylaws and regulations document class
\item[author] Oğuz, Özcan
\index{Author!Oğuz, Özcan}
\item[copyright] Özcan Oğuz (2021-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0.0 (2024-03-13)
\item[last changes] 2024-03-13
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The  \texttt{tuzuk} class provides a standardized format for writing bylaws and regulations 
          in Turkish-governmental style. It includes features for creating numbered articles, subsections, and 
          signature areas commonly found in legal documents.

          \textbf{Features:} 

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Easy creation of numbered articles with the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}madde} command,
          \item Section titles with  \texttt{{\textbackslash}bolumadi} ,
          \item Automatic lettered lists with the  \texttt{fikra} environment,
          \item Built-in signature area formatting with  \texttt{{\textbackslash}imzalar} ,
          \item Full Turkish language support.
          \end{itemize}
Built originally for creating the regulation for Özgür Yazılım Derneği (The Free Software Association 
          in Turkey),  \href{https://oyd.org.tr/}{https://oyd.org.tr/} .

          Explanation of the package name: ''tüzük'' in Turkish means ''regulations'', as a document. For example, 
          GDPR, which stands for ''General Data Protection Regulation'', translates as ''Genel Veri Koruma Tüzüğü''. 
          In Turkish law, the non-profit associations have a ''tüzük'' as their constitution-like governing document.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tuzuk/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Example of use}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/tuzuk/oyd_tuzuk_2023.pdf}

\item[version]  (2009-01-14)
\item[last changes] 2009-01-14
\item[year] 2009
\index{Year!2009}
\item[description] (no language specified) Txfonts supplies virtual text roman fonts using Adobe Times (or URW NimbusRomNo9L) with some modified 
          and additional text symbols in the OT1, T1, and TS1 encodings; maths alphabets using Times/URW Nimbus; 
          maths fonts providing all the symbols of the Computer Modern and AMS fonts, including all the Greek capital 
          letters from CMR; and additional maths fonts of various other symbols.

          The set is complemented by a sans-serif set of text fonts, based on Helvetica/NimbusSanL, and a monospace 
          set.

          All the fonts are in Type 1 format (AFM and PFB files), and are supported by TeX metrics (VF and TFM 
          files) and macros for use with LaTeX.

\section[\texttt{type1cm} -- Arbitrary size font selection in LaTeX]{\texttt{type1cm} -- Arbitrary size font selection in LaTeX}\label{pkg:type1cm}
\index{Package!type1cm}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/type1cm}
\item[name] \texttt{type1cm}
\item[caption] Arbitrary size font selection in LaTeX
\item[author] Carlisle, David
\index{Author!Carlisle, David}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[description] (no language specified) LaTeX, by default, restricts the sizes at which you can use its default computer modern fonts, to a fixed 
          set of discrete sizes (effectively, a set specified by Knuth). The type1cm package removes this restriction; 
          this is particularly useful when using scalable versions of the cm fonts (Bakoma, or the versions from 
          BSR/Y\&Y, or True Type versions from Kinch, PCTeX, etc.). In fact, since modern distributions will 
          automatically generate any bitmap font you might need, type1cm has wider application than just those 
          using scaleable versions of the fonts.

          Note that the LaTeX distribution now contains a package  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fix-cm}{fix-cm} , 
          which performs the task of type1cm, as well as doing the same job for T1- and TS1-encoded \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ec}{ec} fonts.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/type1cm/type1cm-doc.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./4892635328-type1cm-doc.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/type1cm}
\item[on Mik\TeX] \texttt{type1cm}
\item[on \TeX Live] \texttt{type1cm}

          i.e., the  \emph{type} of checklist entries.

\section[\texttt{typedref} -- Eliminate errors by enforcing the types of labels]{\texttt{typedref} -- Eliminate errors by enforcing the types of labels}\label{pkg:typedref}
\index{Package!typedref}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/typedref}
\item[name] \texttt{typedref}
\item[caption] Eliminate errors by enforcing the types of labels
\item[author] Seidman, Gregory
\index{Author!Seidman, Gregory}
\item[author] Ashton, James
\index{Author!Ashton, James}
\item[copyright] Gregory Seidman (2001-2013)
\item[license] other-nonfree = License that prevents distribution (not free)
\index{License!other-nonfree}
\index{License!License that prevents distribution}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The package is provided to help users avoid cross-reference errors; it replaces  \texttt{{\textbackslash}ref} with \texttt{{\textbackslash}figureref} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}sectionref} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}eqref} , 
          etc., so that you're forced to specify the kind of label you’re referencing. Each reference command also 
          generates appropriate text automatically, so that instead of typing \texttt{Figure{\textasciitilde}{\textbackslash}ref{\textbraceleft}figure:key{\textbraceright}} , 
          all you need is \texttt{{\textbackslash}figureref{\textbraceleft}figure:key{\textbraceright}} . 
          The \texttt{{\textbackslash}label} command is redefined to record the type with the 
          label defined, so that each type of label has its own namespace.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/typedref/typedref.pdf}

\section[\texttt{typeface} -- Select a balanced set of fonts]{\texttt{typeface} -- Select a balanced set of fonts}\label{pkg:typeface}
\index{Package!typeface}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/typeface}
\item[name] \texttt{typeface}
\item[caption] Select a balanced set of fonts
\item[author] Jones, Geoffrey
\index{Author!Jones, Geoffrey}
\item[copyright] Geoffrey Jones (2012)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 0.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides the means of establishing a consistent set of fonts for use in a LaTeX document. 
          It allows mixing and matching the Type 1 font sets available on the archive (and it may be extended, 
          via its configuration file, to support other fonts).

          Font-set definition takes the form of a set of options that are read when the package is loaded: for 
          each typographic category (main body font, sans-serif font, monospace font, mathematics fonts, text figures, 
          and so on), a font or a transformation is given in those options.

          The approach enables the user to remember their own configurations (as a single command) and to borrow 
          configurations that other users have developed.

          The present release is designated ''for review''.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/typeface/README}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides macros for measuring alphabet lengths (i.e. the length occupied by the characters 
          ''abcd…xyz''), em-widths and ex-heights, which may help in making typesetting decisions.

          The package is compatible with pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, and XeLaTeX, and will accept font family switches 
          defined via the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontspec}{fontspec} package.

          The plan is that future versions shall be able to provide even more diagnostic tools, and some LuaTeX-specific 
          special commands, too.

          The package relies on the following other LaTeX packages:  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/array}{array} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/booktabs}{booktabs} ,

\section[\texttt{typog} -- Typographic fine-tuning and micro-typographic enhancements]{\texttt{typog} -- Typographic fine-tuning and micro-typographic enhancements}\label{pkg:typog}
\index{Package!typog}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/typog}
\item[name] \texttt{typog}
\item[caption] Typographic fine-tuning and micro-typographic enhancements
\item[author] Spiel, Chris
\index{Author!Spiel, Chris}
\item[copyright] Ch. L. Spiel (2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.5 (2025-10-27)
\item[last changes] 2025-10-27
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides macros for micro-typographic enhancements. It covers a variety of topics:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Precise hyphenation control
          \item Disable/break ligatures
          \item Manual italic correction
          \item Extra kerning for slash and hyphen
          \item Raising selected characters (e.g. hyphen, en-dash, and em-dash)
          \item Aligning of the last line of a paragraph
          \item Filling of the last line of a paragraph
          \item Word spacing control
          \item Microtype front-end
          \item Slightly sloppy paragraphs
          \item Vertically partially-tied paragraphs
          \item Breakable displayed equations
          \item Setspace front-end
          \item Smooth ragged-right paragraphs
          \end{itemize}
Moreover, typog provides an environment to flag interesting parts of the information deluge typically 
          accumulating in a LaTeX log-file and an associated tool,  \texttt{typog-grep} , that selectively 
          retrieves these parts.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/typog/docs/typog.pdf}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/ucalgmthesis}
\item[name] \texttt{ucalgmthesis}
\item[caption] LaTeX thesis class for University of Calgary Faculty of Graduate Studies
\item[author] Zach, Richard
\index{Author!Zach, Richard}
\item[copyright] Richard Zach (2019)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version]  (2023-03-18)
\item[last changes] 2023-03-18
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) \texttt{ucalgmthesis.cls} is a LaTeX class file that produces documents according to the \href{https://grad.ucalgary.ca/current-students/thesis-based-students/thesis/building-thesis}{thesis 
          guidelines} of the \href{https://grad.ucalgary.ca/}{University of Calgary Faculty of 
          Graduate Studies} .

          It uses the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/memoir}{memoir} class, which provides very powerful 
          and flexible mechanisms for book design and layout. All \texttt{memoir} commands for changing 
          chapter and section headings, page layout, fancy foot- and endnotes, typesetting poems, etc., can be 
          used. (Memoir is meant as a replacement for the standard LaTeX classes, so all standard LaTeX commands 
          such as \texttt{{\textbackslash}chapter} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}section} , 
          etc., still work.) Likewise, any of \texttt{memoir} ’s class options can be passed as options 
          to \texttt{ucalgmthesis} , in particular \texttt{12pt} to select 12 point type 
          (11 point is the default).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/ucalgmthesis/README.md}

\item[description] (no language specified) The bundle provides the  \texttt{ucs} package, and \texttt{utf8x.def} , together 
          with a large number of support files.

          The  \texttt{utf8x.def} definition file for use with \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/inputenc}{inputenc} covers 
          a wider range of Unicode characters than does \texttt{utf8.def} in the LaTeX distribution. 
          The package provides facilities for efficient use of its large sets of Unicode characters.

          Glyph production may be controlled by various options, which permits use of non-ASCII characters when 
          coding mathematical formulae.

          Note that the bundle previously had an alias '' \texttt{unicode} ''; that alias has now been 
          withdrawn, and no package of that name now exists.

\index{Package!uktex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}

\item[name] \texttt{UK-TeX}
\item[caption] The UK TeX digest
\item[license] pd = Public Domain Software (free)
\index{License!pd}
\index{License!Public Domain Software}
\item[description] (no language specified) The UK TeX digest started (at a time when TeXhax was also available), at least partly justified by the 
          oddities of internet access in the UK. The organisation of the digest was odd: a team of enthusiasts 
          tried to provide answers to questions before the digest was published, so that readers would encounter 
          a problem closely followed by a solution in the same issue.

          Eventually, the UK TeX digest was merged with the TeXhax digest, and the merged list was run in the UK 
          for a time, but without the distinctive experts group.

          The archives are arranged by year, and run from 1987 to 1994.
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/info/digests/uktex}

          break over line ends; this technique may be used to replace \texttt{{\textbackslash}em} (both 
          in that form and as the \texttt{{\textbackslash}emph} command), so as to make output

\item[description] (no language specified) With the package,  \texttt{{\textbackslash}\_} in text mode (i.e., \texttt{{\textbackslash}textunderscore} ) 
          prints an underscore so that hyphenation of words either side of it is not affected; a package option 
          controls whether an actual hyphenation point appears after the underscore, or merely a break point.

          The package also arranges that, while in text, ‘ \texttt{\_} ’ itself behaves as \texttt{{\textbackslash}textunderscore} (the 
          behaviour of \texttt{\_} in maths mode is not affected).

          Korean TeX ( \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hlatex-fonts}{HLaTeX} ) in the late 1990's and 
          released it under the GPL license.

          \item UnGungseo: cursive, brush-stroke
          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{unicode-alphabets} -- Macros for using characters from Unicode’s Private Use Area]{\texttt{unicode-alphabets} -- Macros for using characters from Unicode’s Private Use Area}\label{pkg:unicode-alphabets}
\index{Package!unicode-alphabets}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/unicode-alphabets}
\item[name] \texttt{unicode-alphabets}
\item[caption] Macros for using characters from Unicode’s Private Use Area
\item[author] Eriksen, Mikkel Eide
\index{Author!Eriksen, Mikkel Eide}
\item[license] cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
\index{License!cc-by-sa-4}
\index{License!CC BY-SA 4.0}
\item[version]  (2023-02-27)
\item[last changes] 2023-02-27
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) While Unicode supports the vast majority of use cases, there are certain specialized niches which require 
          characters and glyphs not (yet) represented in the standard. Thus the Private Use Area (PUA) at code 
          points E000–F8FF, which enables third parties to define arbitrary character sets.

          This package allows configuring a number of macros for using various PUA character sets in LaTeX (AGL, 
          CYFI, MUFI, SIL, TITUS, UCSUR, UNZ), to enable transcription and display of medieval and other documents.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Example of use}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/unicode-alphabets/docs/specimen.pdf}

\section[\texttt{unicode-data} -- Unicode data and loaders for TeX]{\texttt{unicode-data} -- Unicode data and loaders for TeX}\label{pkg:unicode-data}
\index{Package!unicode-data}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/unicode-data}
\item[name] \texttt{unicode-data}
\item[caption] Unicode data and loaders for TeX
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[author] Wright, Joseph
\index{Author!Wright, Joseph}
\item[copyright] The LaTeX3 Project (2015-2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.18 (2025-01-07)
\item[last changes] 2025-01-07
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This bundle provides generic access to Unicode Consortium data for TeX use. It contains a set of text 
          files provided by the Unicode Consortium which are currently all from Unicode 8.0.0, with the exception 
          of  \texttt{MathClass.txt} which is not currently part of the Unicode Character Database.

          Accompanying these source data are generic TeX loader files allowing this data to be used as part of 
          TeX runs, in particular in building format files. Currently there are two loader files: one for general 
          character set up and one for initialising XeTeX character classes as has been carried out to date by 
          \texttt{unicode-letters.tex} .

          The source data are distributed in accordance with the license stipulated by the Unicode Consortium. 
          The bundle as a whole is co-ordinated by the LaTeX3 Project as a general resource for TeX users.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/unicode-data/README.md}

\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a comprehensive implementation of unicode maths for XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX. Unicode 
          maths requires an OpenType mathematics font, of which there are now a number available via CTAN.

          While backwards compatibility is strived for, there are some differences between the legacy mathematical 
          definitions in LaTeX and  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath}{amsmath} , and the Unicode 
          mathematics definitions. Care should be taken when transitioning from a legacy workflow to a Unicode-based 
          one.

\section[\texttt{unifront} -- Give notes a unique front page for every chapter and section\ldots]{\texttt{unifront} -- Give notes a unique front page for every chapter and section}\label{pkg:unifront}
\index{Package!unifront}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/unifront}
\item[name] \texttt{unifront}
\item[caption] Give notes a unique front page for every chapter and section
\item[author] Wei, Weifan
\index{Author!Wei, Weifan}
\item[copyright] Weifan Wei (2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0 (2023-05-07)
\item[last changes] 2023-05-07
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package can help you format your notes easily and give them a unique front page for every chapter 
          and section.

          It calculates your progress and then displays the progress bar under the title.

          It also displays a partial table of contents under every progress bar and only shows the subdirectories 
          of the current part.

          To generate this, you can simply enter your current completed titles with a command that accepts Variable 
          Arguments. Still, that also helps you review your notes.

          You can also customise the colour of the bar.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/unifront/unifront-manual.pdf}

\item[author] निरंजन

\item[copyright] निरंजन (2022)
\item[license] fdl = Free Documentation License (free)

\index{License!gpl3+}

\item[version] 0.2 (2022-04-29)
\item[last changes] 2022-04-29
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) LaTeX produces small caps with  \verb|\textsc{text}| or \texttt{{\textbraceleft}{\textbackslash}scshape text{\textbraceright}} . Neither of these commands produce small caps in Unicode. If the output text is copied and pasted somewhere it shows the same characters as used in the input. This package aims to internally convert all the characters provided to the commands mentioned above. It assumes that the file using this package is compiled with Lua/XeLaTeX and a good Unicode font which has the small caps characters, e.g., \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/charissil}{Charis SIL} .

\item[version] 0.2
\item[description] (no language specified) Many packages for typesetting units have been written for use in LaTeX2e. Some define macros to typeset 
          a lot of units but do not suit to the actual font settings, some make the characters needed available 
          but do not predefine any unit. This package tries to comply with both requirements. It predefines common 
          units, defines an easy to use interface to define new units and changes the output concerning to the 
          surrounding font settings.

          Linguistics at the University of Vienna.

          particularly suited for the field of (Applied) Linguistics and pre-load some packages that are considered

\section[\texttt{upmendex} -- Multilingual index processor]{\texttt{upmendex} -- Multilingual index processor}\label{pkg:upmendex}
\index{Package!upmendex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/upmendex}
\item[name] \texttt{upmendex}
\item[caption] Multilingual index processor
\item[author] Tanaka, Takuji
\index{Author!Tanaka, Takuji}
\item[copyright] ASCII MEDIA WORKS (2009)
\item[copyright] TANAKA Takuji (2015-2026)
\item[copyright] ASCII Corporation (1995)
\item[license] bsd3 = 3-clause BSD License (free)
\index{License!bsd3}
\index{License!3-clause BSD License}
\item[version] 1.22 (2026-02-15)
\item[last changes] 2026-02-15
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package is a multilingual index processor with the following features:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Mostly compatible with makeindex and upper compatible with mendex.
          \item Supports UTF-8 and works with upLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX.
          \item Supports Latin (including non-English), Greek, Cyrillic, Korean Hangul and Chinese Han (Hanzi ideographs) scripts, as well as Japanese Kana.
          \item Supports four kinds of sort orders (Pinyin, Radical-Stroke, Stroke and Zhuyin) for Chinese Han scripts (Hanzi ideographs).
          \item Support Brahmic (Bengali, Devanagari, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Kannada, Lao, Malayalam, Oriya, Sinhala, Tamil, Telugu, Thai),  Arabic and Hebrew scripts (experimental).
          \item Applies International Components for Unicode (ICU) for sorting process.
          \end{itemize}

\section[\texttt{upquote} -- Show “realistic” quotes in verbatim]{\texttt{upquote} -- Show “realistic” quotes in verbatim}\label{pkg:upquote}
\index{Package!upquote}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/upquote}
\item[name] \texttt{upquote}
\item[caption] Show “realistic” quotes in verbatim
\item[author] Covington, Michael
\index{Author!Covington, Michael}
\item[author] Mittelbach, Frank
\index{Author!Mittelbach, Frank}
\item[author] Kuhn, Markus
\index{Author!Kuhn, Markus}
\item[copyright] Michael A. Covington, Frank Mittelbach (2003)
\item[license] lppl1.2 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.2}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.2}
\item[version] 1.3
\item[description] (no language specified) Typewriter-style fonts are best for program listings, but Computer Modern Typewriter prints  \texttt{'} and \texttt{'} as 
          bent opening and closing single quotes. Other fonts, and most programming languages, print \texttt{'} as 
          a grave accent and \texttt{'} upright; \texttt{'} is used both to open and to 
          close quoted strings.

          The package switches the typewriter font to Computer Modern Typewriter in  \texttt{OT1} encoding, 
          and modifies the behaviour of \texttt{verbatim} , \texttt{verbatim*} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}verb} , 
          and \texttt{{\textbackslash}verb*} to print in the '' \texttt{'} and \texttt{'} way''. 
          It does this regardless of other fonts or encodings in use, so long as the package is loaded after the 
          other fonts were.

          The package does not affect  \texttt{{\textbackslash}tt} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}texttt} , 
          etc.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/upquote/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/upquote/upquote.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./3863891164-upquote.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/upquote}
\item[on Mik\TeX] \texttt{upquote}

\item[description] (no language specified) upTeX is an extension of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ptex}{pTeX} , using UTF-8 input 
          and producing UTF-8 output. It was originally designed to improve support for Japanese, but is also useful 
          for documents in Chinese and Korean.

          It can process Chinese simplified, Chinese traditional, Japanese, and Korean simultaneously, and can 
          also process original LaTeX with  \texttt{{\textbackslash}inputenc{\textbraceleft}utf8{\textbraceright}} and 
          Babel (Latin/Cyrillic/Greek etc.) by switching its \texttt{{\textbackslash}kcatcode} tables.

\item[author] Arseneau, Donald
\index{Author!Arseneau, Donald}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 3.4 (2013-09-16)
\item[last changes] 2013-09-16
\item[year] 2013
\index{Year!2013}
\item[description] (no language specified) The command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}url} is a form of verbatim command that allows 
          linebreaks at certain characters or combinations of characters, accepts reconfiguration, and can usually 
          be used in the argument to another command. (The \texttt{{\textbackslash}urldef} command 
          provides robust commands that serve in cases when \texttt{{\textbackslash}url} doesn't 
          work in an argument.) The command is intended for email addresses, hypertext links, directories/paths, 
          etc., which normally have no spaces, so by default the package ignores spaces in its argument. However, 
          a package option ''allows spaces'', which is useful for operating systems where spaces are a common part 
          of file names.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/url/url.pdf}

\section[\texttt{user-persona} -- Typesetting User Persona sheets for UX and HCI (Human-Comput\ldots]{\texttt{user-persona} -- Typesetting User Persona sheets for UX and HCI (Human-Computer Interaction)}\label{pkg:user-persona}
\index{Package!user-persona}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/user-persona}
\item[name] \texttt{user-persona}
\item[caption] Typesetting User Persona sheets for UX and HCI (Human-Computer Interaction)
\item[author] Tam, Claire
\index{Author!Tam, Claire}
\item[copyright] fractuscontext (2026)
\item[copyright] Claire Tam (2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0.0
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a structured environment and command set for typesetting professional user persona 
          sheets in LaTeX. A user persona is a research-grounded representation of a target user group, synthesizing 
          observed behaviours, goals, and frustrations into a humanized archetype (Cooper, 1999).

          The package is intended for User Experience (UX) researchers, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) practitioners, 
          and product designers who maintain documentation within a LaTeX workflow.

          The central  \texttt{persona} environment produces a two-column layout comprising a portrait 
          image, an identity table, a pull-quote, and a set of colour-coded content cards. Cards may be placed 
          in the left column, right column, or as a full-width span below both columns. Predefined semantic colours 
          are supplied for common persona sections (Goals, Behaviours, Pain Points, Context). Inline pill labels 
          and icon badges are supported via \texttt{{\textbackslash}personapill} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}personabrand} (using \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontawesome5}{fontawesome5} ).
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Example of use (1)}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/user-persona/user-persona-example.pdf}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/user-persona/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Example of use (2)}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/user-persona/user-persona-detailed.pdf}

\item[description] (no language specified) Knuth's hyphenation patterns for English in American orthography (his hyphen.tex) appear here as ushyph1.tex; 
          these patterns will be installed for the default language in any conventional TeX distribution.

          In 1990, extended patterns for hyphenation of US English were published (TUGboat 11(1)). They appear 
          here as ushyphen.tex (the basic set) and ushyphmax.tex (a set that is believed to find all admissable 
          hyphenation points).

          in LaTeX. It is based on the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/listings}{listings} package and

\item[description] (no language specified) A slide format which produces slides with a simple Power Point like appearance. Several useful features 
          include: use of standard titlepage to produce title slide; several slide environments including plain 
          (page with a title), double slide (two column page with slide title), item slide (item list with title), 
          left item slide, and right item slide. Logos are placed in the upper left corner of each slide if the 
          logo file logo.eps is present. Preconfigured in landscape mode by default and uses Times Roman by default 
          (originally, it was claimed, for simple conversion to PDF format).

\section[\texttt{varioref} -- Intelligent page references]{\texttt{varioref} -- Intelligent page references}\label{pkg:varioref}
\index{Package!varioref}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/varioref}
\item[name] \texttt{varioref}
\item[caption] Intelligent page references
\item[author] Mittelbach, Frank
\index{Author!Mittelbach, Frank}
\item[copyright] Frank Mittelbach (1992-2020)
\item[copyright] The LaTeX3 Project et al. (1993-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.6g (2025-01-14)
\item[last changes] 2025-01-14
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package introduces commands  \texttt{{\textbackslash}vref} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}vpageref} . 
          The \texttt{{\textbackslash}vref} command refers to labels in the same way as does \texttt{{\textbackslash}ref} , 
          but if the thing referred to is on a different page, the result will be decorated with ''on the facing 
          page'' or ''on page \&lt;n\&gt;'', and so on, as appropriate. The \texttt{{\textbackslash}vpageref} command 
          similarly decorates a page number; there are also commands \texttt{{\textbackslash}vrefrange} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}vpagerefrange} for 
          ranges of labels.

          The package is language-sensitive, and has definitions for its ‘decorative’ words in several languages.

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools}{latex-tools} bundle 
          in the LaTeX \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/required}{required} distribution.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{The document itself}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/varioref.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./3045205370-varioref.pdf|

          breaking up the input lines into pieces of a given length, which are output as figures. These figures 
          are posted using the  \texttt{[H]} specification, which forces LaTeX to place the figure 
          at the spot of invocation, rather than floating the figures to the top of the next page.

          The package requires the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/verbatim}{verbatim} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/here}{here} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/vrbexin}{vrbexin} packages.

\item[last changes] 2023-08-08

\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides a  \texttt{verbbox} environment (which uses techniques similar to those 
          of the \texttt{boxedverbatim} environment of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/moreverb}{moreverb} package) 
          to place its contents into a globally available box, or into a box specified by the user.

          The global box may then be used in a variety of situations (for example, providing a replica of the  \texttt{boxedverbatim} environment 
          itself). A valuable use is in places where the standard \texttt{verbatim} environment (which 
          is based on a \texttt{trivlist} ) may not appear.

          The package makes use of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/verbatim}{verbatim} package 
          (which is a required part of any LaTeX distribution).

\section[\texttt{verifycommand} -- Verifies definitions are unchanged, such as before patching]{\texttt{verifycommand} -- Verifies definitions are unchanged, such as before patching}\label{pkg:verifycommand}
\index{Package!verifycommand}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/verifycommand}
\item[name] \texttt{verifycommand}
\item[caption] Verifies definitions are unchanged, such as before patching
\item[author] Dunn, Brian
\index{Author!Dunn, Brian}
\item[copyright] Brian Dunn (2024-2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.11 (2025-03-07)
\item[last changes] 2025-03-07
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package is intended for package authors who patch code from other packages.

          To improve reliability, the  \texttt{verifycommand} package provides a way to verify that 
          macros or environments have not changed. This allows a package author to check before patching a definition. 
          If a definition is not as expected, a warning is issued. At the end of the compile, a list of all changed

\item[description] (no language specified) The vita class provides necessary macros to prepare your Curriculum Vitae or Resume. The class may be

\section[\texttt{vocaltract} -- Visualise the vocal tract using LaTeX and PSTricks]{\texttt{vocaltract} -- Visualise the vocal tract using LaTeX and PSTricks}\label{pkg:vocaltract}
\index{Package!vocaltract}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/vocaltract}
\item[name] \texttt{vocaltract}
\item[caption] Visualise the vocal tract using LaTeX and PSTricks
\item[author] Ververidis, Dimitrios
\index{Author!Ververidis, Dimitrios}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1
\item[description] (no language specified) The package enables the user to visualise the vocal tract. The vocal tract (in the package) is manipulated 
          by a vector of articulation parameters according to the  \emph{S. Maeda} model. Animation 
          may be achieved by providing a sequence of vectors over time (e.g., from Matlab). A sequence of vectors 
          for certain German phonemes is embedded in the package, which allows for animation when no other vector 
          is available.

          The package’s graphics are produced using  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pstricks-base}{pstricks} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Example model}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pstricks/contrib/vocaltract/vtLatex_FigureDemo.pdf}

\item[author] Oberdiek, Heiko

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.2
\item[description] (no language specified) VPE is a system to make the equivalent of ''source special'' marks in a PDF file. Clicking on a mark 
          will activate an editor, pointing at the source line that produced the text that was marked.

          The system comprises a perl file (vpe.pl) and a LaTeX package (vpe.sty); it will work with PDF files 
          generated via LaTeX/dvips, pdfTeX (version 0.14 or better), and LaTeX/VTeX. Using the LaTeX/dvips or 
          pdfLaTeX routes, the (pdf)TeX processor should be run with shell escapes enabled.

\item[description] (no language specified) The LaTeX 2.09-based program SliTeX, and the corresponding LaTeX  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/slides}{slides} class, 
          use invisible fonts when producing multi-coloured overlays on foils. SliTeX distributions included a 
          set of invisible versions of the Metafont sources of the Computer Modern fonts (an odd concept, but it 
          worked). The present bundle provides a (somewhat more intellectually satisfying) set of virtual fonts 
          that provide the same information (i.e., effectively metrics only) without the need to compile a Metafont 
          source to get it.

\item[description] (no language specified) A set of font installation packs for commercial fonts (none of which is itself available from CTAN: the 
          user must acquire them from the commercial supplier).

          Fonts supported are:\\Adobe Garamond, Aldus, Futura, Stempel Garamond, Frutiger, Melior, Minion, 
          Myriad, Optima, Rotis, Sabon and Syntax;\\Berthold ConcordeBE and BaskervilleBQ;\\Bitstream Humanist 
          777 (Frutiger), Letter Gothic, Latin 725 (Meridien), News Gothic, Dutch 809 (Concorde), Zapf Humanist 
          601 (Optima), Zurich (Univers) and Venetian 301 (Centaur);\\FontFont Dingbests, InterOffice and QType 
          Extended Book;\\Lintoype Adobe Garamond LT, Aldus LT, ITC Charter, Frutiger Next, Futura LT, Stempel 
          Garamond LT, Meridien LT, Melior LT, Minion, Myriad, ITC Officina Sans, Optima Nova, Sabon LT, Syntax 
          LT, ITC Zapf Chancery LT, Zapf Essentials LT and Zapfino One plus Ornaments;\\Monotype TimesNR, NR 
          Seven, Small Text;\\Springer SMinion and SMyriad; and\\Underware Dolly.

          For each font(set) there’s a  \texttt{.zip} file of metrics, and a \texttt{.txt} file 
          of instructions. In some cases there's also a \texttt{-source.zip} file of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/fontinst}{fontinst} sources 
          for the family.

\index{Package!wargame}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/wargame}
\item[name] \texttt{wargame}
\item[caption] A LaTeX package to prepare hex’n’counter wargames
\item[author] Holm Christensen, Christian
\index{Author!Holm Christensen, Christian}
\item[copyright] Christian Holm Christensen (2022-2024)
\item[license] cc-by-sa-4 = CC BY-SA 4.0 (free)
\index{License!cc-by-sa-4}
