\item[version] 0.8 (2024-11-19)
\item[last changes] 2024-11-19
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package can help make classic Hex’n’Counter wargames using LaTeX. The package provides tools for 
          generating

          \begin{itemize}
          \item Hex maps and boards
          \item Counters for units, markers, and so on
          \item Counter sheets
          \item Order of Battle charts
          \item Illustrations in the rules using the defined maps and counters
          \end{itemize}
The result will often be a PDF (or set of PDFs) that contains everything one will need for a game (rules, 
          charts, boards, counter sheets).

          \begin{itemize}
          \item The package uses NATO App6 symbology for units.
          \item The package uses NATO App6 symbology for units.
          \item The package uses TikZ for most things.
          \item The package supports exporting the game to a VASSAL module
          \end{itemize}
See also the README.md file for more, and of course the documentation (including the tutorial in tutorial/game.pdf).

          macros are provided to enable variations on this column type to be defined. Usage of the package is superficially 
          similar to that of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dcolumn}{dcolumn} ; however, the alignment 
          scheme is different, and the packages have different, though overlapping, applications.

\section[\texttt{web2w} -- Converting TeX from WEB to cweb]{\texttt{web2w} -- Converting TeX from WEB to cweb}\label{pkg:web2w}
\index{Package!web2w}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/web2w}
\item[name] \texttt{web2w}
\item[caption] Converting TeX from WEB to cweb
\item[author] Ruckert, Martin
\index{Author!Ruckert, Martin}
\item[copyright] Martin Ruckert (2017)
\item[license] gpl3+ = GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer (free)
\index{License!gpl3+}
\index{License!GNU General Public License, version 3 or newer}
\item[version] 0.4
\item[description] (no language specified) This package contains a project to convert the TeX source code written by Donald E. Knuth as a WEB into 
          a cweb.

          A WEB is a literate program, i.e. a program which is written as a form of literature and consequently 
          published as a book. Of course there is a way of converting such a piece of literature into an ordinary 
          program: it contains Pascal code. \\Over the years, the support for Pascal as a major programming 
          language has decreased and Pascal was replaced by C as the system programming language of choice. Consequently, 
          WEB was replaced by cweb, leading to the obvious question: can we convert the TeX source code to cweb. 
          And the answer is: yes and no.

          No, because TeX is rather a large program, so translating it manually is very expensive, and translating 
          literature by means of an automatic process is not feasible either.

          Yes, because the program contained in this project, a literate program itself, is specifically tailored 
          to the TeX source code and achieves a good approximation to such a translation.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/web/web2w/web2w.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./3218072415-web2w.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/web/web2w/README}
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/web/web2w}
\item[keyword] \texttt{litprog} (literate programming)
\index{Topic!litprog}
\item[language(s)] no language specified
\index{Language in description/documentation!no language specified}
\item[year] 2017
\index{Year!2017}
\item[last access] 2025-02-07
\end{labeling}

\item[last changes] 2021-11-21
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides a way of associating counters to an existing driver counter so that incrementing 
          the driver counter will increase its associated counters as well.

          This package can be regarded as a supplement to the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/totcount}{totcount} package 
          by Vasileios Koutavas, but it can be used without it, too.

          \texttt{xassoccnt} is a successor and a complete rewrite of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/assoccnt}{assoccnt} package 
          by the same author. However, as of 2017-03-05, some features of \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/assoccnt}{assoccnt} are 
          not (yet) contained in \texttt{xassoccnt} so that the older package cannot yet be regarded 
          as obsolete.

\item[year] 2020
\index{Year!2020}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package defines the concept of a document bundle, which is a collection of documents that are to 
          be built separately, but have a common bookmark tree.

          The only options are driver options, these are dvips (Acrobat Distiller or ps2pdf these can be used as 
          the PDF creator), pdfLaTeX (and LuaLaTeX, which is treated the same as pdfLaTeX), and XeLaTeX.

          The package auto-detects pdfLaTeX and XeLaTeX, and dvips is the default, so there is actually no need 
          to pass the driver option.

\section[\texttt{xcoffins} -- Rich boxed material for LaTeX 3]{\texttt{xcoffins} -- Rich boxed material for LaTeX 3}\label{pkg:xcoffins}
\index{Package!xcoffins}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xcoffins}
\item[name] \texttt{xcoffins}
\item[caption] Rich boxed material for LaTeX 3
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[copyright] LaTeX3 Project (2010-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version]  (2024-03-14)
\item[last changes] 2024-03-14
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) Coffins are boxes which contain typeset material. Along with the box itself, the coffin structure holds 
          information about the size and shape of the box, and alignment information in the form of a set of ''poles'' 
          (horizontal and vertical lines at particular positions defined relative to the box). The points where 
          these poles intersect are ''handles'', which are the points used to define the placing of a coffin.

          The package provides a design-level interface to the LaTeX 3 kernel functions which provide coffins.

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/l3experimental}{l3experimental} bundle.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Bundle readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/l3experimental/README.md}

          and provides easy driver-independent access to several kinds of color tints, shades, tones, and mixes 
          of arbitrary colors. It allows a user to select a document-wide target color model and offers complete 
          tools for conversion between eight color models. Additionally, there is a command for alternating row 
          colors plus repeated non-aligned material (like horizontal lines) in tables. Colors can be mixed like

\item[author] Voß, Herbert
\index{Author!Voß, Herbert}

\item[version] 1.40 (2024-11-03)
\item[last changes] 2024-11-03
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package defines an environment that  \emph{only} typesets specified environments within 
          its scope.

          So, for example, if you want nothing but the  \texttt{figure} and \texttt{table} environments 
          in your document, you can enclose the whole document with an \texttt{xcomment} environment 
          that excludes everything but. This is a lot easier than excluding the chunks of text between the environments 
          you want, or creating an entire document containing only those environments.

          The package was previously part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/seminar}{seminar} bundle 
          for typesetting presentations.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xcomment/README}

\section[\texttt{xdoc} -- Extending the LaTeX doc system]{\texttt{xdoc} -- Extending the LaTeX doc system}\label{pkg:xdoc}
\index{Package!xdoc}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xdoc}
\item[name] \texttt{xdoc}
\item[caption] Extending the LaTeX doc system
\item[author] Hellström, Lars
\index{Author!Hellström, Lars}
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] prot2.5
\item[description] (no language specified) Xdoc is a project to rewrite the implementation of the LaTeX doc package (in a broader sense) to make 
          its features more general and flexible. For example, where doc only provides commands for documenting 
          macros and environments, xdoc also provides commands for similarly documenting package options and switches. 
          This is furthermore done in such a way that it is very easy to add more such commands for documenting 
          things, such as e.g., templates (an important concept in the future LaTeX3) and program components for 
          other languages (functions, classes, procedures, etc.). A side effect is that many minor bugs in doc 
          are fixed.

          The design aims to take advantage of many still experimental features of future versions of LaTeX, but 
          since these are neither reasonably stable nor widely available, the configuration interfaces and package 
          author commands of xdoc are likely to change. To still provide a stable interface for other packages 
          to build upon, the actual package names include a "major version number" of sorts. The drop-in replacement 
          package for standard doc is xdoc2; it requires nothing outside standard LaTeX2e.

          The  \texttt{docindex} / \texttt{docidx2e} package changes the index and list 
          of changes typesetting so that none of the formatting has to be controlled via the index style file. 
          The docindex package provides control of formatting via templates (nice interface, but requires several 
          experimental packages), whereas the docidx2e package has traditional raw macro interfaces and works with 
          standard LaTeX2e.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Demonstration of usage}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xdoc/xdocdemo.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./4532148316-xdocdemo.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{docindex documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xdoc/docindex.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./9685732465-docindex.pdf|
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xdoc/README}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{xdoc2 documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xdoc/xdoc2.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./8868216404-xdoc2.pdf|
\item[on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xdoc}

\item[author] Tolušis, Sigitas

\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0 (2026-02-11)
\item[last changes] 2026-02-11
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This LaTeX package bundle offers support for  \texttt{xdvipsk} , an extension of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/dvips}{dvips} binary.

          \texttt{xdvipsk} supports BMP, PCX, TIFF, JPEG, and PNG formats and performs scaling, rotating, 
          trim, and viewport operations like EPS images. The \texttt{xdvispk.def} driver for the graphics 
          package offers a LaTeX interface. However, it lacks clipping, trimming, and viewport operations.

          The LuaLaTeX package  \texttt{xdvipskmaps} provides OpenType font support for \texttt{xdvipsk} . 
          It generates map files containing information about OpenType fonts used in DVI files.

\item[author] Robbers, Yuri
\index{Author!Robbers, Yuri}
\item[author] Isambert, Paul

\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)

\item[last changes] 2019-04-24
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package finds strings (e.g. (parts of) words or phrases) and manipulates them (apply any macro), 
          thus turning each word or phrase into a possible command.

          It is written in plain XeTeX and should thus work with any format (it is known to work with LaTeX and 
          ConTeXt).

          The main application for the moment is XeIndex, an automatic index for XeLaTeX, but examples are given 
          of simple use to check spelling, count words, and highlight syntax of programming languages.

\section[\texttt{xetex} -- An extended variant of TeX for use with Unicode sources]{\texttt{xetex} -- An extended variant of TeX for use with Unicode sources}\label{pkg:xetex}
\index{Package!xetex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xetex}
\item[name] \texttt{xetex}
\item[caption] An extended variant of TeX for use with Unicode sources
\item[author] Hosny, Khaled
\index{Author!Hosny, Khaled}
\item[author] Kew, Jonathan
\index{Author!Kew, Jonathan}
\item[author] The TeX Live Team
\index{Author!The TeX Live Team}
\item[author] Rosendahl, Arthur
\index{Author!Rosendahl, Arthur}
\item[license] x11 = X11 License (free)
\index{License!x11}
\index{License!X11 License}
\item[description] (no language specified) XeTeX is a TeX typesetting engine using Unicode and supporting modern font technologies such as OpenType, 
          TrueType or Apple Advanced Typography (AAT), including OpenType mathematics fonts. XeTeX supports many 
          extensions that reflect its origins in linguistic research; it also supports micro-typography (as available 
          in pdfTeX). XeTeX was developed by the  \href{https://scripts.sil.org/xetex}{SIL} (the 
          first version was specifically developed for those studying linguistics, and using Macintosh computers).

          XeTeX’s immediate output is an extended variant of DVI format, which is ordinarily processed by a tightly 
          bound processor (called  \texttt{xdvipdfmx} ), that produces PDF.

          XeTeX is released as part of TeX Live; documentation has arisen separately. Source code is available 
          from  \href{https://mirror.ctan.org/systems/texlive/Source/}{ctan:/systems/texlive/Source/} .

          are:

          \begin{itemize}

\section[\texttt{xevlna} -- Insert non-breakable spaces using XeTeX]{\texttt{xevlna} -- Insert non-breakable spaces using XeTeX}\label{pkg:xevlna}
\index{Package!xevlna}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xevlna}
\item[name] \texttt{xevlna}
\item[caption] Insert non-breakable spaces using XeTeX
\item[author] Wagner, Zdeněk
\index{Author!Wagner, Zdeněk}
\item[license] lppl1.3 = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3 (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 1.1 (2017-03-25)
\item[last changes] 2017-03-25
\item[year] 2017
\index{Year!2017}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package will directly insert nonbreakable spaces (in Czech, vlna or vlnka), after nonsyllabic prepositions 
          and single letter conjuctions, while the document is being typeset. (The macros recognised maths and 
          verbatim by TeX means.)

          (Inserting nonbreakable spaces by a preprocessor will probably never be fully reliable, because user 
          defined macros and environments cannot reliably be recognised.)

\section[\texttt{xfp} -- Interface to the LaTeX3 floating point unit]{\texttt{xfp} -- Interface to the LaTeX3 floating point unit}\label{pkg:xfp}
\index{Package!xfp}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xfp}
\item[name] \texttt{xfp}
\item[caption] Interface to the LaTeX3 floating point unit
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[copyright] The LaTeX3 Project (2017-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version]  (2024-08-16)
\item[last changes] 2024-08-16
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package is deprecated in favor of methods integrated into the LaTeX kernel from 2022-06-01.

          This package provides a LaTeX2e document-level interface to the LaTeX3 floating point unit (part of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/expl3}{expl3} ).

          The expandable command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}fpeval} takes as its argument a floating 
          point expression and will produce a result using the normal rules of mathematics. As this command is 
          expandable it can be used where TeX requires a number and for example within a low-level \texttt{{\textbackslash}edef} operation 
          to give a purely numerical result.

          From 2022-06-01 release of LaTeX this will be included in the format so that the package doesn't need 
          loading any longer.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme for the whole bundle}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/l3packages/README.md}

\item[version] 3.5.0 (2025-01-28)
\item[last changes] 2025-01-28
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package has been designed so to allow people to typeset Greek language documents using XeLaTeX or 
          LuaLaTeX. It is released in the hope that people will use it and spot errors, bugs, features so to improve 
          it. Practically, it provides all the capabilities of the greek option of the babel package. The package 
          can be invoked with any of the following options:  \texttt{monotonic} (for typesetting modern 
          monotonic Greek), \texttt{polytonic} (for typesetting modern polytonic Greek), and \texttt{ancient} (for 
          typesetting ancient texts). The default option is \texttt{monotonic} .

          The command  \texttt{{\textbackslash}setlanguage{\textbraceleft}<lang>{\textbraceright}} activates 
          the hyphenation patterns of the language \texttt{<lang>} . This, however, can only be done 
          if the format file has not been built with the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/babel}{babel} mechanism.

\section[\texttt{xint} -- Expandable arbitrary precision floating point and integer op\ldots]{\texttt{xint} -- Expandable arbitrary precision floating point and integer operations}\label{pkg:xint}
\index{Package!xint}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xint}
\item[Alias] \texttt{xintexpr}
\index{Package!xintexpr (alias for xint)}
\index{Alias!xintexpr (for xint)}
\item[name] \texttt{xint}
\item[caption] Expandable arbitrary precision floating point and integer operations
\item[author] Burnol, Jean-François
\index{Author!Burnol, Jean-François}
\item[copyright] Jean-François Burnol (2013-2022, 2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.4o (2025-09-06)
\item[last changes] 2025-09-06
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) Loading  \texttt{xintexpr} provides \texttt{{\textbackslash}xinteval} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}xintfloateval} .

          \texttt{{\textbackslash}xintfloateval} evaluates numerical expressions. The floating 
          point precision defaults to 16 decimal digits and can be set by user. Trigonometry, exponential and logarithms 
          are implemented up to a maximal precision of 62 decimal digits.

          \texttt{{\textbackslash}xinteval} computes exactly with integers, fractions, and decimal 
          numbers or numbers in scientific notation. Note though that multiplying two floating point numbers will 
          about double the number of digits, and so on, because the algebra is done exactly.

          Both are compatible with expansion-only context.

          Loading  \texttt{xintexpr} imports automatically various other modules that it depends upon. 
          Among them:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{xinttools} : utilities such as expandable and non-expandable loops,
          \item  \texttt{xint} : macros implementing in particular the basic operations on arbitrarily long integers,
          \item  \texttt{xintbinhex} : conversions between decimal and binary, octal, or hexadecimal bases for arbitrarily long integers,
          \item  \texttt{xintfrac} : macros implementing in particular the basic operations on arbitrarily large fractions, decimal numbers, or numbers in scientific notation.
          \end{itemize}
Further modules of independent interest include  \texttt{xintgcd} , \texttt{xintseries} and \texttt{xintcfrac} .

          You can use  \texttt{xintexpr} (and the other components) with LaTeX (via \texttt{{\textbackslash}usepackage} ) 
          or also with Plain TeX, OpTeX, or ConTeXt (via \texttt{{\textbackslash}input xintexpr.sty} ).

          All the components are documented in the file  \texttt{xint.pdf} , which also contains the 
          commented source code.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/xint/xint.pdf}

\item[author] Burnol, Jean-François
\index{Author!Burnol, Jean-François}
\item[copyright] Jean-François Burnol (2021)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)

\item[version] 0.4alpha (2021-11-01)
\item[last changes] 2021-11-01
\item[year] 2021
\index{Year!2021}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides support for interactive computing sessions with  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etex}{etex} (or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/pdftex}{pdftex} ) 
          executed on the command line, on the basis of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xint}{xintexpr} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/polexpr}{polexpr} packages.

          Once xintsession is loaded,  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/etex}{eTeX} becomes an interactive 
          computing software capable of executing arbitrary precision calculations, or exact calculations with 
          arbitrarily big fractions. It can also manipulate polynomials as algebraic entities.

          Numerical variables and functions can be defined during the session, and each evaluation result is stored 
          in automatically labeled variables. A file is automatically created storing inputs and outputs.

\item[description] (no language specified) In the year 2010, Randall Munroe on  \href{https://blog.xkcd.com/2010/05/03/color-survey-results/}{posted 
          a really funny and nice article} on \href{https://xkcd.com/}{xkcd} . He made a very 
          curious experiment: showing colors to a lot of people and asking to name each one.

          Afterward, he processed the data and sorted the names for each color by popularity — that means, how 
          many people gave the same name to the same color.

          This package makes the collected color names usable with LaTeX.

\item[description] (no language specified) Xlop (eXtra Large OPeration) will typeset arithmetic problems either in-line or ''as in school'' (using 
          French school conventions). So for example,  \texttt{{\textbackslash}opadd{\textbraceleft}2{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}3{\textbraceright}} can 
          give either \texttt{\$2+3=5\$} or something similar to: \texttt{{\textbackslash}begin{\textbraceleft}tabular{\textbraceright}{\textbraceleft}r{\textbraceright} 
          2{\textbackslash}{\textbackslash} +3{\textbackslash}{\textbackslash} {\textbackslash}hline 
          5{\textbackslash}end{\textbraceleft}tabular{\textbraceright}} .

          Furthermore, numbers may be very large, e.g 200 figures (with a very long compilation time). Many other 
          features allow to deal with numbers (tests, display, some high level operations, etc.)

\item[description] (no language specified) The XMP (eXtensible Metadata platform) is a framework to add metadata to digital material to enhance 
          the workflow in publication. The essence is that the metadata is stored in an XML file, and this XML 
          stream is then embedded in the file to which it applies. How you create this XML file is up to you, but 
          the author started investigating this because he wanted to embed licensing information in the files he 
          created. The license the author chose is one of the Creative Commons licenses, and their web-site offers 
          this information in a valid XML-file, suitable for direct inclusion.

\section[\texttt{xpunctuate} -- Process trailing punctuation which may be redundant]{\texttt{xpunctuate} -- Process trailing punctuation which may be redundant}\label{pkg:xpunctuate}
\index{Package!xpunctuate}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xpunctuate}
\item[name] \texttt{xpunctuate}
\item[caption] Process trailing punctuation which may be redundant
\item[author] Ratcliffe, Philip G.
\index{Author!Ratcliffe, Philip G.}
\item[copyright] Philip G. Ratcliffe (2012-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 2.0 (2023-08-13)
\item[last changes] 2023-08-13
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package provides commands enabling the user (or package writer) to insert punctuation after a macro. 
          The method is similar to that of  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xspace}{xspace} , but goes 
          further.

          The package provides the commands  \texttt{{\textbackslash}xperiod} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}xcomma} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}xperiodcomma} , 
          which follow a similar procedure to that of \texttt{{\textbackslash}xspace} , and insert 
          punctuation \emph{if and only if} it is necessary.

          It also provides  \texttt{{\textbackslash}xperiodafter} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}xcommaafter} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}xperiodcommaafter} and \texttt{{\textbackslash}xspaceafter} , 
          which all take one argument, the word or phrase to be punctuated. These then avoid problems with the 
          spacing of periods and commas after emphasised words.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xpunctuate/xpunctuate-doc.pdf}

\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xpunctuate/README.md}

\section[\texttt{xsavebox} -- Saveboxes for repeating content without code replication, ba\ldots]{\texttt{xsavebox} -- Saveboxes for repeating content without code replication, based on PDF Form XObjects}\label{pkg:xsavebox}
\index{Package!xsavebox}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xsavebox}
\item[name] \texttt{xsavebox}
\item[caption] Saveboxes for repeating content without code replication, based on PDF Form XObjects
\item[author] Grahn, Alexander
\index{Author!Grahn, Alexander}
\item[copyright] Alexander Grahn (2016-2022)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 0.18 (2022-08-04)
\item[last changes] 2022-08-04
\item[year] 2022
\index{Year!2022}
\item[description] (no language specified) The package defines commands for saving content that can be repeatedly placed into the document without 
          replicating DVI/PDF code in the output file, allowing for smaller file size of the final PDF and improved 
          content caching for faster display in certain PDF viewers. The method makes use of ‘Form XObjects’ defined 
          in the PDF specification.

          The user commands are modelled after the standard LaTeX commands  \texttt{{\textbackslash}savebox} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}sbox} , \texttt{{\textbackslash}usebox} and 
          the \texttt{lrbox} environment.

          All common TeX engines and back-ends are supported:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item pdfLaTeX, LuaLaTeX
          \item LaTeX → dvips → ps2pdf/Distiller
          \item (Xe)LaTeX → (x)dvipdfmx
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xsavebox/README.md}

\section[\texttt{xsipa} -- Short XSAMPA-based commands for IPA transcription in LaTeX]{\texttt{xsipa} -- Short XSAMPA-based commands for IPA transcription in LaTeX}\label{pkg:xsipa}
\index{Package!xsipa}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xsipa}
\item[name] \texttt{xsipa}
\item[caption] Short XSAMPA-based commands for IPA transcription in LaTeX
\item[author] Akpoué, Kouamé Josué
\index{Author!Akpoué, Kouamé Josué}
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0 (2025-05-16)
\item[last changes] 2025-05-16
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This LaTeX package provides a lightweight phonetic transcription system inspired by XSAMPA. It translates 
          modified XSAMPA sequences into proper IPA symbols, using either the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/tipa}{tipa} package 
          (for pdfTeX users) or Unicode IPA symbols via \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xunicode}{xunicode} (for 
          XeTeX and LuaTeX users).

          The package was designed to simplify phonetic transcription in LaTeX by offering concise macros such 
          as  \texttt{{\textbackslash}xsE} for \texttt{{\textbackslash}textepsilon} , 
          and \texttt{{\textbackslash}xs*...*} as a shortcut for multi-symbol sequences (e.g., \texttt{{\textbackslash}xs*EO*} for \texttt{ɛɔ} ). 
          These commands are modeled after XSAMPA but adapted for LaTeX compatibility — including custom replacements 
          for reserved characters.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/xsipa/README.md}

\section[\texttt{xspace} -- Define commands that appear not to eat spaces]{\texttt{xspace} -- Define commands that appear not to eat spaces}\label{pkg:xspace}
\index{Package!xspace}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xspace}
\item[name] \texttt{xspace}
\item[caption] Define commands that appear not to eat spaces
\item[author] Carlisle, David
\index{Author!Carlisle, David}
\item[author] Høgholm, Morten
\index{Author!Høgholm, Morten}
\item[author] The LaTeX Project Team
\index{Author!The LaTeX Project Team}
\item[copyright] David Carlisle, Morten Høgholm (2004-2006)
\item[copyright] The LaTeX3 Project et al. (1993-2023)
\item[copyright] David Carlisle (1991-1997)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.13 (2014-10-28)
\item[last changes] 2014-10-28
\item[year] 2014
\index{Year!2014}
\item[description] (no language specified) The xspace package provides a single command that looks at what comes after it in the command stream, 
          and decides whether to insert a space to replace one ''eaten'' by the TeX command decoder. The decision 
          is based on what came after any space, not on whether there was a space (which is unknowable): so if 
          the next thing proves to be punctuation, the chances are there was no space, but if it’s a letter, there’s 
          probably a need for space. This technique is not perfect, but works in a large proportion of cases.

          The package is part of the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-tools}{latex-tools} bundle 
          in the LaTeX \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/required}{required} distribution.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/required/tools/xspace.pdf}

\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/xyling}
\item[name] \texttt{xyling}
\item[caption] Draw syntactic trees, etc., for linguistics literature, using xy-pic
\item[author] Vogel, Ralf
\index{Author!Vogel, Ralf}
\item[copyright] Ralf Vogel (2006)
\item[license] lppl = The LaTeX Project Public License (free)
\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.1
\item[description] (no language specified) The macros in this package model the construction of linguistic tree structures as a genuinely graphical 
          problem: they contain two types of objects,  \emph{BRANCHES} and \emph{NODE LABELS} , 
          and these are positioned relative to a \emph{GRID} . It is essential that each of these three 
          elements is constructed independent of the other two, and hence they can be modified without unwanted 
          side effects. The macros are based on the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xypic}{xy-pic} package.

\item[author] Fujita, Shinsaku
\index{Author!Fujita, Shinsaku}

\index{License!lppl1.3}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3}
\item[version] 5.06
\item[description] (no language specified) XyMTeX is a set of packages for drawing a wide variety of chemical structural formulas in a way that 
          reflects their structure. The package provides three output modes: ‘LaTeX’, ‘PostScript’ and ‘PDF’.

          XyMTeX’s commands have a systematic set of arguments for specifying substituents and their positions, 
          endocyclic double bonds, and bond patterns. In some cases there are additional arguments for specifying 
          hetero-atoms on the vertices of heterocycles. It is believed that this systematic design allows XyMTeX 
          to operate as a practical (device-independent) tool for use with LaTeX.

\section[\texttt{yathesis} -- A LaTeX class for writing a thesis following French rules]{\texttt{yathesis} -- A LaTeX class for writing a thesis following French rules}\label{pkg:yathesis}
\index{Package!yathesis}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/yathesis}
\item[name] \texttt{yathesis}
\item[caption] A LaTeX class for writing a thesis following French rules
\item[author] Bitouzé, Denis
\index{Author!Bitouzé, Denis}
\item[copyright] Denis Bitouzé (2012-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 1.0.12 (2024-03-07)
\item[last changes] 2024-03-07
\item[year] 2024
\index{Year!2024}
\item[description] (no language specified) The purpose of  \texttt{yathesis} is to facilitate the typesetting of theses prepared in 
          France, whatever the disciplines and institutes. It implements most notably recommendations from the 
          Ministry of Higher Education and Research, and this transparently to the user. It has also been designed 
          to (optionally) take advantage of powerful tools available in LaTeX, including packages:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/biblatex}{BibLaTeX} for the bibliography;
          \item  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/glossaries}{glossaries} for the glossary, list of acronyms and symbols list.
          \end{itemize}
The  \verb|yathesis| class, based on the book class, aims to be both simple to use and, to some extent, (easily) customizable.

          \verb|yathesis| comes with templates and samples in the \verb|doc/latex/yathesis/french/exemples/| directory in the distribution. They can also be tested on ShareLaTeX ( \href{https://fr.sharelatex.com/templates/thesis/yathesis-template}{template} and \href{https://fr.sharelatex.com/templates/thesis/yathesis-specimen}{specimen} ) and on Overleaf ( \href{https://www.overleaf.com/latex/templates/template-of-a-thesis-written-with-yathesis-class/nhtmtthnqwtd}{template} and \href{https://www.overleaf.com/latex/examples/sample-of-a-thesis-written-with-yathesis-class/nbcfvfqgnjfq}{specimen} ).

          Note: The '' \texttt{ya} '' in the package name stands for ''yet another''.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/yathesis/README.md}

\index{License!lppl}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License}
\item[version] 1.03
\item[description] (no language specified) YaX is advertised as a key system, but it rather organizes attributes in parameters, which parameters 
          can be executed, so that YaX is halfway between key management and macro definition (and actually hopes 
          to provide a user’s interface).

          Values assigned to attributes can be retrieved and tested in various ways, with full expandability ensured 
          as much as possible.

          Finally, YaX’s syntax is a quite peculiar (as few braces as possible), but may be customized.

          YaX is based on  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/texapi}{texapi} and thus requires e-TeX.

          unfinished) alternative to the  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/ltxdoc}{ltxdoc} class and 
          the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/doc}{doc} or \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xdoc}{xdoc} packages. 
          The aim is to provide a different layout and more modern styles (using the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xcolor}{xcolor} , \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/hyperref}{hyperref} packages, 
          etc.)

          might change. Nevertheless, the author uses it to document his own packages.

\section[\texttt{yquant} -- Typesetting quantum circuits in a human-readable language]{\texttt{yquant} -- Typesetting quantum circuits in a human-readable language}\label{pkg:yquant}
\index{Package!yquant}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/yquant}
\item[name] \texttt{yquant}
\item[caption] Typesetting quantum circuits in a human-readable language
\item[author] Desef, Benjamin
\index{Author!Desef, Benjamin}
\item[copyright] Benjamin Desef (2019-2023)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.7.5 (2023-11-26)
\item[last changes] 2023-11-26
\item[year] 2023
\index{Year!2023}
\item[description] (no language specified) This LaTeX package allows to quickly draw quantum circuits.

          It bridges the gap between the two groups of packages that already exist: those that use a logic-oriented 
          custom language, which is then translated into TeX by means of an external program; and the pure TeX 
          versions that mainly provide some macros to allow for an easier input.

          yquant is a pure-LaTeX solution — i.e., it requires no external program — that introduces a logic oriented 
          language and thus brings the best of both worlds together. It builds on and interacts with TikZ, which 
          brings an enourmous flexibility for customization of individual circuit.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/yquant/README.md}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/graphics/pgf/contrib/yquant/doc/yquant-doc.pdf}

\index{Contact!bugs}

\section[\texttt{zeckendorf} -- Knuth Fibonacci multiplication, Zeckendorf and Bergman repre\ldots]{\texttt{zeckendorf} -- Knuth Fibonacci multiplication, Zeckendorf and Bergman representations of big integers}\label{pkg:zeckendorf}
\index{Package!zeckendorf}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/zeckendorf}
\item[name] \texttt{zeckendorf}
\item[caption] Knuth Fibonacci multiplication, Zeckendorf and Bergman representations of big integers
\item[author] Burnol, Jean-François
\index{Author!Burnol, Jean-François}
\item[copyright] Jean-François Burnol (2025)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.9d (2025-11-16)
\item[last changes] 2025-11-16
\item[year] 2025
\index{Year!2025}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package extends the  \texttt{{\textbackslash}xinteval} syntax to do algebra in 
          Q(phi) (where phi is the golden ratio), and compute Fibonacci numbers, Zeckendorf representations of 
          positive integers and Bergman phi-representations of the positive elements of Z[phi]. The \texttt{\$} character 
          is used to compute the Knuth Fibonacci multiplication.

          The package can be used either in a LaTeX document, or with Plain eTeX, or on the command line in an 
          interactive session using eTeX.

          Being based upon  \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xint}{xintexpr} , it allows to compute with 
          ''arbitrarily'' big integers, the reasonable use being with integers of at most a few hundreds of digits.
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/generic/zeckendorf/zeckendorf-doc.pdf}

\item[caption] Line spacing for CJK documents
\item[author] Zhang, Ruixi
\index{Author!Zhang, Ruixi}

\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}

\item[version] 1.0e (2019-05-15)
\item[last changes] 2019-05-15
\item[year] 2019
\index{Year!2019}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package supports typesetting CJK documents. It allows users to specify the two ratios between the 
          leading and the font size of the body text and the footnote text. For CJK typesetting, these ratios usually 
          range from 1.5 to 1.67. This package is also capable of restoring the math leading to that of the Latin 
          text (usually 1.2 times the font size). Finally, it is possible to achieve the  \emph{Microsoft 
          Word multiple line spacing} style using \texttt{zhlineskip} .
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Readme}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/language/chinese/zhlineskip/README.md}

          fact at all CJK fonts share the same metrics; it provides macros that create the NFSS font definition 
          and actual font mappings dynamically.

          TrueType CJK fonts may be used to generate PDF output with pdfTeX or with the DVIPDFMx driver.

\section[\texttt{zref} -- A new reference scheme for LaTeX]{\texttt{zref} -- A new reference scheme for LaTeX}\label{pkg:zref}
\index{Package!zref}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/zref}
\item[name] \texttt{zref}
\item[caption] A new reference scheme for LaTeX
\item[author] Oberdiek, Heiko
\index{Author!Oberdiek, Heiko}
\item[copyright] Heiko Oberdiek (2006-2012)
\item[copyright] Oberdiek Package Support Group (2016-2026)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 2.37 (2026-03-07)
\item[last changes] 2026-03-07
\item[year] 2026
\index{Year!2026}
\item[description] (no language specified) This package offers a means to remove the limitation, of only two properties, that is inherent in the 
          way LaTeX’s reference system works. The package implements an extensible referencing system, where properties 
          may be defined and used in the course of a document. It provides an interface for macro programmers to 
          access the new reference scheme and some modules that use it.

          Modules available are:

          \begin{itemize}
          \item  \texttt{zref-user} , use \texttt{zref} for ''traditional'' labels and references;
          \item  \texttt{zref-abspage} , retrieve absolute page numbers (physical pages, as opposed to the ‘logical’ page number that is normally typeset when a page number is requested;
          \item  \texttt{zref-lastpage} , provide a zref-label for the last page of the document;
          \item  \texttt{zref-nextpage} , provide the page number of the next page of the document;
          \item  \texttt{zref-totpages} , provide the total number of pages in the document;
          \item  \texttt{zref-pagelayout} , provide the page layout parameters of a each page (which may then be printed at the end of the document);
          \item  \texttt{zref-perpage} , make a counter reset for each new page;
          \item  \texttt{zref-titleref} , make section title or caption text available through the reference system; \texttt{zref-savepos} , make positions on a page available;
          \item  \texttt{zref-dotfill} , controlled dot-filling;
          \item  \texttt{zref-env} , record the latest environment’s name and the line it started on; and
          \item  \texttt{zref-xr} , provide the facilities of the \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xr}{xr} and \href{https://ctan.org/pkg/xr-hyper}{xr-hyper} packages.
          \end{itemize}
\item[documentation]  (no language specified) \textit{Package documentation}: \url{https://ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/zref/zref.pdf}
\item[-- local file] \verb|./5898491911-zref.pdf|

\index{Contact!repository}

\section[\texttt{zref-check} -- Flexible cross-references with contextual checks based on zr\ldots]{\texttt{zref-check} -- Flexible cross-references with contextual checks based on zref}\label{pkg:zref-check}
\index{Package!zref-check}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/zref-check}
\item[name] \texttt{zref-check}
\item[caption] Flexible cross-references with contextual checks based on zref
\item[author] gusbrs
\index{Author!gusbrs}
\item[copyright] gusbrs (2021-2024)
\item[license] lppl1.3c = The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c (free)
\index{License!lppl1.3c}
\index{License!The LaTeX Project Public License 1.3c}
\item[version] 0.3.7
\item[description] (no language specified) This package provides an user interface for making LaTeX cross-references flexibly, while allowing to 
          have them checked for consistency with the document structure as typeset. 

          Statements such 
          as ''above'', ''on the next page'', ''previously'', ''as will be discussed'', ''on the previous chapter'' 
          and so on can be given to \texttt{{\textbackslash}zcheck} in free-form, and a set of 
          ''checks'' can be specified to be run against a given ''label'', which will result in a warning at compilation 
          time if any of these checks fail.

          \texttt{{\textbackslash}zctarget} and 
          the \texttt{zcregion} environment are also defined as a means to easily set label targets 
          to arbitrary places in the text which can be referred to by \texttt{{\textbackslash}zcheck} .

\index{Package!zztex}

\begin{labeling}{Web page on CTAN}
\item[Web page on CTAN] \url{https://ctan.org/pkg/zztex}
\item[name] \texttt{ZzTeX}
\item[caption] A full-featured TeX macro package for producing books, journals, and manuals
\item[author] Anagnostopoulos, Paul C.
\index{Author!Anagnostopoulos, Paul C.}
\item[copyright] Paul C. Anagnostopoulos (1989-2020)
\item[license] mit = MIT License (free)
\index{License!mit}
\index{License!MIT License}
\item[version] 17.7
\item[description] (no language specified) The ZzTeX macro package is a full-featured TeX macro package specially designed for producing books, 
          journals, and manuals. Development of the package began in 1989. Since then, about 500 textbooks and 
          journals have been produced with it for a variety of publishers. Numerous authors have used the package 
          to produce subsequent editions of their books.

          ZzTeX runs under Plain TeX.

          The only documentation available for the package is contained in the  \texttt{zz*.dat} files 
          that accompany the TeX files.
